It is recorded here only because TC-AUTH-ISO-003 step 2 expects the API to *reject* (401/403) a JWT whose `tenant_id` does not match the resolved subdomain, and `/auth/me` does not — the same missing `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId` invariant, on the read path. SAME root cause as BUG-003; NOT re-filed. No data mutated.
  - **US-AUTH-007 `TenantResolutionMiddleware` — ★ ROOT LOCUS of this bug ★ — CONFIRMED 2026-06-25 (cross-tenant READ of users on TWO independent victim tenants, plus a log-level smoking gun for the split-brain).** US-AUTH-007 is the user story that *owns* the tenant-resolution middleware where this defect lives; TC-AUTH-054 (the story's "resolved tenant context prevents cross-tenant data exposure" case) is arguably the canonical test for BUG-003, and it **FAILS**. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (JWT `tenant_id=acme` `019ef3ba-…`), `GET /api/v1/tenant/users` under header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: e2e` → **HTTP 200** returning the **e2e** tenant's user list (`owner@e2e.test`), and under `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → **HTTP 200** returning **techoneglobal's** user list (`sachithra@techoneglobal.org`) — NOT acme's 6 users. **Log-level smoking gun (Serilog `hrm-20260625.log`, RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI2QT`/`…QU`):** the `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` line for the suspended-tenant arm logged `Authorization denied … Tenant=019ef3ba-…[acme] … MissingPermission=Tenant.ManageUsers` while the SAME request's Serilog `tenant_id` enricher property read `019efa84-…[qa04-react-1]` — i.e. the **authz layer evaluates the permission against the TOKEN's tenant (`CurrentUser.TenantId`), while the data/query layer + status middleware operate on the SUBDOMAIN-RESOLVED tenant (`ITenantContext.TenantId`)**, and the two are never required to match. That split-brain is the mechanical heart of BUG-003: a token whose role-permissions happen to satisfy the check is then served entirely in the foreign resolved tenant's context. **Same-request confirmation of the status path:** the acme Tenant Admin token under suspended `X-Tenant-Subdomain: qa04-react-1` reached `TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware` and got **HTTP 451** (`tenant_suspended`) — proving the acme token was treated as an authorized principal of qa04-react-1 (it passed authz against the foreign resolved tenant before the suspension gate fired). **Contrast that localizes it:** the SAME acme token with the CORRECT `acme` subdomain returns ONLY acme's 6 users — the EF query filter on the resolved tenant scopes correctly; the only hole is the unvalidated pre-auth `X-Tenant-Subdomain` (dev) / host (prod) selecting the tenant with no `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId` guard after authentication (`TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs:56-146` runs before `UseAuthentication`/`UseAuthorization` at `Program.cs:360/363-364`, and nothing downstream re-links token↔resolved-tenant). NOT re-filed — this is the root-story confirmation, so the canonical fix belongs here (add the invariant in/after auth and an integration test that replays tenant-A's token against tenant-B's subdomain expecting 403). **READ-ONLY probe — ZERO writes to e2e/techoneglobal/qa04-react-1; no data mutated.** (This is why TC-AUTH-054 FAILS, and reinforces the already-recorded TC-AUTH-ISO-001/ISO-003 failures.)

### BUG-004 — Tenant password policy is STORED but NEVER ENFORCED: password reset validates against a HARDCODED rule, ignoring the configured policy — AC-4/FR-5 enforcement contract unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #127, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-006 · TC-ADM-006-12 (AC-4 enforcement "read from the CURRENT tenant policy")
- **Title:** US-ADM-006 persists a per-tenant password policy (min length, complexity flags, history count, max age) to the Tenant row, but no password-setting path reads it. `ResetPasswordValidator` enforces a **hardcoded** policy (min 12 + upper/lower/digit/special); password history and max-age are enforced nowhere; and there is **no change-password endpoint at all**. So tightening or loosening the tenant policy via the settings API has zero effect on what passwords are actually accepted.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `ResetPasswordValidator` (`src/backend/HRM.Application/Features/Auth/Validators/ResetPasswordValidator.cs`) hardcodes `.MinimumLength(12)` + `.Matches("[A-Z]"|"[a-z]"|"[0-9]"|"[^a-zA-Z0-9]")` with no reference to the tenant's `MinPasswordLength`/`RequireUppercase`/… columns. A repo-wide grep shows the tenant password-policy fields (`MinPasswordLength`, `RequireUppercase`, `PasswordHistoryCount`, `PasswordMaxAgeDays`, …) are referenced **only** by `TenantSettingsService` (which writes them) and its unit test — **no** consumer reads them for enforcement. There is no `IPasswordPolicyService`/`PasswordValidator` that loads the tenant policy. `AuthController` exposes only `forgot-password`/`reset-password` (`AuthController.cs:144-174`); there is no authenticated change-password action, so an in-session user cannot even trigger a tenant-policy-validated change. History (`PasswordHistoryCount`) and max-age (`PasswordMaxAgeDays`) have no enforcement seam at all.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `PUT /api/v1/tenant/settings/password-policy` with `minLength: 8` (or any value) → 200, persisted (verified via GET).
  2. Inspect `ResetPasswordValidator` — its `MinimumLength(12)` and complexity matches are literal constants, independent of tenant `minLength`. A reset still demands ≥12 even though the tenant policy now says 8; conversely setting `minLength: 20` would NOT be enforced (reset still allows 12). The validator never loads the tenant row.
  3. Grep `RequireUppercase|PasswordHistoryCount|PasswordMaxAgeDays` across `src/backend/**/*.cs` (excluding migrations/tests) → only `TenantSettingsService.cs` (writer) matches; no reader/enforcer.
- **Evidence:** `password-policy` PUT → 200 persisted; `ResetPasswordValidator` source shows hardcoded `MinimumLength(12)` + complexity, no tenant lookup; grep confirms zero enforcement consumers of the policy fields; no `change-password` route in any controller. (Persona passwords were NOT actually reset — this is established by code path + the persistence/grep evidence, fail-closed, to avoid lockout risk.)
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — AC-4/FR-5 (a core, security-relevant story acceptance criterion: "policy enforced from the live tenant configuration; a tighter policy takes effect immediately") is genuinely absent. A tenant admin who tightens the policy for compliance gets a false sense of protection — the tighter rule is silently ignored. Not CRIT because a reasonable hardcoded floor (12 + full complexity) *does* apply on reset, so the system isn't accepting trivially weak passwords; the defect is that the **configured** policy is inert and history/max-age/loosening/tightening are unenforced.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev should introduce a tenant-policy-aware password validator consulted by reset/change paths, add an authenticated change-password endpoint, and implement history + max-age checks; add an integration test that sets `minLength: 20` and asserts a 12-char reset is rejected.)

### BUG-005 — Localization update validates ONLY the language; invalid date-format, IANA time zone, and ISO-4217 currency are silently accepted and stored — FR-4 "no silent acceptance of an unrenderable value" unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #162, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05) — **STILL PRESENT (regression re-confirmed 2026-06-27)**: acme PUT `/tenant/settings/localization` with `dateFormat:"QQ-WW-ZZ", timeZone:"Mars/Olympus", currency:"ZZZ"` → 200 "Localization settings updated." stored verbatim. Reverted to sane values after probe. Unchanged.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-006 · TC-ADM-006-09 (steps 2/3/4)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/tenant/settings/localization` rejects an unsupported `defaultLanguage` (good) but performs NO validation on `dateFormat`, `timeZone`, or `currency` — a garbage date-format token (`QQ-WW-ZZ`), a non-existent IANA zone (`Mars/Olympus`), and a non-ISO currency (`ZZZ`) are all accepted with HTTP 200 and persisted verbatim, becoming the tenant-wide default that downstream rendering cannot honor.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~95%):** `TenantSettingsService.UpdateLocalizationAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/TenantSettingsService.cs:96-121`) validates only the language (`SupportedLanguages.IsSupported`, `:99`) and then trims-and-stores `DateFormat`/`TimeZone`/`Currency` with no validation (`:111-114`). There is no localization validator class (only Org/Password/Session validators exist under `Features/TenantSettings/Validators/`), and no IANA-timezone or ISO-4217-currency or date-format-token check anywhere in the path.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`.
  2. `PUT http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/settings/localization` body `{"defaultLanguage":"en","dateFormat":"QQ-WW-ZZ","numberFormat":"1,234.56","timeZone":"UTC","currency":"USD"}` → **HTTP 200** (garbage date format stored).
  3. `… "timeZone":"Mars/Olympus" …` → **HTTP 200** (non-IANA zone stored).
  4. `… "currency":"ZZZ" …` → **HTTP 200** (non-ISO currency stored); `GET /api/v1/tenant/settings` echoes `currency:"ZZZ"`.
  5. Contrast: `defaultLanguage:"xx"` → **HTTP 400** "Unsupported language 'xx'. Supported: en, si, ta." (language IS validated).
- **Evidence:** three PUTs above each returned `{"success":true,...,"message":"Localization settings updated."}` HTTP 200; the follow-up GET returned the bogus `timeZone`/`currency` values. (acme localization reverted to baseline `en / dd MMM yyyy / 1,234.56 / UTC / USD` after the run.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-4 explicitly requires rejecting an unrenderable date-format/time-zone/currency ("no silent acceptance"), and the value becomes the tenant-wide default for all users without a preference, so a bad value degrades rendering tenant-wide; but it is contained (tenant-scoped, no security/data-integrity impact, recoverable by re-saving) and language — the most user-visible field — IS validated. Above LOW because it is a stated FR with a concrete unmet behavior, not cosmetic.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Validate `timeZone` against `TimeZoneInfo.TryFindSystemTimeZoneById`/IANA, `currency` against an ISO-4217 set, and `dateFormat` against an allow-list of supported tokens; mirror the existing language allow-list pattern.)

### ISSUE-008 — Branding logo at/near the 2 MB cap is rejected at the Kestrel request-size limit with an opaque 400, before the friendly validator runs — at-limit boundary (TC-05 step 2 "accept") fails
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #364, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-006 · TC-ADM-006-05 (step 2 — "~2MB PNG logo → 200 accepted at boundary")
- **Title:** `[RequestSizeLimit(MaxUploadBytes)]` on the upload actions equals the validator's `LogoMaxBytes` (exactly 2,097,152 bytes) and caps the **whole multipart request**, while `BrandingFileValidator` caps the **file body** with `content.Length > maxBytes` (i.e. a file *equal* to 2 MB is meant to be accepted). Because the multipart envelope (boundary + part headers) adds ~150-200 bytes, a logo whose body is at/just under 2 MB pushes the total request over the Kestrel limit and is rejected with a generic `400 "Failed to read the request..."` (RFC9110 problem-details) before the friendly "Logo exceeds the maximum size of 2 MB" path can run.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `TenantSettingsController` sets `MaxUploadBytes = BrandingFileValidator.LogoMaxBytes` (2 MB) as the `[RequestSizeLimit]` (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Controllers/TenantSettingsController.cs:25,125/137/147`), but that limit applies to the entire request body including multipart overhead, whereas `BrandingFileValidator.Validate` compares only `content.Length` against the same 2 MB (`BrandingFileValidator.cs:49-55`, `>` not `>=`). The two limits being numerically equal leaves a dead-band: file bodies in roughly `[2MB − overhead, 2MB]` are rejected by Kestrel with an opaque message instead of being accepted (or rejected with the friendly validator message). Live probe: 2,000,000-byte logo → 200; 2,097,152-byte (== cap) logo → 400 opaque.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`.
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/settings/branding/logo` (multipart `file=@logo.png`) with a valid-PNG body of **2,000,000** bytes → **HTTP 200** accepted.
  3. Same with a valid-PNG body of **2,097,152** bytes (exactly `LogoMaxBytes`) → **HTTP 400** `{"type":".../rfc9110#section-15.5.1","title":"One or more validation errors occurred.","errors":{"":["Failed to read the request..."]}}` — Kestrel size-limit rejection, not the friendly "Logo exceeds the maximum size of 2 MB."
- **Evidence:** 2,000,000 B → 200 `{"assetKind":"Logo",...}`; 2,097,152 B → 400 RFC9110 problem-details "Failed to read the request"; 2.5 MB → same opaque 400 (over-limit, correctly rejected but with the opaque message). The favicon over-limit path (600 KB) DID return the friendly "Favicon exceeds the maximum size of 500 KB." because the favicon body (>500 KB) reaches the validator under the 2 MB request cap.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the security intent (reject oversize) still holds; the defect is a thin at-the-cap boundary band where a nominally-acceptable file is rejected with a confusing generic error instead of being accepted or given the clear validator message. No security/data impact; a user just re-exports a slightly smaller logo. Contract/UX correctness only.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Set `[RequestSizeLimit]` slightly above the validator cap to leave room for multipart overhead, or align the validator to `>=` and document the effective cap, so the friendly validator message is what users see at the boundary.)

### ISSUE-009 — Session-policy update has no cross-field idle ≤ absolute invariant: idle 1440 min (24 h) with absolute 1 h is accepted — TC-13 step 5 "reject idle > absolute" unmet (also: minutes-vs-hours unit mismatch)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #364, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-006 · TC-ADM-006-13 (step 5 — "PUT idle 600 > absolute 480 → reject; idle must be ≤ absolute")
- **Title:** `UpdateSessionPolicyValidator` enforces each field's range independently but has **no** cross-field rule that idle ≤ absolute, so a nonsensical policy where the idle timeout exceeds the absolute timeout is accepted (HTTP 200). Compounding it, `idleTimeoutMinutes` is in MINUTES while `absoluteTimeoutHours` is in HOURS, so the TC's literal data (idle 600, absolute 480) is not even a real conflict (600 min = 10 h < 480 h) — but a genuine conflict (idle 1440 min = 24 h, absolute 1 h) is still accepted.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `UpdateSessionPolicyValidator` (`src/backend/HRM.Application/Features/TenantSettings/Validators/UpdateSessionPolicyValidator.cs:11-26`) has only per-field `InclusiveBetween` rules (idle 1-1440 min, absolute 1-720 h, max-concurrent 1-100) and a strategy allow-list — no `.Must(... idleHours <= absoluteHours ...)` relating the two. The DTO/columns store idle as minutes and absolute as hours (`SessionPolicyDto(IdleTimeoutMinutes, AbsoluteTimeoutHours, …)`), so any cross-field rule must normalize units first.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`.
  2. `PUT /api/v1/tenant/settings/session-policy` body `{"idleTimeoutMinutes":1440,"absoluteTimeoutHours":1,"maxConcurrentSessions":3,"concurrentSessionStrategy":"revoke_oldest"}` → **HTTP 200** (idle 24 h > absolute 1 h, accepted).
  3. The TC's own data `{"idleTimeoutMinutes":600,"absoluteTimeoutHours":480,...}` → **HTTP 200** as well — note 600 min < 480 h, so it is not a true conflict (unit mismatch in the TC).
  4. Single-field boundaries all behave: idle 0/1441 → 400, absolute 721 → 400, max-concurrent 0/101 → 400, strategy "bogus" → 400.
- **Evidence:** idle-1440/absolute-1 PUT → `{"success":true,...,"idleTimeoutMinutes":1440,"absoluteTimeoutHours":1,...}` HTTP 200; all single-field out-of-range arms correctly 400. (acme session policy reverted to baseline idle 60 / absolute 24 h / max 5 / revoke_oldest.)
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth / config-sanity only; a self-inflicted nonsensical policy by a tenant admin, no cross-tenant or security impact, and enforcement (Authentication module) would apply the absolute cap regardless. The single-field ranges that actually bound the values all work. Worth recording because the TC explicitly asserts the idle ≤ absolute relation and it is absent; the TC's literal data also can't trigger it due to the minutes/hours mismatch.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Add a cross-field rule normalizing units, e.g. reject when `idleTimeoutMinutes > absoluteTimeoutHours * 60`; and reconcile the TC's example data with the minutes-vs-hours unit convention.)

> **Audit-completeness theme (recurrence, not re-filed):** US-ADM-006 settings audit rows (`tenant_settings.*`) written by `TenantSettingsService.PersistAsync` (`TenantSettingsService.cs:267-288`) carry actor/action/before/after/timestamp/tenant correctly, but — like [[ISSUE-006]] for US-ADM-005's `UserManagementService.WriteAudit` — leave `ip_address` and `user_agent` NULL (no `IHttpContextAccessor` sourced). Verified in psql across all six `tenant_settings.*` event types. Per the run instruction, this is referenced against ISSUE-006 (same forensic-envelope gap, distinct service) rather than re-filed. Denied/unauthenticated settings attempts correctly wrote NO settings-change audit row (TC-14 step 6 / TC-16 step 8 satisfied).

### BUG-006 — Restoring an archived workflow while another active workflow exists for the same entity type throws HTTP 500 (BR-2 auto-archive-on-restore collides with the partial unique index) — FR-6/BR-2 restore path broken on real Postgres
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #172, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out) — **(historical pre-fix note, since fixed by #172; regression re-confirmed 2026-06-27)**: in acme, created Leave workflow A (`activate:true`), archived it, created Leave workflow B (`activate:true`), then `POST /tenant/workflows/{A}/restore` → 500. Serilog: `SqlState: 23505 … duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ix_workflow_definitions_tenant_entitytype_active"` (`hrm-20260627.log` RequestId 0HNMJGENHI1IC). Both test workflows deleted afterward; acme back to 0-workflow baseline. NOTE the create request now carries an explicit `activate` bool (workflows are created Draft/inactive unless `activate:true`) and step approver is `approverIdentifier` (Guid role/user id) — a contract refinement vs the baseline pass. Unchanged defect.
- **Layer:** BE (DB-interaction)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-007 · TC-ADM-007-09 (step 5 — restore governed by the same one-active-per-entity-type/BR-2 rule)
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/tenant/workflows/{id}/restore` returns **HTTP 500 "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."** when the archived workflow being restored has the same entity type as a currently-ACTIVE workflow. The restore is supposed to auto-archive the conflicting active workflow (BR-2) and reactivate the target; instead it crashes. Restore with NO same-type conflict works correctly (200).
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~85%):** `WorkflowService.RestoreAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/WorkflowService.cs:300-333`) calls `ArchiveActiveForEntityTypeAsync(workflow.EntityType, …, excludeId: workflow.Id)` to flip the conflicting active row `is_active true→false`, then sets the restored row `is_active = true`, and persists **both** mutations in a single `PersistAsync` → `SaveChangesAsync` (`:528-545`). PostgreSQL enforces a **partial unique index** `ix_workflow_definitions_tenant_entitytype_active ON (tenant_id, entity_type, is_active) WHERE is_active = true AND is_deleted = false` (verified via `pg_indexes`). EF Core does not guarantee the UPDATE-to-false is flushed before the UPDATE-to-true within one `SaveChanges`, so the index transiently sees two `is_active=true` rows for `(acme, Leave)` and raises a unique-violation, which surfaces as the generic 500. The CREATE path's BR-2 auto-archive does NOT hit this (the new row is an INSERT, ordered after the UPDATE-to-false), which is why TC-ADM-007-03 (create second active) passed while restore-with-conflict fails. Confidence ~85%: the index + the dual-UPDATE-in-one-SaveChanges are confirmed; the exact EF statement ordering that trips it is the inferred mechanism (a dev should capture the inner `DbUpdateException`/SQLSTATE 23505 from the server log to confirm).
- **Why it slipped through:** `WorkflowServiceTests.Restore_AutoArchivesCurrentActiveForSameType()` (`src/backend/HRM.Tests/Unit/WorkflowServiceTests.cs`) **passes** (19/19) because it runs on the EF **InMemory** provider, which does NOT enforce the partial unique index — a mock/provider-divergence: the unit test gives false confidence that the BR-2-on-restore path works. This is the classic real-Postgres-vs-InMemory gap; only a Testcontainers/real-DB integration test (or this live API run) catches it.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-24 as `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. Create an active Leave workflow "Leave-B" (`POST /api/v1/tenant/workflows` `{"entityType":"Leave","activate":true,"steps":[…1 valid step…]}`) → 200.
  2. Archive it (`POST .../{leaveB}/archive`) → 200 (status Archived).
  3. Create a NEW active Leave workflow "Leave-C" (`activate:true`) → 200 (now the single active Leave).
  4. Restore the archived Leave-B (`POST .../{leaveB}/restore`) → **HTTP 500** `{"success":false,"message":"An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."}`.
  5. Control — remove the conflict first: archive Leave-C (`POST .../{leaveC}/archive`) → 200, THEN restore Leave-B → **HTTP 200** "Workflow restored." (proves the workflow itself is restorable; only the same-type-conflict path crashes).
- **Evidence:** step-4 → HTTP 500 generic body; step-5 control → HTTP 200 "Workflow restored."; `pg_indexes` shows the partial unique index `ix_workflow_definitions_tenant_entitytype_active … WHERE ((is_active = true) AND (is_deleted = false))`; `WorkflowServiceTests` (InMemory) reports the same scenario as passing (19/19, 0 failed).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a documented FR-6/BR-2 restore behavior is broken (and returns an opaque 500 rather than a clean result or a 409), but it is contained: it only triggers when restoring into an entity type that already has an active workflow, the happy restore path (no conflict) works, no data is corrupted (the transaction rolls back — no partial state was left after the failed restore in repro), and there is no security/isolation impact. Above LOW because it is a genuine functional defect on a primary management action, not cosmetic; below HIGH because the conflict-free restore path (the common case) works and there is a manual workaround (archive the conflicting active workflow first).
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would order the writes so the conflicting row's `is_active=false` is flushed before the restored row's `is_active=true` — e.g. an intermediate `SaveChanges`, a deferred-constraint approach, or explicit statement ordering — and add a **real-Postgres** (Testcontainers) integration test for restore-with-same-type-conflict, since the InMemory unit test cannot reproduce it.)

### ISSUE-010 — BR-2 auto-archive of a prior active workflow writes NO `workflow.archived` audit row (NFR-4 "archive transition is audited" unmet for the auto-archive side)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #366, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-007 · TC-ADM-007-03 (step 5 — "audit_log has entries for Leave-B create AND Leave-A auto-archive")
- **Title:** When creating (or restoring) an active workflow auto-archives the previously-active workflow for the same entity type (BR-2), only ONE audit row is written — `workflow.created` (or `workflow.restored`) for the NEW workflow. The auto-archived prior workflow gets **no** `workflow.archived` audit row, and the create's `after` snapshot does not reference the sibling that was archived. TC-03 step 5 explicitly requires an audit entry for the auto-archive; NFR-4 says the archive transition is audited.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `ArchiveActiveForEntityTypeAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/WorkflowService.cs:485-498`) flips the conflicting active rows to `is_active=false`/`Archived` in-memory but writes **no** audit row of its own; the single `PersistAsync` call in the caller (`CreateAsync` `:179-180` / `RestoreAsync` `:330`) audits only the NEW/target workflow. There is no per-archived-sibling `workflow.archived` audit emission in the auto-archive helper.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`), create an active Leave workflow "A" → 200.
  2. Create a SECOND active Leave workflow "B" (`activate:true`) → 200 (auto-archives "A" per BR-2).
  3. `SELECT event_type, resource_id FROM audit_logs WHERE event_type LIKE 'workflow.%' ORDER BY created_at DESC` → you see `workflow.created` for B but **no** `workflow.archived` (or any) row referencing A's id from the auto-archive.
- **Evidence:** psql audit query after a create-second-active sequence showed `workflow.created` rows only (one per explicit create); the auto-archived prior workflow's id had no `workflow.archived` row. (Explicit user-initiated `POST /{id}/archive` DOES write a `workflow.archived` row — confirmed in TC-09 — so only the IMPLICIT BR-2 auto-archive side is unaudited.)
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the BR-2 invariant itself works correctly (exactly one active workflow remains) and the explicit archive action is audited; this is an audit-completeness/forensic gap (a tenant admin can't see in the audit trail that workflow A was retired as a side effect of activating B). No security, data-correctness, or functional impact. Same family as the broader audit-envelope gaps ([[ISSUE-005]] denied-not-audited / [[ISSUE-006]] missing IP/UA), recorded here because TC-03 step 5 explicitly asserts it.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Emit a `workflow.archived` audit row for each row the BR-2 helper auto-archives, or include the archived sibling id(s) in the creating workflow's audit `after` snapshot.)

### ISSUE-011 — Workflow create/edit/archive/restore return HTTP 200 (not 201) and the plan-limit rejection is 409 (not 400/422) — contract drift vs the US-ADM-007 TCs
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · WONTFIX (LOW-tier triage 2026-07-18 — reason in LOW-TIER-TRIAGE.md §B)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-007 · TC-ADM-007-02 (step 1 "201") / TC-ADM-007-03/-04 / TC-ADM-007-05 (step 3 "HTTP 400/422")
- **Title:** Several US-ADM-007 endpoints diverge from the status codes the TCs specify: (a) `POST /api/v1/tenant/workflows` (create) returns **200** with the created body, not **201 Created** + `Location` as TC-02/-03 assert; and (b) the plan-limit rejection is **409 Conflict** with code `workflow_limit_reached`, while TC-05 step 3 expects **400/422**. The behaviors are otherwise correct (creation works, the exact AC-4 plan-limit MESSAGE is produced) — only the HTTP status contract drifts.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~95%):** `WorkflowsController.Create` returns `Ok(ApiResponse<…>.Ok(…, "Workflow created."))` (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Controllers/WorkflowsController.cs:70`) — `Ok(...)` is 200; there is no `CreatedAtAction`/201. `EnsureWithinPlanLimitAsync` returns `Result.Failure(string.Format(PlanLimitMessageTemplate, limit.Value), 409, "workflow_limit_reached")` (`WorkflowService.cs:477-479`), so the controller's `StatusCode(result.StatusCode ?? 400, …)` emits **409**, not 400/422. This mirrors the same 200-instead-of-201 convention seen across the other Admin Console controllers in this codebase (US-ADM-001 create-tenant was 201, but US-ADM-005/006 mutations and now US-ADM-007 use 200) — i.e. it is a house style, surfaced here because the TC text literally says 201/400.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`), `POST /api/v1/tenant/workflows` with a valid 1-step body → **HTTP 200** (TC-02 expects 201), body is the created `WorkflowDetailDto`.
  2. (Plan-limit arm — code path only, see TC-05 BLOCKED note): when a tenant with a finite `MaxWorkflows` is at its limit, create returns **HTTP 409** `{"code":"workflow_limit_reached","message":"You have reached the maximum number of workflows ({limit}) for your plan. Please upgrade or archive an existing workflow."}` (TC-05 expects 400/422; the MESSAGE itself is exactly correct).
- **Evidence:** live create → `__HTTP__200` with `{"success":true,"data":{…"version":1…},"message":"Workflow created."}`; plan-limit status/code read from `WorkflowService.cs:477-479` (`409`, `workflow_limit_reached`) + the exact-message template at `:40-41`. Edit/archive/restore similarly return 200 (correct for those).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — pure contract/status-code drift; every operation is functionally correct and the FE (which reads the `success` envelope, not the HTTP status) is unaffected. No data, security, or behavioral impact. Recorded because the TCs assert specific codes (201 on create, 400/422 on plan-limit) that the API does not emit — a strict contract test or a client keying off status codes would see a mismatch.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Either align the API to 201-on-create / 400-or-422-on-plan-limit, or update the US-ADM-007 TCs to the codebase's house convention of 200 + `success:false` envelope and 409 for limit conflicts — a documentation/convention decision, not a defect to silently fix.)

### BUG-007 — Audit-log keyword `search=` returns HTTP 500 on real Postgres: `string.Contains` is run against `jsonb` before/after columns and cannot be translated — FR-1 full-text search 100% non-functional
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #125, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE (DB-interaction)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-008 · TC-ADM-008-07 (keyword search over before/after JSON)
- **Title:** `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?search={any-non-empty}` returns **HTTP 500 "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."** for EVERY non-empty search term. The absent/empty-string cases work (200), so the keyword-search filter (a documented AC-2/FR-1 capability) is completely broken on the production PostgreSQL provider. All other list filters (date/actor/action/resourceType/combined/multi-select) work correctly.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `AuditLogService.BuildFilteredQuery` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AuditLogService.cs:212-219`) implements the search as `query.Where(a => (a.Before != null && a.Before.Contains(q)) || (a.After != null && a.After.Contains(q)) || (a.Detail != null && a.Detail.Contains(q)))`. The CLR type of `AuditLog.Before`/`AuditLog.After` is `string`, but they are mapped to PostgreSQL **`jsonb`** columns (`AuditLogConfiguration.cs:42-45` `.HasColumnType("jsonb")`; verified in `information_schema.columns`: `before`/`after` = `jsonb`, `detail` = `character varying`). Npgsql cannot translate `string.Contains` (a `LIKE '%q%'`) over a `jsonb` column — `jsonb` has no implicit text-pattern operator — so the query throws at execution and `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` returns the generic 500. `detail` (varchar) alone would translate fine; it is the two `jsonb` predicates that break it. A correct implementation would cast `before::text`/`after::text` (e.g. `EF.Functions.ILike(EF.Property<string>(a,"Before") + "", ...)` via a text cast, or `a.Before` typed as `string` over a `text` column, or a jsonb-aware `@>`/`jsonb_path` search).
- **Why it slipped through:** `AuditLogServiceTests` (`src/backend/HRM.Tests/Unit/AuditLogServiceTests.cs`, 26/26 green) exercises the search filter on the EF **InMemory** provider, where `Before`/`After` are plain in-memory strings and `.Contains` evaluates client-side without any jsonb translation — so the unit test passes while the real-Postgres path 500s. This is the SAME mock/real-Postgres divergence pattern as [[BUG-006]] (InMemory hides a Postgres-only constraint/translation failure); only a Testcontainers/real-DB test or this live run catches it.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-24 as `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?search=qa07` → **HTTP 500** `{"success":false,"message":"An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.","code":null,...}`.
  2. `GET .../audit-logs?search=PrimaryColor` → **HTTP 500** (same).
  3. Control: `GET .../audit-logs` (no search) → **HTTP 200**; `GET .../audit-logs?search=` (empty) → **HTTP 200**. Only a non-empty `search` triggers the crash.
  4. **Re-confirmed 2026-06-25 during the US-CHR-007 run** (incidental, while checking location audit coverage): `GET .../audit-logs?search=ocation` → **HTTP 500**; the Serilog log (`hrm-20260625.log`) captured the exact exception `Npgsql.PostgresException 42883: operator does not exist: jsonb ~~ jsonb` thrown from `AuditLogService.ListAsync` at `AuditLogService.cs:line 75`, surfaced by `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:line 27` — confirming the `LIKE` (`~~`) over a `jsonb` column root cause above with a real logged stack. SAME defect; NOT re-filed.
- **Evidence:** both non-empty-search calls returned the generic 500 problem body; no-search and empty-search returned 200. `information_schema.columns` → `audit_logs.before`/`after` = `jsonb`. The service search predicate is a `string.Contains` over those columns (`AuditLogService.cs:212-219`). `AuditLogServiceTests` reports the search scenario as passing on InMemory (26/26, 0 failed).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a documented AC-2/FR-1 list capability (full-text search over the change summary) is **entirely** non-functional on the real database (every term 500s) AND it fails with an opaque 500 rather than a graceful empty/400, which is a poor failure mode an operator hits the moment they type in the search box. Not CRIT: it is one optional filter, no data/security/isolation impact, and the other six filter dimensions + list/detail/export all work, so the audit log remains usable without search. (The export path does NOT accept `search` server-side in the same broken way only because callers rarely pass it, but `ExportAsync` runs the identical `BuildFilteredQuery` — an export WITH `search` would 500 too.)
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev should make the search jsonb-aware — cast `before::text`/`after::text` for the `LIKE`, or use a jsonb text-search operator — keep the `detail` varchar branch, and add a **real-Postgres** (Testcontainers) integration test asserting `search=<term>` returns 200 with the matching subset, since InMemory cannot reproduce the failure.)

### ISSUE-012 — Audit-log inverted date range (`startDate > endDate`) returns HTTP 200 with 0 rows instead of 400 — TC-03 step 5 "invalid range" unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #364, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-008 · TC-ADM-008-03 (step 5 — "GET with start_date > end_date → 400 validation error")
- **Title:** `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?startDate={later}&endDate={earlier}` is accepted as a valid request and returns **HTTP 200** with an empty result set, rather than the **400** the TC requires for an invalid (inverted) range. The two bounds are applied as independent `>=`/`<=` predicates with no cross-field check, so a reversed range simply matches nothing.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `AuditLogService.BuildFilteredQuery` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AuditLogService.cs:191-195`) applies `StartDate` and `EndDate` as separate `query.Where(a => a.CreatedAt >= start)` / `query.Where(a => a.CreatedAt <= end)` clauses, and `ListAuditLogsQuery`/its handler have no `startDate <= endDate` validator (there is no FluentValidation validator for the list query at all). An inverted range therefore yields `CreatedAt >= later AND CreatedAt <= earlier`, which is satisfiable by no row → 200 / empty. Same silent-no-op-instead-of-400 family as [[ISSUE-003]] (invalid status enum) and the broader "validate inputs, don't silently widen/empty" theme.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`), `GET .../audit-logs?startDate=2026-06-25T00:00:00Z&endDate=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` → **HTTP 200**, `totalCount=0`.
  2. Contrast: a correct range (`startDate=2026-06-24T00:00:00Z&endDate=2026-06-25T00:00:00Z`) → 200 with the day's rows; boundary inclusivity verified (start=end=exact-row-UTC-timestamp → that 1 row returned).
- **Evidence:** inverted-range call → HTTP 200 `totalCount=0` (no `message`/error code); correct-range and boundary-inclusive calls behave correctly. No list-query validator exists; the date predicates are independent `>=`/`<=` (`AuditLogService.cs:191-195`).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — contract-correctness only; the happy-path and boundary date filtering are correct, an inverted range harmlessly returns empty (no data leak, no error), and the FE date-picker normally prevents it. Worth recording because TC-03 step 5 explicitly asserts a 400 for an invalid range and the API does not produce one.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Add a list-query validator that rejects `startDate > endDate` with 400 `invalid_date_range`; mirror the existing per-endpoint FluentValidation pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.)

### BUG-008 — Plan-limit propagation is BROKEN: a plan edit does NOT reach existing tenants AND per-tenant overrides have NO runtime effect — `Tenant.MaxEmployees` snapshot is enforced, the live plan + `PlanLimitResolver` + override table are never consulted (AC-3 / AC-5 / FR-4 runtime contract unmet)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #126, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-009 · TC-ADM-009-07 (AC-3 edit-propagation) + TC-ADM-009-10 (AC-5/FR-4 override runtime effect)
- **Title:** Editing a plan's `max_employees` (100→200) updates the plan row but does **not** change the enforced limit for tenants already provisioned on that plan — the tenant keeps its provisioning-time snapshot (`tenants.max_employees`). Likewise, a per-tenant `plan_limit_override` created via the management API has **zero effect** on what is actually enforced. The only live employee-limit check reads the static `Tenant.MaxEmployees` column and never reads the live plan, never calls `PlanLimitResolver.Resolve`, and never reads the `plan_limit_override` table. AC-3 ("existing tenants on that plan immediately benefit from the increased limit") and the AC-5/FR-4 runtime-resolution contract are therefore unmet — the resolver + override table exist and are correct in isolation, but are not wired into any enforcement path.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~92%):** Two coordinated gaps.
  1. **Snapshot, not live-read.** `TenantProvisioningService.ProvisionAsync` copies the plan's limits onto the tenant row at provisioning: `MaxEmployees = plan.MaxEmployees` and `EnabledModules = DeriveTenantModules(plan)` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/TenantProvisioningService.cs:116,120`). Nothing re-derives these when the plan later changes.
  2. **Enforcement reads the snapshot.** `EmployeeService.CheckPlanLimitAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/EmployeeService.cs:745-763`) loads `tenant.MaxEmployees` and compares the active employee count to it (`:751,757`). It does **not** load the `SubscriptionPlan` by the tenant's `PlanId`, does not call `PlanLimitResolver`, and does not read `plan_limit_override`. A repo-wide grep confirms `PlanLimitResolver.Resolve` has **no live callers at all** — it is referenced only by `PlanLimitResolverTests` and `SubscriptionPlanIntegrationTests`. So the override table is write-only from the platform's runtime perspective: rows can be created/updated/removed and audited, but never consulted.
  The service's own XML doc-comment is actively misleading here: `SubscriptionPlanService.cs:21-22` claims "Limits are read live from the plan at runtime, so a plan edit benefits existing tenants immediately (AC-3) — no propagation code." That is false for the employee dimension (the only enforced one) — it reads the tenant snapshot, not the plan. Confidence ~92%: live-proven for `max_employees` below; the "no live caller" claim is grep-confirmed; the only residual uncertainty is whether some *other* limit key (storage/api/etc.) has a different, plan-live enforcement path — but none of those keys have any create-time enforcement at all (see [[BUG-002]]-adjacent note / TC-ADM-009-16 conditional), so the resolver is unreachable platform-wide.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-24 as `admin@hrm.local`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: admin`):**
  1. Create plan `qa09-growth` with `maxEmployees:100` → 201. Provision a throwaway tenant `qa09-ovr-1` on it (`POST /api/v1/system/tenants` with `subscriptionPlanId=<qa09-growth id>`) → 201; verify psql `tenants.max_employees=100` for the new tenant and `GET /api/v1/system/monitoring/tenants/{tid}` → `employeeUsage.limit=100` (snapshot inherited — TC-11 path, correct).
  2. `PUT /api/v1/system/plans/{qa09-growth id}` with `maxEmployees:200` → 200; `GET /api/v1/system/plans/{id}` → `maxEmployees:200` (plan updated).
  3. Re-inspect the tenant: psql `SELECT max_employees FROM tenants WHERE id='<tid>'` → **still 100**; `GET .../monitoring/tenants/{tid}` → `employeeUsage.limit` **still 100**. The plan edit did NOT propagate.
  4. Override arm: `POST /api/v1/system/plans/overrides {tenantId, limitKey:"max_employees", value:200}` → 200, row persisted + audited (`Plan.OverrideCreated`). But `EmployeeService.CheckPlanLimitAsync` never reads `plan_limit_override`, so the effective enforced cap for the tenant is unchanged by the override (code-path confirmed; the resolver that WOULD apply it has no caller).
- **Evidence:** plan `maxEmployees` 100→200 (HTTP 200, GET confirms 200); tenant `max_employees` stayed 100 (psql + monitoring `employeeUsage.limit=100`) after the edit; `EmployeeService.cs:745-763` reads `tenant.MaxEmployees` only; grep shows `PlanLimitResolver.Resolve` called solely from `HRM.Tests/Unit/PlanLimitResolverTests.cs` + `HRM.Tests/Integration/SubscriptionPlanIntegrationTests.cs` (zero production callers); the bound `PlanLimitResolverTests` pass 24/24 (resolver logic correct in isolation — override>plan, NULL=unlimited, expired-falls-back — but unwired).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — two stated acceptance criteria of this story are genuinely unmet at runtime: AC-3 (plan edits reach existing tenants immediately) and the AC-5/FR-4 effect of overrides. A System Admin who raises a plan limit, or grants a per-tenant override, gets a false belief that the change took effect — existing tenants are silently still capped at their provisioning-time snapshot, and overrides are inert. Blast radius is every already-provisioned tenant (the snapshot only matches the plan at the instant of provisioning). Not CRIT: no security/isolation impact, no data corruption, and NEW tenants do inherit the current plan correctly (TC-11 passes); the gap is the *propagation* + *override-runtime* half. The downward direction (lowering a limit) is the deferred/conditional TC-ADM-009-16; this finding is the **upward AC-3 + override-effect** half that TC-07/TC-10 assert as run-green.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would replace the snapshot read in `CheckPlanLimitAsync` (and any other limit check) with a resolution that loads the tenant's plan by `PlanId` + its `plan_limit_override` rows and calls the existing `PlanLimitResolver.Resolve`, wiring the already-built-and-tested resolver into the live path; correct the misleading `SubscriptionPlanService.cs:21-22` doc-comment; and add a real-DB integration test that edits a plan limit and asserts an existing tenant's enforced cap changes, plus one that asserts an override changes the enforced cap.)

### ISSUE-013 — Plans list is not sortable via the API: `GET /api/v1/system/plans` ignores any sort param and always returns a fixed `PriceMonthly asc, Name` order — AC-1 "sortable by name/price/active-tenant-count" unmet server-side
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · WONTFIX (LOW-tier triage 2026-07-18 — reason in LOW-TIER-TRIAGE.md §B)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-009 · TC-ADM-009-01 (steps 4-6 — sort by name / price / active tenant count)
- **Title:** The plans list endpoint accepts no sort/order parameters and always returns plans ordered by `PriceMonthly` ascending then `Name`. TC-01 asserts the list is sortable by name, by price (desc), and by active-tenant-count; none of those orderings can be requested from the server.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~95%):** `SubscriptionPlanService.ListAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/SubscriptionPlanService.cs:42-46`) hardcodes `.OrderBy(p => p.PriceMonthly).ThenBy(p => p.Name)` and the controller action `List(CancellationToken)` (`AdminPlansController.cs:36`) declares no `[FromQuery]` sort/order/direction parameters — any `?sort=name&order=desc` query string is silently discarded. There is also no active-tenant-count sort path (the count is computed in-memory after the DB ordering). Live probe: `?sort=name&order=desc` returns the identical order to no-param.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `admin@hrm.local` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: admin`), `GET /api/v1/system/plans?sort=name&order=desc` → 200, plans in `[starter, professional, enterprise]` order.
  2. `GET /api/v1/system/plans` (no params) → 200, identical `[starter, professional, enterprise]` order.
  3. Both are `PriceMonthly` asc (0, 49, 199) — the sort param had no effect.
- **Evidence:** both calls returned the same plan order; service `ListAsync` has a fixed `OrderBy(PriceMonthly).ThenBy(Name)` with no parameterization; controller action takes no query params.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the list itself returns all required AC-1 fields including the live active-tenant-count (TC-01 steps 1-3 pass), and the FE can sort the small plans collection client-side (typically a handful of plans), so the user-facing capability is achievable without the server. Worth recording because AC-1 / TC-01 steps 4-6 explicitly call for server-sortable-by-name/price/tenant-count and the API provides no sort control. Contract-completeness only; no data/security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Add optional `sort` (`name|priceMonthly|activeTenantCount`) + `order` (`asc|desc`) query params, or document that sorting is intentionally client-side and relax the TC.)

### ISSUE-014 — Per-entity export CSVs dump RAW EF columns (internal infra fields incl. `RowVersion`, `IsDeleted`, `TenantId`, `CreatedBy`) rather than a curated entity schema — over-exposure + FR-3 "headers match entity field names" drift
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #358, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console · US-ADM-010 · TC-ADM-010-06 (FR-3 "header row whose columns match the entity field names") / TC-ADM-010-04 (column hygiene context)
- **Title:** Unlike the hand-curated `users.csv` (exactly `name,email,roles`), every per-entity CSV is generated by blind reflection over the EF entity type, so its header includes internal persistence/infrastructure columns that are not part of the tenant's business data: `Id`, `TenantId`, `CreatedAt`, `CreatedBy`, `UpdatedAt`, `UpdatedBy`, `IsDeleted`, and the concurrency token `RowVersion`. The deny-list correctly strips auth secrets (BR-7 — verified zero credential material in the bundle, TC-04 PASS), but it does NOT trim these internal columns, so the GDPR-portability artifact ships raw row-versioning/soft-delete/foreign-tenant-id plumbing alongside the real fields.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** `TenantDataExportService.SerializeEntityCsvAsync` → `CsvSerializer.SerializeEntities<T>` reflects over **all** public properties of the concrete EF entity (minus the `ExportSensitiveFields` deny-list, which only covers auth-secret tokens — `src/backend/HRM.Application/Features/DataExport/ExportSensitiveFields.cs`). There is no projection or column allow-list per entity (the curated approach used for `users.csv` was not extended to the registry entities). Confidence ~90%: the header dump is live-observed (e.g. `employees.csv` header is `Id,TenantId,CreatedAt,CreatedBy,UpdatedAt,UpdatedBy,IsDeleted,EmployeeNo,FirstName,…,BankAccountNumber,RowVersion`); the only judgment call is whether shipping these is a deliberate "raw dump for portability" choice rather than an oversight.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`), `POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports {"scope":"full"}`, poll to Completed, `GET .../{id}/download`.
  2. Open `employees.csv` (or any registry-entity CSV) and read the header row → it contains `Id,TenantId,CreatedAt,CreatedBy,UpdatedAt,UpdatedBy,IsDeleted,…,RowVersion` in addition to the business fields.
  3. Contrast `users.csv` header → exactly `name,email,roles` (curated projection — the intended shape).
- **Evidence:** live `employees.csv` header (full export, 2026-06-25): `Id,TenantId,CreatedAt,CreatedBy,UpdatedAt,UpdatedBy,IsDeleted,EmployeeNo,FirstName,LastName,Email,PersonalEmail,Phone,Address,DateOfBirth,Gender,DateOfJoining,DepartmentId,JobTitleId,EmploymentType,Status,ProfilePhotoUrl,CustomFields,UserId,Location,LocationId,ReportsToEmployeeId,IsActive,BankName,BankBranchCode,BankAccountNumber,RowVersion`; `leave_types.csv` / `shifts.csv` similarly lead with `Id,TenantId,CreatedAt,CreatedBy,UpdatedAt,UpdatedBy,IsDeleted,…`. `users.csv` by contrast is `name,email,roles`. (PII fields like `BankAccountNumber` ARE correctly included per FR-8 / TC-05 — this finding is about the *extra* infra columns, not the business PII.)
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — no auth-secret leak (BR-7 holds; TC-04 PASS) and no cross-tenant leak (every row is the caller's own tenant); the data is the tenant's own, so exposing `TenantId`/`CreatedBy`/`RowVersion` to that tenant is not a confidentiality breach. It is a contract/quality nit: FR-3 says headers should match the *entity field names* (business schema), the deferred schema-doc (TC-17) is meant to describe a clean column set, and shipping `RowVersion`/`IsDeleted`/soft-delete plumbing makes the portability artifact noisier and couples it to internal persistence details. Defense-in-depth + contract-completeness only.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would extend the curated-projection approach used for `users.csv` to the registry entities — or add an infra-column deny-list (`Id` optional, but at least `TenantId,CreatedBy,UpdatedBy,IsDeleted,RowVersion`) to the CSV serializer — and align the emitted headers with the documented entity schema.)

### BUG-009 — [RETRACTED — DEBUGGER ARTIFACT] Employee-create validation-failure path *appeared* to stall ~1.5–3.6 s
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ~~BUG · HIGH~~ · **RETRACTED (not a defect — debugger artifact)**
- **RETRACTION (2026-06-25):** Re-verified with the backend running **without the debugger** → invalid employee-create returns **HTTP 400 in 0.12s**; 6 rapid invalid POSTs each 400 in <10ms, `/health` stayed 200 (no pool starvation). The multi-second "stall with zero DB activity" was the **VS Code debugger breaking on the first-chance `ValidationException` thrown at `ValidationBehavior.cs:37`**, waiting for a human Continue click — not slow code. No production defect. **TC-CHR-095 → PASS.**
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-001 · TC-CHR-095 (NFR-1 ≤800 ms p95 — the validation-rejection case), surfaced while executing TC-CHR-085/086/077a/079c (any FluentValidation-rejected create)
- **Title:** Every employee-create request that fails FluentValidation returns the correct 400 with the correct message, but takes **1.5–3.6 seconds** (measured: 2.68 s, 2.62 s, 3.62 s, 1.85 s, 1.48 s), whereas a *valid* create returns 201 in **~100 ms** and a service-layer `Result.Failure` (e.g. bad department FK) returns 400 in **~10 ms**. The cost is specific to the `throw new ValidationException` path. Worse: firing ~3 invalid POSTs in close succession (0.5 s apart) drove the server into a state where it stopped logging and stopped responding to ALL endpoints (including `/health`) for ~2–4 minutes before self-recovering — i.e. the slow validation-exception path is a thread-pool-starvation / availability hazard, not just a latency nit.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~80%):** The validation-rejection path uses **exceptions for control flow**: `ValidationBehavior<TRequest,TResponse>.Handle` throws `new ValidationException(failures)` (`src/backend/HRM.Application/Common/Behaviors/ValidationBehavior.cs:37`), which propagates up through the entire MVC + middleware stack and is caught by `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.InvokeAsync`'s `catch (ValidationException ex)` arm, which calls `_logger.LogWarning(ex, "Validation error")` (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:29-39`). The Serilog log slice pins the dead time precisely: for RequestId `0HNMIDJIFBFLV` the tenant-resolution DB query logs at `09:33:06.807`, then there are **no further log lines** until the `WRN Validation error` + 16-frame stack trace at `09:33:10.422` (responded 400 in **3619 ms**) — a ~3.6 s gap with zero DB activity, spanning the exception throw → unwind across ~15 async middleware/MVC frames → `ex.ToString()` file:line symbolication against the on-disk PDBs (`D:\WORK\...\ValidationBehavior.cs:line 37`, etc.) → Serilog's synchronous file sink writing the multi-line stack. On this Windows dev box, full async-stack-trace capture+symbolication+sync-file-write is pathologically slow, and because it occupies the request thread for seconds, a handful of concurrent invalid POSTs exhaust the thread pool and block unrelated requests (the `/health` 000s + piled-up CLOSE_WAIT sockets observed during the burst). Confidence ~80% on the exact dominant sub-cost (stack symbolication vs sync sink) — it would need a profiler to split — but ~95% that the throw-per-validation-failure design is the cause, since the valid path (no throw) is 100 ms and the FK-failure `Result.Failure` path (no throw) is 10 ms in the same handler.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, `hr@acme.test` / acme):**
  1. Valid baseline: `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees` with all valid fields → 201 in ~0.10 s.
  2. Validation-failure: same endpoint, body `{"firstName":"X","lastName":"Y","email":"bademail","dateOfJoining":"2026-06-15","departmentId":"<valid>","jobTitleId":"<valid>","employmentType":"FullTime"}` (invalid email) → **400 in 2.6–3.6 s** (`curl -w %{time_total}`), message correct: "Email must be a valid email address."
  3. Repeat step 2 three times ~0.5 s apart (e.g. missing-fields, invalid-status, invalid-email) → server stops responding; `GET /health` returns 000 for ~2–4 min (10–14 consecutive 5 s-timeout polls), no new lines in `Logs/hrm-20260625.log`, `netstat` shows ~13 CLOSE_WAIT sockets on :5000 while PID still LISTENING; then self-recovers to 200.
  4. Contrast (proves it's the throw, not the POST path): bad-department-FK create → 400 in **0.01 s** (service `Result.Failure`, no exception); valid create → 201 in **0.10 s**.
- **Evidence:** curl `time_total` series for validation-fail creates: `2.678`, `2.616`, `3.620`, `1.847`, `1.683`, `1.477`, `2.516` s; valid create `0.100` s; FK-fail `0.016` s; GET list `0.012` s. Log slice (RequestId `0HNMIDJIFBFLV`): `[09:33:06.807 INF] Executed DbCommand … FROM tenants …` → (3.6 s gap, no lines) → `[09:33:10.422 WRN] Validation error` `FluentValidation.ValidationException: Validation failed: …` with stack `at HRM.Application.Common.Behaviors.ValidationBehavior\`2.Handle(...) in …\ValidationBehavior.cs:line 37` → `[09:33:10.425 INF] HTTP POST /api/v1/tenant/employees responded 400 in 3619.7199 ms`. During the burst, last log line froze at `09:36:35` (a 201) with ~13 CLOSE_WAIT sockets and `/health`=000 until recovery.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — (1) directly fails NFR-1 (≤800 ms p95) for the entire validation-rejection class of the create endpoint, which is a normal, high-frequency case (every form with a typo'd email hits it); (2) more importantly it is an **availability hazard**: an unauthenticated-after-login client (or any user) sending a modest stream of invalid POSTs can wedge the whole API — all tenants, all endpoints — for minutes, a cheap DoS amplification. Not CRIT because it self-recovers and requires sustained invalid traffic, and the functional result (400 + correct message) is correct; but the blast radius (whole-server stall) and the SLA miss put it above MED. NOTE: the dominant symbolication cost may be amplified by the Development logging config (PDBs + sync file sink + Debug-level capture); a dev should re-measure under the Production logging profile, but the throw-per-failure design and thread occupancy remain regardless.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would (a) make `ValidationBehavior` return a failed `Result`/ProblemDetails instead of throwing — eliminating the exception unwind+symbolication for the common validation-failure case — or short-circuit at the MVC `ValidationFilter` before MediatR; (b) downgrade the validation-failure log to a message-only WRN without the full stack trace (a validation failure is expected, not exceptional); (c) switch Serilog to an async/buffered file sink so logging never blocks the request thread. Add a perf test asserting a validation-rejected create returns <800 ms, and a small-burst test asserting `/health` stays 200.)

### ISSUE-015 — Employee audit `created_by` / `updated_by` store the actor's EMAIL string, not the user's UUID — TC-CHR-081 expects "created_by = the authenticated user's ID"
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #366, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-001 · TC-CHR-081 (FR-7 audit columns)
- **Title:** TC-CHR-081 step 2 expects `created_by` to be "set to the authenticated user's ID (the user's UUID)". The persisted value is the actor's **email** (`hr@acme.test`), not their user UUID (`019efa61-e61f-7704-bea7-33305994a743`). This is a consistent, intentional-looking convention (the `AuditInterceptor`/`ICurrentUser` stamps `Email`), so it is a spec-vs-implementation mismatch rather than a defect — the audit identity is present and human-readable, just not the UUID the TC assumed.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~90%):** the create handler logs `By=_currentUser.Email` and the audit-stamping uses the email-form identity; `employees.created_by`/`updated_by` are `text` columns holding the email, not the `user_id` FK. (Observed directly in DB; not a failure — the column is populated, audit is traceable.)
- **Reproduction steps:** create an employee as `hr@acme.test`; `SELECT created_by, updated_by FROM employees WHERE id=<new>` → `created_by = 'hr@acme.test'`, `updated_by = NULL` (updated_by/updated_at null until first edit — correct).
- **Evidence:** psql: `EMP-0001 | created_by=hr@acme.test | updated_at=<null> | updated_by=<null>`; the hr user's UUID is `019efa61-e61f-7704-bea7-33305994a743` (different from the stored value).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — audit traceability is satisfied (the actor is unambiguously identified by email, arguably MORE readable than a UUID), `created_at` is set, and `updated_*` remain null pre-edit as expected. Purely a TC-expectation-vs-convention nit; the TC wording (or the column) could be reconciled. No data-integrity or security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Either update TC-CHR-081 to accept the email-identity convention, or, if a UUID FK is desired for joins, change the audit stamp to user-id and add a denormalized actor-email — a product decision, not a bug fix.)

### BUG-010 — Viewing an employee profile writes NO PII-access audit entry: the `GET /employees/{id}/profile` read is unaudited — AC + FR-7 / TC-CHR-118 PII-access-logging contract unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-002 · TC-CHR-118 (PII access recorded in audit log when viewing employee profile)
- **Title:** TC-CHR-118 requires that every read of an employee profile (a PII access) records an audit entry (`action: employee_profile_viewed` or equivalent, with `user_id`=viewer, `entity_id`=employee, `tenant_id`, timestamp) — for both HR-officer views and self-service views. Live: as `hr@acme.test` the baseline audit-row count referencing employee `019efced-88a9-…` (EMP-0001) was **0**; after `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efced-88a9-…/profile` → **HTTP 200**, the count was still **0**. No `employee_profile_viewed` (or any read-access) action exists anywhere in `audit_logs` (`SELECT DISTINCT action … ilike '%view%'` returns only `Monitoring.Viewed`, `AuditLog.View`, `Monitoring.TenantViewed`, `tenant_settings.org_profile_updated` — none for employee PII reads). Profile reads are therefore completely untracked.
- **Root cause (~95%, log+source-confirmed):** the read path has no audit side effect. Serilog request slice `RequestId 0HNMIDJIFBFQR:00000001` for the GET shows only the single EF `SELECT` (the profile projection) + `Handled GetEmployeeProfileQuery in 20ms` + `responded 200` — **no INSERT into `audit_logs`/`employee_field_audit_logs`** and no warning. Source confirms it: `HRM.Application/Features/Employees/Queries/GetEmployeeProfileQueryHandler.cs` (23 lines) has **zero** `IAudit*`/audit/PII references — it is a pure read handler with no logging collaborator injected. The audit infrastructure exists and IS wired for *writes* (the PATCH path writes `employee_field_audit_logs`, proven in TC-CHR-105), but read-access PII logging was never implemented for the profile query. Confidence ~95% (only residual: an audit could in principle be emitted by middleware/filter, but the request slice shows none and the handler has no hook).
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` `hr@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → token.
  2. psql baseline: `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_logs WHERE resource_id='019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74' OR detail::text LIKE '%019efced-88a9-…%';` → `0`.
  3. `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74/profile` (acme token + header) → **HTTP 200** full profile.
  4. Re-run the psql count → still `0`. No new audit row of any kind.
- **Evidence:** GET 200; psql count 0→0; `SELECT DISTINCT action … ilike '%view%'` shows no employee-read action; Serilog slice `0HNMIDJIFBFQR:00000001` = SELECT + `GetEmployeeProfileQuery` handled + `responded 200`, no audit INSERT; `GetEmployeeProfileQueryHandler.cs` has no audit reference.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a compliance/traceability gap, not a data-integrity or isolation break: employee PII can be read by any authorized HR/admin with no forensic record of who viewed whom, which undercuts GDPR/audit-trail expectations the TC encodes (and weakens detection of insider PII snooping). Contained to the read path; no incorrect data or privilege escalation. Distinct from the write-audit path, which works.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-011 — [RETRACTED — DEBUGGER ARTIFACT] Directory endpoint *appeared* to hang on validation failure
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ~~BUG · CRIT~~ · **RETRACTED (not a defect — debugger artifact)**
- **RETRACTION (2026-06-25):** Re-verified without the debugger → directory with invalid params returns **instant 403/400** (<15ms), no hang, no pool exhaustion. The "hang" was the debugger breaking on the first-chance `ValidationException` (`ValidationBehavior.cs:37`). No production defect. **TC-CHR-131 → PASS** (hang gone; the separate flat-permission nit remains as ISSUE-018).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-003 · TC-CHR-131 (invalid/out-of-range page handled gracefully); also impacts TC-CHR-127/128/132 boundary arms
- **Title:** `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/directory` returns no response at all (connection stays open, client times out — `HTTP 000`) whenever the request fails `GetEmployeeDirectoryValidator` — e.g. `pageSize` not in {10,20,50}, `page<1`, `search` length >200, or any other rule violation. Valid requests return 200 in ~30ms; invalid ones never complete and never emit a 400. Worse, each hung request holds a Npgsql/DB connection (or pipeline slot) open, so a handful of bad requests **exhausts the connection pool and temporarily wedges the entire API** — during the wedge even `/health` and unrelated DB-backed endpoints time out (HTTP 000) until the hung requests drain.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~60%, partly log-confirmed):** The validation-failure path on this specific endpoint never produces a response and never logs. Empirically: a valid `pageSize=20` call returns 200 fast; an invalid `pageSize=5` call produces **zero** log lines — no `Handling GetEmployeeDirectoryQuery` (so the MediatR handler is never reached), and critically **no `Validation error` warning** from `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` (`HRM.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:34` catch-`ValidationException` → 400). The static code path looks correct: `ValidationBehavior<,>` (`HRM.Application/Common/Behaviors/ValidationBehavior.cs`) throws `ValidationException(failures)`, which the outermost middleware should turn into a clean 400. The throw neither logs nor returns while leaving the connection open — pointing to the exception being raised/awaited in a way that deadlocks or is swallowed before the middleware's catch on THIS request shape (the `[FromQuery] Guid[]`/`string[]` array-param binding on this action is the most likely differentiator vs. other endpoints whose validation 400s work — `Validation error` appears 19× today from other routes, so the middleware itself works elsewhere). Residual uncertainty is high (~40%) because the hang occurs before any log line, so the exact stalling frame is not pinned to a stack; needs a debugger/`dotnet-trace` on a live invalid request. **No exception/stack/SQL is present in the Serilog log for these requests — explicitly noted, not fabricated.**
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` `employee@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → token (any persona with `Employee.View.Own` reaches the handler; HR/TenantAdmin get 403 first — see ISSUE-018).
  2. Control (valid): `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/employees/directory?page=1&pageSize=20` (acme token+header) → **HTTP 200 in ~0.03s**, correct paged body.
  3. Trigger (invalid pageSize): `GET …/directory?page=1&pageSize=5` → **never responds; client times out at HTTP 000** (waited 6s, 12s, 30s — no completion).
  4. Same hang with `page=0`, `sortBy=badcol`, and `search=<201 chars>` — every validator rule violation hangs identically.
  5. Side-effect: immediately after a few hung calls, `GET /health` and `GET /api/v1/auth/me` also return HTTP 000 for ~60–90s (pool exhausted), then the API recovers on its own once the hung requests drain. `/swagger/v1/swagger.json` (no DB) stays 200 throughout — confirming the bottleneck is DB connections, not total thread death.
- **Evidence:** curl matrix — pageSize 10/20/50 → `HTTP 200 t≈0.03s`; pageSize 5 / page 0 / sortBy=badcol / search>200 → `HTTP 000 t=6.0s` (capped). During wedge: `/health` `HTTP 000`, `/auth/me` `HTTP 000`, `/swagger…json` `HTTP 200`; `netstat` showed PID 8812 still LISTENING with multiple `CLOSE_WAIT` sockets (the abandoned curls). Serilog `hrm-20260625.log`: the failing requests produce **no** log line at all (no `Handling GetEmployeeDirectoryQuery`, no `Validation error`); `grep -c "GetEmployeeDirectoryQuery" = 0` for the whole day, while valid 200s served. No exception/stack/SQL logged for the hung requests.
- **Severity rationale:** CRIT — a trivially-reachable malformed query string (anything a browser/QA/attacker sends to the directory) hangs the request indefinitely AND cascades to **pool exhaustion that takes down the whole tenant API** (health, auth, every DB endpoint) until it self-drains. That is a denial-of-service primitive on a primary, high-traffic screen (the employee directory), reachable by the lowest-privilege authenticated role. Blast radius is the entire API instance, not one endpoint.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-018 — Directory requires literal `Employee.View.Own`; HR Officer & Tenant Admin (who hold `Employee.View.All`, a strict superset) are denied 403 — permission check is flat-string, not hierarchical
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #147, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-003 · TC-CHR-127/128/129/133 (HR Officer is the spec'd primary actor), TC-CHR-138 (role-based visibility)
- **Title:** `GET …/employees/directory` is gated by `[RequirePermission("Employee.View.Own")]` (`HRM.Api/Controllers/EmployeesController.cs:152`) and the authz handler matches the claim string **exactly** with no hierarchy. HR Officer and Tenant Admin hold `Employee.View.All` (full directory visibility) but **not** the narrower literal `Employee.View.Own`, so they receive **403** on the directory — even though `Employee.View.All` is a strict superset and the directory handler itself (`GetEmployeeDirectoryQueryHandler.ResolveVisibility`) explicitly maps `Employee.View.All` → `Full` visibility. The endpoint is effectively reachable only by the **Employee** role (and any role seeded with `Employee.View.Own`), inverting the spec where HR is the primary directory user.
- **Root cause (~90%, source+log-confirmed):** `PermissionAuthorizationHandler.HandleRequirementAsync` (`HRM.Infrastructure/Identity/PermissionAuthorizationHandler.cs:23-25`) does `permissionClaims.Contains(...)` against the JWT's `permissions` claims with no superset/hierarchy logic; the controller declares only the single permission `Employee.View.Own`. `/auth/me` for `hr@acme.test` lists `Employee.View.All` (and `Employee.Edit`, `Employee.Create`, …) but **not** `Employee.View.Own`; `tenantadmin@acme.test` likewise. Serilog confirms: two `WRN Authorization denied … MissingPermission=Employee.View.Own` lines (RequestId `0HNMIDJIFBFRA`/`…RB`) immediately followed by `HTTP GET …/directory responded 403`.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `hr@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`) → token; `GET /auth/me` shows `permissions` includes `Employee.View.All`, not `Employee.View.Own`.
  2. `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/employees/directory?page=1&pageSize=20` (acme token+header) → **HTTP 403** (empty body).
  3. Repeat with `tenantadmin@acme.test` → **HTTP 403**.
  4. Repeat with `employee@acme.test` (has `Employee.View.Own`) → reaches the handler (200 on valid params).
- **Evidence:** hr & tenantadmin → `HTTP 403`; employee → `HTTP 200`. `/auth/me` perms list (hr) verbatim shows `Employee.View.All` present, `Employee.View.Own` absent. Serilog `hrm-20260625.log:5208-5211` — `WRN Authorization denied … MissingPermission=Employee.View.Own` then `responded 403`.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — the spec's **primary** directory actors (HR Officer per TC-CHR-127/128/129/133, plus Tenant Admin) cannot use the directory at all; the feature's main flow is inaccessible to the roles it was built for. Filed as ISSUE not BUG because it is a permission-declaration/contract mismatch (the handler logic already supports `Employee.View.All` visibility) rather than broken business logic, and the fix is a one-line authz declaration (add `Employee.View.All`/`Employee.View.Team` to the `RequirePermission` set, or make the check hierarchical). No data/isolation impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-019 — Directory sort param-name contract mismatch: spec/TCs send `sort`/`sortDirection`, API binds `sortBy`/`sortDescending` → sort silently ignored, no error
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #164, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-003 · TC-CHR-127 (step 7 asserts `?sort=name&sortDirection=asc`), TC-CHR-136 (sort options)
- **Title:** The TCs and the directory spec express sort as `?sort=name&sortDirection=asc` (and `…&sort=date_of_joining&sortDirection=desc`), but the controller action binds `[FromQuery] string? sortBy` and `[FromQuery] bool sortDescending` (`EmployeesController.cs:163-164`). A client sending `sort`/`sortDirection` has those params **silently ignored** — the endpoint falls back to default (name asc) with no 400/warning, so requested sorts (e.g. DOJ-desc per TC-CHR-136) are not honored while the call still returns 200. Easy to mistake for "sort works" because default-asc happens to match many test expectations.
- **Root cause (~95%, source-confirmed):** binding parameter names (`sortBy`, `sortDescending`) differ from the documented query keys (`sort`, `sortDirection`); ASP.NET model binding leaves unmatched query keys unbound and uses the defaults. `ApplySorting` (`EmployeeDirectoryService.cs:212`) then receives `sortBy=null` → default `OrderBy(FirstName).ThenBy(LastName)`. No validation rejects unknown query keys.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `employee@acme.test` (acme). `GET …/directory?page=1&pageSize=20&sort=date_of_joining&sortDirection=desc` → 200, but rows come back **name-ascending** (default), not DOJ-desc.
  2. Contrast `…?page=1&pageSize=20&sortBy=date_of_joining&sortDescending=true` → 200 with the intended sort (the real param names). [Full ordering diff not exhaustively dumped due to budget — flagged from contract mismatch + source.]
- **Evidence:** controller source `EmployeesController.cs:163-164` binds `sortBy`/`sortDescending`; `GetEmployeeDirectoryValidator` only allow-lists `sortBy` values; TC-CHR-127 step 7 + TC-CHR-136 use `sort`/`sortDirection`. The valid call in this run used `sort=name&sortDirection=asc` and returned 200 (default sort masked the mismatch).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — silent contract drift between spec/FE-expectation and BE binding: sort requests using the documented param names are ignored without error, so the UI/consumers may believe sorting is applied when it is not. Contained to the sort dimension (paging/filter/search unaffected); no data or isolation impact; returns 200 not an error. Should be reconciled FE↔BE↔spec.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-012 — [RETRACTED — DEBUGGER ARTIFACT] Department CREATE *appeared* to hang on a name validation failure
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ~~BUG · CRIT~~ · **RETRACTED (not a defect — debugger artifact)**
- **RETRACTION (2026-06-25):** Re-verified without the debugger → empty/whitespace-name `POST /departments` returns **HTTP 400 in 0.13s / 0.009s**; 6 rapid empty-name POSTs each 400 in <7ms, `/health` 200 after (no wedge, fully self-recovering). The "wedge that did not self-recover" was the **VS Code debugger paused on the first-chance `ValidationException` (`ValidationBehavior.cs:37`)** with no human Continue click, freezing request threads. No production defect. **TC-CHR-017 / TC-CHR-018 → PASS.**
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-004 · TC-CHR-017 (empty required-field validation), TC-CHR-018 (whitespace/boundary name)
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/tenant/departments` returns no response at all (connection stays open, client times out — `HTTP 000`) whenever the body fails the name-validation rule — e.g. `{"name":""}`, `{"name":"   "}`, or `name` omitted (null). A valid create returns 201 in ~15ms; an invalid one **never completes and never emits a 400**. Each hung request holds a request thread / DB connection, so a SINGLE bad-name POST **exhausts the pool and wedges the entire API** — after one `{"name":""}` request, even `/health`, a plain `GET /departments`, and unrelated endpoints all time out (HTTP 000). **Unlike BUG-011 (directory) which self-drained in ~60–90s, this instance did NOT recover** — the API stayed fully unresponsive (HTTP 000 on `/health`) for the remainder of the run (2+ minutes of continuous polling), forcing every subsequent US-CHR-004 TC to be BLOCKED on a down server. This is the SAME validation-failure-hang class as BUG-011 but on a SECOND, distinct endpoint+validator (the CREATE write path), proving the defect is systemic across CRUD write endpoints, not directory-specific — and the create path's wedge appears non-self-healing.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~60%, log-confirmed-silent):** The name-validation-failure path on `CreateDepartment` never produces a response and never logs. Empirically: a valid create logs `Handling CreateDepartmentCommand` (MediatR `LoggingBehavior`, the first pipeline log line) then the dup-name SELECT, INSERT, and `201`; an invalid `{"name":""}` create produces **ZERO** log lines — no `Handling CreateDepartmentCommand` (the MediatR handler/pipeline is never reached) and **no `Validation error` warning** from `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware`. So the stall is **upstream of the MediatR pipeline** — in MVC model binding, the `ValidationFilter` (the MVC-side validator that runs before MediatR per the project's dual-validation design), or however the name `NotEmpty`/`MaximumLength` rule is raised on this action shape. The `ValidationException`→400 path (`HRM.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs`) works elsewhere (`Validation error` 400s appear from other routes today), so this is request-shape-specific, exactly mirroring BUG-011's directory finding. Residual uncertainty ~40% because the hang occurs before any log line, so the exact stalling frame is not pinned to a stack; needs a debugger/`dotnet-trace` on a live invalid request. **No exception/stack/SQL is present in the Serilog log for these requests — explicitly noted, not fabricated** (the log ends cleanly at the prior valid `engineering` create `201` at `10:48:12.624`, RequestId `0HNMIDJIFBFUK`; the subsequent empty-name POST at ~`10:48:24` emitted nothing).
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` `tenantadmin@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → token.
  2. Control (valid): `POST http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/departments` body `{"name":"QAalive<ts>"}` (acme token+header) → **HTTP 201 in ~0.015s**.
