  3. Trigger (invalid): `POST …/departments` body `{"name":""}` → **never responds; client times out at HTTP 000** (`--max-time 12` → `t=12.01s`, `0 bytes received`). Same hang with `{"name":"   "}` (whitespace) and `{}`/`{"code":"X"}` (name omitted/null).
  4. Immediately after step 3, a NEW valid create (`{"name":"QAalive<ts>"}`) — which worked in step 2 — also returns **HTTP 000 t=12s**, and `GET /health` returns **HTTP 000 t=8s**, and `GET /api/v1/tenant/departments` returns **HTTP 000 t=8s**: the whole API is wedged.
  5. Polled `/health` repeatedly for 2+ minutes → **HTTP 000 every time; the server did NOT self-recover** within the run (contrast BUG-011 directory which drained in ~60–90s). A backend restart is required to clear it.
- **Evidence:** curl matrix — valid create → `HTTP 201 t=0.015s`; `{"name":""}` / `{"name":"   "}` / `{}` → `HTTP 000 t=12.01s` (`* Operation timed out after 12015 ms with 0 bytes received`). Post-trigger: valid create `HTTP 000 t=12s`, `/health` `HTTP 000 t=8s`, `GET /departments` `HTTP 000 t=8s`; six consecutive `/health` polls all `000`. Serilog `hrm-20260625.log`: `grep -c "Handling CreateDepartmentCommand" = 7` total for the day, last at `10:48:12.610`; the empty-name POST after it produced **no** log line (log tail ends at the prior valid `engineering` `201`, `10:48:12.624`). No exception/stack/SQL logged for the hung requests.
- **Severity rationale:** CRIT — a trivially-reachable malformed body (empty/whitespace department name — the exact thing a form-submit or QA negative test sends) hangs the request indefinitely AND a SINGLE such request cascades to pool exhaustion that **takes down the whole tenant API** (health, all CRUD), with **no observed self-recovery**. That is a one-shot denial-of-service primitive on a primary write endpoint, reachable by any Tenant Admin / HR user. Blast radius is the entire API instance. More severe than BUG-011 because (a) it is the WRITE path, (b) a single request triggers it, and (c) it did not auto-drain in this run.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Same systemic fix locus as BUG-011 — make the validation-failure path on MVC-bound write actions return a 400 without holding the request open; root-cause why the `ValidationException`/`ValidationFilter` short-circuit deadlocks for these request shapes.)

### BUG-013 — Department name uniqueness is CASE-SENSITIVE: "engineering" is accepted alongside existing "Engineering" → BR-1/AC-3 case-insensitive-uniqueness contract unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #161, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-004 · TC-CHR-022 (case-insensitive duplicate within tenant), relates to TC-CHR-003 (exact-dup, which PASSES)
- **Title:** Per BR-1/AC-3 and TC-CHR-022, department-name uniqueness within a tenant must be **case-insensitive** ("Engineering", "engineering", "ENGINEERING" are the same name). The exact-match dup check works (creating a second "Engineering" → HTTP 400 "A department with this name already exists."), but creating **"engineering"** (lowercase) while acme already has **"Engineering"** was **accepted — HTTP 201**, producing two departments that differ only by case. The uniqueness guard is a case-sensitive equality, not a case-insensitive one.
- **Root cause (~85%, log-confirmed SQL):** the create dup-check query logged for the `engineering` request is `… AND d.name = @name` (Serilog `hrm-20260625.log`, RequestId `0HNMIDJIFBFUK`, `DepartmentService` create path) — a case-**sensitive** `=` comparison on `name`, with no `LOWER(d.name) = LOWER(@name)` / `ILIKE` / case-insensitive collation. So "Engineering" ≠ "engineering" at the DB level and the second create passes the guard, then INSERTs (logged `Department created … Name=engineering, Code=DUP2`). Fix locus is the name-existence check in the department create/update service (make it case-insensitive, matching BR-1).
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → token. acme already has dept "Engineering".
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/departments` body `{"name":"Engineering","code":"DUP1"}` → **HTTP 400** "A department with this name already exists." (exact dup correctly blocked — TC-CHR-003 PASS).
  3. `POST /api/v1/tenant/departments` body `{"name":"engineering","code":"DUP2"}` → **HTTP 201**, new dept `019efd36-e08a-7366-b481-d8ec9ffa0725` created (TC-CHR-022 FAIL). (Cleanup: this stray dept was immediately deactivated, leaving it inactive in acme's admin list — it could not be hard-deleted; flagged.)
- **Evidence:** step-2 `{"success":false,"message":"A department with this name already exists."}` HTTP 400; step-3 `{"success":true,"data":{"id":"019efd36-e08a-…","name":"engineering",…}}` HTTP 201. Serilog: create dup-check SQL `WHERE NOT (d.is_deleted) AND (… ) AND d.name = @name` (case-sensitive `=`), followed by `Department created. … Name=engineering, Code=DUP2`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a genuine business-rule violation (BR-1 case-insensitive uniqueness) that allows confusing near-duplicate departments within a tenant, but contained to data-quality (no isolation/security/availability impact) and requires a deliberate case-variant input; the exact-dup guard still works. Should be made case-insensitive to meet AC-3.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-014 — Department `managerId` is NOT tenant-validated: a Tenant Admin can set ANOTHER tenant's employee as their department's manager (cross-tenant FK accepted → 200)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #139, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-004 · TC-CHR-020 (assign department manager; BR-2 / FR-4 / AC-1)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/tenant/departments/{id}` accepts a `managerId` that belongs to a **different tenant's** employee and persists it (HTTP 200). Unlike `parentDepartmentId` — which is validated through a tenant-scoped EF query and cleanly rejects a foreign-tenant or non-existent parent with 400 "Parent department not found or is not active." — `managerId` is written straight to `UPDATE departments SET manager_id = @p18` with **no existence/same-tenant check**. The only thing that constrains it is the global Postgres FK `fk_departments_employees_manager_id`, which is satisfied by ANY existing employee row regardless of tenant. Result: an acme department now references a techoneglobal employee as its manager (BR-2 "manager must be an employee in the same tenant" / FR-4 violated; risks leaking the foreign employee's name/avatar into acme's UI).
- **Root cause (~90%, log-confirmed SQL):** the update path (`DepartmentService` update, dispatched by `UpdateDepartmentCommand`) validates `name`/`code` uniqueness and `parentDepartmentId` (tenant-filtered lookup) but performs **no** validation of `managerId` before `SaveChanges`. Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI135` shows, for the cross-tenant-manager PUT, the name/code EXISTS checks and then `UPDATE departments SET manager_id = @p18, updated_at = @p19 WHERE id = @p20` succeeding → `Department updated.` → HTTP 200, with no employee-tenant predicate anywhere in the request's SQL. Contrast: invalid `parentDepartmentId` returns 400 from an in-app tenant-scoped check before any UPDATE. Fix locus: add a same-tenant existence check on `managerId` in the create/update department service (mirror the parent-department validation), matching BR-2.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test`/`Admin@123!` header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → token. Create a throwaway acme dept `MgrDept…` (`019efd50-ed55-…`).
  2. Discover a techoneglobal employee id read-only (no writes to techoneglobal): `019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a` (techoneglobal's `EMP-0001`, the BUG-003 proof employee).
  3. Control (same-tenant): `PUT …/departments/019efd50-ed55-…` body `{"name":"MgrDept…","code":"MG…","managerId":"019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74"}` (acme `EMP-0001`) → **HTTP 200**, `managerId` set (correct).
  4. Trigger (cross-tenant): same PUT with `"managerId":"019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a"` (techoneglobal employee) → **HTTP 200**, response shows `"managerId":"019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a"` persisted onto the acme department. (Cleanup: manager reset to `null` on this throwaway dept.)
- **Evidence:** step-4 response `{"success":true,"data":{"id":"019efd50-ed55-…","managerId":"019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a","updatedAt":"2026-06-25T05:46:58.426555Z"}}` HTTP 200. Serilog RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI135`: name/code EXISTS checks then `UPDATE departments SET manager_id = @p18 …` committed, `Department updated. Id="019efd50-ed55-…" By=tenantadmin@acme.test`, responded 200 — no employee-tenant validation in the request's logged SQL.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — breaks a core tenant-isolation invariant (BR-2: manager must be a same-tenant employee) on a primary management flow, persisting a cross-tenant FK that can surface another tenant's PII (employee name/avatar) in the wrong tenant's UI. Contained to a dangling cross-tenant reference written into the actor's OWN tenant row (not a read/write of another tenant's row, so narrower than BUG-003), and requires the actor to know a foreign employee id — hence HIGH not CRIT. Distinct from BUG-003 (which is the unvalidated `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header bypass): this one fires with the correct subdomain and is a missing same-tenant FK-target check.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-015 — Non-existent `managerId` on department update returns HTTP 500 (unhandled FK violation) instead of a clean 400
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #139, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-004 · TC-CHR-020 (manager assign — invalid-id arm)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/tenant/departments/{id}` with a `managerId` that does not exist at all (e.g. `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa`) returns **HTTP 500** ("An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.") because the FK violation is thrown from the DB and bubbles up unhandled, rather than being pre-validated into a 400 like `parentDepartmentId` is. A fast 4xx on bad input would be correct; a 500 is not. (NOT a debugger artifact — this is a genuine 500 response returned in ~58ms, with the exception fully logged.)
- **Root cause (~95%, log-confirmed exception+SQL):** same missing-validation root as BUG-014 — `managerId` is not checked for existence before `SaveChanges`. With a non-existent id the global FK `fk_departments_employees_manager_id` fails at the DB: Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI134` logs `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbUpdateException` → inner `Npgsql.PostgresException (0x80004005): 23503: insert or update on table "departments" violates foreign key constraint "fk_departments_employees_manager_id"` (`SqlState 23503`, `Routine: ri_ReportViolation`), surfaced via `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` (`ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:27`) as a generic 500. The handler does not translate `DbUpdateException`/`23503` into a validation 400. Fix locus: pre-validate `managerId` (same-tenant existence) in the department update/create service — the same fix that closes BUG-014 also turns this 500 into a 400.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` (acme). `PUT …/departments/019efd50-ed55-…` body `{"name":"MgrDept…","code":"MG…","managerId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa"}`.
  2. → **HTTP 500** `{"success":false,"message":"An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."}` in ~0.058s.
  3. Contrast: invalid `parentDepartmentId` (bogus uuid) → **HTTP 400** "Parent department not found or is not active." (clean validation) — proving the manager path lacks the equivalent guard.
- **Evidence:** Serilog RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI134`: `[ERR] An exception occurred in the database while saving changes …` → `PostgresException … 23503 … fk_departments_employees_manager_id`, `[ERR] Error handling UpdateDepartmentCommand after 40ms`, `[ERR] Unhandled exception {SourceContext: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware}`, `[ERR] HTTP PUT …/departments/019efd50-ed55-… responded 500 in 57.6924 ms`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — incorrect error contract (500 on bad client input that should be a 400), contained to a single malformed request with no data corruption (the txn rolls back) and no isolation impact. Cosmetically poor and could mask monitoring (500s page on-call), so worth fixing alongside BUG-014.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-020 — Department deactivate is audited as `Department.Update` with a delta summary, not a distinct `Department.Deactivate` action with before/after snapshots
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #366, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-004 · TC-CHR-031 (audit entries for create/update/deactivate; NFR-5)
- **Title:** The department lifecycle IS audited (create/update/deactivate all produce tenant-scoped rows with actor user_id, actor email, resourceType=Department, resourceId, timestamp, ipAddress — NFR-5 core met → TC-CHR-031 PASS). But two contract details from the TC are not met: (a) **deactivate** is recorded as `action: Department.Update` (with `summary: {"IsActive":false}`), not the distinct `department_deactivated` action the TC/spec expects; and (b) the audit `summary` is a **changed-fields delta** (e.g. `{"Name":"AuditUpd…"}`, `{"IsActive":false}`), not the full **before/after snapshots** the TC describes for each action.
- **Root cause (~80%, response-confirmed):** the audit writer for department mutations emits a single `Department.Update` action for any non-create change (including deactivate) and serializes only the changed fields into `summary`, rather than action-typing deactivate separately and capturing full before/after objects. Observed directly from `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?resourceId=…`: three rows — `Department.Create` (summary = new department object), `Department.Update` (`{"Name":"AuditUpd1782366250"}`), `Department.Update` (`{"IsActive":false}`).
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. As `tenantadmin@acme.test` (acme): create `AuditTest…` (`019efd53-21e2-…`) → update name → deactivate.
  2. `GET …/tenant/audit-logs?resourceId=019efd53-21e2-…&page=1&pageSize=20` → 3 rows: `Department.Create`, `Department.Update`(name), `Department.Update`(`{"IsActive":false}`) — all actor=tenantadmin@acme.test, ipAddress=::1, tenant-scoped.
- **Evidence:** audit row JSON: `{"action":"Department.Update","resourceType":"Department","resourceId":"019efd53-21e2-…","actorEmail":"tenantadmin@acme.test","summary":"{\"IsActive\":false}"}` for the deactivate; the create/update rows likewise use delta summaries, no separate `*.Deactivate` action and no full before/after snapshot fields.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the requirement that state-changing department ops are auditable with actor/tenant/timestamp/what-changed is satisfied; this is a fidelity/contract nit (action-name granularity + snapshot completeness) that a forensic consumer expecting a `Department.Deactivate` action or full before/after may need. No security/data impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-021 — Job title `gradeId` is accepted with NO validation: any arbitrary GUID is persisted as the grade link (no SalaryGrade subsystem / FK exists) — AC-4 grade-link integrity unverifiable
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · DEFERRED (feature-blocked: no SalaryGrade entity — see reports-archive/PRODUCT-DECISIONS-NEEDED-2026-07-05.md)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-005 · TC-CHR-037 (create job title with salary-grade link; AC-4)
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/tenant/job-titles` (and PUT) stores the `gradeId` field verbatim with **zero validation** — no existence check, no tenant-scope check, no FK constraint. A wholly fabricated GUID (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ff`) is accepted and returned on the created record (HTTP 201). There is no SalaryGrade entity, DbSet, controller, or `grade_id` foreign key anywhere in the backend, so AC-4 ("link to an existing salary grade") cannot be satisfied or verified, and any value the client sends becomes a dangling reference.
- **Root cause (~95%, source-confirmed):** `JobTitleService.CreateAsync` / `UpdateAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/JobTitleService.cs:57` and `:97`) assign `GradeId = gradeId` directly with no lookup. `CreateJobTitleValidator` / `UpdateJobTitleValidator` validate only `TitleName` + `Description` length — `GradeId` is unvalidated. Confirmed by absence of any `SalaryGrade` DbSet in `AppDbContext` and no grades controller (`grep -ri grade HRM.Api/Controllers` finds only unrelated PerformanceDashboard/Recommendation). The `job_title.grade_id` column is a bare nullable `Guid?` with no FK constraint, so even the DB cannot reject a bogus value.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`.
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/job-titles` body `{"titleName":"QA GradeLink <ts>","gradeId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ff"}`.
  3. Response: HTTP 201, `data.gradeId = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ff"` — the fabricated id is persisted, no error.
- **Evidence:** `{"success":true,"data":{"id":"019efd62-463e-7691-899e-a2f97ebd04f3","titleName":"QA GradeLink 1782367536","gradeId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ff","employeeCount":0,"isActive":true,...}}` HTTP 201. No exception in `hrm-20260625.log` (the write succeeds cleanly — that is the problem).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — data-integrity gap on a contained field: a job title can carry a grade link that points to nothing (or, by the BUG-014 class, potentially another tenant's grade id were a grades subsystem to exist). No cross-tenant read/write of another tenant's row today (so below HIGH), but AC-4 is structurally unmet and the field can silently hold garbage. Because the grades subsystem does not exist at all, TC-CHR-037's happy path (link to an *existing* grade) is unverifiable → TC marked FAIL on the AC-4 integrity contract, not on a transient error.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-016 — Job title name uniqueness is CASE-SENSITIVE (create AND update): "software engineer" / "SOFTWARE ENGINEER" are accepted alongside existing "Software Engineer" → AC-3/BR-1 case-insensitive-uniqueness contract unmet (same class as BUG-013)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #161, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-005 · TC-CHR-047 (case-insensitive dup; also weakens TC-CHR-045 update-path uniqueness)
- **Title:** The `title_name` uniqueness check is an exact, case-sensitive string compare. With existing `Software Engineer`, both `POST {"titleName":"software engineer"}` and `POST {"titleName":"SOFTWARE ENGINEER"}` succeed (HTTP 201) — three distinct rows that AC-3/BR-1 (and TC-CHR-047) require to be treated as duplicates of one name. The same hole exists on the **update** path: renaming a title to `senior engineer` succeeds (200) despite an existing `Senior Engineer` (the exact-case rename is correctly rejected 400 — TC-CHR-045 primary arm PASSes — but the case variant leaks).
- **Root cause (~95%, source-confirmed):** `JobTitleService.CreateAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/JobTitleService.cs:46`) and `UpdateAsync` (`:90`) test uniqueness with `j.TitleName == titleName` — an ordinal/collation-default equality with no `ToLower()`, no case-insensitive collation, and no normalization. This is the identical defect class as BUG-013 (departments) on a second entity. EF translates this to a SQL `WHERE title_name = @p` which under the column's default collation is case-sensitive, so the `AnyAsync` returns false for a case variant and the INSERT/UPDATE proceeds.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` (acme already has `Software Engineer`).
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/job-titles` `{"titleName":"software engineer"}` → HTTP 201 (`id 019efd64-18ef-…`).
  3. `POST …` `{"titleName":"SOFTWARE ENGINEER"}` → HTTP 201 (`id 019efd64-194a-…`).
  4. Update arm: create a throwaway title, `PUT …/{id}` `{"titleName":"senior engineer"}` → HTTP 200 despite existing `Senior Engineer`.
- **Evidence:** `{"success":true,"data":{"id":"019efd64-18ef-73ca-a8fb-d92dc2a73235","titleName":"software engineer",...}}` HTTP 201 (create); `{"success":true,"data":{...,"titleName":"senior engineer","updatedAt":"2026-06-25T06:07:50.47…"}}` HTTP 200 (update). No exception in `hrm-20260625.log` (the writes succeed — that is the defect).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — duplicate-by-case job titles in one tenant degrade data quality and the assignment UX (two near-identical titles), and the AC-3/BR-1 uniqueness invariant is broken on both write paths. No cross-tenant or security impact, contained to one tenant's own rows, and requires the actor to deliberately vary case — hence MED, matching BUG-013's rating. Should be fixed with the same normalization/collation fix as BUG-013 (apply to both entities).
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-022 — Job title `title_name` leading/trailing whitespace is NOT trimmed on create/update — TC-CHR-046 trim expectation unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #362, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-005 · TC-CHR-046 (boundary values incl. whitespace trimming)
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/tenant/job-titles` `{"titleName":"  Trim Probe  "}` persists the name with leading/trailing spaces verbatim (`titleName = "  Trim Probe 1782367638  "`). TC-CHR-046 expects leading/trailing whitespace to be trimmed. Combined with the case-sensitive compare (BUG-016), an untrimmed name also evades the duplicate check (`" Software Engineer"` ≠ `"Software Engineer"`).
- **Root cause (~90%, source-confirmed):** neither `CreateJobTitleValidator`/`UpdateJobTitleValidator` nor `JobTitleService.Create/UpdateAsync` normalize/`Trim()` the name before storing — `TitleName = titleName` is assigned as received (`JobTitleService.cs:55`,`:95`). FluentValidation's `NotEmpty` does reject a *purely* whitespace string (TC-CHR-044 whitespace arm → 400, correct), but a name with surrounding spaces around real text passes through untrimmed.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25):** as `tenantadmin@acme.test` (acme), `POST …/job-titles` `{"titleName":"  Trim Probe <ts>  "}` → HTTP 201, response `titleName` retains the surrounding spaces.
- **Evidence:** response field `"titleName":"  Trim Probe 1782367638  "` (brackets added in test output: `titleName=[  Trim Probe 1782367638  ]`).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/data-hygiene; surrounding whitespace is invisible in most UI but pollutes sorting/search and lets a near-duplicate slip past the (already case-sensitive) uniqueness check. No security/isolation impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-023 — Org-tree `reportingViewAvailable` flag contradicts itself between views: department view reports `false` while the reporting view simultaneously returns data (`true`) for the same tenant/data
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #362, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-006 · TC-CHR-153 (reporting-view availability) / TC-CHR-151 (department-view payload)
- **Title:** The `org-tree` response carries a `reportingViewAvailable` boolean that a UI would use to show/hide the Department↔Reporting toggle. For acme's same data, `GET …?view=department` returns `reportingViewAvailable: false` while `GET …?view=reporting` returns `reportingViewAvailable: true` and a populated reporting tree. A client that loads the default (department) view first reads `false` and would hide the Reporting toggle, yet the reporting view is fully functional — a self-contradicting contract field.
- **Root cause (hypothesis, ~55%):** the flag appears to be computed per-request relative to the *current* view rather than as a stable tenant-level capability. In department view it is likely derived from "do any manager→report links exist among the *loaded* department-scoped nodes" (acme's seed has employees but no manager assignments / parent links, so it computes `false`), whereas the reporting query materializes employee nodes and returns `true`. I did not open the handler source to pin the exact expression, so confidence is moderate; the observed behavior (false in dept view, true in reporting view, identical underlying tenant data) is certain. (No server error in the log for these calls.)
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`.
  2. `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/org-tree?view=department&depth=2` → `data.reportingViewAvailable = false`.
  3. `GET http://localhost:5000/api/v1/tenant/org-tree?view=reporting&depth=2` → `data.reportingViewAvailable = true` and `data.nodes` is a non-empty list of `employee` nodes.
- **Evidence:** dept-view body `…"view":"department","reportingViewAvailable":false`; reporting-view body `…"view":"reporting","reportingViewAvailable":true` (non-empty `nodes`), same acme tenant, same run. HTTP 200 both.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — no security/data impact and the reporting view itself works; the risk is purely UX/contract: a client trusting the department-view flag would incorrectly disable a working feature (the reporting toggle, AC-3). Contained, recoverable, cosmetic-adjacent.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Make `reportingViewAvailable` a view-independent tenant capability, or document that it is view-relative so clients don't gate the toggle on the department-view value.)

### BUG-017 — Office-location name uniqueness is CASE-SENSITIVE and not TRIMMED: "colombo head office" / "  Colombo Head Office  " are both accepted alongside existing "Colombo Head Office" → BR-1/FR-2 per-tenant unique-name contract trivially bypassable
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #161, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE (DB-interaction)
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-007 · TC-CHR-175 (duplicate-name rejection) — also touches TC-CHR-172 (whitespace stored verbatim). Same class as [[BUG-013]] (Department case-sensitive uniqueness) + [[ISSUE-022]] (whitespace not trimmed).
- **Title:** With location "Colombo Head Office" already present in tenant `acme`, `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations` with `name:"colombo head office"` → **HTTP 201** (case-variant accepted) and with `name:"  Colombo Head Office  "` → **HTTP 201** (whitespace-padded duplicate accepted, AND stored with the leading/trailing spaces verbatim). The exact-match duplicate is correctly rejected (400 "A location with this name already exists."), so uniqueness exists but is defeated by case or surrounding whitespace — three rows that are the "same" business name now coexist in one tenant.
- **Root cause (~90%, source-confirmed):** `LocationService.CreateAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LocationService.cs:47-48`) does the uniqueness check as `await _dbContext.Locations.AnyAsync(l => l.Name == name, …)`. On PostgreSQL the default column collation is **case-sensitive**, so `Name == "colombo head office"` does not match the stored `"Colombo Head Office"` → no conflict detected. The incoming `name` is also **never `.Trim()`-ed** before the comparison or the insert (the Create path stores `Name = name` verbatim, `:57`), so `"  Colombo Head Office  "` is a distinct string that both passes the uniqueness check and persists with the padding. The backing unique index `(TenantId, Name)` with `HasFilter("is_deleted = false")` (`LocationConfiguration.cs:62-64`) is likewise a plain case-sensitive/whitespace-sensitive index — no `LOWER()`/`citext`/normalization — so even the DB layer would not catch the case/whitespace variants. The identical pattern is in `UpdateAsync` (`:99-100` `l.Name == name && l.Id != locationId`). No server-side exception (all three calls returned 201/INF-logged cleanly) — this is a logic gap, not a crash.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25 as `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations {"name":"Colombo Head Office","timeZone":"Asia/Colombo", …}` → 201 (baseline, id `019efd75-374c-…`).
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations {"name":"Colombo Head Office","timeZone":"Asia/Colombo"}` → **HTTP 400** "A location with this name already exists." (exact dup correctly blocked).
  3. `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations {"name":"colombo head office","timeZone":"Asia/Colombo"}` → **HTTP 201** (id `019efd75-b37a-…`) — case-variant accepted.
  4. `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations {"name":"  Colombo Head Office  ","timeZone":"Asia/Colombo"}` → **HTTP 201** (id `019efd75-b3e6-…`, `name` echoed `"  Colombo Head Office  "` with padding) — whitespace-padded duplicate accepted and stored untrimmed.
- **Evidence:** step-3 response `{"success":true,"data":{"id":"019efd75-b37a-716a-…","name":"colombo head office",…}}` HTTP 201; step-4 response `…"name":"  Colombo Head Office  "…` HTTP 201; Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` shows three `Location created` INF lines (`LocationService`) for the variants, no error. Source: `LocationService.cs:47-48` (`l.Name == name`, no normalization), `:57` (`Name = name` untrimmed), `LocationConfiguration.cs:62-64` (plain `(TenantId,Name)` unique index).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — contained, no security/isolation/data-corruption impact, but it defeats the stated per-tenant unique-name guarantee (BR-1/FR-2): users can create visually-identical duplicate locations differing only by case or padding, polluting assignment dropdowns and the locations list. Recoverable (dedupe later) and tenant-local. Same class already filed for Departments ([[BUG-013]]) — a normalization fix should be applied consistently across name-uniqueness surfaces.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would `name = name.Trim()` on Create/Update and compare case-insensitively — e.g. `EF.Functions.ILike` or a normalized `LOWER(name)` column/`citext` — backed by a case-insensitive unique index, mirroring whatever fix lands for [[BUG-013]].)

### BUG-018 — Office-location create/update/deactivate are NEVER written to the audit log: no `Location.*` audit action exists, only a `LogInformation` Serilog line → AC/TC-185 "audit entries for create, update, and deactivate" unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-007 · TC-CHR-185 (audit log entries for create/update/deactivate) — also weakens the audit-trail intent of TC-CHR-172 step 13 / TC-CHR-174.
- **Title:** Performing `POST /api/v1/tenant/locations` (create), `PUT .../locations/{id}` (update), and `POST .../locations/{id}/deactivate` produces **zero** rows in the tenant audit log. The audit `filter-options` action catalog for `acme` lists `Department.Create/Update`, `JobTitle.Create/Update`, `tenant_settings.*`, etc. but **no `Location.*` action of any kind** — so location lifecycle changes are invisible to the audit trail (TC-CHR-185 expects create/update/deactivate to each be recorded).
- **Root cause (~90%, source-confirmed):** `LocationService` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LocationService.cs`) records each mutation with only `_logger.LogInformation("Location created/updated/deactivated …")` (`:73-75`, `:117-119`, `:157-159`) — a Serilog application log, NOT an audit-log domain write. Unlike the Department/JobTitle services (which emit `Department.Create`/`JobTitle.Create` audit actions, visible in the `filter-options` catalog), the Location service makes **no** call to the audit-log writer, and the generic `AuditInterceptor` does not capture it either (the `Location` entity changes save without producing an `audit_logs` row of a `Location.*` action). So the create/update/deactivate are logged to the rolling text log but absent from the queryable, tenant-scoped, exportable audit trail.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25 as `tenantadmin@acme.test`/`hr@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. Create (`POST`), update (`PUT`), and deactivate (`POST .../deactivate`) the "Colombo Head Office" location — all succeed (201/200/200), Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` shows the matching `Location created/updated/deactivated` INF lines from `HRM.Infrastructure.Services.LocationService`.
  2. `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=40` → 40 rows returned, **0** of which reference a location (distinct actions seen: `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`, `JobTitle.Create/Update` — the most recent row predates all the location ops).
  3. `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs/filter-options` → `actions` array (32 entries) contains `Department.Create`, `JobTitle.Create`, `tenant_settings.*`, etc. but **no `Location.*`** entry (`[a for a in actions if 'location' in a.lower()]` = empty).
- **Evidence:** the 40-row audit pull contained zero location entries; `filter-options.actions` (32) has no `Location.*` action; Serilog confirms the ops happened (6 `LocationService` INF lines for create/update/deactivate in the run window) yet none reached the audit store. Source: `LocationService.cs` uses `_logger.LogInformation` for all three mutations, with no audit-writer call (contrast Department/JobTitle which surface `*.Create`/`*.Update` audit actions).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no security/isolation/data impact and the operations themselves work, but US-CHR-007's audit requirement (AC + TC-CHR-185 "Audit log entries created for create, update, and deactivate operations") is unmet: location lifecycle changes leave no forensic trail in the tenant audit log, weakening compliance/accountability for a config surface that controls employee assignment. Contained (one entity type) and not a data-loss bug, hence MED not HIGH.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would emit `Location.Create`/`Location.Update`/`Location.Deactivate` audit actions from `LocationService` — or via the shared audit interceptor/writer the Department/JobTitle services use — and add an assertion to TC-CHR-185's automation that the audit list/`filter-options` includes the new actions after each op.)

### BUG-019 — Employee-document LIST endpoint has NO authorization: any authenticated tenant user (Manager, or an Employee viewing someone else's record) gets a 200 with full document metadata → BR-2/BR-3 bypass, PII metadata leak
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #138, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-008 · TC-CHR-199 (RBAC: Manager denied, Employee own-only) — also weakens TC-CHR-198 / TC-CHR-ISO-029 intent for the list surface.
- **Title:** `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/{employeeId}/documents` returns **HTTP 200** with the full categorized document list (file names, categories, descriptions, expiry dates, uploader id, sizes) to **any** authenticated user in the tenant. A `manager@acme.test` (whom BR-3 must deny) and an `employee@acme.test` querying a **different** employee's documents (whom BR-2 restricts to own-only) both received the complete list. The download and upload/delete endpoints on the same resource correctly enforce authz (manager → 403, non-owner employee download → 404), but the **list** endpoint does not.
- **Root cause (~95%, source-confirmed):** `EmployeeDocumentService.ListAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/EmployeeDocumentService.cs:184-222`) **never calls `AuthorizeDocumentAccess`** — it only checks `IsResolved` and `employee exists`, then returns the documents. Contrast `GetDownloadUrlAsync` (`:234`) and `DeleteAsync` (`:274`) which DO gate (download calls `AuthorizeDocumentAccess`, delete checks `EmployeeDocument.Delete`). The controller action `GetDocuments` (`EmployeesController.cs:399-415`) is annotated only `[Authorize]` with the comment "Permission check at service level (EmployeeDocument.View or EmployeeDocument.ViewOwn)" — but that service-level check was never implemented for List. So BR-2 (employee own-only) and BR-3 (manager blocked) are unenforced on the list path.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`, employee `019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74`, which has documents):**
  1. Login `manager@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → token. `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74/documents` → **HTTP 200**, body `{"items":[{...full doc metadata...}],"totalCount":2}`. BR-3 expects 403.
  2. Login `employee@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` (not the owner of that employee record) → token. Same GET → **HTTP 200** with the same full list. BR-2 expects own-only (403/404 for another employee's docs).
  3. Cross-check the gated siblings work: manager download of a doc → **403** "You do not have permission to access employee documents."; non-owner employee download → **404** "Document not found."; manager/employee upload → **403**. Only the LIST leaks.
- **Evidence:** manager list response `{"success":true,"data":{"items":[...],"totalCount":2}}` HTTP 200; employee list response identical HTTP 200. Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` confirms both: `Document list accessed. EmployeeId="019efced…", Count=2, … By=manager@acme.test` (RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI1CJ:00000001`) and `… By=employee@acme.test` (RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI1CN:00000001`) — both 200, no authz rejection. Source: `EmployeeDocumentService.cs:184-222` (`ListAsync`) lacks the `AuthorizeDocumentAccess` call present in the download/delete paths.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — defeats a primary access-control requirement of the story (BR-2 employee own-only, BR-3 manager blocked) on the list surface, exposing every employee's document *metadata* (file names, categories, descriptions, expiry, uploader) to any authenticated tenant user. Not CRIT because it is the metadata listing only (the file *content* download IS gated → no raw-file exfil within-tenant), and it is in-tenant (cross-tenant is the separate BUG-003 class below). Still HIGH: document file names/descriptions are themselves PII-revealing (e.g. "termination-letter.pdf", medical certs) and the listing is the discovery step that an attacker would chain.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would call `AuthorizeDocumentAccess(employeeId, …)` at the top of `ListAsync` exactly as `GetDownloadUrlAsync` does, and add a TC-CHR-199 automation arm asserting manager→403 and non-owner-employee→403/404 on the list endpoint, not only on download.)

### BUG-020 — Employee-document list/download honor a spoofed `X-Tenant-Subdomain`: an acme-issued token operates inside the techoneglobal tenant context (BUG-003 class extends to the document/PII surface)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (systemic `TenantAccessGuardMiddleware`, PR #119; ISO-verified 2026-07-03 — all `/tenant/*` cross-arm requests now 403 `cross_tenant_denied`. Reconciled 2026-07-04. NOTE: the *within-tenant* no-authz gap on the document LIST endpoint is a SEPARATE finding — see BUG-019, which STAYS OPEN.)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-008 · TC-CHR-197 (cross-tenant download → 403) / TC-CHR-198 / TC-CHR-ISO-029 / TC-CHR-ISO-030. Same systemic root as **BUG-003** — extending the affected-surface list, not re-filing.
- **Title:** The document endpoints trust the request's `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header to resolve the tenant **without validating it against the JWT's tenant**. Presenting an `hr@acme.test` access token together with `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` causes the API to run the document query inside the **techoneglobal** tenant context: `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/{techoneglobal-employee-id}/documents` returns **HTTP 200** (the request is served as techoneglobal, not rejected as cross-tenant). The correct path (acme token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` against a techoneglobal employee id) correctly 404s via the global query filter — so isolation holds *only* when the header is honest, which an attacker controls.
- **Root cause (~90%, BUG-003 systemic, log-confirmed):** `TenantResolutionMiddleware` resolves the tenant purely from the subdomain (here the dev `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header) and never cross-checks it against the authenticated token's tenant claim. Once resolved to techoneglobal, `ITenantContext.TenantId` = techoneglobal's id and the EF global query filter happily scopes to techoneglobal, so an acme-issued token executes reads in another tenant. This is the same unvalidated-`X-Tenant-Subdomain` bypass documented as BUG-003 (CRIT) on settings/workflows/audit/data-export; the document surface (`employees/{id}/documents` list + `/download`) is now confirmed as an additional affected endpoint.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, READ-ONLY — no writes to techoneglobal):**
  1. Login `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → acme access token.
  2. `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a/documents` with `Authorization: Bearer <acme token>` and **`X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** (target is a techoneglobal employee) → **HTTP 200** `{"items":[],"totalCount":0}` — request **served in the techoneglobal context** (empty only because that specific employee has no documents; the access itself was granted, not rejected).
  3. Control: same acme token + **`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`** + the techoneglobal employee id → **HTTP 404** "Employee not found" (query filter scopes to acme — correct). The difference proves the header, not the token, decides the tenant.
  4. `GET .../019efcf4-…/documents/{any-doc-id}/download` with the same acme-token + techoneglobal header → 404 "Document not found" (served as techoneglobal; would return a techoneglobal signed URL for a real techoneglobal doc id).
- **Evidence:** Serilog `hrm-20260625.log`: `Document list accessed. EmployeeId="019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a", Count=0, TenantId="019ef3c3-16ce-7279-8e6d-bb5674ad4261", By=hr@acme.test` (RequestId `0HNMIFE5GI1CR:00000001`, `tenant_subdomain":"techoneglobal"`) — an **acme** user (`By=hr@acme.test`) executing a document query stamped with the **techoneglobal** tenant id (`019ef3c3…`). The honest-header control returned HTTP 404. **0 writes were made to techoneglobal** (list + download GET only).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH (systemic root is CRIT per BUG-003) — this is document/PII exfiltration across tenant boundaries: a techoneglobal employee *with* documents would have their document metadata listed and a techoneglobal-scoped signed download URL minted for an acme-token holder. Filed HIGH on this surface because the live repro hit an employee with zero documents (no data actually egressed in this run) and it is one more instance of the already-tracked CRIT BUG-003 rather than a new root cause; the underlying defect's blast radius (every tenant, every document) is CRIT and should be fixed at the middleware once.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Fix is the shared BUG-003 remediation: `TenantResolutionMiddleware`/auth pipeline must reject any request whose resolved tenant ≠ the authenticated token's tenant — fail-closed — which closes this and all other BUG-003 surfaces at once.)

### ISSUE-024 — Employee-document upload/download/delete are NOT written to the audit log: only Serilog `LogInformation` lines exist, no `EmployeeDocument.*` audit action (PII-access/mutation not audited — BUG-010/BUG-018 class)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-008 · TC-CHR-207 ("document view and download events logged").
- **Title:** Uploading, downloading (signed-URL generation), and soft-deleting an employee document produces **zero** rows in the tenant audit log. A `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` after performing several uploads + a download + a delete returns no document-related entries, and no `EmployeeDocument.*` action exists in the audit catalog — so document access/mutation (a PII-sensitive surface) leaves no forensic trail in the queryable audit store. TC-CHR-207 expects view/download events to be logged.
- **Root cause (~90%, source-confirmed):** `EmployeeDocumentService` records every operation only via `_logger.LogInformation(...)` — upload (`EmployeeDocumentService.cs:175`), download URL (`:250`), delete (`:289`) — i.e. Serilog application-log lines, not audit-log domain writes. The service makes no call to the audit-log writer, and the generic interceptor does not surface an `EmployeeDocument.*` action. Same omission class as BUG-018 (locations) and the BUG-010 PII-access pattern.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. As `hr@acme.test`: upload several documents (`POST …/documents`, 201s), generate a download URL (`GET …/{docId}/download`, 200), and soft-delete a document (`DELETE …/{docId}`, 200) for employee `019efced-…`.
  2. As `tenantadmin@acme.test`: `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` → 50 rows, **0** referencing a document (`'ocument' in json` filter = 0 matches; actions seen are `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`, etc.).
- **Evidence:** audit pull of 50 rows contained zero document entries despite multiple upload/download/delete ops in the run window; Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` confirms the ops happened (`Document uploaded.`, `Document download URL generated.`, `Document soft-deleted.` INF lines from `HRM.Infrastructure.Services.EmployeeDocumentService`) yet none reached the audit store. Source: `EmployeeDocumentService.cs:175/250/289` use `_logger.LogInformation` only.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no security/isolation/data-integrity impact and the operations themselves work, but US-CHR-008's audit expectation (TC-CHR-207, view/download events logged) is unmet for a PII-sensitive surface, weakening compliance/accountability (who downloaded/deleted which employee document, when). Filed ISSUE·MED (consistent with BUG-018's MED audit-gap rating) rather than BUG since it is a missing-control/contract gap on an otherwise-working feature.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would emit `EmployeeDocument.Upload/Download/Delete` audit actions from `EmployeeDocumentService` via the shared audit writer the Department/JobTitle services use, and assert their presence in the audit list/`filter-options` in TC-CHR-207 automation.)

### BUG-021 — Employee status-change READ surface honors a spoofed `X-Tenant-Subdomain`: an acme-issued token reads another tenant's employee status, valid transitions, and full profile/employment-history (BUG-003 class extends to the status surface)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (systemic `TenantAccessGuardMiddleware`, PR #119; ISO-verified 2026-07-03 — all `/tenant/*` cross-arm requests now 403 `cross_tenant_denied`. Reconciled 2026-07-04.)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-009 · TC-CHR-ISO-033 (Tenant A status change + employment history not visible to Tenant B → FAIL). Same systemic root as **BUG-003** (CRIT) — extending the affected-surface list, not re-filing.
- **Title:** The employee status endpoints resolve the tenant purely from the request's `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header without cross-checking it against the JWT's tenant claim. Presenting an `hr@acme.test` access token together with `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` causes `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/{techoneglobal-employee-id}/status/transitions` to run inside the **techoneglobal** tenant context and return **HTTP 200** with that employee's `currentStatus` + valid transitions; the matching `…/profile` likewise returns the techoneglobal employee's full record including its `employmentHistory` timeline (status-change history of another tenant). The honest-header control (acme token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` against the techoneglobal id) correctly **404s** via the EF global query filter — proving the *header*, not the token, decides the tenant.
- **Root cause (~90%, BUG-003 systemic, source+response-confirmed):** `TenantResolutionMiddleware` resolves the tenant from the subdomain (dev `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header) and never validates it against the authenticated token's tenant claim. Once resolved to techoneglobal, `ITenantContext.TenantId` = techoneglobal's id, and both `EmployeeStatusService.GetValidTransitionsAsync` (`EmployeeStatusService.cs:212`) and the profile query scope their `_dbContext.Employees` lookup through the EF global query filter to techoneglobal — so an acme-issued token executes the read in another tenant. Identical unvalidated-`X-Tenant-Subdomain` bypass already documented as BUG-003 (CRIT) on settings/workflows/audit/data-export and extended to documents in BUG-020; the **employee status/transitions/profile read surface** is now confirmed as an additional affected endpoint. (No 5xx/exception in `hrm-20260625.log` — the request succeeds as designed under the wrong tenant; the defect is the missing token-vs-subdomain check, not a thrown error.)
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, READ-ONLY — no writes to techoneglobal):**
  1. Login `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → acme access token.
  2. `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a/status/transitions` with `Authorization: Bearer <acme token>` and **`X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** → **HTTP 200** `{"currentStatus":"Active","validTransitions":["Suspended","Terminated","Inactive"]}` — served in the techoneglobal context.
  3. Control: same acme token + **`X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`** + the techoneglobal employee id → **HTTP 404** "Employee not found." (query filter scopes to acme — correct).
  4. `GET .../019efcf4-…/profile` with acme token + techoneglobal header → **HTTP 200** returning the techoneglobal employee `EMP-0001 "Cross Write" crosswrite@example.com`, department `ToneEng`, and its `employmentHistory` array — i.e. another tenant's status-change timeline is fully readable cross-tenant.
- **Evidence:** Step 2 response (techoneglobal employee's transitions) vs step 3 control (404) under the *same acme token* — the only difference is the `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header value. Step 4 leaked techoneglobal PII (`firstName":"Cross","lastName":"Write","email":"crosswrite@example.com"`, `departmentName":"ToneEng"`). No ERR/FTL lines in Serilog `hrm-20260625.log` for the run window (the cross-tenant reads returned 200, not exceptions). **0 writes were made to techoneglobal** — all four cross-tenant requests were GETs.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH (systemic root is CRIT per BUG-003) — cross-tenant disclosure of employee status, the valid-transition state, and full employee profile + employment-history (PII + lifecycle/disciplinary history) to any authenticated user of another tenant who controls the dev header. Filed HIGH on this surface as one more instance of the already-tracked CRIT BUG-003 rather than a new root cause; the underlying defect's blast radius (every tenant, every read endpoint) is CRIT and should be fixed once at the middleware.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Fix is the shared BUG-003 remediation: the tenant-resolution/auth pipeline must reject any request whose resolved tenant ≠ the authenticated token's tenant claim — fail-closed — closing this and every other BUG-003 surface at once.)

### ISSUE-025 — Status-change before/after audit snapshot is written to `employee_field_audit_logs` (write-only) but is NOT in the queryable generic `/audit-logs` and has no read endpoint — NFR-5 audit trail is not retrievable
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #165, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-009 · TC-CHR-230 (audit log records before/after snapshot for status change → FAIL). Missing-audit/forensic-gap class (BUG-010/BUG-018/ISSUE-024).
- **Title:** A status change DOES write a before/after audit row (`EmployeeFieldAuditLog`, `Section="StatusChange"`, before=`{Status,IsActive}` / after=`{Status,IsActive}`) — so NFR-5 is *partially* met at the write layer — but that row is **not** surfaced anywhere a verifier or auditor can read it: it is absent from the queryable tenant `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs` store, and no `EmployeeFieldAuditLog` read/list endpoint exists on the Employees controller (only `/profile` exposes the separate `EmploymentHistory` timeline, which carries actor/reason/previous-value/new-value but NOT the structured before/after snapshot the NFR-5/TC-230 audit-log entry describes). So the dedicated audit before/after snapshot is effectively write-only.
- **Root cause (~85%, source+response-confirmed):** `EmployeeStatusService.ApplyStatusChangeAsync` (`EmployeeStatusService.cs:174-184`) adds the before/after entry to `_dbContext.EmployeeFieldAuditLogs`, a separate table from the generic tenant audit log read by `/audit-logs`. There is no controller action exposing `EmployeeFieldAuditLog`, and the status change does not also emit a generic-audit-log domain action — so `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` after the change returns 0 status/employee-related rows. The before/after snapshot exists in the DB but is unreachable via API.
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. As `hr@acme.test`: `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efcf5-49bc-…/status` `{newStatus:4,reason:"Pending disciplinary investigation",effectiveDate:"2026-06-25"}` → 200 (Active→Suspended). Source confirms an `EmployeeFieldAuditLog` row is added with before/after snapshots.
  2. As `tenantadmin@acme.test`: `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` → 50 rows, **0** referencing the status change or that employee (`'status'/'Employee'` filter = 0 matches).
  3. Inventory the Employees controller: only `…/profile` returns history (`employmentHistory` = actor/reason/prev/new value, no structured before/after snapshot); no endpoint exposes `EmployeeFieldAuditLog`.
- **Evidence:** post-change `/audit-logs?pageSize=50` returned 50 rows with zero status/employee hits; `EmployeeStatusService.cs:174-184` writes the before/after to `EmployeeFieldAuditLogs`; `grep` of `EmployeesController.cs` shows no `field-audit`/`EmployeeFieldAuditLog` route. The `/profile` employment-history (2 entries after Active→Suspended→Active) confirms the *history* trail is readable, but the NFR-5 *audit before/after snapshot* TC-230 asserts is not.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — not a security/isolation/data-integrity defect (the write happens; the status change is correct and the employment-history timeline IS readable), but TC-230's NFR-5 expectation that the before/after audit snapshot be retrievable for the operation is unmet: an auditor cannot pull the status-change audit entry through the queryable audit store or any read API, weakening compliance/accountability. Filed ISSUE·MED (consistent with ISSUE-024's audit-gap rating) rather than BUG since the underlying record is written and the feature works.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would either also emit a generic tenant-audit-log action for status changes, or add a read endpoint over `EmployeeFieldAuditLog`/`Section="StatusChange"`, and assert its retrievability in TC-CHR-230 automation.)

### BUG-022 — Bulk employee import is NEVER written to the audit log: importing N employees (and the bulk-import job itself) produces no `EmployeeImport.*`/`Employee.Create` audit action, only a `LogInformation` Serilog line → TC-CHR-251 (AC) "audit log records the import operation with file name, row count, success count, and failure count" unmet
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-010 · TC-CHR-251 (audit log records import operation → FAIL). Missing-audit/forensic-gap class — same as [[BUG-010]]/[[BUG-018]]/[[ISSUE-024]]/[[ISSUE-025]], now on the bulk-import surface.
- **Title:** A successful bulk import (and every employee it creates) leaves NO entry in the queryable tenant audit log. Across three live imports at 06:58–06:59 that created ~14 employees in `acme`, `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?fromDate=2026-06-25T06:55:00Z&pageSize=50` returned **0** rows whose action references import or employee-create (only `JobTitle.Create/Update` and `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`). The import writes a `BulkImportJob` *tracking* row (file name, total/success/failed counts, initiatedBy) and a Serilog `LogInformation` line, but neither is the tenant audit trail TC-CHR-251 requires, and there is no read endpoint over `BulkImportJob` beyond per-job `/status`.
- **Root cause (~95%, source+response-confirmed):** `BulkEmployeeImportService` records the operation only via `_logger.LogInformation("Bulk import completed (sync). File={FileName}, Total=…, Success=…, Failed=…", …)` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/BulkEmployeeImportService.cs:832-834`, and the async equivalent `:310-312`). It never writes an `AuditLog` domain row for the import, and `CreateEmployeeBatchAsync` (`:857-928`) bulk-`AddRange`s `Employee` entities directly with no per-employee `Employee.Create` audit action either. The `AuditInterceptor` stamps audit *fields* (created_by/at) on the rows but does not emit queryable audit-log *actions*. Net: the import is invisible to `/audit-logs`. Confirmed live: the audit feed since 06:55 (covering all three imports) shows only JobTitle + session actions, 0 import/employee rows. (No 5xx/exception in `hrm-20260625.log`; the imports logged `INF Bulk import completed (sync)` with `tenant_id=019ef3ba-…`, `RequestId 0HNMIFE5GI1EV:00000001` etc. — they succeeded, the audit write simply does not exist.)
- **Reproduction steps (live-confirmed 2026-06-25, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`):**
  1. As `hr@acme.test`: `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees/import` with a 10-row valid CSV (`-F file=@valid10.csv`) → 200 `{total:10,success:10,failed:0,jobId:019efd92-ba46-…}`; two more partial imports (`partial.csv` 3/2, `dup.csv` 1/1) at 06:59.
  2. As `tenantadmin@acme.test`: `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?fromDate=2026-06-25T06:55:00Z&pageSize=50` → distinct actions = `{JobTitle.Create:13, JobTitle.Update:9, concurrent_session_oldest_revoked:28}`; **0** rows whose action/resourceType references import, bulk, or Employee-create.
  3. Confirm the only persisted trace is the per-job tracking record (`GET …/import/{jobId}/status` returns file name + counts) and the Serilog line — neither is in the audit store.
- **Evidence:** `/audit-logs` action histogram above (0 import/employee rows for the import window); `BulkEmployeeImportService.cs:832-834` (`_logger.LogInformation` only, no audit write); `:857-928` (`AddRange` of `Employee` with no per-row audit action); server log `hrm-20260625.log:20811` `INF Bulk import completed (sync). File=valid10.csv, Total=10, Success=10` (`RequestId 0HNMIFE5GI1EV`, `tenant_id 019ef3ba-…`) confirming the import path ran and only application-logged.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no security/isolation/data-integrity impact (the import works correctly, rows are tenant-stamped, and a `BulkImportJob` tracking row preserves file name + counts), but US-CHR-010's audit expectation (TC-CHR-251) that the bulk import be recorded in the *audit log* with file name and success/failure counts is unmet, weakening compliance/accountability for a high-impact mutating operation (mass employee creation). Filed MED consistent with the BUG-018 audit-gap rating; not HIGH because a partial tracking trail (the job record) does exist and is per-job retrievable.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would emit a generic tenant-audit-log action for the import — e.g. `EmployeeImport.Completed` with file name/total/success/failed — and/or per-employee `Employee.Create` actions, then assert retrievability via `/audit-logs` in TC-CHR-251 automation. Same shared fix shape as BUG-018/ISSUE-024.)

### ISSUE-026 — Bulk employee import POST is a BUG-003-affected WRITE surface: `TenantResolutionMiddleware` resolves the import tenant from the (dev-spoofable) `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header and never validates it against the authenticated token's tenant — so an acme-issued token could import employees INTO another tenant. Code-confirmed; not live-proven (would pollute a real tenant). NOTE: the import job-status/errors READ surface is correctly query-filtered and does NOT leak.
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · HIGH · RESOLVED (systemic `TenantAccessGuardMiddleware`, PR #119; guard fires pre-controller so the spoofed-subdomain import WRITE is now 403 `cross_tenant_denied`. ISO-verified 2026-07-03 across all `/tenant/*`. Reconciled 2026-07-04.)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-010 · TC-CHR-252 (tenant_id from session, file cannot override) / TC-CHR-ISO-037 (Tenant A imports not visible to Tenant B) / TC-CHR-ISO-038 (reject without tenant context). Same systemic root as **BUG-003** (CRIT) — extending the affected-surface list, not re-filing.
- **Title:** The bulk-import write path stamps rows to whatever tenant the `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header resolves to (`TenantInterceptor` → `ITenantContext.TenantId`), and the resolution middleware never cross-checks that resolved tenant against the JWT's `tenant_id` claim. So an actor with `Employee.Import` permission in tenant A, by setting the dev header to tenant B's subdomain, would have their uploaded employees created in tenant B. This is the WRITE-side instance of BUG-003 on the import surface. **Not live-demonstrated** because doing so requires POSTing employees into a second real tenant (`techoneglobal`), which the run was forbidden to pollute — so confidence rests on source + the read-side probe behavior, not an executed cross-tenant insert.
- **Root cause (~85%, BUG-003 systemic, source-confirmed):** `TenantResolutionMiddleware` (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Middleware/TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs`) resolves the tenant purely from the subdomain (dev `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header) — a `grep` for `tenant_id`/`token`/`user_tenant` in that file finds only Serilog log-context pushes (`:138-141`), no comparison against the authenticated token's tenant claim. `BulkEmployeeImportService.ProcessRowsAsync`/`CreateEmployeeBatchAsync` then stamp every `Employee` and the `BulkImportJob` with `_tenantContext.TenantId` (`BulkEmployeeImportService.cs:799, 881, 942`), i.e. the resolved (spoofable) tenant — file content can NOT override it (TC-252's stated threat is closed), but the *header* dictates the destination tenant. Identical unvalidated-`X-Tenant-Subdomain` bypass already documented as BUG-003 (CRIT) on settings/workflows/audit/data-export and extended to documents (BUG-020) and employee-status reads (BUG-021); the **bulk-import write** is one more affected surface.
- **Reproduction steps (read-side live-probed; write-side code-reasoned only — NO cross-tenant insert performed):**
  1. **Read side (live, confirms isolation on the GET path):** with `hr@acme.test` token, `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/import/019efd92-ba46-…/status` (an acme job) but header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → **404 "Import job not found"** (also `platform` → 404). Header `<none>` → **400 "Tenant context is not resolved"** (TC-ISO-038 PASS). Bogus subdomain → **404 workspace-not-found** at the middleware. So the job-status/errors READ surface is properly query-filtered and does NOT leak across tenants.
  2. **Write side (NOT executed — would pollute `techoneglobal`):** the same header-substitution on `POST …/employees/import` would resolve `ITenantContext` to the header's tenant and stamp the imported rows there; no token-vs-subdomain guard exists to stop it. Verified by source inspection, not by an actual cross-tenant POST.
- **Evidence:** read-probe outputs — acme-token + techoneglobal header on acme job = HTTP 404 `{"message":"Import job not found."}`, no-header = HTTP 400 `{"message":"Tenant context is not resolved."}`; `TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs` grep shows no token/subdomain match (only `:138-141` log-context pushes); `BulkEmployeeImportService.cs:799/881/942` stamp `_tenantContext.TenantId`. The happy-path import log line `tenant_id=019ef3ba-…` (hrm-20260625.log:20811) confirms rows follow the *resolved* tenant.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH (systemic root is CRIT per BUG-003) — a successful cross-tenant write would inject employee records (PII) into another tenant under an attacker-controlled header, a mutating cross-boundary breach. Filed HIGH/ISSUE rather than re-filing the CRIT because (a) it is one more instance of the already-tracked BUG-003 root, and (b) the cross-tenant *insert* was deliberately not executed in this run (no pollution allowed), so it is source-confirmed but not live-proven on the write path; the read path was proven clean. Blast radius (every tenant, every write endpoint) is CRIT and should be closed once at the middleware.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Fix is the shared BUG-003 remediation: the tenant-resolution/auth pipeline must reject any request whose resolved tenant ≠ the authenticated token's tenant claim — fail-closed — closing the import write surface and every other BUG-003 surface at once. A targeted negative test should attempt an acme-token import with a foreign subdomain into a *disposable* tenant and assert rejection.)

### BUG-023 — Manager-assignment writes NO audit-log entry: `POST /employees/{id}/manager` and `POST /employees/bulk-assign-manager` succeed (FK persisted, before/after returned in the response) but emit zero tenant audit rows, so the reporting-structure change history (AC-2 / FR-6 / NFR-5) does not exist
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-011 · TC-CHR-268 (step 8 audit before/after) / TC-CHR-271 (step 9: 5 individual audit entries) / TC-CHR-278 (2 audit + 2 employment-history entries). Same **missing-audit class** as BUG-018 / ISSUE-024 / ISSUE-025.
- **Title:** Assigning, reassigning, or bulk-assigning a reporting manager does not produce any audit-log record. The assign succeeds and the API response itself carries `previousManagerId/previousManagerName → newManagerId/newManagerName` (so the before/after data is computed and available), but it is never written to the audit store. After ~10 successful assignments in this run (1 single + 3 bulk + 1 cross-dept + 2 cycle-setup + the 268 happy path), `GET /audit-logs?pageSize=100` shows only `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`, `Department.Update`, `JobTitle.Create/Update` — **zero** Employee/manager/reports_to actions.
- **Root cause (~80%, response+audit-store confirmed):** the `AssignManager` / `BulkAssignManager` command handlers update `Employee.ReportsToEmployeeId` and return a populated result DTO, but never call the tenant audit-log writer (the same writer that records `Department.*` / `JobTitle.*`). The Serilog log for this run shows **no ERR** on any assignment call (all clean 200/400), so this is a silent omission in the handler, not a failed write — the audit path is simply not invoked. The data needed for before/after is already in hand (the result DTO proves it), so this is a wiring gap, not a data-availability gap. (No exception in `hrm-20260625.log` for the `…/manager` RequestIds — confirms not a swallowed write error.)
- **Reproduction steps (live):**
  1. Authenticate `tenantadmin@acme.test` (subdomain `acme`, pw `Admin@123!`).
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efd92-bab1-75d6-9e01-c54c8fb413cf/manager` body `{"managerEmployeeId":"019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74","reason":"qa"}` → **200**, response `previousManagerName/newManagerName` populated.
  3. `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=100` (header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`) → histogram = `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked:49, Department.Update:27, JobTitle.Create:15, JobTitle.Update:9`; **no** row with action/entityType referencing Employee, manager, or reports_to.
  4. Same for `POST …/bulk-assign-manager` (3 employees → John Doe, all `success:true`) — no audit rows appear.
- **Evidence:** assign 200 body `{"employeeId":"019efd92-bab0-…","previousManagerName":"Imp1782370711_2 Test","newManagerName":"John Doe","message":"… now reports to John Doe."}`; audit histogram above (0 employee/manager rows over the 08:00–08:03 window despite ~10 assigns); no ERR for any `…/manager` RequestId in `hrm-20260625.log`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no security/isolation/data-integrity impact (the FK is persisted correctly and the change is reversible/visible via `/direct-reports`), but a documented compliance/accountability requirement (AC-2 + FR-6 + NFR-5: every reporting-manager change must be auditable with before/after + acting officer) is entirely unmet for a mutating org-structure operation. Same MED rating and shape as the BUG-018 / ISSUE-024 / ISSUE-025 audit-gap family; not HIGH because the operation works and is independently observable, not CRIT because no cross-boundary/PII exposure.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would have the AssignManager/BulkAssignManager handlers emit a tenant audit action — e.g. `Employee.ManagerAssigned` with before/after manager id+name and acting user — reusing the existing Department/JobTitle audit writer, and assert retrievability in TC-268/271/278 automation. Shared remediation shape with BUG-018.)

### ISSUE-027 — `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/{id}` detail DTO omits the reporting-manager FK entirely (no `reportsToEmployeeId`/`managerName`), so a client cannot read an employee's current manager from the profile endpoint — only indirectly via the manager's `/direct-reports`; plus the bulk-assign result mislabels the success message into the `employeeName` field
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #362, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-011 · TC-CHR-268 (step 5: "employee record has `reports_to_employee_id` set") / TC-CHR-269 (Reporting Manager field shows current manager or "Not Assigned").
- **Title:** Two contract nits on the manager surface: (a) the employee-detail response (`GET /employees/{id}`) has **no** field exposing the reporting manager — its keys are `id, employeeNo, firstName, lastName, email, phone, dateOfBirth, gender, dateOfJoining, departmentId, departmentName, jobTitleId, jobTitleName, employmentType, status, profilePhotoUrl, location, customFields, userId, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt` — so TC-268 step 5 / TC-269's "read the current manager off the profile" cannot be satisfied from this endpoint (the FK IS persisted; it's just confirmable only via the manager's `/direct-reports`). (b) `bulk-assign-manager` returns each item's success **message** string in the field named `employeeName` (e.g. `employeeName: "Manager assigned successfully. Et FullTime now reports to John Doe."`), a mislabel — `employeeName` should hold the employee's name, with the message in a separate field or the `message`/`error` field.
- **Root cause (~85%, response-confirmed):** the `EmployeeDetailDto` projection does not select/expose `ReportsToEmployeeId` (nor a resolved manager name), and the `EmployeesBulkAssignManagerItemResult.EmployeeName` is populated from the per-row result message instead of the employee's display name. Both observed directly from the JSON responses; no server error involved (clean 200s, no log entry needed).
- **Reproduction steps (live):**
  1. `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/019efd92-bab0-72f6-bda0-9a33ffc4bfcb` (acme, after a confirmed assign) → 200; response `data` has none of `reportsToEmployeeId`/`managerEmployeeId`/`managerName` (key list above).
  2. `POST …/bulk-assign-manager` → each `results[i].employeeName` = the success sentence, not the name.
- **Evidence:** employee-detail key list (above) with no manager field; bulk result item `{"employeeId":"019efcfb-dd3f-…","success":true,"error":null,"employeeName":"Manager assigned successfully. Et FullTime now reports to John Doe."}`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/contract drift, no functional/security/data impact: the FK is correctly persisted and the relationship is fully readable via `/direct-reports`; the bulk mislabel is a field-naming nit (data is present, just under the wrong key). It does, however, mean an FE rendering "current manager" on the profile (TC-269) has no API field to bind to, which is worth a contract fix.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (Add `reportsToEmployeeId` + resolved `managerName` to `EmployeeDetailDto`; populate `EmployeesBulkAssignManagerItemResult.EmployeeName` with the actual name and move the sentence to a `message` field.)

### BUG-024 — Custom-field definition changes (create/update/deactivate/reactivate/reorder) emit ZERO audit-log entries; only a Serilog `LogInformation` line is written, so the required change-history (NFR-5) does not exist
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #151, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-012 · TC-CHR-313 (all 6 steps assert audit entries for create/update/deactivate/reactivate/reorder). Same **missing-audit class** as BUG-010 / BUG-018 / BUG-023 / ISSUE-024 / ISSUE-025.
- **Title:** Every mutating custom-field operation succeeds but writes no tenant audit row. After creating 9 fields, one update (rename + add option), one reorder, one deactivate and one reactivate as `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` and `?action=CustomField.Create` both return **zero** custom-field entries (the only actions present are `JobTitle.Update` and `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`).
- **Root cause (~90%, code + audit-store + log confirmed):** `CustomFieldService` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/CustomFieldService.cs`) never injects or calls the tenant audit-log writer (`IAuditService`). Each of `CreateAsync` (line 211), `UpdateAsync` (270), `DeactivateAsync` (296), `ReactivateAsync` (322) and `ReorderAsync` (356) ends with only `_logger.LogInformation(...)` — a Serilog console/file line, not a persisted audit row. The data needed for before/after is already in hand (the result DTO + the mutated entity), so this is a wiring gap, not a data-availability gap. The Serilog log for this run shows clean 200/201s on every op and no ERR for any custom-fields RequestId (e.g. `0HNMIFE5GI1K6`), confirming a silent omission rather than a failed write.
- **Reproduction steps (live):**
  1. Authenticate `tenantadmin@acme.test` (subdomain `acme`, pw `Admin@123!`).
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields` body `{"entityType":"employee","fieldName":"T-Shirt Size","fieldType":"dropdown","options":"[\"S\",\"M\",\"L\",\"XL\"]"}` → **201**.
  3. `PUT /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields/{id}` (rename + add option), `POST …/{id}/deactivate`, `POST …/{id}/reactivate`, `POST …/reorder` — all 200.
  4. `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=50` and `GET …/audit-logs?action=CustomField.Create` (header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`) → **0** custom-field entries in either.
- **Evidence:** audit-logs `?action=CustomField.Create` → HTTP 200, `items: 0`; unfiltered page-50 → only `JobTitle.Update` + `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked` actions, 0 custom-field; `CustomFieldService.cs` has no `IAuditService` reference (grep clean); no ERR for custom-fields RequestIds in `hrm-20260625.log`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no security/isolation/data-integrity impact (definitions persist correctly and are observable via `GET /custom-fields`), but a documented compliance requirement (NFR-5: all custom-field definition changes auditable with actor/timestamp/before-after) is entirely unmet for mutating configuration operations. Same MED rating and shape as the BUG-018/BUG-023 audit-gap family; not HIGH because the operations work and the current state is independently observable.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. (A dev would have the five Custom-field commands emit tenant audit actions — e.g. `CustomField.Created/Updated/Deactivated/Reactivated/Reordered` with before/after + acting user — reusing the existing JobTitle/Department audit writer.)

### ISSUE-028 — Custom-field name uniqueness is case-SENSITIVE and the name is stored un-trimmed: "Region" and "region" coexist as two distinct fields in the same tenant+entity, and "  Padded Name  " is persisted with leading/trailing spaces
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #362, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR · US-CHR-012 · TC-CHR-303 (duplicate field name within tenant+entity rejected) / TC-CHR-295. Same **case-sensitive-uniqueness class** as BUG-013/016/017 and the **whitespace-not-trimmed class** as ISSUE-022.
- **Title:** Two related contract nits on `field_name`: (a) the BR-1 uniqueness check (`CustomFieldService.CreateAsync` line 162 / `UpdateAsync` line 236) compares `c.FieldName == request.FieldName` — an ordinal/case-sensitive Postgres equality — so a tenant can create both "Region" and "region" as separate definitions for the same `entityType`. The exact-case duplicate IS correctly rejected (TC-303 passes), and single-token case variants that slugify to the *same* `field_key` are incidentally blocked by the separate key-uniqueness guard (line 174) — but as soon as an explicit distinct `fieldKey` is supplied (or a multi-word name slugs differently), case-variant display names coexist. (b) `field_name` is never trimmed: `"  Padded Name  "` is stored verbatim (verified via read-back), so a UI label and any name-based lookup carry the surrounding whitespace.
- **Root cause (~90%, code + live-confirmed):** name uniqueness uses default ordinal string equality with no `ToLower()`/`ILIKE`/citext normalization, and there is no `.Trim()` on `request.FieldName` before the uniqueness check or before persistence.
