## Findings (US-ATT-009 — Attendance Integration with Payroll: feeding hours/days, 2026-06-26)

> **Run context (REPORT-ONLY, API-layer):** 12 owned TCs executed — TC-ATT-118..128 + TC-ATT-ISO-012. Routes discovered on `AttendanceController`: `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=yyyy-MM&employeeIds=<csv>` (`Attendance.View.All`), `GET /period-lock?month=` (`Attendance.View.All`), `POST /period-lock` + `POST /period-lock/{id}/unlock` (`Attendance.Lock.Manage`), `GET /reconciliation?month=` (`Attendance.View.All`). The attendance→payroll **feed is well-built and accurate**: payroll-data reuses the US-ATT-007 monthly summary, so present/absent/lop/work-minutes **reconcile exactly** with the summary AND the reconciliation view (John Doe 2026-06: present 3.0 / absent 13 / lop 13 / work 13057 / OT 360 — identical across all three surfaces). **Approved-OT-only is honored** (John: approved 360, pending 1591, rejected 120 → feed shows only 360, multiplier breakdown `{"1.5":360}`). **Lock lifecycle works** (lock → blocks regularization with exact AC-4 string; overlap → 409; unlock HR-only; re-lock). **Authz clean** (unauth 401, employee/manager 403, HR 200; reads gated `Attendance.View.All`, writes `Attendance.Lock.Manage`). Findings below are the gaps. No 500s in `hrm-20260626.log`. AC-2/AC-3 salary math + FR-5 payroll-input column + BR-8 configurable cutoff are PAYROLL-MODULE / DEFERRED per the TCs' own notes.

### ISSUE-088 — Empty / missing-date `POST /period-lock` body creates a garbage lock for `0001-01-01` (no required-field or sane-date validation on `LockPeriodRequest`)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #162, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-009 · TC-ATT-122 / TC-ATT-127 (S6 lock validation)
- **Title:** A `POST /api/v1/attendance/period-lock` with an empty body `{}` (or omitting either date) returns **200 and persists a real active lock with `periodStart=periodEnd=0001-01-01`** instead of a 400 validation error. `LockPeriodRequest.PeriodStart/PeriodEnd` are non-nullable `DateOnly`, so absent fields bind to `DateOnly.MinValue` (`0001-01-01`); the only guard is `periodEnd < periodStart` (passes, equal) and the overlap check (passes, no other 0001 lock), so a meaningless lock is created.
- **Root cause (~95%, code + live):** there is **no FluentValidation validator and no in-handler required-field/range-sanity check** for `LockPeriodCommand`. `AttendancePayrollService.LockPeriodAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AttendancePayrollService.cs:187-228`) validates only `periodEnd < periodStart` (`invalid_range`) and overlap (`already_locked`); it never rejects the default/min date or an absurd range. The controller `[FromBody] LockPeriodRequest` (AttendanceController.cs:952-968) has no `[Required]` enforcement because `DateOnly` is a value type that silently defaults.
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test` (subdomain `acme`): `curl -X POST :5000/api/v1/attendance/period-lock -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hr>' -H 'X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'` → **200**, body `{"id":"019f0249-…","periodStart":"0001-01-01","periodEnd":"0001-01-01","isLocked":true}`. Verify: `GET /period-lock?month=0001-01` returns the row. (A second `{}` then returns 409 `already_locked` against the first garbage lock — proving it persisted.)
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** created lock `019f0249-f24e-7cd7-8e8d-bdbe4e6af39d` for `0001-01-01`; full JSON captured. **Residue: I unlocked it (is_locked=false) at end of run** — the inactive row remains as history (unlock is a state flip, not a delete). Non-date strings (`periodStart:"banana"`) DO return 400 (model-binding), so the gap is specifically the *omitted/default* date, not malformed strings.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no crash and no cross-tenant impact, but a payroll-critical control (the attendance lock that BR-1 makes a payroll-finalize precondition) accepts garbage input and silently creates spurious lock rows; an integration caller or fat-fingered request pollutes the lock table and could mask/confuse the real period lock. Contained to the acting tenant.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-089 — Lock / unlock actions write no `audit_logs` entry (FR-4 "log lock/unlock in the audit log with HR id + timestamp" only half-met — in-row attribution + Serilog only)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #153, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-009 · TC-ATT-122 (S7) / TC-ATT-123 (S1) / TC-ATT-127 (S7) — FR-4
- **Title:** Locking and unlocking a period stamps `locked_by/locked_at` (and `unlocked_by/unlocked_at`) on the `attendance_period_lock` row and emits a `_logger.LogInformation` line, but writes **no queryable `audit_logs` action row**. FR-4 explicitly states "The system shall log the lock/unlock actions in the audit log with the HR Officer's ID and timestamp." The in-row columns satisfy attribution but are not the central, queryable, immutable audit trail FR-4 names — `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?action=lock` returns 0 rows after a lock+unlock+re-lock cycle.
- **Root cause (~90%, code + live):** the central audit capture (`AuditCaptureInterceptor`, `src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Interceptors/AuditCaptureInterceptor.cs:78-81`) only emits an `audit_logs` row for entities implementing the **opt-in `IAuditableEntity`** marker. `AttendancePeriodLock` is `: BaseEntity` and does **not** implement `IAuditableEntity` (`src/backend/HRM.Domain/Entities/AttendancePeriodLock.cs:21`), so lock/unlock changes are never captured. The service logs only to Serilog (`AttendancePayrollService.cs:223-225, 257-259`). Same systemic family as ISSUE-067/069/071/073/075 (attendance writes skip central audit) — but here the gap is against an **explicit FR-4 audit requirement**, hence MED not LOW.
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme: `POST /period-lock {2026-05-01..2026-05-31}` (200), `POST /period-lock/{id}/unlock` (200). Then as `tenantadmin@acme.test`: `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?action=lock` and `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?pageSize=20`.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** after a full lock→unlock→re-lock cycle, `audit-logs?action=lock` = `{items:[],totalCount:0}`; the only recent audit entry on the tenant is `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked`. The lock rows themselves DO carry `lockedBy=019efa61-… lockedAt=… unlockedBy=… unlockedAt=…` (in-row attribution present). Serilog `hrm-20260626.log` has the `LOCKED`/`UNLOCKED` INF lines.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — an explicit story FR (FR-4) is unmet; lock/unlock is a sensitive payroll-gating control whose history HR/audit must be able to query centrally, and it isn't there. No functional break (the lock works; attribution exists in-row). Blast radius = the audit trail for all period-lock operations.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-090 — `payroll-data` / `reconciliation` auto-generate phantom full-month-absent data for any UNTRACKED period, contradicting the story precondition that the summary must already be generated (TC-ATT-118 S5)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #173, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-009 · TC-ATT-118 (S5 — month with no generated summary)
- **Title:** The story (Preconditions §2, AC-1) requires the monthly attendance summary to be **generated** before payroll pulls it, and TC-ATT-118 S5 expects a clear "summary not generated" contract so payroll cannot proceed on un-generated data. Instead, requesting **any** month (incl. arbitrary past/future periods that were never tracked) returns **200 with a fully-populated row per employee showing every working day as ABSENT and the entire month as LOP** — because the underlying summary service generates on demand. E.g. `month=2025-01` → every acme employee `present 0 / absent 23 / lop 23`; `month=2026-05` (untracked) → `present 0 / absent 20 / lop 20`. There is no "not generated" signal; payroll consuming this would compute a full-month LOP deduction from phantom absences.
- **Root cause (~85%, code):** `GetPayrollDataAsync` calls `_summaryService.GetMonthlyAsync(...)` which "includes ALL non-terminated employees plus **generates on-demand if not yet materialized**" (`AttendancePayrollService.cs:66-69` + comment). A never-tracked month yields a summary where no attendance_log rows exist → every scheduled working day defaults to ABSENT → LOP = absent. The endpoint never distinguishes "generated and genuinely all-absent" from "never tracked → defaulted all-absent."
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme: `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2025-01` → 200, 34 rows, each `totalAbsentDays==totalWorkingDays`, `lopDays==totalWorkingDays`. Same for `month=2026-05`.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** `2025-01` rows = `present 0.0 / absent 23.0 / lop 23.0` for every employee; `2026-05` = `20/20`; only `2026-06` (the tracked month) shows real mixed data. No 400 / no "not generated" marker on any of them.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no crash and tenant-scoped, but a payroll-feed that silently returns "everyone was absent all month → full LOP" for an un-generated period is a real financial-correctness hazard the moment the payroll module consumes it; the story's own precondition/AC-1 intent (don't proceed on un-generated data) is not enforced. Mitigated by the fact that the payroll engine is not yet built (DEFERRED), so no live deduction occurs today.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-091 — Terminated-employee payroll-data row caps `total_working_days` (BR-7 cutoff works) but HARD-ZEROS present/absent/lop instead of computing them up to the last working day (under-counts LOP for terminated staff)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #361, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-009 · TC-ATT-125 (S1/S2 — terminated employee BR-7)
- **Title:** BR-7 ("attendance for terminated employees is included up to their last working day") is **partially** implemented: the terminated employee's `total_working_days` is correctly capped (acme "Doj" shows 19 vs 22 for active staff in 2026-06, proving the EmploymentHistory `status_change→Terminated` cutoff applies), but the row's `total_present_days`, `total_absent_days`, and `lop_days` are all **hard-set to 0** rather than computed up to the last working day. A terminated employee who had unexcused absences (= LOP) before termination therefore feeds payroll `lop_days = 0`, under-counting their loss-of-pay deduction.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** the US-ATT-007 monthly summary **excludes terminated employees**, so `summaryByEmp` has no row for them; the service adds them via the `else if (emp.Status == EmployeeStatus.Terminated)` branch (`AttendancePayrollService.cs:138-153`) which sets `TotalPresentDays/TotalAbsentDays/LopDays = 0m` with the explicit code comment "present/absent/lop for terminated employees up to the cutoff are not re-derived here … defaults to 0 absent the summary row." Only working-days + overtime are carried.
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme: `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2026-06&employeeIds=019efcfa-7503-73d7-b00a-e43d3ef08128` (terminated "Doj").
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** row = `totalWorkingDays 19, totalPresentDays 0, totalAbsentDays 0, lopDays 0, approvedOvertimeMinutes 0, totalWorkMinutes 0`. The working-days cap (19<22) confirms BR-7 cutoff fires; the all-zero present/absent/lop confirms they are not derived.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — affects only terminated employees in their final pay period, and the salary computation that would consume `lop_days` is itself DEFERRED (payroll module not built); but as specified, BR-7 intends attendance (incl. present/absent/LOP) to be included up to the last working day, and today only the day-count denominator honors that.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-092 — Malformed/unparseable `employeeIds` are silently dropped and the whole-tenant set is returned (no 400), contrary to TC-ATT-127 S5 "invalid values yield 400"
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #358, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-009 · TC-ATT-127 (S5 input validation) / TC-ATT-118 (S1 employee list)
- **Title:** `GET /payroll-data?month=2026-06&employeeIds=notauuid,123` (or `employeeIds=';DROP--`) returns **200 with all 34 tenant rows** rather than a 400. The `employeeIds` parser drops anything that isn't a valid GUID; when the parsed set is empty it falls back to the whole tenant. There is **no injection risk** (EF is parameterized; nothing leaked beyond the tenant — see the separate BUG-003 extension note for the actual cross-tenant gap), but a caller that fat-fingers the id list silently receives every employee instead of an explicit error, and TC-ATT-127 S5's "invalid values yield 400" is not met for this input.
- **Root cause (~80%, code):** `ParseEmployeeIds` (AttendanceController) skips non-GUID tokens and returns null/empty for an all-garbage list; `GetPayrollDataAsync` treats a null/empty id set as "whole tenant" (`AttendancePayrollService.cs:79` → `requested = ... : null`). No validation distinguishes "no filter supplied" from "filter supplied but all values invalid."
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme: `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2026-06&employeeIds=notauuid,123` → 200, `rows=34`. `employeeIds=';DROP--` → 200, no SQL error, full set.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** both garbage-id requests returned `success:true, rows:34` (the full tenant set), no 400, no SQL/server error in `hrm-20260626.log`. SQL/XSS in the `month` param correctly returns 400 (`invalid_month`).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — no leakage and no crash; purely a contract/robustness nit (silent fallback to all-employees on a malformed filter). Defense-in-depth.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-ATT-009 payroll-integration surface, not re-filed.**
> An **acme JWT (`hr@acme.test`, has `Attendance.View.All`) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** on `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2026-06` returns **HTTP 200 scoped to techoneglobal** — **1 row, employee `019efcf4-ce46-78fd-8a31-d54d75c0710a` "Cross Write"** (a distinct single-employee tenant), instead of acme's own 34 rows. The identical leak occurs on `GET /reconciliation?month=2026-06` (returns techoneglobal's "Cross Write" row) and `GET /period-lock?month=` (resolves against the header tenant). This is a **CONFIRMED cross-tenant READ leak of payroll-feed data** (working days / present / absent / LOP / overtime per employee — exactly the GDPR-sensitive aggregate the payroll module consumes): the data query keys off `ITenantContext.TenantId` (header-resolved = techoneglobal) while authorization uses the acme token, and `TenantResolutionMiddleware` never rejects token-tenant ≠ header-resolved-tenant. Same root as the module-wide BUG-003 (root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware). **All cross-tenant probes were READ-ONLY; the lock/unlock WRITE arm was NOT executed against techoneglobal (no-cross-tenant-write rule).** **Within the matching (header=token) acme context, isolation is CLEAN** — payroll-data, reconciliation, and period-lock all scope to acme's 34 employees only; `employeeIds` listing a non-acme id resolves to no rows. (`globex` subdomain returns a "workspace not found" 404 — does not exist.) See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]] and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave module reports for the BUG-003 systemic record.

> **FR-6 payroll-recalculation SIGNAL (TC-ATT-123 S4) — DEFERRED, confirmed absent (not a new finding).**
> AC-5/BR-6/FR-6 require that unlocking a period after a payroll run has started raise a "recalculate affected payroll entries" signal. The attendance side raises **no signal/seam** — `UnlockPeriodAsync` documents it explicitly: "FR-6 (trigger payroll refresh): DEFERRED — no Payroll module to notify. A re-pull of GetPayrollDataAsync after correcting attendance always returns current data" (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AttendancePayrollService.cs:255-256`). The attendance-side unlock→edit→re-lock and fresh-data-on-re-pull DO work; only the recalc-signal is deferred, consistent with the payroll-consumption deferral pattern across US-ATT-006/007/008. Recorded as DEFERRED per the TC's own note, not filed as a defect.

## Findings (US-ATT-010 — Attendance Dashboard and Reports for HR, 2026-06-26)

### BUG-050 — Manager persona is fully locked out of the attendance dashboard/reports (403 on everything); BR-4 "managers see their team" is unreachable because every US-ATT-010 endpoint is gated by `Attendance.View.All`, which Managers do not hold
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #160, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Regression re-test 2026-06-27:** STILL PRESENT (unchanged). Manager persona → `GET /attendance/dashboard` **403**, `GET /attendance/dashboard/live-board` **403**, `GET /attendance/custom-report` **403**. HR (`Attendance.View.All`) gets 200 on all. BR-4 team view still unreachable.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-010 · TC-ATT-137 (S2/S3/S4/S5 manager team scope) + TC-ATT-140 (S3)
- **Title:** Every US-ATT-010 endpoint (`dashboard`, `dashboard/live-board`, `reports/department-comparison`, `reports/custom`, `reports/custom/export`, `reports/trends`, all `reports/scheduled` CRUD) carries `[RequirePermission("Attendance.View.All")]`. The `Manager` role holds `Attendance.View.Team` + `Attendance.Approve.Team` + `Reports.View` but **NOT** `Attendance.View.All`, so a manager gets **403 on the endpoint itself — even with `?scope=team`**. BR-4 ("Managers viewing the dashboard see only their team, scoped by `Attendance.Read.Team`") is therefore **unmet for the actual Manager persona**: the team-scope branch in the service (`ResolveScopeEmployeesAsync` scope=="team") is only reachable by callers who already hold `Attendance.View.All` (i.e. an HR user who is also a line manager). A plain manager cannot view their team's attendance dashboard at all.
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** the controller gates the whole US-ATT-010 surface on `Attendance.View.All` only (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Controllers/AttendanceController.cs:1033,1057,1080,1102,1140,1180,1201,1219,1239,1261`). The service's `scope=team` path (`AttendanceDashboardService.cs:609-637`) correctly narrows to `ReportsToEmployeeId == manager.Id`, but the `[RequirePermission]` filter rejects the manager before the handler runs. The author's own comment acknowledges this: "since these endpoints are gated by Attendance.View.All (HR), team scope is for HR users who are also managers" (`AttendanceController.cs:1019-1022`) — i.e. the BR-4 manager-team capability was deliberately not wired for the team-only permission. The controller never admits `Attendance.View.Team` / `Attendance.Approve.Team`.
- **Reproduction steps:** Login `manager@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` (subdomain `acme`). `GET /api/v1/attendance/dashboard?scope=team` → **403**. `GET /api/v1/attendance/dashboard?scope=all` → 403. Same 403 on `/dashboard/live-board`, `/reports/custom`, `/reports/trends`, `/reports/department-comparison`, `/reports/scheduled`. Confirm perms: `GET /api/v1/auth/me` → `permissions` includes `Attendance.View.Team`, `Attendance.Approve.Team`, `Reports.View` but **no** `Attendance.View.All`.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** manager token on `/dashboard?scope=team` and `?scope=all` both returned HTTP 403; `/auth/me` roles `["Manager"]`, attendance/report perms `['Attendance.Approve.Team','Attendance.View.Team','Reports.View']`. By contrast HR (`hr@acme.test`, holds `Attendance.View.All`) gets 200 on all the same endpoints. No Serilog error — clean authz rejection.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — not a security leak (fail-closed: managers are *denied*, not over-granted) and HR access works, but it breaks a primary user flow the story explicitly specifies (BR-4 manager team dashboard), and the service code to support it already exists and is dead-reachable for the team-only role. Contained to the manager persona on this story's surface.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-093 — Scheduled-report-config create/update/delete writes NO audit_logs entry (TC-ATT-140 S7 unmet); plus spec→impl permission drift (`Reports.View.All`/`Attendance.Read.All` named by the story do not exist — gate is `Attendance.View.All`) and missing recipients/report-type validation
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #153, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-010 · TC-ATT-140 (S5/S7) + TC-ATT-136 (S8) + TC-ATT-129/137 (precondition permission strings)
- **Title:** Three contained nits on the scheduled-report-config + permission surface: **(a)** `POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/attendance/reports/scheduled` mutate a `scheduled_report_config` row with **no audit-log write** — the Create/Update/Delete service methods only `SaveChangesAsync` (+ an INFO Serilog line on create) and never call an audit service, so TC-ATT-140 S7 ("create/update/delete of a scheduled_report_config is recorded with actor + timestamp") is unmet; this matches the module-wide missing-audit-on-config-writes theme (BUG-025/028/031, etc.). **(b)** Spec→impl permission drift: the story preconditions/§2 name `Attendance.Read.All` and `Reports.View.All`; neither exists in `PermissionCatalog` (only `Reports.View`), and the actual gate on the whole surface is `Attendance.View.All`. Functionally HR works (HR holds `Attendance.View.All`), so this is documentation/spec drift, not a break. **(c)** `ValidateScheduledDto` does not validate `recipients` (an empty `recipients:[]` is accepted — TC-ATT-136 S8 expects empty recipients rejected) nor that `reportType` is a known type (any non-empty string accepted).
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** **(a)** `CreateScheduledReportAsync`/`UpdateScheduledReportAsync`/`DeleteScheduledReportAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AttendanceDashboardService.cs:446-519`) contain no `IAuditService`/`AuditLog` emission; delete is a soft-delete (`IsDeleted=true`) with no audit. The `created_by` field (§7) is also not set on the entity in Create (relies on AuditInterceptor stamping, but no domain audit row). **(b)** controller uses `[RequirePermission("Attendance.View.All")]` throughout (AttendanceController.cs:1033…1261); `PermissionCatalog` has `Reports.View` (line 266) but no `Reports.View.All`/`Attendance.Read.All`. **(c)** `ValidateScheduledDto` (AttendanceDashboardService.cs:737-755) checks only reportType-non-empty, frequency∈{DAILY,WEEKLY,MONTHLY}, format∈{CSV,XLSX,PDF}, deliveryTime HH:mm — nothing on recipients or report-type vocabulary.
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme — **(a/c)** `POST /api/v1/attendance/reports/scheduled` body `{"reportType":"MONTHLY_SUMMARY","frequency":"MONTHLY","filters":{"departmentId":"Engineering"},"recipients":[],"deliveryTime":"08:00","format":"XLSX","isActive":true}` → **201** despite empty recipients; then `PUT .../{id}` and `DELETE .../{id}` (→ 204) all succeed with no audit record. (HR cannot read `/api/v1/tenant/audit-logs` — 403 — so audit absence is confirmed from the service code path, not the read API.) **(b)** `GET /auth/me` for HR shows the gate-satisfying perm is `Attendance.View.All`, and `Reports.View.All`/`Attendance.Read.All` named by the story are absent from the catalog.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** create returned 201 with `recipients:[]` honored; PUT changed frequency MONTHLY→WEEKLY + isActive→false; DELETE returned 204; nonexistent DELETE returned 404; bad frequency/format/empty-reportType all correctly 400. Service source shows no audit emission on any of the three mutations. (Residue: the temporary config created in this probe was DELETEd — no acme residue from this finding.)
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth + spec-hygiene: no data exposure, no crash; the audit gap weakens traceability of who scheduled/changed/removed an automated report (a recurring module theme), the permission drift is cosmetic since HR access works, and the recipients/report-type validation gap only lets a no-op config be saved.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ENH-009 — Report CSV/XLSX export does not neutralize formula-injection (CSV-injection) in employee-derived cells; an employee display name beginning with `= + - @` is written verbatim and would execute as a formula in Excel/Sheets
- **Type / Title / Module / Why-it-matters / Suggested-direction:**
- **Type:** ENH (defense-in-depth hardening; not a defect against the current spec — FR-5 only requires the three formats with matching content, which works)
- **Title:** Attendance report CSV/XLSX export emits employee-derived text (employee name, department) into cells without prefixing a guard character, so a name like `=cmd|...` or `+HYPERLINK(...)` would be interpreted as a formula when the exported file is opened in Excel/Google Sheets (CSV/spreadsheet formula injection). Observed live: the acme dataset already contains an employee named `<script>alert(1)</script> Test` and several `AAAA…` long names (prior test residue) that flow verbatim into the CSV `Employee` column. The `<script>` payload is **inert** in a CSV/XLSX context (good — no HTML execution), but a leading `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` in any free-text cell remains an Excel-formula vector.
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance · US-ATT-010 · TC-ATT-133 (export) / TC-ATT-140 (S6 sanitisation)
- **Why it matters:** an HR officer opening an exported attendance report is the exact "trusted user opens an attachment" scenario CSV-injection targets; a malicious tenant employee who can set their own display name could plant a formula that fires in HR's spreadsheet. Low likelihood (needs name control + a vulnerable spreadsheet client), but cheap to harden and consistent across every export surface in the platform.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** prefix any cell whose value starts with `= + - @ ` (and tab/CR) with a leading apostrophe or `'` guard in the CSV/XLSX writer (`AttendanceDashboardService.cs` export rendering, the `ExportColumns` path). Report only — no change made.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-ATT-010 dashboard/reports surface, not re-filed.**
> An **acme JWT (`hr@acme.test`, has `Attendance.View.All`) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** on `GET /api/v1/attendance/dashboard` returns **HTTP 200 scoped to techoneglobal** (`expectedHeadcount:1, clockedIn:0, …`) and `GET /dashboard/live-board` returns **techoneglobal's 1 row — employee name "Cross Write"** (a distinct single-employee tenant), instead of acme's own **33** employees. The dashboard KPIs, live board, department comparison, custom report, trends and scheduled-config list all key off `ITenantContext.TenantId` (header-resolved = techoneglobal) while authorization uses the acme token; `TenantResolutionMiddleware` never rejects token-tenant ≠ header-resolved-tenant. This is a **CONFIRMED cross-tenant READ leak of org-wide attendance aggregates** (the exact org-wide KPI/headcount/per-employee status data the story exposes). Same root as the module-wide BUG-003 (root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware). **All cross-tenant probes were READ-ONLY; no scheduled-config create/update/delete was executed against techoneglobal (no-cross-tenant-write rule).** **Within the matching (header=token) acme context, isolation is CLEAN** — dashboard/live-board/reports/scheduled all scope to acme's own employees only. An acme HR token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: platform` likewise resolves to the platform tenant (returns its all-zero KPIs), confirming the scope-follows-header behavior. (`globex` subdomain returns "workspace not found" 404 — does not exist; techoneglobal used as Tenant B, read-only.) See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]] and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave/US-ATT-009 module reports for the BUG-003 systemic record.

> **DEFERRALS confirmed (per the TCs' own notes, not filed as defects):** SignalR real-time live-board push (FR-2/NFR-2 — board is polled, US-NTF deferred; TC-ATT-130 S7); Redis KPI cache (FR-7/NFR-1 — DB-computed path verified live, cache off in this env; TC-ATT-138); scheduled-report EMAIL delivery (FR-8 — generate+queue seam only, US-NTF deferred; TC-ATT-136 S6); UTC day-boundary (tenant-timezone deferred module-wide). Department-comparison color-band (green/amber/red §8) is a **FE concern** — the API returns `attendanceRatePct` numeric only (no band field), which is the correct API contract; band classification is the chart layer (BLOCKED fe-platform-bound). HOLIDAY status classification IS wired server-side (reads the `Holidays` table, tenant-wide + location-specific) — better than the TCs' "conditional" assumption.

> REPORT-ONLY API-layer run (curl + JWT) against the running stack on `acme` (tenant `019ef3ba-ffb7-7eec-b24f-7ad806ca1cb9`). FE :4200 down + platform-bound → all UI/a11y TCs BLOCKED. **Real routes:** `/api/v1/recruitment/vacancies` (list/get/create/update + `/{id}/publish`,`/{id}/close`,`/{id}/status`, `/status` bulk); public `/api/v1/careers/vacancies` (+ `/{slug}`). **Real permissions (differ from the TC text `Recruitment.Create.All`/`Read.All`):** reads = `Recruitment.View`, all writes = `Recruitment.Manage`. ### BUG-055 — Vacancy create/update/publish/close write NOTHING to the tenant audit trail (FR-7 + AC-3 unmet); the only "audit" is a Serilog file line
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #143, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-001 · TC-REC-001-03 (S4 audit) + TC-REC-001-04 (S2 close audit) + TC-REC-001-06 (S8 transition audit)
- **Title:** FR-7 ("log all vacancy create/update/publish/close actions to the tenant's audit trail") and AC-3 ("an audit log entry is created") require an `audit_logs` row per vacancy lifecycle action. `VacancyService` writes **no `audit_logs` record at all** for create/update/publish/close/status-change — it only emits a Serilog file line (`_logger.LogInformation("Vacancy ...")`) and relies on the `AuditInterceptor` stamping `CreatedBy`/`UpdatedBy`/`UpdatedAt` columns on the `vacancy` row. The dedicated audit trail (`audit_logs`, surfaced at `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs`) never receives a Vacancy entry, so a tenant admin/auditor cannot see who created/published/edited/closed a vacancy.
- **Root cause (~95%, code + log):** `VacancyService.CreateAsync/UpdateAsync/PublishAsync/ChangeStatusAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/VacancyService.cs:82,123,159,181`) call `_logger.LogInformation(...)` but never an `IAuditService`/`audit_logs` insert. The service XML-doc even states the design: "Audit ... is provided by the AuditInterceptor (CreatedBy/UpdatedBy stamping ...) plus structured Serilog entries" (`VacancyService.cs:14-17`) — i.e. the column-stamp + Serilog were treated as satisfying FR-7, but neither lands in the queryable audit trail. Other modules (Department, JobTitle, LeaveRequest, Tenant, User…) DO write `audit_logs` rows, so the trail exists and recruitment is simply not wired in.
- **Reproduction steps:** As `tenantadmin@acme.test`/acme: create a vacancy (`POST /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies`) → 201; publish (`POST /{id}/publish`) → 200; edit (`PUT /{id}`) → 200. Then `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?resourceType=Vacancy` → `totalCount: 0`. DB: `select count(*) from audit_logs where tenant_id='019ef3ba-…' and resource_type ilike '%vacanc%'` → **0**. The Serilog file `hrm-20260626.log` DOES contain `Vacancy created/published/updated` INF lines for the same id, proving the action happened but was only file-logged.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** `audit-logs?resourceType=Vacancy` → `{items:[],totalCount:0}`; `audit-logs?action=vacancy_published` → `totalCount 0`; distinct `resource_type` in acme `audit_logs` = Department, JobTitle, LeaveRequest, Tenant, User, … (no Vacancy). Serilog slice: `[2026-06-26 10:42:28 INF] Vacancy created (Draft). Id="019f0257-…" By=tenantadmin@acme.test` + matching published/updated lines.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — FR-7 + AC-3 are explicit acceptance criteria and a compliance/traceability requirement for a multi-tenant HR product; the entire vacancy lifecycle is unauditable in the product's own audit trail. Same systemic "missing-audit-on-writes" theme as BUG-025/028/031 (Leave) and the Core-HR audit gaps.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-095 — The tenant-level public-careers toggle (`Tenant.PublicCareersEnabled`) has NO writer anywhere in the product; FR-4/S35.2.9 "if enabled in tenant module configuration" is unreachable, so the public careers page can never be turned on for a real tenant
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #164, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-001 · TC-REC-001-02 (precondition: public page enabled) + TC-REC-001-10 (tenant toggle)
- **Title:** `PublicCareersService` correctly gates the anonymous careers listing/detail on `Tenant.PublicCareersEnabled` (off ⇒ empty list / 404). But a repo-wide search shows the flag is only ever **read** (PublicCareersService) and only ever **set in an integration test fixture** — there is **no controller, command, settings DTO, or admin endpoint** that lets a tenant admin enable it. The column defaults to `false` for every seeded/created tenant. Consequently FR-4 ("publish ... to the tenant's public careers page if enabled in tenant module configuration — see S35.2.9") and FR-5 (public SEO slug page) are dead on arrival for any real tenant: an Open, public-toggled vacancy is never publicly visible because the tenant master switch can't be flipped through the product.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `grep PublicCareersEnabled = ` across `src/backend` matches only `HRM.Tests/Integration/VacancyIntegrationTests.cs`; the entity property exists (`Tenant.cs:155`) and is read in `PublicCareersService.IsCareersEnabledAsync` (`PublicCareersService.cs:118-127`), but no write path (tenant settings update / module-config command) sets it. The careers feature was built end-to-end on the vacancy side but the tenant-config switch (S35.2.9) was never wired.
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous, acme subdomain: with an Open + public-toggled vacancy present, `GET /api/v1/careers/vacancies` (X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme) → `data: []`; `GET /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{slug}` → 404 "Vacancy not found." DB shows `public_careers_enabled = f` for acme and there is no API to change it (searched all controllers/commands). Only after a manual `UPDATE tenants SET public_careers_enabled=true` does the public listing/detail return the vacancy (proving the rest of the feature works).
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** pre-toggle: public listing `[]`, slug detail 404. Manual DB enable → public listing returns `[(QA Senior Backend Engineer, qa-senior-backend-engineer, VAC-2026-0001)]` and `/careers/vacancies/{slug}` → 200 with sanitized description; hiring-manager/internal fields correctly omitted from the public DTO. Flag reverted to `false` after the test (no residue).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the public-careers vacancy machinery itself is correct and tenant-isolated; the gap is a missing config control, so the FR-4/FR-5 capability is inaccessible to customers (a feature-completeness gap, not a data/security defect). Becomes HIGH if the public careers page is a contracted Phase-1 deliverable.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-096 — Omitted `headcount` silently defaults to 1 instead of being a validation error (FR-1 "required" not enforced on create)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #365, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-001 · TC-REC-001-07 (S5 blank headcount)
- **Title:** FR-1 lists headcount as a required integer ≥ 1. The create/update request DTO declares `public int Headcount { get; init; } = 1;`, so a body that omits `headcount` entirely is accepted and persists `headcount = 1` rather than returning a "headcount is required" error. Explicit invalid values are correctly rejected (0 → 400 "Headcount must be at least 1", -1 → 400, 2.5 → 400 JSON-int-conversion), but a missing field is silently defaulted.
- **Root cause (~85%, code):** `CreateVacancyRequest.Headcount` / `UpdateVacancyRequest.Headcount` default to `1` (`VacancyDtos.cs:113,132`); `CreateVacancyValidator` only checks `GreaterThanOrEqualTo(1)` and never distinguishes "omitted" from "supplied" (an int can't be null). So an absent field passes as 1.
- **Reproduction steps:** As acme admin: `POST /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies` with body omitting `headcount` (`{"title":"HCblank","departmentId":"…","employmentType":"FullTime","description":"<p>x</p>"}`) → 201, `headcount: 1`.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** HTTP 201, `data.headcount = 1` for the omitted-field body. Explicit 0/-1/2.5 all 400.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — never persists an invalid (<1) headcount; only the "required" semantics are loose (a default substitutes for an error). No data-integrity or security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-REC-001 recruitment-vacancy surface, not re-filed.**
> The recruitment vacancy reads/writes resolve the tenant from `ITenantContext.TenantId` (populated by `TenantResolutionMiddleware` from the request **subdomain/`X-Tenant-Subdomain` header**) and drive the EF global query filter off it, while authorization uses the JWT — and the middleware never rejects **token-tenant ≠ header-resolved-tenant**. Demonstrated live: an **acme JWT (`tenantadmin@acme.test`) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** (and `: e2e`) on `GET /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies/{acmeVacancyId}` returns **HTTP 404** (the read scoped to the *header* tenant, not acme), and the list endpoint returns **0 / the header tenant's set** rather than acme's 13 — i.e. the data context follows the header, not the token. This is the same BUG-003 mechanism (root locus US-AUTH-007 / `TenantResolutionMiddleware`): a user authenticated to tenant A who supplies tenant B's subdomain operates inside tenant B's data context. **The cross-tenant probe was READ-ONLY and the comparison tenants (techoneglobal, e2e) had ZERO vacancies, so no other tenant's vacancy rows were actually returned and NO write was made to any other tenant** — but the context-switch is conclusively present and would expose/permit another tenant's vacancies if they existed. **Within the matching (header=token) acme context, isolation is CLEAN** — every list/get/create scopes to acme only. The `VacanciesController` XML-doc claims "tenant-isolation is enforced in the service layer (AC-4)", but the service relies solely on the same header-resolved `ITenantContext`, so AC-4 ("PostgreSQL RLS policy enforces tenant isolation") is NOT met (this codebase uses EF query filters, not RLS, and the filter keys off the spoofable header). Affects TC-REC-001-10 (multi-tenant isolation). See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]] and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave/Attendance module reports for the systemic record.

### ISSUE-243 — 24 of 26 acme vacancies are `is_deleted = true` in the DB despite no observable user/API delete; cause unpinned (LOW confidence, NEEDS FOLLOW-UP)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · **WONTFIX (not a code defect — QA/DB residue, confirmed 2026-07-18)**
- **Note:** renumbered from ISSUE-097 on 2026-07-05 (ledger ID-hygiene) — the ID collided with the RESOLVED goal-audit ISSUE-097 (US-PRF-001, PR #154). This US-REC-001 vacancy finding is the still-open occurrence and took the fresh ID.
- **Layer:** DB / DATA
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-001 · TC-REC-ISO-001 (read isolation — surfaced the anomaly when an internal list that returned 3+ Open vacancies minutes earlier returned `totalCount: 0`)
- **Title:** During the ISO read-isolation checks, the acme internal vacancy list (`GET /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies`) flipped from returning the seeded/created Open vacancies to `totalCount: 0` with the SAME correct `tenant_id` filter in the SQL. Direct DB inspection shows **24 of 26 acme `vacancy` rows carry `is_deleted = true`** (the global query filter `WHERE NOT (v.is_deleted) AND v.tenant_id = @TenantId` therefore hides them), while only the **2 newest** rows (VAC-2026-0025/0026, created 11:00) are `is_deleted = false` and remain visible. The soft-delete was **not produced by any delete call in this run** — `@test-runner` issued no delete/soft-delete request, the Serilog log for today contains **0** `DELETE FROM vacancy` and **0** `UPDATE vacancy SET is_deleted` statements, the `vacancy` table has **no triggers**, `is_deleted` is **not** a generated column, and the DB column default is `false` (a direct control `INSERT` returns `is_deleted = false`). A row created at 10:56 (VAC-2026-0024) has `updated_at = NULL` yet `is_deleted = true` — i.e. it was never updated after insert, so the flip did not come through the normal EF update path either.
- **Root cause (LOW confidence ~35%, UNPINNED — needs follow-up):** best hypothesis is a **prior-session bulk soft-delete / residue cleanup** (e.g. an earlier `@test-runner` or seed/cleanup routine that soft-deleted its own recruitment residue out-of-band, possibly via direct SQL that wouldn't appear in this process's request log) — supported by the deleted rows having **mixed `updated_by`** (`NULL`, `hr@acme.test`, `tenantadmin@acme.test`) including never-updated rows, which is inconsistent with a single in-run operation. It is **NOT** explained by: the EF global query filter (filter is correct and tenant-scoped), the DB default (false), a trigger (none), or any logged API call in this run. Could alternatively be an EF mapping quirk on `is_deleted` (the column appears in the INSERT `RETURNING` clause, i.e. treated as store-read), but that did not reproduce on the two newest rows, which insert as `false` — weakening that theory. **Cannot be pinned from available evidence; flagged for a developer to reproduce.**
- **Reproduction steps:** As `hr@acme.test`/acme, `GET /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies?pageSize=100` → `totalCount: 0` even though create/publish of new vacancies just succeeded (the brand-new ones DO appear). DB: `SELECT is_deleted, count(*) FROM vacancy WHERE tenant_id='019ef3ba-ffb7-7eec-b24f-7ad806ca1cb9' GROUP BY is_deleted;` → `t|24, f|2`. `SELECT reference_number, is_deleted, updated_at, updated_by FROM vacancy WHERE reference_number='VAC-2026-0024';` → `is_deleted=t, updated_at=NULL`. Serilog `hrm-20260626.log`: `grep -c "DELETE FROM vacancy"` → 0; `grep "UPDATE vacancy SET is_deleted"` → none.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** the list-count SQL slice (RequestId `0HNMJ6R63S0O8`) shows `WHERE NOT (v.is_deleted) AND (@ef_filter__p2 OR v.tenant_id = @ef_filter__TenantId)` with `tenant_id=019ef3ba-…` returning `count(*) = 0`; DB split `t|24 / f|2`; control `INSERT … RETURNING is_deleted` → `f`; no triggers (`information_schema.triggers` empty for `vacancy`); `is_generated = NEVER`; the employees table for the same tenant is all `is_deleted=false` (anomaly is vacancy-specific, not a global-filter regression).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — if a real code path is auto-soft-deleting vacancies it is a data-integrity bug that would make created vacancies vanish (a primary-flow break); but because it could not be reproduced on fresh rows and no in-run cause was found, it may be pre-existing test residue rather than a live defect. Held at MED pending developer reproduction; downgrade to LOW/WONTFIX if confirmed as residue.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only. Developer to attempt reproduction on a clean tenant (create N vacancies, idle, re-query) and check for any out-of-band soft-delete job/cleanup.
- **WONTFIX — code-level investigation (2026-07-18):** conclusively **not a product-code defect**. Repo-wide, the ONLY write to `Vacancy.IsDeleted` in application code is `= false` at create (`VacancyService.cs`); `IVacancyService`/`VacanciesController` expose **no** delete/soft-delete verb (Close/BulkChangeStatus mutate `Status`, a different column); `AppDbContext` has **no** `Remove()→soft-delete` `SaveChanges` override and nothing calls `.Remove(vacancy)`; there is **no** cascade from department/tenant deletion to `Vacancy.IsDeleted`; and no seed/fixture soft-deletes vacancies (`perf/seed` does a **hard** DELETE on the *perf* tenant only). The decisive tell (already in the evidence): `VAC-2026-0024` has `updated_at = NULL` **and** `is_deleted = true` — since the app only writes that column at INSERT (`=false`) and has no EF update path for it, the sole mechanism that flips it while leaving `updated_at` untouched is a **raw `UPDATE vacancy SET is_deleted=true` executed directly against Postgres** (bypassing the EF audit interceptor), i.e. out-of-band QA/DB manipulation on the acme tenant. The app can never legitimately soft-delete a vacancy in production, so created vacancies cannot "vanish" through the app. **No code change; the acme rows are pre-existing test residue** (optional cleanup: `UPDATE vacancy SET is_deleted=false WHERE tenant_id='019ef3ba-…'` if the QA tenant should be reset). A durable guard (DB CHECK/audit trigger on `vacancy.is_deleted`) is possible but out of scope — the app itself never sets it true.

## US-PRF-001 — Manager Sets Goals/KPIs for Team Members (run 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API layer)

> Routes: `/api/v1/tenant/performance/*` (NOT `/api/v1/performance/*` as the TCs spec — FE-spec drift, see ISSUE-100). Single-goal POST (no batch). Permissions: writes/reads admit `Performance.SetGoal.Team` (direct manager) OR `Performance.SetGoal.All` (HR override); BR-4 direct-report check + BR-1/AC-5 window gate + BR-2 count + ≤100% weight all enforced in `GoalService`. Personas: `manager@acme.test` (SetGoal.Team → EMP-MGR01, reports John Doe EMP-0001 + Et Contract EMP-0014), `hr@acme.test` (SetGoal.All, NOT employee-linked), `tenantadmin@acme.test` (SetGoal.All). Seeded 3 acme cycles (QA-PRF001-OPEN/CLOSED/FUTURE) + 1 techoneglobal cycle for isolation; all residue cleaned (see report). 16 TCs executed: 10 PASS / 4 FAIL / 2 BLOCKED.

### BUG-056 — AC-3 / FR-3 "weights must total exactly 100%" is NOT enforced server-side: an under-allocated (<100%) goal set persists silently and the AC-3 error string is never emitted
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · DEFERRED (feature-blocked: no goal-set finalize seam — see reports-archive/PRODUCT-DECISIONS-NEEDED-2026-07-05.md)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-001-02 (also weakens the AC-2 "weights summing to 100%" guarantee)
- **Title:** AC-3/FR-3 require that goal weights for an employee+cycle sum to **exactly** 100%, with the validation error "Goal weights must total 100%" on violation. The server only enforces the **upper** bound (running total > 100% → 422 `weight_exceeds_100`); it never enforces the lower bound. A manager can create goals summing to 95% (or any value < 100%) and every create returns 201 — the employee is left with an under-weighted goal set indefinitely, and the AC-3 message "Goal weights must total 100%" is **never produced by any endpoint**. The exact-100 invariant is delegated entirely to the (currently-down, untestable) UI via the `EmployeeGoalsDto.TotalWeight` rollup.
- **Root cause (~95%, code + self-documented):** `GoalService.CreateAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/GoalService.cs:75-79`) checks only `newTotal > RequiredTotalWeight` (100) → 422; there is no `< 100` or end-of-set "must equal 100" check. The code comment at `GoalService.cs:73-74` explicitly states the exact-100 rule "is surfaced via the employee-goals/dashboard TotalWeight so the UI can block submit" — i.e. it is by-design a UI-only guarantee. Because POST is single-goal (no batch "Save Goals" transaction), there is no server-side moment at which "the set now sums to exactly 100" is asserted. `UpdateAsync` (`:137`) has the same one-sided check.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):**
  1. `manager@acme.test` (SetGoal.Team), cycle QA-PRF001-OPEN (`019eff10-…-a1`, window open), target John Doe (`019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74`).
  2. `POST /api/v1/tenant/performance/goals` weight 50 → **201**; again weight 45 → **201** (running total 95%).
  3. `GET .../employees/{john}/cycles/{cycle}/goals` → `totalWeight: 95`, 2 goals persisted. No error, no block.
  4. Contrast: a third goal weight 45 (would total 140) → **422** "Goal weights for this employee would total 140%, which exceeds 100%." — the *over* arm works.
- **Evidence:** under-alloc both 201, `GET` returns `totalWeight=95 count=2`; over-alloc 422 `weight_exceeds_100`. The AC-3 literal "Goal weights must total 100%" appears in no response.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — contained data-quality/validation gap on a primary flow: it cannot corrupt or leak data and the over-allocation half IS guarded, but it lets an appraisal proceed with goals that don't sum to 100% (defeating the weighted-scoring premise of the performance module) and the AC-3-mandated error is absent. Would be HIGH if downstream weighted-score math divides by an assumed-100 denominator (not verified this run). The single-goal API shape means a true server-side fix needs either a batch "save goals" transaction or a separate "submit/lock goals" step that asserts the exact-100 total.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### BUG-057 — NFR-4 optimistic concurrency is NOT surfaced to the client on goal edit: the cross-session lost-update the spec describes succeeds silently (no version token in the PUT contract)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #169, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-001-10
- **Title:** NFR-4 requires goal edits to be protected by optimistic concurrency so a stale second save is rejected (409) rather than silently overwriting. The `Goal.Version` xmin row-version IS mapped (`GoalConfiguration.cs:60`) and the service DOES catch `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` → 409 (`GoalService.cs:155-160`), but the **HTTP contract (`UpdateGoalRequest`) carries no client-supplied concurrency token** (no ETag / If-Match / version field — see `GoalDtos.cs:75-83`). Each PUT runs in its own scoped DbContext that re-reads the current row immediately before saving, so the xmin check can only ever fire for a race *inside one request's* read→save window — never for the "two sessions both loaded V1, both save" scenario NFR-4/TC-10 specify. Result: a stale second save returns **200** and silently clobbers the first session's change. The "lost update" NFR-4 was meant to prevent is reproducible.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `UpdateGoalRequest` has no version/rowversion/ETag property; `UpdateAsync` reads the goal fresh (`GoalService.cs:116`) then saves — the client's read-time version is never round-tripped, so EF compares the row's current xmin against itself (always equal). The guard is dead for the cross-request case it exists to cover.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** create a goal (weight 40) for John in the open cycle; PUT weight 45 ("S1edit") → **200** (xmin bumps); PUT weight 35 ("S2edit") representing a session that loaded the pre-S1 state → **200** (no 409); `SELECT` shows `weight=35, title='S2edit'` — S1's save was lost with no conflict surfaced.
- **Evidence:** both PUTs HTTP 200; final DB row = S2's values; zero `concurrency_conflict` returned. (A true in-request race was not engineered, but the user-facing TC-10 step-3 expectation of 409 on the stale save is unmet.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — data-integrity / lost-update gap on a low-frequency concurrent-edit path; the defense-in-depth mechanism is present at the DB layer but not wired to the API, so the NFR-4 guarantee the client relies on doesn't hold. Not a security/isolation issue. Fix needs the API to accept and forward the client's row-version (ETag/If-Match) into the update.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-097 — Goal create/update/delete are NOT written to the central `audit_logs` trail (FR-6) — only `created_by`/`updated_by` stamping + Serilog
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #154, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-001-01 (FR-6)
- **Title:** FR-6 requires the system to "log all goal create/update/delete operations in the **tenant audit trail**." After creating 3 goals, the `audit_logs` table has **no** rows with `resource_type='Goal'` (only auth/session events `concurrent_session_oldest_revoked` and `AuditLog.View` in the same window). Goal writes are traced only by the `AuditInterceptor` stamping `created_by`/`updated_by` on the row (verified: `created_by='manager@acme.test'`) plus a structured Serilog "Goal created/updated/deleted" line. There is no queryable, tenant-scoped audit record of the goal mutation — so the FR-6 audit trail is not satisfied via the platform's central audit facility.
- **Root cause (~90%, code + self-documented):** `GoalService` writes only `_logger.LogInformation(...)` + relies on `AuditInterceptor` (CreatedBy/UpdatedBy). The class XML-doc at `GoalService.cs:18-19` explicitly says audit "is provided by the AuditInterceptor (CreatedBy/UpdatedBy stamping on SaveChanges) plus structured Serilog entries" — i.e. by-design no central `audit_logs` write. Same recurring missing-central-audit theme as ISSUE-067 (attendance), ISSUE-069 (clock-out), ISSUE-071 (regularization), BUG-025/028/031 (leave config), BUG-010/018/022/023/024 (Core HR).
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** create 3 goals as manager → `SELECT action, event_type, resource_type FROM audit_logs WHERE tenant_id=acme AND created_at > now()-'15 min'` shows only session/login events, none with `resource_type='Goal'`. `SELECT created_by FROM goal …` shows `manager@acme.test` (partial traceability).
- **Evidence:** audit_logs window contains zero Goal rows; goal.created_by stamped. Serilog `hrm-20260626.log` has "Goal created. Id=… By=manager@acme.test".
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-6 is an explicit functional requirement and the central audit trail is the contracted mechanism (consistent with prior MED rating where a story explicitly mandates audit). Mitigated to not-HIGH by the `created_by`/`updated_by` stamping + Serilog providing partial, non-queryable traceability.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-098 — A not-yet-open (future) goal-setting window returns the *closed* message "The goal-setting window for this cycle has closed" instead of a "not yet open" message
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #365, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-001-08 (step 4, before-window case)
- **Title:** TC-08 step 4 attempts to create a goal in cycle QA-PRF001-FUTURE whose goal-setting window starts in the future. The request is correctly blocked (409 `goal_setting_closed`) — but the message is "The goal-setting window for this cycle has closed", which is inaccurate for a window that has **not opened yet**. The block behavior is correct; only the user-facing wording is wrong for the pre-window case.
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** `GoalService.GetOpenCycleAsync` (`GoalService.cs:333-335`) returns a single message whenever `!IsGoalSettingOpen(now)`, conflating "closed (past)" and "not yet open (future)". `AppraisalCycle.IsGoalSettingOpen` returns false for both before- and after-window instants.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** `POST .../goals` with `cycleId`=QA-PRF001-FUTURE (`019eff10-…-a3`, goal_setting_start in ~20 days) → 409 "The goal-setting window for this cycle has closed."
- **Evidence:** HTTP 409 `goal_setting_closed` with the "has closed" string for a future-start window.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/UX wording only; the security-relevant gate (no writes outside the window) is correct. Could mislead a manager into thinking they missed a deadline when the window simply hasn't opened.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-099 — `GET /api/v1/tenant/performance/goals/{id}` is a stub that returns HTTP 200 + empty body for ANY id (non-existent, foreign-tenant) instead of fetching the goal or 404
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #358, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-ISO-002 (step 4 IDOR arm)
- **Title:** The named route `GetGoalById` exists only so `CreatedAtRoute` can emit a Location header; its body is `=> Ok(ApiResponse.Ok())` (`GoalsController.cs:64-71`) — it never reads the goal. So `GET .../goals/{anyGuid}` (including a non-existent id, or a foreign-tenant goal id) returns **200** with an empty success envelope. The IDOR concern in ISO-002 step 4 is benign here (no goal data is ever returned, so nothing leaks), but a public endpoint that 200s for every id — including ones that don't exist or belong to another tenant — is a misleading contract and an authorization/existence-check gap on a route that advertises `404 NotFound` in its `[ProducesResponseType]`.
- **Root cause (~99%, code):** intentional stub, `GoalsController.cs:68-71` returns `Ok(ApiResponse.Ok())` unconditionally with a comment that clients should use the employee-goals endpoint.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** as acme manager, `GET .../goals/019f026d-029b-75e2-a208-5a99608b20f6` (a techoneglobal goal id) → **200** `{"success":true}` empty. Also returns 200 for a random/non-existent guid.
- **Evidence:** HTTP 200, body `{"success":true,"message":null,...}` for a foreign/arbitrary id; no goal data in the response (no leak).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth/contract hygiene only: no data is exposed (the body is empty), so there is no real IDOR. But the endpoint should 404 for unknown/foreign ids (or be removed from the public surface) to match its documented behavior and avoid a misleading 200.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-100 — Test cases (and likely the FE) target `/api/v1/performance/goals*`; the live API is `/api/v1/tenant/performance/*` (route prefix drift)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · OPEN
- **Layer:** TEST (and potentially FE)
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-001 · TC-PRF-001-01/02/03/06/11, TC-PRF-ISO-001/002 (all reference the un-prefixed path)
- **Title:** Every US-PRF-001 TC writes the endpoint as `POST /api/v1/performance/goals`, `GET /api/v1/performance/goals/team`, etc. The actual controller route is `[Route("api/v1/tenant/performance")]` with endpoints `POST .../goals`, `GET .../cycles/{cycleId}/team-dashboard`, `GET .../employees/{employeeId}/cycles/{cycleId}/goals` (`GoalsController.cs:21,33,49,77`). The TCs' paths and resource shapes (e.g. `goals/team?cycleId=`) do not match the live API. This is documentation/spec drift in the TC files; if any Angular performance service also omits the `/tenant/` prefix it would 404 (same class as the systemic FE↔BE `/tenant/` prefix mismatch already recorded — FE could not be verified this run as :4200 is down).
- **Root cause (~80%):** TCs authored from the user-story sketch (`/api/v1/performance/goals`) before the controller settled on the `/tenant/performance` prefix + employee/cycle path structure.
- **Reproduction steps:** compare any US-PRF-001 TC "Test Steps" endpoint to `GoalsController` `[Route]`/`[HttpGet]`/`[HttpPost]` attributes.
- **Evidence:** TC files say `/api/v1/performance/goals`; live 201/200 only at `/api/v1/tenant/performance/...` (all PASS responses above use the prefixed path).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — TEST/doc drift; does not affect product behavior. Flagged for traceability and as a FE-contract risk to verify when the frontend is reachable. Per REPORT-ONLY policy the TC objective/steps were NOT edited.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-PRF-001 goals surface (READ *and* WRITE leak for `.All` holders), not re-filed.**
> The goals endpoints resolve the tenant from `ITenantContext.TenantId` (subdomain / `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header) and drive the EF global query filter + `TenantInterceptor` off it, while `AuthorizeForEmployeeAsync` (`GoalService.cs:300-301`) grants access to any `Performance.SetGoal.All` holder **without** checking that the caller's JWT tenant matches the resolved tenant — the same missing `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId` invariant (root locus US-AUTH-007 / `TenantResolutionMiddleware`). Confirmed live today, both arms, on the goals surface:
> - **READ leak:** `tenantadmin@acme.test` (JWT tenant_id=acme `019ef3ba-…`, holds SetGoal.All) + header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `GET /api/v1/tenant/performance/employees/{tgEmp}/cycles/{tgCycle}/goals` → **HTTP 200** returning **techoneglobal's** goal ("TG-secret-goal", totalWeight 10). Contrast: same token + correct `acme` header returns only acme's goals. (TC-PRF-ISO-001 FAIL.)
> - **WRITE leak:** same acme TenantAdmin token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `POST .../goals` for the techoneglobal employee → **HTTP 201**, and the persisted row's `tenant_id = techoneglobal` (`019ef3c3-…`) — a foreign-tenant goal written using an acme-issued token. **The probe row was hard-deleted immediately; ZERO residue left in techoneglobal.** (TC-PRF-ISO-003 FAIL.)
> - **Self-protected arms (NOT a leak):** the `Performance.SetGoal.Team` **manager** path is self-protecting — acme manager token + techoneglobal header → create / team-dashboard → **403 `no_employee_record`** (the manager's UserId resolves to no employee in the foreign tenant, `GoalService.cs:306-309`), same pattern as the leave/attendance employee-self-resolve surfaces. And within the **correct** subdomain, write isolation is CLEAN: body-injected `tenant_id` is ignored (server-derived = acme), foreign `employee_id` → 404 `employee_not_found`, foreign `cycle_id` → 404 `cycle_not_found` (TC-PRF-ISO-003 in-tenant arms all PASS).
> So the cross-tenant exposure on this surface fires specifically through an `.All`-holding actor (TenantAdmin/HR) over the spoofable header. NFR-2's stated mechanism (PostgreSQL RLS on the Goals table) is NOT implemented — isolation is EF query filters keyed off the resolved tenant, which is correct *only* when the header matches the token. See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]], the root-locus confirmation at US-AUTH-007, and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave/Attendance/Recruitment module reports for the systemic record.
