## US-REC-002 — Applicant Submits Application with Resume Upload (API-layer pass 2026-06-26)

### BUG-058 — Resume MIME validation trusts the client-supplied Content-Type only (no content/magic-byte sniffing); a Windows .exe renamed to .pdf is accepted and stored (AC-2/BR-4/FR-1 content-based validation unmet)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · ✅ RESOLVED (already fixed in a prior PR; ledger was stale — verified 2026-07-16)
- **Resolution:** `HRM.Application/Common/Security/FileSignatureValidator.cs` sniffs the real leading "magic bytes"
  (PDF `%PDF`, DOCX/OOXML `PK\x03\x04`, DOC/OLE `D0CF11E0…`, plus image types) and is **fail-closed** (an unknown/
  unmappable declared type is rejected). It is wired into `ApplicantService.SubmitAsync` (before the virus scan):
  a spoofed type → **400 `invalid_file_type`**. Same seam reused by the employee-document + self-assessment upload
  paths. Tested by `FileSignatureValidatorTests` (21 arms, incl. `FileSignature_MzExe_Rejected_BUG058` — the exact
  renamed-`.exe` case — PNG-claimed-PDF, blank/unmapped-type, and correct-bytes-OK), all green. No further work.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-002 · TC-REC-002-04 (S1/S5 content-based MIME validation)
- **Title:** AC-2/BR-4/FR-1 and TC-REC-002-04 require the resume MIME type to be validated **from the actual file content (magic bytes / sniffed content type)**, not the filename extension or the client-declared `Content-Type`. The submit pipeline validates **only** the client-supplied `IFormFile.ContentType` against the allow-list (PDF/DOCX/DOC). A Windows PE executable (`MZ` magic bytes) renamed to `malware.pdf` and uploaded with a spoofed `Content-Type: application/pdf` is **accepted (HTTP 201), stored, and an applicant row is created**. There is no compensating control because the virus scanner is a no-op stub (see ISSUE-101), so an executable can be both uploaded and persisted to recruiter-downloadable storage.
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** `SubmitApplicationValidator` rule `RuleFor(x => x.ResumeContentType).Must(ct => AllowedResumeMimeTypes.Contains(ct))` (`SubmitApplicationValidator.cs:67-69`) and the defensive re-check in `ApplicantService.SubmitAsync` (`ApplicantService.cs:64-65`) both test the caller-provided `resume.ContentType` (bound straight from the multipart `Content-Type` header in `CareersController.Apply` / `ApplicantsController.SubmitInternal`). Nothing reads the stream's leading bytes. The disallowed-by-declared-type path (e.g. `image/png`) IS correctly rejected, but it is trivially bypassed by declaring `application/pdf`.
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous, acme subdomain. Create `malware.pdf` whose bytes start with `MZ\x90\x00...` (a fake PE). `POST /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{openVacancyId}/apply` (X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme) multipart with `resume=@malware.pdf;type=application/pdf`, FirstName/LastName/Email set → **HTTP 201**, `applicationReferenceNumber: APP-2026-0003`, applicant persisted, file stored under `recruitment/{vacancyId}/{applicantId}/{uuid}.pdf`. Contrast: the same endpoint with `photo.png;type=image/png` → 400 "Resume must be a PDF, DOC, or DOCX file." (rejection is purely by declared type).
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** malware.pdf submit → `{"success":true,...,"applicationReferenceNumber":"APP-2026-0003"}` HTTP 201; Serilog shows `Virus scan SKIPPED (stub scanner). FileName=malware.pdf` then `File uploaded to local storage ... .pdf` then `Application submitted (Applied)`. The png submit → 400 `resume_type_not_allowed`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the stored file is renamed to a server-side UUID and is never executed by the backend, so this is not RCE; the real exposure is malware/disguised-content distribution to recruiters who download the resume (combined with ISSUE-101 the scan does not catch it either) and a bypass of the BR-4 allow-list intent. Defense-in-depth gap with a real but contained blast radius. Would be HIGH if resumes were rendered/opened automatically server-side.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-101 — Virus scanning (FR-3/NFR-4) is a no-op stub: every file (incl. EICAR) passes and is persisted; "scan before storing the URL" is not actually enforced
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #177, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-002 · TC-REC-002-10 (S1 EICAR reject / S3 clean accept)
- **Title:** FR-3 ("perform virus scanning (ClamAV or cloud service) on uploaded files before persisting the storage URL") and NFR-4 require an infected upload to be rejected with no row/blob created. The registered `IVirusScanner` is `AllowWithLogVirusScanner`, which returns `VirusScanResult.Clean()` for **every** file and emits a Warning log. An EICAR-signature `eicar.pdf` is **accepted (HTTP 201)** and stored. The scan IS invoked in the correct order (before persistence) and the seam is real + DI-wired + visibly logged — but no actual malware detection occurs. (FR-4 EXIF-strip is correctly N/A: resumes are PDF/DOC(X), documented in `ApplicantService.cs:124-125`.)
- **Root cause (~99%, code):** `AllowWithLogVirusScanner.ScanAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/AllowWithLogVirusScanner.cs:21-32`) always `return Task.FromResult(VirusScanResult.Clean())`. Class XML-doc explicitly marks it a stub: "TODO(prod): Wire ClamAV ... This stub exists as a real seam for DI — it is NOT a silent no-op." So this is a **documented Phase-1 deferral**, not a hidden defect — but FR-3/NFR-4 are listed as functional/NFR requirements (not in the US §10 out-of-scope list, which only defers resume parsing/AI screening), so the requirement is unmet.
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous, acme. Build `eicar.pdf` carrying the standard `EICAR-STANDARD-ANTIVIRUS-TEST-FILE` signature. `POST /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{openVacancyId}/apply` with `resume=@eicar.pdf;type=application/pdf` → **HTTP 201**, `APP-2026-0011`, applicant + blob persisted.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** eicar submit → 201; Serilog `Virus scan SKIPPED (stub scanner). FileName=eicar.pdf` immediately followed by `File uploaded to local storage` and `Application submitted (Applied)` for the same RequestId.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — explicit requirement (FR-3/NFR-4) is functionally unmet and there is no compensating control (pairs with BUG-058 so a disguised executable is neither type-sniffed nor scanned); contained because files are UUID-renamed and not auto-executed. Documented-deferred, so an ISSUE rather than a BUG. Raise to HIGH if malware scanning is a contracted Phase-1 deliverable.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-102 — Public application endpoint has NO rate limiting or CAPTCHA: 15 rapid anonymous submits all succeed (S10 spam/bot constraint unmet; unauthenticated write+disk-write DoS vector)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #157, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-002 · TC-REC-002-11 (S2 burst / S3 CAPTCHA)
- **Title:** The US constraint S10 (and TC-REC-002-11) require the anonymous public application form to be protected from automated abuse via rate limiting and/or CAPTCHA. `POST /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{id}/apply` is `[AllowAnonymous]` with no throttling middleware, no per-IP limit, and no CAPTCHA token check. A burst of 15 rapid submissions (distinct emails) from one client **all returned HTTP 201** — zero 429s. Each accepted request creates an `applicant` DB row and writes a resume file to disk, so the endpoint is an unauthenticated amplification vector for DB-row + disk-space spam (and confirmation-notification fan-out).
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `CareersController.Apply` is `[AllowAnonymous]` and no ASP.NET rate-limiter / CAPTCHA filter is applied to it (no `[EnableRateLimiting]`, no captcha validation in the command/handler). The duplicate-email check (BR-1) only blocks the *same* email re-applying to the *same* vacancy; distinct emails (or distinct vacancies) are unbounded.
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous, acme. Loop `POST /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{openVacancyId}/apply` 15× with `Email=burst-1@…` … `burst-15@…` and a valid PDF → all 15 return HTTP 201 (`APP-2026-0012` … `APP-2026-0026`).
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** burst result line `201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201 201` (no 429). 15 new acme applicant rows created by the burst.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — no auth means anyone on the internet can flood a tenant's pipeline with junk applicants and fill disk with uploaded files; contained to the recruitment data set and gated by the vacancy having to be Open, but it is a real availability/abuse gap on a public surface (and S10 names it explicitly). Not CRIT because it doesn't breach isolation or corrupt other data.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-103 — Applicant free-text fields (name, cover letter) are stored verbatim with no server-side sanitization, while the sibling vacancy Description IS sanitized (stored-XSS / inconsistency)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #358, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-002 · TC-REC-002-11 (S4 anti-XSS input sanitization)
- **Title:** TC-REC-002-11 expects free-text inputs (cover letter, name) to be sanitized/escaped so an injected payload is not stored to be executed later. Submitting `FirstName=<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` and `CoverLetter=<script>alert(1)</script>` stores both **verbatim** on the applicant record (only trimmed). By contrast `VacancyService` runs `_sanitizer.Sanitize(description)` on the vacancy description — so the codebase HAS an HTML sanitizer, but `ApplicantService.SubmitAsync` does not apply it to applicant fields. This is a stored-XSS risk if any consumer (recruiter admin UI, exported report, notification email body) renders the field as HTML; Angular interpolation escapes by default, so it is mitigated unless the FE uses `[innerHTML]` or the value is reused in a non-Angular context (email/PDF/CSV).
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `ApplicantService.SubmitAsync` sets `FirstName = input.FirstName.Trim()`, `CoverLetter = ... .Trim()` etc. (`ApplicantService.cs:145-149`) with no sanitizer call; the `IHtmlSanitizer` seam used by `VacancyService` is not injected/used here.
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous, acme. `POST /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{id}/apply` with `--form-string 'FirstName=<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'` and `--form-string 'CoverLetter=<script>alert(1)</script>'` → 201. Read back via recruiter `GET /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies/{id}/applicants/{applicantId}` → `firstName: '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'`, `coverLetter: '<script>alert(1)</script>'` (unescaped).
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** stored values returned verbatim by the applicant-detail API: `firstName: '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'`, `coverLetter: '<script>alert(1)</script>'`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — Angular's default escaping mitigates the primary admin-UI render path, so this is a defense-in-depth / consistency gap (the product sanitizes vacancy HTML but not applicant HTML) rather than a confirmed live XSS; elevate if the resume/applicant data is rendered as HTML in emails, PDFs, or any `[innerHTML]` binding.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-104 — Application submission writes NO `audit_logs` entry (only a Serilog line); the create event is unauditable in the tenant audit trail (same systemic missing-audit theme as BUG-055/025/028)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #154, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-002 · TC-REC-002-01 (AC-1 application saved/traceable)
- **Title:** A successful application submission emits a Serilog `Application submitted (Applied)` INF line and fires the FR-5/FR-7 notification seams, but writes **no `audit_logs` row**. `ApplicantService` only writes `audit_logs` on *stage changes* (`WriteStageChangeAuditLog`, US-REC-003) — the initial Applied creation is not recorded in the queryable tenant audit trail. US-REC-002 does not list an explicit audit AC (unlike US-REC-001 FR-7), so this is a consistency/traceability gap rather than a spec violation, but it mirrors the systemic "missing-audit-on-writes" theme flagged across Recruitment (BUG-055), Leave (BUG-025/028/031) and Core-HR.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `ApplicantService.SubmitAsync` (`ApplicantService.cs:139-191`) adds the `Applicant` + fires notifications + logs to Serilog but never inserts an `AuditLog`. The `AuditInterceptor` stamps `CreatedBy`/`CreatedAt` columns, but for an anonymous public submit `CreatedBy` is null (no user), so even the column-stamp carries no actor.
- **Reproduction steps:** Submit any application (TC-01 flow) → 201. As acme admin `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs?action=...` finds no application-received/applicant-created entry; the only trace is the `hrm-<date>.log` Serilog line.
- **Evidence (live, acme, today):** Serilog `Application submitted (Applied). ApplicantId=019f026c-5108-… Ref=APP-2026-0001` present; no corresponding `audit_logs` row (applicant-create is not in the audit-write path — confirmed by reading `ApplicantService`, which only audits stage moves).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — no explicit AC requires it for US-REC-002 and the action is captured in structured Serilog + the row's own `applied_at`/`source`; the gap is that the application-received event is invisible in the product's queryable audit trail. Consistency issue, no data/security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-REC-002 applicant surface (READ + RESUME-DOWNLOAD + WRITE all confirmed), not re-filed.**
> Same root mechanism as the documented locus (US-AUTH-007 / `TenantResolutionMiddleware`): authorization uses the JWT's tenant/permissions while the data context (`ITenantContext.TenantId` → EF global query filter) is resolved from the request **subdomain/`X-Tenant-Subdomain` header**, and no guard rejects token-tenant ≠ header-resolved-tenant. **Unlike the US-REC-001 vacancy probe (which was read-only against EMPTY comparison tenants), this run produced a CONCRETE cross-tenant LEAK and a CONCRETE cross-tenant WRITE on the applicant surface:**
> - **READ leak (TC-REC-ISO-005):** with an **acme JWT (`tenantadmin@acme.test`, no techoneglobal membership) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`**, `GET /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies/{tgVacancyId}/applicants` returned **HTTP 200 with techoneglobal's applicant PII** (`TGSecret Applicant`, `tg-secret@techone.test`, ref APP-2026-0001) — `Recruitment.View`-gated, authz passed on the acme token, data scoped to the header tenant.
> - **RESUME leak (TC-REC-ISO-008):** same token+header, `GET /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{tgApplicantId}/resume` returned **HTTP 200** — the other tenant's resume blob was downloaded (the storage key is read from the header-resolved tenant context).
> - **WRITE breach (TC-REC-ISO-007):** same acme token + techoneglobal header, `POST /api/v1/recruitment/vacancies/{tgVacancyId}/applicants` (internal submit, with a real techoneglobal employee id) created an applicant (`AcmeIntruder`, ref APP-2026-0002) **stamped with techoneglobal's tenant_id** and a resume blob under techoneglobal's path — a write into another tenant by a user with no membership there.
> **This is NOT a new finding — it is the same BUG-003 mechanism (token vs header), simply demonstrated with non-empty cross-tenant data so the leak/write actually materialized.** Within the matching (header=token) acme context, isolation is CLEAN (every list/get/download/submit scopes to acme only). AC-5's claim of "PostgreSQL RLS enforces tenant isolation" is NOT met: this codebase uses EF query filters keyed off the spoofable header, not RLS. **All cross-tenant probe writes were REVERTED** — the seeded techoneglobal vacancy + both probe applicants (`tg-secret`, `acme-intruder`) + stage history were hard-deleted via psql; techoneglobal recruitment tables verified back to 0 rows (prior state). See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]] and the prior module reports for the systemic record.

## US-PRF-002 — Employee Self-Rates Against Goals (run 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API layer)

> Routes: `/api/v1/tenant/performance/self-assessments/*` — `GET cycles/{cycleId}/me`, `PUT draft`, `POST submit`. All require `Performance.Read.Self`; the service self-resolves the CALLING employee (UserId→employee) and tenant-filters every read/write, so an employee only ever touches their own record (NFR-2). Window gate (BR-1/AC-4)→409 `self_assessment_closed`; all-goals-rated+comment≥20→422 `incomplete_ratings`/`comment_too_short`; submitted-lock (BR-3)→409 `already_submitted`; weighted score = Σ(rating×weight)/Σweight rounded 2dp (FR-4). Hangfire reminder job `performance-self-assessment-reminders` (7/3/1-day thresholds, excludes submitters, log-only seam). Personas: `employee@acme.test`→John Doe (EMP-0001, 3 goals seeded in QA-SA-OPEN). 19 TCs executed: 12 PASS / 1 FAIL / 6 BLOCKED. **Self-assessment isolation is CLEAN — BUG-003 does NOT extend here** (the surface admits only `Read.Self` + always self-resolves the employee, so a spoofed `X-Tenant-Subdomain` yields 403 `no_employee_record`, not a leak — unlike the goals surface where `.All` holders bypassed it).

### BUG-242 — Submitted self-assessment cannot be reopened: the manager/HR reopen flow (BR-3 / AC-2 "unless reopened") is not implemented, so a submitted assessment is permanently locked
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #175, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Note:** renumbered from BUG-059 on 2026-07-05 (ledger ID-hygiene) — the ID collided with the US-REC-003/004 "Hired is terminal" BUG-059. This US-PRF-002 self-assessment-reopen occurrence took the fresh ID; its fix is PR #175 (regression TC-PRF-004-16). The recruitment finding keeps BUG-059 (fix PR #174).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-002 · TC-PRF-002-13
- **Title:** AC-2 ("prevents further edits **unless reopened**") and BR-3 ("locked **unless the manager or HR explicitly reopens it**") require a reopen capability. The lock half works (employee submit/edit after submission → 409 `already_submitted`), but there is **no reopen endpoint, command, or service method anywhere** — `SelfAssessmentController` exposes only GetMine/draft/submit, and the `SelfAssessmentStatus` enum has only `Draft`/`Submitted`. Consequently a submitted self-assessment is **irreversibly locked**: neither a manager, HR, nor any role can return it to editable, so an employee who submits with a mistake has no remediation path. TC-002-13 steps 2-4 (employee-cannot-reopen / manager-or-HR-can-reopen / re-submit after reopen) are unexecutable because the capability does not exist.
- **Root cause (~98%, code + self-documented):** no reopen route in `SelfAssessmentController.cs`; `grep -i reopen` across the self-assessment service/interface/commands returns nothing. The `SelfAssessmentStatus` enum doc (`src/backend/HRM.Domain/Enums/SelfAssessmentStatus.cs`) states the locked status holds "unless a manager/HR reopens it (BR-3 — **reopen flow is a later story**)" — i.e. deliberately deferred, leaving the documented AC-2/BR-3 behavior unmet today.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** submit John's self-assessment in QA-SA-OPEN → status Submitted, locked. Any subsequent `POST submit`/`PUT draft` (as employee) → 409 `already_submitted`. There is no endpoint for a manager/HR to reopen — none exists in the controller or service.
- **Evidence:** lock confirmed (409 `already_submitted` on both submit and draft post-submission); no reopen route (404 would result; the route simply isn't defined); enum comment explicitly defers the reopen flow.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a primary-flow gap (a wrongly-submitted self-assessment cannot be corrected, blocking the documented revise-and-resubmit path) and AC-2/BR-3 are explicitly unmet, but it is a deferred-feature gap rather than a data/security defect, and the protective lock itself works correctly. Escalate to HIGH if the appraisal cycle depends on employees being able to revise after a manager requests changes.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-105 — File-attachment evidence (FR-5/NFR-4) has a data model but NO API: no upload/list/delete endpoint, so attachments cannot be added at all
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #177, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-002 · TC-PRF-002-10 (FR-5 limits), TC-PRF-002-11 (NFR-4 scan/storage)
- **Title:** FR-5 ("file attachments per goal, max 5 files, 10MB each") and NFR-4 (virus scan + tenant-scoped storage) describe an evidence-upload feature. The `SelfAssessmentAttachment` entity, its EF configuration, and the read-side `SelfAssessmentAttachmentDto` all exist, but there is **no upload/list/delete endpoint** on `SelfAssessmentController` (no `IFormFile` action, no attachment route) and the save/submit request DTO (`SaveSelfAssessmentRequest`) has no file field. So an employee cannot attach evidence at all — the 5-file/10MB limits (TC-10), the virus-scan seam, the tenant-scoped storage path, and cross-tenant file retrieval (TC-11) are untestable because the capability is unimplemented at the API.
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** controller exposes only GetMine/draft/submit; attachments appear only on the read DTO. The attachment write path was scaffolded in the domain model but never wired to an endpoint (likely deferred with the file-management/document infra dependency named in §9/§10).
- **Reproduction steps:** inspect `SelfAssessmentController.cs` — no upload action; `grep -i "attachment|upload|IFormFile"` on the controller returns nothing. `SaveSelfAssessmentRequest` (`SelfAssessmentDtos.cs:76`) carries only `CycleId` + `Items` (rating/achievement/comment), no files.
- **Evidence:** TC-10/TC-11 BLOCKED (feature-not-wired) — no endpoint to exercise; attachments DTO is read-only and always empty in responses.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-5 is a named functional requirement that is entirely absent at the API (not merely partial), so a documented capability is missing; contained to a not-yet-built feature with a clear dependency (document-management infra), no data/security risk. Becomes HIGH if evidence attachments are a contracted Phase-1 deliverable.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-106 — Self-assessment save/submit/reminder write NO `audit_logs` entry (only Serilog); the create/submit events are unauditable in the tenant audit trail
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #154, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-002 · TC-PRF-002-01 (submit), TC-PRF-002-05 (draft)
- **Title:** A self-assessment submit (a material performance-record event) and draft saves produce only a structured Serilog line ("Self-assessment submitted/saved (draft)…") plus `created_by`/`updated_by` row stamping — no row in the central `audit_logs` table. The same recurring missing-central-audit theme as the goals surface (ISSUE-097) and the attendance/leave/recruitment modules (ISSUE-067/069/071, BUG-025/028, ISSUE-104). US-PRF-002 doesn't have an explicit FR-6-style audit requirement (unlike US-PRF-001), so this is an ISSUE rather than a spec-violation BUG, but submission of a self-rating that feeds the final appraisal score should be in the queryable audit trail.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `SelfAssessmentService.UpsertAsync` writes only `_logger.LogInformation(...)`; no `IAuditLogger`/audit_logs insert. Audit relies on the `AuditInterceptor` created_by/updated_by stamping.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** submit John's self-assessment → `SELECT * FROM audit_logs WHERE tenant_id=acme AND resource_type='SelfAssessment' AND created_at > now()-'15 min'` → 0 rows; Serilog `hrm-20260626.log` has the "Self-assessment submitted" line.
- **Evidence:** no SelfAssessment rows in audit_logs after submit; Serilog line present; row created_by stamped.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — consistent with the module-wide audit-gap rating; the submit event materially affects the appraisal but is only traceable via logs, not the audit trail. No data/security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-107 — Closing-window message is used for a NOT-YET-OPEN self-assessment window: future cycle returns "The self-assessment period for this cycle has ended" (wording inaccurate for the before-window case)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (PR #365, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-002 · TC-PRF-002-07 (step 3, before-window case)
- **Title:** Submitting/saving in a cycle whose self-assessment window has not yet opened is correctly blocked (409 `self_assessment_closed`) but returns "The self-assessment period for this cycle has **ended**" — inaccurate for a window that hasn't started. Same pattern as the goal-module wording issue (ISSUE-098): `SelfAssessmentService.UpsertAsync` (`:93-95`) and `AppraisalCycle.IsSelfAssessmentOpen` return a single closed message for both before- and after-window instants. The block is correct; only the message is wrong for the pre-window case. (The exact AC-4 text "The self-assessment period for this cycle has ended" IS correct for the genuinely-closed case — verified.)
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** single failure message for `!IsSelfAssessmentOpen(now)` regardless of before-vs-after; `IsSelfAssessmentOpen` returns false symmetrically.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** `POST submit` with `cycleId`=QA-SA-FUTURE (self-assessment window ~20 days out) → 409 `self_assessment_closed` "…has ended."
- **Evidence:** HTTP 409 with the "has ended" string for a future-start window.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/UX wording; the gate (no writes outside the window) is correct. Twin of ISSUE-098 on the self-assessment surface.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — DOES NOT extend to the US-PRF-002 self-assessment surface (CLEAN), recorded for completeness.**
> Every self-assessment endpoint admits only `Performance.Read.Self` and resolves the actor via `UserId → employee in the resolved tenant` (`SelfAssessmentService.GetCurrentEmployeeAsync`). Demonstrated live: an acme employee token (or acme TenantAdmin token) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` on `GET .../self-assessments/cycles/{id}/me` → **403 `no_employee_record`** (the caller's UserId has no employee in the foreign tenant) — NOT a 200 with foreign data. This is the SAME self-protecting pattern as the leave-apply/clock-out/regularization surfaces, and the OPPOSITE of the goals surface (where a `.All`-holding TenantAdmin/HR bypassed the employee-link check → BUG-003 read+write leak). Within the correct subdomain, write isolation is also clean: body-injected `tenant_id` ignored (stored row = acme), foreign `goal_id` → 400 `unknown_goal`, foreign `cycle_id` → 404 `cycle_not_found`. No cross-tenant read/write was achievable on this surface; no probe data was written to techoneglobal. (This is why TC-PRF-ISO-005/006/007 PASS.)

> **Route-prefix drift (ISSUE-100 class) applies to US-PRF-002 too, not re-filed.** The TCs reference `.../self-assessments/{id}` and `.../employees/{id}/self-assessment?cycleId=` style paths; the live API is `GET/PUT/POST /api/v1/tenant/performance/self-assessments/{cycles/{id}/me | draft | submit}` only (no by-id or by-employeeId read route exists — which is why the TC-002-09 IDOR-by-id arms return 404 and cross-employee read is structurally impossible). Recorded under ISSUE-100; TC objective/steps were NOT edited (REPORT-ONLY).

### BUG-059 — BR-6 "Hired is terminal" is NOT enforced and the convert-to-employee seam never fires: an applicant can be moved OUT of Hired (forward to Rejected or backward to Offer), and moving INTO Hired triggers no US-REC-010 conversion signal
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #174, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-003 · TC-REC-003-09 (BR-6)
- **Title:** US-REC-003 BR-6 states the "Hired" stage is **terminal** (no further forward transition) and that moving an applicant to Hired **triggers the convert-to-employee workflow** (US-REC-010). Neither half is implemented. Live: a Hired applicant was moved Hired→Rejected (HTTP 200) AND Hired→Offer (HTTP 200) — Hired is freely exitable in both directions. Moving Offer→Hired logged only the generic stage-move + a stage-changed notification; **no convert-to-employee trigger/signal/queue entry** is emitted. The single hard guard in `ApplyStageMove` is the same-stage no-op (409) and the Closed/Cancelled-vacancy block — there is no terminal-stage rule and no conversion seam.
- **Root cause (~97%, code):** `ApplicantService.ApplyStageMove` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/ApplicantService.cs:603-696`) has no branch rejecting a move whose `fromStage == ApplicantStage.Hired`, and `MoveStageAsync`/`ApplyStageMove` contain **zero references** to any conversion service (`grep "Convert|Conversion|IApplicantConversion" ApplicantService.cs` → no matches). `ApplicantConversionService` exists but is reachable only via the separate manual US-REC-010 endpoint; the Hired transition does not call/queue it.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** seed applicant at Offer → `POST /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{id}/move-stage {"toStage":"Hired"}` → 200 (only a headcount warning, no conversion). Then on a Hired applicant: `POST .../move-stage {"toStage":"Rejected","reason":"x","rejectionReason":"Other"}` → 200, stage now Rejected; and `{"toStage":"Offer","reason":"rescind"}` → 200, stage now Offer. All persisted with history rows.
- **Evidence:** three HTTP 200 responses (Offer→Hired, Hired→Rejected, Hired→Offer) with successful `fromStage:"Hired"` results; Serilog `hrm-20260626.log` lines `From="Hired", To="Offer"` / `From="Offer", To="Hired"` with no conversion log; `grep` of ApplicantService.cs shows no conversion reference.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — workflow/data-integrity gap, not a security/isolation breach: "Hired" loses its terminal guarantee (a hired candidate can silently be reverted, and an unhired/odd state reached), and the documented hire→employee handoff (BR-6 → US-REC-010) is not auto-initiated, so a recruiter must remember a separate manual step. Contained to the recruitment domain; no cross-tenant/PII exposure. Not HIGH because the move itself is audited and reversible and US-REC-010 conversion is still callable manually; not LOW because a Must-Have story's named business rule is wholly unmet.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

### ISSUE-244 — Applicant detail leaks the raw resume blob storage key (`resumeStorageKey`) in the embedded profile DTO, partially undercutting NFR-5 ("no raw blob path exposed")
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (stale-fixed — verified in code; LOW-tier sweep 2026-07-18)
- **Note:** renumbered from ISSUE-105 on 2026-07-05 (ledger ID-hygiene) — the ID collided with the US-PRF-002 self-assessment attachment-API ISSUE-105 (fix PR #177). This US-REC-003 resume-blob-key occurrence took the fresh ID.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-003 · TC-REC-003-03 (AC-3/NFR-5)
- **Title:** US-REC-003 NFR-5 requires the resume be served via a signed/short-lived reference with "no raw blob path exposed to the browser." The pipeline detail endpoint correctly returns a relative authenticated `resumeDownloadUrl` (`/api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{id}/resume`) instead of a blob URL — **but** the `ApplicantDetailDto.Profile` (the embedded `ApplicantDto`) still serializes `resumeStorageKey` (e.g. `recruitment/{vacancyId}/{applicantId}/{uuid}.pdf`), exposing the internal tenant-scoped storage path in the same response. (Pre-existing on the `ApplicantDto`/US-REC-002 surface; surfaces again here because the detail panel reuses that DTO.)
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** `ApplicantService.GetDetailAsync` (`:386-397`) sets `Profile = ToDto(applicant, vacancyTitle)`, and `ToDto` (`:834-855`) maps `ResumeStorageKey = a.ResumeStorageKey`. The detail-specific `ResumeFileName`/`ResumeDownloadUrl` fields correctly hide the path, but the nested profile object still carries it.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** `GET /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{acmeApplicantId}/detail` (acme manager token) → response `data.profile.resumeStorageKey` = `recruitment/019f027e-…/r1/r.pdf`.
- **Evidence:** detail JSON `profile.resumeStorageKey` populated with the relative blob path while `data.resumeDownloadUrl` is the safe route.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth/info-exposure nit, not an exploitable leak: the path is tenant-relative (not a public/signed URL), reaching the file still requires the authenticated tenant-scoped `/resume` route (which is EF-filtered and 404s cross-tenant — verified), and the value is only returned to already-authorized `Recruitment.View` holders. But it contradicts NFR-5's "no raw blob path" intent and should be omitted from the wire DTO.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-REC-003 pipeline stage-move (WRITE) + stage-history surface, not re-filed.**
> The pipeline board/detail reads and the move-stage / bulk-move WRITES all resolve the tenant from `ITenantContext.TenantId` (populated by `TenantResolutionMiddleware` from the `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header / subdomain) and drive the EF global query filter + `TenantInterceptor` stamping off it, while authorization uses the JWT — and the middleware never rejects **token-tenant ≠ header-resolved-tenant**. Demonstrated live with NON-empty cross-tenant data so the write actually materialized: a throwaway applicant was seeded in **techoneglobal** (Tenant B), then an **acme JWT (`tenantadmin@acme.test`, holds `Recruitment.Manage`) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`** on `POST /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{tgApplicantId}/move-stage {"toStage":"Screening"}` returned **HTTP 200** and **moved techoneglobal's applicant** Applied→Screening — writing an `applicant_stage_history` row stamped with **techoneglobal's tenant_id** but `changed_by_user_id` = the acme user. An acme-authenticated principal thus mutated another tenant's recruitment data and the in-module audit trail attributes it under the foreign tenant. This is the same BUG-003 mechanism (root locus US-AUTH-007 / `TenantResolutionMiddleware`), now confirmed as a **cross-tenant WRITE** on the stage-management surface (the READ arm was also confirmed: with matched header=token, acme ids 404 under a techoneglobal context — ISO-009 PASS — but the spoofed-context WRITE is honoured — ISO-011 FAIL). **Within the matching (header=token) acme context, isolation is CLEAN** — every board/detail/move/bulk scopes to acme only; a bulk-move that includes a foreign applicant id under the acme context 404s (all-or-nothing). AC-5's claim of "PostgreSQL RLS prevents cross-tenant leakage" is NOT met: this codebase uses EF query filters keyed off the spoofable header, not RLS. **The cross-tenant probe WRITE was REVERTED** — the seeded techoneglobal vacancy + applicant + the stage-history row it produced were hard-deleted via psql and techoneglobal's recruitment tables verified back to 0 rows (prior state). Affects TC-REC-ISO-011. See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]] and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave/Attendance/US-REC-001/US-REC-002 module reports for the systemic record.

---

> **US-REC-004 (Move Applicant Through Pipeline Stages) -- REPORT-ONLY API run (curl + JWT) on `acme` (tenant `019ef3ba-ffb7-7eec-b24f-7ad806ca1cb9`), 2026-06-26.** FE :4200 down + platform-bound -> no UI/a11y TCs in scope. **Real route for stage moves:** `POST /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{applicantId}/move-stage` (body `{toStage, reason, notes, rejectionReason}`; toStage/rejectionReason accept enum name or int) + `POST /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/bulk-move-stage`; reads `GET .../applicants/{id}/detail` (timeline) and `GET .../vacancies/{id}/pipeline`. **Real permissions** (differ from TC text Recruitment.Manage.All / Read.All): all writes = `Recruitment.Manage`, reads = `Recruitment.View`. The TCs assume `PATCH .../stage`; the live verb/path is `POST .../move-stage`. **RejectionReason enum** = NotQualified/PositionFilled/Withdrew/Other. **Solid:** full forward pipeline + 4 history rows (each from/to/changed_by/changed_at/tenant stamped); structured rejection-reason validation (no-reason 400, reason-only-no-dropdown 400, out-of-enum string/int 400, valid -> stored as queryable enum); reject from every active stage; backward move (Manage-gated + mandatory reason, regressive history row); Closed/Cancelled vacancy blocks advancement but allows rejection; headcount-filled soft warning on Offer/Hired; Offer-scorecard soft warning; non-Manage -> 403; stage-change audit_logs written (recruitment.applicant.stage_changed, summary carries from->to + reason, tenant-scoped); transition latency P95 ~24 ms (NFR-1 <=800 ms) with stage+history in one SaveChangesAsync transaction (atomic). **Hired-not-terminal + no conversion seam = already-filed BUG-059** (TC-REC-004-07 and TC-REC-004-03 step 6 map to it -- re-confirmed live: Hired->Offer/Screening/Rejected all 200). Findings BUG-060, ISSUE-108/109/110 below.

### BUG-060 -- BR-2 not enforced: a Rejected applicant can be advanced FORWARD directly (Rejected->Interview/Offer) with only a reason, instead of being required to first reactivate back to an active stage
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #174, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-004 · TC-REC-004-06 (BR-2, step 1)
- **Title:** BR-2 / TC-REC-004-06 step 1 require that a Rejected applicant CANNOT be advanced to a forward stage directly -- they must first be reactivated (moved BACK to an active stage) by a Manage user, after which normal forward transitions resume. Live, a Rejected applicant was moved straight Rejected->Interview (HTTP 200) (and Rejected->Offer is likewise reachable), skipping the reactivation-to-active-stage step and bypassing the intervening Screening/Interview gates entirely.
- **Root cause (~90%, code):** ApplicantService.ApplyStageMove (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/ApplicantService.cs:603-696) defines isReactivation = fromStage == Rejected && toStage != Rejected and only requires that such a move carry a reason (:631). It does NOT constrain the reactivation target to an active/adjacent stage, nor block a forward jump out of Rejected -- any Rejected->{Screening|Interview|Offer|Hired} with a reason is accepted. There is no "rejected applicants cannot advance without first reactivating to an active stage" rule.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** seed applicant, move Applied->Screening->Rejected (reason + rejectionReason). Then POST /api/v1/recruitment/applicants/{id}/move-stage {"toStage":"Interview","reason":"jump"} -> HTTP 200, stage now Interview, no prior reactivation to Screening required.
- **Evidence:** HTTP 200 with data.fromStage:"Rejected", data.toStage:"Interview"; Serilog hrm-20260626.log From="Rejected", To="Interview". Code path has no active-stage-target guard.
- **Severity rationale:** MED -- workflow-integrity gap, not a security/isolation breach: the move is Manage-gated, reason-required and audited, so it is controlled, but a rejected candidate can be jumped straight to Offer/Hired with no re-screen, silently defeating BR-2's reactivation control and the stage gates. Contained to the recruitment domain. Not HIGH (controlled + audited); not LOW (a Must-Have story's named business rule is unmet).
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none -- report only.

### ISSUE-108 -- FR-1/BR-1 Interview-stage soft-gate seam is absent: moving to Interview with no scheduled interview produces NO warning (only Offer-scorecard + headcount soft gates exist)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · OPEN
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-004 · TC-REC-004-04 (FR-1/BR-1, step 3)
- **Title:** BR-1's default gates are "Screening->notes, Interview->>=1 scheduled interview, Offer->>=1 completed scorecard." The Offer-scorecard soft warning and the BR-4 headcount warning are implemented, but moving an applicant Screening->Interview with no scheduled interview returns warnings: [] -- there is no soft-gate seam (not even a stub warning) for the Interview gate. TC-REC-004-04 step 6 explicitly says do NOT weaken to "no gate at all"; the Interview gate is exactly that.
- **Root cause (~92%, code):** ApplyStageMove (ApplicantService.cs:644-665) builds the warn list from only two conditions -- Offer/Hired-over-headcount (:648) and Offer-without-scorecard (:660). There is no branch evaluating an interview-schedule criterion when toStage == Interview (the US-REC-005 schedule data source is also not yet wired).
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** applicant at Screening with no interview scheduled -> POST .../move-stage {"toStage":"Interview"} -> HTTP 200, data.warnings = [].
- **Evidence:** 200 response with empty warnings array on the Screening->Interview move (vs the populated warnings on the Offer move).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW -- the move is allowed (correct for a soft gate) and the Offer gate seam exists, so the framework is present; only the Interview-criterion warning is missing, and it is dependency-conditional on US-REC-005. Advisory-only; no data/security impact.
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none -- report only.

### ISSUE-109 -- No optimistic-concurrency token on the Applicant record: concurrent stage moves never return 409 (story assumption #10.3 unmet)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #169, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-004 · TC-REC-004-11 (NFR-3 / assumption #10.3) -- TC marked BLOCKED
- **Title:** Story assumption #10.3 states "Concurrent stage transitions on the same applicant are handled with optimistic concurrency (EF Core concurrency token on the applicant record)." The Applicant entity / ApplicantConfiguration define NO [Timestamp]/xmin/IsConcurrencyToken mapping, so two concurrent moves on the same applicant both return 200 (no 409 conflict) -- the second winner overwrites the first's outcome (serialized last-write-wins, not optimistic-conflict).
- **Root cause (~95%, code):** grep -niE "rowversion|xmin|concurrency|IsConcurrencyToken" Applicant.cs ApplicantConfiguration.cs -> no matches. MoveStageAsync loads-then-saves with no version check, so EF issues no concurrency-guarded UPDATE.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** applicant at Screening; fire two simultaneous moves -- {"toStage":"Interview"} and {"toStage":"Rejected",...} -- in parallel. Both returned HTTP 200 (one Screening->Interview, the other Interview->Rejected); neither got a 409. Two history rows written, no conflict surfaced.
- **Evidence:** two concurrent 200 responses; final state Rejected with 3 sequential history rows (the second move read the post-first state due to DB row serialization -- no lost-update corruption observed in this two-call probe, but also no optimistic-concurrency 409 as the story requires).
- **Severity rationale:** MED -- under genuine simultaneous load a true lost update (two readers of the same pre-state) is possible because nothing rejects a stale write; the documented concurrency guarantee is absent. Not HIGH because Postgres row locking serializes the two UPDATEs (no crash/corruption seen) and the surface is Manage-gated. TC-REC-004-11 marked BLOCKED per its step-6 DEFERRED directive ("do NOT weaken to last-write-wins").
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none -- report only.

### ISSUE-110 -- Stage-transition notifications are synchronous log-only (not queued via Hangfire/outbox, NFR-5) and perform no BR-5 template variable substitution
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · OPEN
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment · US-REC-004 · TC-REC-004-10 (FR-6/NFR-5/BR-5) -- TC PASS-conditional
- **Title:** Each stage transition fires IRecruitmentNotificationService.NotifyStageChangedAsync, but the only implementation is LogOnlyRecruitmentNotificationService, which writes a single _logger.LogInformation line inside the request (fire-and-forget, non-blocking) -- there is NO outbox/notification row and NO Hangfire job enqueued (NFR-5 "queued via Hangfire for async delivery"), and NO BR-5 template variable substitution (the log carries only stage names + applicant email; {applicantName}/{vacancyTitle}/{companyName} are never resolved or rendered).
- **Root cause (~93%, code):** LogOnlyRecruitmentNotificationService.NotifyStageChangedAsync (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LogOnlyRecruitmentNotificationService.cs:50-) only logs; no outbox table write, no BackgroundJob.Enqueue, no template lookup/substitution. The Notification System (S25) is acknowledged as an external dependency in the TC's CONDITIONAL note.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** POST .../move-stage {"toStage":"Screening"} -> 200 (prompt, non-blocking) -> Serilog shows Notification event stage-changed for applicant "..." ... stage Applied -> Screening (notify lat@...) and nothing in any outbox/queue.
- **Evidence:** Serilog hrm-20260626.log LogOnlyRecruitmentNotificationService INF lines; no Hangfire/outbox artifact; log text contains no rendered template variables.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW -- matches the increment's documented log-only stub (the TC explicitly treats async-queue + template substitution as CONDITIONAL on S25 wiring, "not a gap"); the non-blocking + log-seam contract IS met and the transition succeeds independently of notification. Flagged so the NFR-5/BR-5 wiring follow-up is tracked. Failure isolation verified (a notification failure cannot fail the committed transition -- try/catch around the call).
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none -- report only.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) -- applies to the US-REC-004 stage-history / multi-transition / rejection-reason surface too (same mechanism as the US-REC-003 ISO-011 record), not re-filed.** TC-REC-ISO-013 dimension. With matched header=token (acme context), the stage-history surface is fully isolated on reads AND the load-before-write path: an acme applicant's /detail timeline and the vacancy /pipeline board both return 404 under a X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal context, and a move-stage write targeting an acme applicant id under a techoneglobal context 404s with no acme mutation (verified: target applicant unchanged), and a body-injected tenantId/tenant_id is ignored (the DTO has no tenant field; the history row's TenantId is stamped from _tenantContext.TenantId). The residual exposure is the systemic header-spoof itself: an acme JWT + X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal is accepted and operates in techoneglobal's context (a spoof-read of TG's vacancy list returned HTTP 200 with TG scope -- TG simply had 0 recruitment rows to surface), so an acme principal holding Recruitment.Manage could move/reject/reactivate techoneglobal's applicants and write applicant_stage_history rows stamped with techoneglobal's tenant_id (this exact cross-tenant WRITE was already proven + reverted-to-0-rows in the US-REC-003 run, ISO-011). No new mechanism. To avoid leaving cross-tenant residue, NO techoneglobal recruitment data was seeded in this run (the write-bypass is already filed); no cross-tenant rows were written or left (the acme-data probes all 404'd before any write). Root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware. TC-REC-ISO-013 -> FAIL (systemic BUG-003), consistent with TC-REC-ISO-011.

### ISSUE-111 — FR-7 "all rating submissions shall be audit-logged with the manager's user ID + timestamp" is NOT written to the central `audit_logs` trail (only `created_by`/`updated_by` row stamping + Serilog)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #154, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested (red pre-fix / green post-fix); merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05; combined merged-tree audit suite green)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Performance · US-PRF-003 · TC-PRF-003-11 (FR-7), also touches TC-PRF-003-08 step 5 (reopen audited)
- **Title:** FR-7 explicitly requires that **all** manager rating submissions (and per TC-11 the reopen + re-submit) be audit-logged with the acting user's id + timestamp, queryable + tenant-scoped. After a submit + an HR reopen, the central `audit_logs` table has **zero** rows referencing the review (no `resource_type`/`action`/`event_type` containing "review"). The acting user + timestamp ARE captured, but only via (a) `created_by`/`updated_by` row stamping (verified: `created_by=manager@acme.test`, `updated_by=hr@acme.test` after the HR reopen) and (b) structured Serilog lines ("Manager review submitted/reopened. Id=… By=manager@acme.test / By=hr@acme.test"). There is no entry in the queryable tenant audit trail, so TC-11 step 4 (a globex user must not see acme's review audit entries) is moot — there are none to scope. Same recurring missing-central-audit theme as ISSUE-097 (goals FR-6), ISSUE-106 (self-assessment), and the attendance/leave/recruitment modules (ISSUE-067/069/104, BUG-025/028).
- **Root cause (~90%, code + self-documented):** `ManagerReviewService.UpsertAsync`/`ReopenAsync` write only `_logger.LogInformation(...)`; the class XML-doc (`ManagerReviewService.cs:19-20`) states audit "rides the AuditInterceptor (manager user id + timestamp stamped on SaveChanges) plus structured Serilog entries" — i.e. by-design no central `audit_logs` insert. The AuditInterceptor stamps created_by/updated_by but does not emit a discrete submit/reopen audit event.
- **Reproduction steps (live, acme, today):** as `manager@acme.test` submit John's review → as `hr@acme.test` reopen it → `SELECT * FROM audit_logs WHERE tenant_id=acme AND created_at>now()-'5 min' AND (resource_type ILIKE '%review%' OR event_type ILIKE '%review%' OR action ILIKE '%review%')` → **0 rows**. `SELECT created_by,updated_by FROM manager_review …` → `manager@acme.test` / `hr@acme.test`. Serilog has the submit + reopen lines with `By=`.
- **Evidence:** 0 audit_logs review rows; created_by/updated_by stamped; Serilog "Manager review submitted/reopened … By=…".
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-7 is an EXPLICIT functional requirement ("shall be audit-logged with the manager's user ID and timestamp") and the contracted central audit trail is not written; mitigated to not-HIGH because the user id + timestamp are still captured via created_by/updated_by + Serilog (partial, non-queryable traceability). Consistent with the ISSUE·MED rating given to the twin explicit-audit gap ISSUE-097 (goals FR-6).
- **Suggested direction (NOT applied):** none — report only.

> **BUG-057 (optimistic concurrency not surfaced to the client — no version/ETag token in the write DTO) — EXTENDED to the US-PRF-003 manager-review surface, not re-filed.**
> Identical architectural omission as the goals surface (BUG-057) and self-assessment: the `Goal.Version`/review `xmin` row-version IS mapped and `ManagerReviewService.UpsertAsync` catches `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` → 409 `concurrency_conflict` (`ManagerReviewService.cs:261-266`), but `SaveManagerReviewRequest` (`ManagerReviewDtos.cs:123`) carries **no client-supplied concurrency token**, so the cross-session "HR and manager both loaded V1" lost-update scenario NFR-3/TC-PRF-003-10 specify is NOT prevented. Demonstrated live: manager draft sets G1 rating 4 ("RaviEdit") → 200; HR draft (stale intent) sets G1 rating 2 ("NadiaEdit") → **200** (no 409); final DB row = rating 2 / "NadiaEdit" — the manager's change was silently lost. The in-request xmin guard exists but is dead for the cross-request case it's meant to cover. This is why **TC-PRF-003-10 FAILs**. Same fix as BUG-057: the API must accept + round-trip the client's row-version (ETag/If-Match). (NFR-3 here names HR-vs-manager concurrency specifically; the gap is the same one-DTO-no-token omission across all three performance write surfaces — goals/self-assessment/manager-review.)

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-PRF-003 manager-review surface (READ leak + cross-tenant WRITE incl. reopen, for `.All` holders), not re-filed.**
> The review endpoints resolve the tenant from `ITenantContext` (subdomain / `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header) and `AuthorizeForEmployeeAsync` grants any `Performance.Review.All` holder without checking that the caller's JWT tenant matches the resolved tenant (`ManagerReviewService.cs:497-499`) — same missing `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId` invariant (root locus US-AUTH-007). Confirmed live today, both arms, then reverted:
> - **READ leak (TC-PRF-ISO-009):** acme `tenantadmin@acme.test` (JWT tenant_id=acme, holds Review.All) + header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `GET .../reviews/cycles/{tgCycle}/employees/{tgEmp}` → **HTTP 200** returning techoneglobal's review (employeeName "Cross Write", weightedManagerScore 4.00, finalScore 4.00, summaryComment "TG confidential review"). The TC's "HR `.All` is tenant-bounded / cannot reopen another tenant's review" claim is therefore FALSE.
> - **WRITE breach (TC-PRF-ISO-011):** same acme TenantAdmin token + techoneglobal header → `POST .../reopen` flipped techoneglobal's submitted review to Draft (`updated_by=tenantadmin@acme.test`), then `POST .../submit` overwrote it (summaryComment "TG confidential review" → "ACME-INTRUDER-EDIT", manager rating 4 → 1) — a full mutation of another tenant's appraisal data by a principal with no membership there. **All techoneglobal probe data (cycle + goal + review + item) was hard-deleted immediately; techoneglobal verified back to 0 perf rows.**
> - **Mismatch not rejected (TC-PRF-ISO-010 step 3):** the acme-token + globex/techoneglobal-subdomain mismatch is accepted, not rejected — the core token↔tenant invariant the TC requires. (This is why TC-PRF-ISO-009/010/011 FAIL.)
> - **Self-protected arms (NOT a leak):** the `Performance.Review.Team` **manager** path is self-protecting — acme manager token + techoneglobal header → workspace 404 `employee_not_found` / team dashboard 403 `no_employee_record` (the manager's UserId has no employee in the foreign tenant). And within the **correct** subdomain, write isolation is CLEAN: body-injected `tenant_id` ignored (stored row = acme), foreign `employee_id` → 404 `employee_not_found`, foreign `goal_id` → 400 `unknown_goal` (TC-PRF-ISO-011 in-tenant arms PASS); fail-closed on no-tenant (400) / invalid subdomain (404).
> So, like the goals surface (and UNLIKE the self-assessment surface which is self-scoped and clean), the cross-tenant exposure fires through an `.All`-holding actor (HR/TenantAdmin) over the spoofable header — here it reaches the most sensitive operation yet (reopen + overwrite a locked, submitted appraisal in another tenant). NFR-2's stated RLS is not implemented; isolation is EF query filters keyed off the resolved tenant, correct only when header matches token. See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]], the root-locus confirmation at US-AUTH-007, and the goals/Admin/Core-HR/Leave/Attendance/Recruitment records.

> **Route-prefix drift (ISSUE-100 class) note for US-PRF-003:** the TCs reference `.../reviews/{id}` and by-id IDOR routes; the live API uses `GET /api/v1/tenant/performance/reviews/cycles/{cycleId}/employees/{employeeId}` (employee+cycle keyed, no standalone review-by-id route). The IDOR-by-review-id arms (TC-ISO-009 step2 / TC-ISO-010 step4) therefore have no literal route; cross-tenant access is instead exercised via the employee/cycle workspace (which IS where the BUG-003 leak fires). Recorded under ISSUE-100; TC steps not edited (REPORT-ONLY).

## US-PAY-001 — Salary Structure & Component Configuration (test-runner, 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API run)

> **Scope:** TC-PAY-001-01..12 + TC-PAY-ISO-001..004 (the four ISO TCs scoped to US-PAY-001). API-layer (curl + JWT), acme tenant, persona = `tenantadmin@acme.test` (the ONLY persona holding `Payroll.Configure`). UI/a11y (TC-12) and Redis-cache (ISO-004) BLOCKED. All test residue (acme + techoneglobal payroll rows + salary audit_logs) hard-deleted post-run; tables verified back to 0/baseline.
>
> **Routes + permissions discovered (for next runners):**
> - `GET|POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-components`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/payroll/salary-components/{id}` — perm **`Payroll.Configure`**. (NOT `/payroll/components` and NOT `Payroll.*.All` as the TCs assume.)
> - `GET|POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-structures`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/payroll/salary-structures/{id}`; `POST .../{id}/components` (link), `DELETE .../{id}/components/{linkId}` (unlink), `POST .../{id}/components/reorder`, `POST .../{id}/clone` — all perm **`Payroll.Configure`**.
> - **No PATCH and no dedicated `/activate` endpoint.** Activation = `PUT` the whole structure with `isActive:true` (FR-5 earning-check runs on the PUT). PUT **replaces the whole component-link set**.
> - **`Payroll.Configure` is held by Tenant Admin only.** HR Officer/Manager carry zero payroll perms; Employee carries `Payroll.View.Own` (see BUG-060). Codes normalised `Trim().ToUpperInvariant()` (case-insensitive uniqueness, BR-2 OK). Code regex = `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` (hyphens rejected).
> - Delete = **soft-delete** (`is_deleted=true`). Component create/update/delete ARE audited to central `audit_logs` (resource_type `SalaryComponent`, with before/after JSON). **Structure writes are NOT audited** (ISSUE-108).

### BUG-060 — HR Officer cannot configure salary components/structures (403 on read AND write) despite US-PAY-001 requiring it

- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #254, 2026-07-11) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** Added `Payroll.Configure` (+ `View/Run/Export`) to the HR Officer role in `PermissionCatalog.DefaultPermissionsFor`; idempotent startup reconcile applies it to existing tenants. Regression: `PermissionCatalogTests.HrOfficer_HasPayrollRunConfigureExport_BUG060_071_077`.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-08 (also breaks the AC-1/AC-3 persona)
- **Title:** The `HR Officer` role holds no `Payroll.Configure` permission, so every payroll-config endpoint returns 403 for HR — but the story names "Tenant Admin **or HR Officer**" as the persona and AC-1/AC-3/preconditions explicitly require HR to create/edit components and structures.
- **Root cause:** Role->permission seeding gap (confidence 90%). The `HR Officer` role's permission set (decoded live from the JWT: 48 perms, **zero** Payroll perms) does not include `Payroll.Configure`; only `Tenant Admin` carries the full Payroll bundle (`Payroll.Approve/Configure/Export/Run/View/ViewSensitive`). The controllers gate every action with `[RequirePermission("Payroll.Configure")]`, so HR is uniformly denied. No server log line (clean 403 from the authz filter). Same "HR locked out of a module they own" class seen in Leave (BUG-027/034) and Attendance (BUG-049).
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`, `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`; decode JWT `permissions` -> no `Payroll.Configure`.
  2. `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-components` (HR bearer + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`) -> **403**.
  3. `GET /api/v1/payroll/salary-components` (HR bearer) -> **403** (even read is denied).
  4. Same calls as Tenant Admin -> 201 / 200.
- **Evidence:** `HROfficer: WRITE(POST)=403  READ(GET)=403` ; `TenantAdmin: WRITE(POST)=201  READ(GET)=200`. Manager=403, Employee=403, anon=401 (those denials are correct).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a named primary persona is entirely locked out of a Must-Have module's core flow; the feature is unusable by HR as specified, forcing all payroll config onto Tenant Admin.

### BUG-061 — Negative monetary value accepted for a Fixed component (no lower-bound validation)

- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #281, 2026-07-13) — `Create`/`UpdateSalaryComponentValidator` now require a `Fixed`-method value `>= 0` (`negative_fixed_value` code); tests cover negative-fails + zero-boundary + percentage regression. · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-06 (boundary)
- **Title:** Creating a `Fixed` salary component with `defaultValue = -100.00` succeeds (201) and persists `-100.00` in `salary_component.default_value`; TC-06 step 3 requires a 422 rejection.
- **Root cause:** Validator gap (confidence 95%). `CreateSalaryComponentValidator` only bounds the value `InclusiveBetween(0,100)` for `PercentageOfBasic`/`PercentageOfGross`; for `Fixed` it merely requires `NotNull` — there is no `>= 0` guard. Service `ValidateCalculation` likewise only range-checks percentages. Any negative amount for a Fixed/override value is stored verbatim (DB row `BNEG|-100.00` confirmed).
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As Tenant Admin (acme): `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-components` `{"name":"BNeg","code":"BNEG","type":"Earning","calculationMethod":"Fixed","defaultValue":-100.00,"isActive":true}` -> **201**.
  2. DB: `SELECT default_value FROM salary_component WHERE code='BNEG'` -> `-100.00`.
- **Evidence:** `negative -100 fixed ... status=201 msg=None`; DB row `BNEG|-100.00`.
- **Severity rationale:** MEDIUM — corrupts downstream payroll math (a negative earning/deduction inverts pay), but contained to config-time and requires the `Payroll.Configure` privilege; no cross-tenant or security impact.

### BUG-062 — BR-4 not enforced: a structure with deductions exceeding gross earnings is accepted

- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #281, 2026-07-13; **user decision: WARN not block**) — deduction>gross (negative net) is intentionally NOT rejected (legitimate for loan/advance over-recovery); instead the non-blocking negative-net advisory now fires (via the BUG-074 fix) so HR is warned. Test asserts not-rejected AND warned. · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-06 (BR-4)
- **Title:** A salary structure linking an Earning of 50000 and a Deduction whose value is 60000 (deduction > gross) is created with 201 — BR-4 ("deduction components cannot exceed the gross earnings total; validated during structure definition") is unimplemented.
- **Root cause:** Missing validation (confidence 95%). Neither `SalaryStructureService.ValidateLinks` nor any validator computes gross-earnings-vs-deductions; no code path references such a comparison. The check appears omitted entirely.
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. As Tenant Admin (acme): create Earning `BASIC` (Fixed 50000) and Deduction `BIGDED` (Fixed 60000).
  2. `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-structures` with both linked (deduction overrideValue 60000) -> **201 created**, no error.
- **Evidence:** `BR-4 structure (earning 50000, deduction 60000) status=201 CREATED`.
- **Severity rationale:** MEDIUM — produces structurally-invalid pay definitions (negative net) a later payroll run would have to catch; contained to config and privileged, no security/isolation impact.

### ISSUE-108 — Salary-structure writes are not audit-logged (NFR-5 half-unmet)

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #334, 2026-07-17) · **Layer:** BE
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17):** Finding was **partially stale** — `SalaryStructureService` already injects `IPayrollAuditLogger` and audits **Create/Update/Clone** (added since the finding was filed). The real remaining gap was **Delete / Link / Unlink / Reorder** (verified: no `_audit.Log` in those 4). Added 4 new action constants (`SalaryStructure.Deleted/.ComponentLinked/.ComponentUnlinked/.ComponentsReordered`) and an `_audit.Log(...)` (before/after payload) to each of the 4 methods, committed atomically with the business change. 4 integration arms through the real MediatR pipeline + real `PayrollAuditLogger` assert the audit rows land (15/15); mutation-verified (swapping the 4 new actions to `Created` fails exactly the 4 arms). NFR-5 now met for all structure writes.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-01/-10
- **Title:** Component create/update/delete are audited to `audit_logs` (with before/after), but **structure** create/update/delete/link/unlink/reorder/clone/activate produce **zero** audit entries. NFR-5 requires "all write operations on salary components **and structures**" to be audit-logged.
- **Root cause:** `SalaryStructureService` has no `IPayrollAuditLogger` dependency and never calls `_audit.Log(...)` — only `SalaryComponentService` does (confidence 100%, read both services). Confirmed live: after creating + activating a structure with 3 links + a reorder, `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_logs WHERE resource_type ILIKE '%SalaryStructure%'` = **0**.
- **Reproduction steps:** Create a structure, link components, reorder, PUT-activate (all 200/201). Query `audit_logs` for `SalaryStructure*` -> 0 rows. Compare: 3 `SalaryComponent.Created` rows exist for the same run.
- **Evidence:** `=== count salary structure audit (should be 0) === 0`. Twin of the pervasive no-central-audit theme (Attendance ISSUE-067 family, Leave BUG-025/028/031).
- **Severity rationale:** MEDIUM — NFR-5 explicit + compliance-relevant (payroll config changes are high-value), but no functional/data-integrity break; component writes ARE audited so the gap is partial.

### ISSUE-109 — AC-5 delete-guard reports affected *structures*, not the affected *employee* count

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-04
- **Title:** Deleting an in-use component is correctly prevented with 409, but the message says "used by N salary structure(s)" — AC-5 specifies "an error message listing the **count of affected employees**." The guard counts `salary_structure_component` links, never the employees assigned to those structures.
- **Root cause:** `SalaryComponentService.DeleteAsync` counts `SalaryStructureComponents` where `SalaryComponentId == id` and returns that count (confidence 100%). It does not join through `EmployeeSalaryComponent`/assignment to count employees. Behaviourally this is *stricter* (blocks even a component linked to an employee-less structure), but the message and the AC-5 metric diverge.
- **Reproduction steps:** Link `BASIC` to a structure (no employees), `DELETE /api/v1/payroll/salary-components/{basicId}` -> 409 "used by 2 salary structure(s)..."; in-use statutory also 409.
- **Evidence:** `status=409 ... used by 2 salary structure(s) and cannot be deleted`. Unused component deletes 200.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — AC-5's core intent (prevent destructive delete) is met and is actually stricter; only the reported metric/wording deviates.

### ISSUE-110 — NFR-1 Redis caching of component/structure lists is unimplemented

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-02 (step 3) / TC-PAY-001-11 / TC-PAY-ISO-004
- **Title:** Neither salary service references any cache (`IMemoryCache`/`IDistributedCache`/Redis); there is no 15-min-TTL cached list and no per-tenant cache key. NFR-1 (and the tenant-scoped-cache assertion in ISO-004) cannot be satisfied because no payroll cache exists.
- **Root cause:** No caching code in `SalaryComponentService`/`SalaryStructureService` (confidence 100%, grep clean). Reads go straight to EF every time. Dev runs Redis-off (in-memory fallback) per `appsettings.Development.json`. Side effect: TC-02 step 3 "no stale read after write" passes *trivially* (always fresh), and ISO-004 has no shared key to leak — but NFR-1 itself is not built.
- **Evidence:** grep for `cache|redis|IMemoryCache|IDistributedCache` in both services -> no matches; `"Redis": ""` in dev config.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — a performance NFR, not a correctness/security defect; light-load latency is already far inside SLA (TC-11 p95 7ms) so the cache is not yet needed for the SLA.

### ISSUE-111 — Large/over-precision decimals echoed un-rounded in the API create response (DB stores correct numeric(18,2))

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-06
- **Title:** Two response-serialization mismatches vs the persisted value: (a) `defaultValue=9999999999999999.99` round-trips in the **create response** as `1e+16` (scientific-notation precision loss in JSON), while the DB column correctly stores `9999999999999999.99`; (b) `defaultValue=1234.5678` is **echoed as `1234.5678`** in the create response but the DB rounds it to `1234.57` (numeric(18,2)). The persisted data is correct in both cases; only the immediate API echo is wrong.
- **Root cause:** The create/update DTO is projected from the in-memory entity *before* the DB round-trip applies the column scale, and `decimal`->JSON serialization renders very large magnitudes in exponent form (confidence 85%). A re-fetch returns the correctly-scaled value.
- **Reproduction steps:** Create with `defaultValue:9999999999999999.99` -> response `defaultValue: 1e+16`; DB `9999999999999999.99`. Create with `1234.5678` -> response `1234.5678`; DB `1234.57`.
- **Evidence:** `status=201 val=1e+16` ; DB `BMAX|9999999999999999.99`, `BPREC|1234.57`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/echo-only; the source of truth (DB) is correct, a subsequent GET returns the right value. No 2dp-rounding rule is documented/enforced at the API layer, so consumers shouldn't rely on the create echo.

### ISSUE-112 — Formula component referencing an unknown variable is accepted at config-time

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-07 (step 4)
- **Title:** `POST salary-components` with `calculationMethod=Formula, formulaExpression="basic + unknownComp"` succeeds (201). TC-07 step 4 expects rejection of a reference to a non-existent component/identifier.
- **Root cause:** `SalaryFormula.Validate` only checks **syntax** (the grammar), not whether identifiers resolve to real component codes — the unknown-variable error is raised only at **evaluation** time (`Evaluate` throws "Unknown variable" when variable values are supplied during a payroll run). Self-reference / circular detection likewise fires only when the component is **linked into a structure** (`DetectCircularReferences`), not at component creation — verified: `pf2 + 100` accepted as a component (201), but rejected 400 ("Circular reference … PF2 -> pf2") when linked into a structure. Deliberate layering (service comment: circular-ref is "a structure concern").
- **Reproduction steps:** `POST salary-components {"calculationMethod":"Formula","formulaExpression":"basic + unknownComp",...}` -> 201. Then link a self-referencing formula component into a structure -> 400 circular.
- **Evidence:** `unknown identifier 'basic + unknownComp' ... status=201`; structure-level cycle `status=400 Circular reference detected ... CYA -> cyb -> cya`. BR-6 circular + safe-eval (no code exec for `System.exit(0)`/`import os`) all enforced correctly at the structure layer.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — caught at run-time and at structure-link time; an unresolvable formula can't silently produce wrong pay (it throws), and the real BR-6 protections (circular, safe-eval) work where they matter.

### ISSUE-113 — TEST-layer drift: TC test data uses hyphenated codes and 422/route/PATCH expectations the implementation does not use

- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** TEST
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-001 / TC-PAY-001-01/-04/-05/-06
- **Title:** Benign spec-vs-impl drifts (not product defects): (1) TC-01 uses structure code `FT-IN` and TC-04 `OLD-BONUS`, but both code validators enforce `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` (hyphens -> 400); tests must use `FT_IN`/`OLD_BONUS`. (2) TC-05/-06 expect **422** for FR-5/validation; the implementation returns **400** (equivalent rejection, code `no_earning_component`). (3) TCs reference routes `/api/v1/payroll/components`+`/structures` and a `PATCH .../{id}` activate; live routes are `/payroll/salary-components`+`/salary-structures` and activation is via `PUT` (no PATCH).
- **Root cause:** Test cases authored against the story's illustrative examples before the API contract settled (confidence 90%). Not weakened/edited (REPORT-ONLY) — recorded so a maintainer can reconcile the TC text.
- **Evidence:** `POST salary-structures {code:"FT-IN"}` -> 400 "Structure code may contain only letters, digits, and underscores."; FR-5 activate -> 400 not 422.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — test-asset accuracy only; no product impact. Verdicts above judged against actual correct behaviour, not the literal TC status codes.

> **BUG-003 (cross-tenant JWT-vs-subdomain mismatch) — EXTENDED to the US-PAY-001 salary-component/structure surface (READ + WRITE), not re-filed.**
> Same root locus (US-AUTH-007 / `TenantResolutionMiddleware`): the middleware resolves the tenant from the `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header and drives the EF global query filter + `TenantInterceptor` stamping off it, while authorization uses the JWT — and never rejects **token-tenant != header-tenant**. Confirmed live on payroll with non-empty data:
> - **WRITE breach (TC-PAY-ISO-003):** acme `tenantadmin@acme.test` token (holds `Payroll.Configure`) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` on `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-components` returned **201** and persisted the row stamped with **techoneglobal's tenant_id** (`019ef3c3-…`), not acme. An acme principal with no membership in techoneglobal created payroll config there.
> - **READ breach (TC-PAY-ISO-002 step 3):** same acme token + techoneglobal header on `GET /api/v1/payroll/salary-components` returned **200** with techoneglobal's `XTENANT` component (`total 1`) — cross-tenant config disclosure; the mismatch is not rejected.
> - **Self-protected / CLEAN arms (NOT a leak):** within a **matched** (header=token) acme context isolation is correct — acme cannot see techoneglobal's component in its list, and `GET/PUT/DELETE` of a foreign techoneglobal id all **404** (EF query filter). **Body-injection is ignored**: `POST` with `tenant_id`/`tenantId` set to techoneglobal under the acme context stored the row under **acme** (TenantInterceptor overrides the body — TC-PAY-ISO-003 step 1 PASS). Fail-closed on no-tenant (400 "Tenant context is not resolved") and invalid subdomain (404 "Workspace not found").
> AC-6/FR-8's claim of "PostgreSQL RLS enforces isolation at the database level" is **NOT met**: this codebase uses EF global query filters keyed off the spoofable resolved-tenant, not RLS — correct only when header matches token. Affects TC-PAY-ISO-002, TC-PAY-ISO-003 (FAIL). **The cross-tenant probe was REVERTED** — the techoneglobal `XTENANT` row (and all acme test payroll rows + salary `audit_logs`) were hard-deleted via psql; techoneglobal verified back to 0 payroll rows. See [[auth-full-test-pass-2026-06-25]], the root-locus at US-AUTH-007, and the Admin/Core-HR/Leave/Attendance/Recruitment/Performance module records.
