> Compensation is NOT implemented across the module: `currentCompensation` is always `null` (workspace + DTO), documented seam ("compensation lives in Payroll; not joined here"). Downstream integration (BR-6 Core HR/Payroll/Training) is a documented seam that raises an `IntegrationRaised` event but does NOT write to any module ("seam; not wired"). pgcrypto compensation-at-rest (NFR-3) does not exist. Story-acknowledged deferrals, captured as ISSUE-149/ISSUE-150 for traceability.

### BUG-069 — BUG-003 cross-tenant leak extends to US-PRF-010 recommendations: `.All`-gated surfaces LEAK cross-tenant READ **and WRITE**; manager/employee self-scoped surfaces CLEAN
- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #119, verified 2026-07-02) · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-ISO-037, TC-PRF-ISO-038, TC-PRF-ISO-039, TC-PRF-ISO-040
- **Title:** An acme `Performance.Publish.All` holder (hr@/tenantadmin@acme.test) sending `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` (with the acme JWT) executes in techoneglobal's tenant context and (a) READS techoneglobal recommendations by id + the techoneglobal recommendation summary, and (b) **WRITES** — overrode techoneglobal's recommendation (bonus to 31337, justification `ACME-INJECTED-OVERRIDE`, `updated_by=hr@acme.test`) while the row stays under techoneglobal's tenant_id. The token's `tenant_id` is never validated against the resolved subdomain. Same root locus as platform-wide BUG-003; this extends it to the recommendation read+write surfaces. The WRITE arm is worse than the PRF-009 variant (BUG-068, which self-protected on writes) because the recommendation create/override path keys off `employeeId`+`cycleId` (not the caller's identity), so a foreign-tenant write succeeds outright.
- **Root cause (confidence 96%):** classic BUG-003 split — authorization reads `_currentUser.Permissions` (the acme HR genuinely has Publish.All) while every query/write is scoped by `_tenantContext.TenantId` (resolved from the spoofed subdomain header), with NO guard asserting `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId`. `RecommendationService.IsHr` (`RecommendationService.cs:50`) short-circuits authorization on permission only; `GetAsync`/`GetSummaryAsync`/`SaveAsync` (`:143`,`:542`,`:258`) and the `TenantInterceptor` all bind to the resolved (foreign) tenant. No token-vs-context tenant check exists in the controller or service. Self-scoped surfaces (manager workspace/`GetAsync` via `Performance.Review.Team`, employee@ with no perm) are CLEAN — they 403 in the foreign context because the manager resolves their direct-report set via UserId inside the tenant filter (no foreign reports) and the employee lacks the permission entirely.
- **Reproduction:** seed a techoneglobal recommendation (`bonus 7777`, just `TECH-SECRET-JUSTIFICATION`). READ: `curl .../recommendations/<techRecId> -H "Authorization: Bearer <acme-hr-jwt>" -H "X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal"` to 200 with `bonusAmount 7777`, `justification "TECH-SECRET-JUSTIFICATION"`; same id with `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` to 404 `recommendation_not_found` (control). `.../summary?cycleId=<techCycle>` with the tech header to 200 `totalRecommendations 1, bonusPool 7777`. WRITE: `POST .../recommendations -H acme-jwt -H "X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal" {"employeeId":"<techEmp>","cycleId":"<techCycle>","type":"Bonus","justification":"ACME-INJECTED-OVERRIDE","details":{"bonusAmount":31337}}` to 200; DB row `019efddd-0002-...C1` then `tenant_id=019ef3c3(techoneglobal)`, `bonus_amount=31337`, `updated_by=hr@acme.test`. (Reverted/deleted in cleanup.)
- **Evidence:** rules list as proof of context-switch — acme header returns acme's 2 QAFIX rules, techoneglobal header (same acme token) returns 0 (techoneglobal's empty set, not acme's). Cross-tenant GET-by-id returned the techoneglobal secret justification. Cross-tenant override mutated the techoneglobal row (verified in DB). ISO-038 fail-closed arms PASS: no tenant header to 400; invalid/unknown subdomain to 404. Body `tenant_id` injection is structurally impossible (SaveRecommendationRequest has no tenant_id field) — the leak vector is the spoofed subdomain header, not body injection.
- **Severity rationale:** Confirmed live cross-tenant **disclosure + mutation** of another tenant's recommendation (compensation/justification PII) through an `.All`-gated surface, using only a legitimate same-role token + a header. HIGH (consistent with the BUG-003 family; not CRIT only because it requires a valid `.All` token and the platform-wide root cause is already filed as the CRIT BUG-003 — this is the per-surface extension). Same fix as BUG-003: assert `CurrentUser.TenantId == ITenantContext.TenantId` (or reject the subdomain/JWT mismatch in `TenantResolutionMiddleware`).

### ISSUE-145 — Budget over-spend (BR-4) is a pure flag, not a gated proceed: submitting over budget needs NO justification (the "proceed with justification" gate is absent)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #298, 2026-07-14) · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-05 (steps 3-4), BR-4
- **Resolution (BE, PR #298):** `RecommendationService.SubmitAsync` rejects an over-budget submit with a blank Justification (400 `over_budget_requires_justification`) BEFORE charging; justified over-budget still proceeds (soft warning).
- **Title:** BR-4 + TC-010-05 require that exceeding the budget is a *soft warning* AND that "proceeding over budget requires a justification (the justification is the gate, not a hard cap)." The implementation gives a soft warning (correct — `isExceeded=true`, `remaining` goes negative, never hard-blocks) but enforces NO justification to proceed: a $20k bonus that pushes consumed from $90k to $110k of a $100k budget submitted successfully with an empty body `{}`. There is no over-budget-justification check anywhere.
- **Root cause (confidence 95%):** `RecommendationService.SubmitAsync` calls `ChargeBudgetAsync` (`RecommendationService.cs:437`, `:869`) which simply increments `budget.ConsumedAmount` and returns the `IsExceeded` bool as a non-blocking warning; the returned `warning` is only logged (`:445-448`), never used to require a justification or alter the submit outcome. BR-4's "proceed with justification" half is unimplemented — the soft-warning half is.
- **Reproduction:** create budget $100k for the cycle; submit a $90k bonus (consumed $90k); submit a $20k bonus with no justification to 200 `Submitted`, budget then `consumed 110000, remaining -10000, isExceeded true`. No justification was demanded at any point.
- **Evidence:** budget after first submit `consumed 90000/remaining 10000/exceeded false`; after second `consumed 110000/remaining -10000/exceeded true`; both submits succeeded; the over-budget submit body was `{}`.
- **Severity rationale:** Budget tracking + the soft-warning-not-hard-block invariant (the core of BR-4/FR-8) work correctly and the math is exact; the gap is the missing justification gate on over-budget proceed — a contained control-weakness (an over-budget recommendation can be submitted silently), not a calculation error or crash. MED.

### ISSUE-146 — FR-6 mandates PDF export; only csv/xlsx exist — `format=pdf` returns 400 `invalid_format`
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-13 (step 3), FR-6
- **Title:** FR-6 (and TC-010-13 step 3) require a PDF recommendation-summary report with tenant branding. The export endpoint supports only `csv` and `xlsx`; `format=pdf` is rejected 400 `invalid_format` (the controller doc says "PDF deferred"). The xlsx/csv exports themselves are correct and match the dashboard aggregates.
- **Root cause (confidence 99%):** `RecommendationService.ExportSummaryAsync` (`RecommendationService.cs:567-570`) whitelists `("csv" or "xlsx")` only and 400s anything else; there is no QuestPDF/PDF rendering path. The xlsx path uses ClosedXML (`RenderXlsx`).
- **Reproduction:** `GET .../summary/export?format=xlsx&cycleId=<fy25>` to 200, a valid `PK`-magic XLSX (7321 bytes), correct content-type + filename, values match the summary (6 recs / 1 promo / $110k bonus pool / status counts). `format=csv` to 200 matching CSV. `format=pdf` and `format=docx` to 400 `invalid_format`.
- **Severity rationale:** Excel/CSV export (the primary leadership-review formats) fully work and are tenant-scoped + authz-gated + dashboard-accurate; only the PDF half of FR-6 is missing — a documented deferral, low business impact since xlsx covers the data need. LOW.

### ISSUE-147 — FR-1 "custom" recommendation type accepts ANY free-text label with no tenant-configuration gate (custom types are not tenant-defined as the spec requires)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-12 (step 6), FR-1
- **Title:** FR-1 + TC-010-12 expect custom recommendation types to be *tenant-configured* (a known "Spot Award", with an unconfigured "RandomType" rejected). The implementation has a fixed `RecommendationType.Custom` enum member that accepts ANY `customTypeLabel` free-text with no per-tenant custom-type catalog or validation — so there is no notion of a configured-vs-unconfigured custom type. (Separately, a truly unknown enum string like "RandomType" IS correctly rejected at model-binding to 400, satisfying TC step 1.)
- **Root cause (confidence 92%):** `RecommendationType` (HRM.Domain/Enums) defines `Custom = 6`; `SaveAsync`/`ApplyDetails` (`RecommendationService.cs:894`) persist `CustomTypeLabel` verbatim with no lookup against any tenant custom-type config table (none exists). FR-1's "tenant-configurable custom types" is modelled as a single open enum value + free label, not a configurable catalog.
- **Reproduction:** `POST .../recommendations {"type":"Custom","details":{"customTypeLabel":"'; DROP TABLE recommendation;--"}}` to 200, label stored verbatim (table intact — SQLi safely parameterized). No tenant config governs which custom labels are allowed. `type:"RandomType"` to 400 (enum bind reject).
- **Severity rationale:** Type integrity for the fixed enum is enforced and SQLi is neutralized; the gap is the missing tenant custom-type configuration surface (any label is accepted) — a spec/feature gap with low risk (label is inert text, output-encoding-dependent). LOW.

### ISSUE-148 — BR-1/BR-2 gates fire at SUBMIT, not at CREATE; + override/justification rejections return 422 where some TCs say 400; + 1000% increment cap is loose
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-08, TC-PRF-010-03, TC-PRF-010-12
- **Title:** Three small spec-vs-impl reconciliations bundled. (a) **Gate timing:** TC-010-08 steps 1/3 word the BR-1 (ratings published) and BR-2 (calibration complete) gates as blocking *creation*. The impl allows draft *creation* on any cycle and enforces BR-1/BR-2 only at *submit* (create on an Active cycle to 200 Draft; submit to 422 `final_ratings_not_published`; submit on calibration-enabled+unsubmitted to 422 `calibration_incomplete`). The gates ARE enforced server-side, just at the submit boundary. (b) **Status code:** override-missing-justification (FR-3) and promotion-missing-grade/date (BR-5) rejections return **422** (codes `justification_required`/`promotion_details_required`), whereas TC-010-03/-08 say "400". 422 is defensible for a business-rule violation and is consistent module-wide. (c) **Range cap:** TC-010-12 expects a 500% increment rejected; the validator cap is **1000%**, so 500% is *accepted* — only >=1000% rejects. 1000% is an unrealistically loose ceiling for a salary increment.
- **Root cause (confidence 95%):** (a) `SaveAsync` (`RecommendationService.cs:258`) has no cycle-status gate; the BR-1/BR-2 checks live in `SubmitAsync` (`:379`,`:385`). (b) the service returns `Result.Failure(..., 422, code)` for these business violations (`:280`,`:328`). (c) `SaveRecommendationValidator` caps `IncrementPercent`/`BonusPercent` at `InclusiveBetween(0,1000)` (`RecommendationValidators.cs:24-29`).
- **Reproduction:** create Bonus on Active cycle FY26-A to 200 Draft, submit to 422 `final_ratings_not_published`; create on calibration cycle FY26-B to 200, submit to 422 `calibration_incomplete`; override with blank justification to 422 `justification_required`; Promotion missing grade/date to 422 `promotion_details_required`; increment 500% to 200 (persisted 500.0); increment 1500% to 422 "must be between 0 and 1000".
- **Severity rationale:** Every actual business rule (BR-1/BR-2/BR-5/FR-3) IS enforced server-side and cannot be bypassed; these are wording/timing/status-code/threshold mismatches between the TCs and a reasonable implementation, not security or correctness defects. LOW.

### ISSUE-149 — No central `audit_logs` row for any recommendation write; + justification & custom-label text stored RAW (no server-side XSS sanitization)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-12, TC-PRF-ISO-040
- **Title:** Two defense-in-depth nits bundled (recurring cross-module theme). (a) Recommendation writes append immutable `recommendation_event` rows (a complete per-rec history — FR-7 met) + Serilog, but write ZERO rows to the central `audit_logs` table, so recommendation actions never surface in the unified audit-search surface. (b) `justification` and `customTypeLabel` are persisted verbatim — `<script>alert(1)</script>` is stored raw with no HTML escaping/sanitization server-side; safety relies entirely on the FE (Angular interpolation) output-encoding. SQLi payloads are safely parameterized (EF Core — `recommendation` table intact after `'; DROP TABLE recommendation;--`).
- **Root cause (confidence 88%):** `RecommendationService` calls `SaveChangesAsync` + `AppendEvent` (append-only RecommendationEvent) + Serilog but never a central audit writer (consistent with the leave/attendance/core-HR/PIP/PRF-009 "no central audit on writes" findings). Free-text fields are only `.Trim()`-ed (`ApplyDetails` `:897-905`, `Justification` `:319`/`:335`) — no sanitization.
- **Reproduction:** create + override + submit + approve a recommendation, then query `audit_logs` for recommendation/promotion/bonus actions to 0 rows (the trail is the `recommendation_event` table only). `POST .../recommendations {"justification":"<script>alert(1)</script>"}` to stored verbatim; `{"details":{"customTypeLabel":"'; DROP TABLE recommendation;--"}}` to label stored literal, table intact (6 rows).
- **Severity rationale:** The legally-meaningful immutable history exists (append-only `recommendation_event`, tenant-scoped) and SQLi cannot execute; gaps are (a) unified-audit visibility and (b) reliance on FE encoding for XSS — both defense-in-depth, matching documented platform patterns. LOW.

### ISSUE-150 — NFR-3 compensation-at-rest encryption (pgcrypto) is entirely absent; comp comparison/masking (FR-5, AC-5 comp-gate) cannot be exercised — `currentCompensation` always null
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** **PARTIALLY RESOLVED (PR #273, merged 2026-07-12)** — the NFR-3 **compensation-at-rest encryption** half is DONE (P3-4): the 5 Recommendation comp fields (`CurrentCompensation`/`BonusAmount`/`BonusPercent`/`IncrementAmount`/`IncrementPercent`) are now AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (columns migrated `numeric→text`; verified `enc:v1:` ciphertext on real Postgres; no DB-aggregation regression — comp math is app-side over materialized lists). **Still open (separate concern):** `currentCompensation` is still always-null (the comp SNAPSHOT/join from Payroll is a documented seam, not built), so the FR-5 comparison + AC-5 comp-gate masking still can't be exercised — that's a feature seam, not encryption. · **Layer:** BE · **US/TC:** US-PRF-010 / TC-PRF-010-06, TC-PRF-010-09 (steps 5-6), TC-PRF-010-11
- **Title:** Compensation is not modelled in recommendations: `currentCompensation` is hardcoded `null` in every workspace row + DTO (documented seam "compensation lives in Payroll; not joined here"), so (FR-5) the current-vs-recommended *compensation* comparison has no current side; (AC-5/Constraints) the comp-visibility role gate has nothing to mask (a comp-hidden HR sees the same null everyone sees); and (NFR-3) pgcrypto compensation-at-rest encryption does not exist (bonus/increment numerics stored plain — same posture as US-PRF-008). The recommendation amount fields (bonusAmount/incrementAmount) ARE stored, but the employee's *current* compensation snapshot and the encryption boundary are unimplemented.
- **Root cause (confidence 95%):** `GetWorkspaceAsync` sets `CurrentCompensation = null` with the inline seam comment (`RecommendationService.cs:117`); no Payroll join, no `IFieldEncryptor`/pgcrypto wiring anywhere in the recommendation path; `recommendation` numeric columns are plain `numeric`.
- **Reproduction:** workspace + GET rec for any employee to `currentCompensation: null`; the only comp-ish data is the recommendation's own bonus/increment amounts (plain numeric in DB). No comp-mask difference between a Publish.All and a (hypothetical) comp-hidden role because there is no comp to mask.
- **Severity rationale:** A documented, story-acknowledged deferral (NFR-3/comp-visibility are CONDITIONAL seams, same as US-PRF-008); no security exposure today *because* there is no real compensation data flowing through recommendations — but FR-5's comp comparison and the AC-5 comp-gate are unmet. LOW (traceability, not a live defect).

### ENH-015 — Auto-generate is idempotent-by-skip but offers no regenerate/preview; downstream `IntegrationRaised` event has no replay/outbox
- **Type:** ENH · **Title:** Two observations. (a) `auto-generate` correctly skips employees who already have a recommendation in the cycle (re-running produced created=0, skipped=all) — good idempotency — but there is no way to *refresh* suggestions after a rule change (HR must delete recs first), and no server-side rule-precedence *preview* step (TC-010-02 step 2 expects a preview "BEFORE applying"; the API applies+persists Draft directly). (b) On final approval an immutable `IntegrationRaised` event is appended and `IRecommendationIntegrationService.RaiseAsync` is invoked, but it's a no-op seam (BR-6 "not wired") with no outbox/replay — when Core HR/Payroll/Training wiring lands, an idempotent outbox would be needed for exactly-once downstream delivery (the seam currently fires inline, post-commit, with no retry record).
- **Module/US:** Performance / US-PRF-010 (TC-PRF-010-02, TC-PRF-010-10). **Why it matters:** keeps auto-gen re-runnable after rule edits and makes the eventual downstream integration exactly-once-safe. **Suggested direction:** add a preview/dry-run mode to auto-generate; add an outbox row for the IntegrationRaised seam so the deferred BR-6 wiring is replay-safe. Not a defect — do not auto-apply.

## US-PAY-002 — Assign Salary Structure to Employee (test-runner, 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API run)

Scope: 12 functional TCs (TC-PAY-002-01..12) + 4 isolation TCs (TC-PAY-ISO-005..008), executed API-layer (curl + JWT) against http://localhost:5000, acme tenant. FE (:4200) + Docker down → UI/a11y/perf-browser/Testcontainers arms BLOCKED. Routes discovered: `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments/preview`, `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments`, `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments/bulk`, `GET /api/v1/payroll/employees/{id}/compensation`, `GET /api/v1/payroll/employees/{id}/revision-history` — all `[RequirePermission("Payroll.Configure")]` (Tenant Admin only; HR/Manager hold zero payroll perms → see BUG-060). Seed already present: FT_IN (active, BASIC 40%GROSS / HRA 20%BASIC / CONV fixed 24000 / SPECIAL fixed 288000 → balances exactly at CTC 600000), LEG_24 (inactive), SR_FT (active). NOTE: implementation has NO automatic CTC balancer (SPECIAL is fixed, not a residual) — structures only "balance" at the CTC their fixed components were designed for.

### ISSUE-151 — Salary-assignment POST returns 200 OK, not 201 Created (REST contract drift)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · WONTFIX (LOW-tier triage 2026-07-18 — reason in LOW-TIER-TRIAGE.md §B)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-002 / TC-PAY-002-01 (also -02, -05)
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments` returns 200 OK on resource creation; TCs + REST convention expect 201 Created with a Location header.
- **Root cause:** `EmployeeSalaryController.Assign` returns `Ok(...)` (HTTP 200) on success rather than `Created(...)`. Confidence 99% (read `EmployeeSalaryController.cs:58` — `return ... : Ok(ApiResponse<CtcBreakdownDto>.Ok(result.Value!));`; the `[ProducesResponseType(... Status200OK)]` attribute confirms 200 is intentional). No exception in log; pure design choice.
- **Reproduction steps:** TA token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`; `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments` with a valid body → HTTP 200 (body is the CTC breakdown, not the created entity, and no Location header).
- **Evidence:** `HTTP 200` on assign (TC-PAY-002-01 step 4); response body = `CtcBreakdownDto` not the created `employee_salary_component` rows.
- **Severity rationale:** Cosmetic/contract-only; clients keying off `success:true` work fine; no functional impact.

### BUG-070 — No automatic CTC balancer: a single component override (AC-3) is rejected unless the user manually re-balances another component
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #178, merged 2026-07-06; fixed + regression-tested; fix-campaign close-out)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-002 / TC-PAY-002-02 (AC-3); also affects TC-PAY-002-01/-06 premises
- **Title:** The spec (FR-2 "auto-calculate component values from CTC", AC-3 override of one component, UI/UX S8 "CTC breakdown … balancer", multiple TCs referencing a "Special Allowance / CTC balancer") implies a residual/balancer component that absorbs the difference so the sum always equals CTC. The implementation has NO balancer — `CtcBreakdownCalculator` resolves each component from its own fixed/percentage rule and `AssignInternalAsync` hard-rejects (400 `ctc_sum_mismatch`) when the resulting sum deviates >±1 from CTC. Overriding just HRA (60000 vs calculated 48000) on FT_IN → sum 612000 vs CTC 600000 → 400. The HR user must manually override a SECOND component (e.g. SPECIAL) to re-balance, defeating the point of a single targeted override.
- **Root cause:** `SPECIAL` is seeded as a `Fixed`-method component (defaultValue 288000), not a residual balancer; `CtcBreakdownCalculator.ResolveRule` has no "remainder = CTC − sum(others)" method, and `AssignInternalAsync` (`SalaryAssignmentService.cs:243`) enforces FR-6 tolerance strictly. So the structure only "balances" at the exact CTC its fixed components were designed for (600000 for FT_IN). Confidence 95% (read `CtcBreakdownCalculator.cs` ResolveRule — only Fixed/PercentageOfGross/PercentageOfBasic/Formula; no residual method — and confirmed empirically: HRA-only override → 400 `ctc_sum_mismatch`; HRA+SPECIAL override → 200). No exception in log (clean 400). Whether this is a true defect vs. a deliberate "components must be authored to balance" design is a product decision — but it contradicts the written ACs/FRs/UI-UX of US-PAY-002, hence BUG not ISSUE.
- **Reproduction steps:** TA token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`. `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments` with FT_IN, CTC 600000, single override `{HRA: 60000}` → HTTP 400 `ctc_sum_mismatch` ("612000 does not match … 600000"). Add a second override `{SPECIAL: 276000}` → HTTP 200, persisted.
- **Evidence:** Preview with HRA-only override: `balanced:false, totalAnnualEarnings:612000`. Assign: `400 {"code":"ctc_sum_mismatch","message":"The sum of earning components (612000) does not match the declared CTC (600000) within the ±1 tolerance."}`. Two-override assign: `HTTP 200`, DB rows `HRA 60000 is_override=t, SPECIAL 276000 is_override=t, BASIC 240000 f, CONV 24000 f`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — assignment still works when components are authored/overridden to balance, and CTC-derived percentage structures (no fixed comps) balance naturally; but the documented single-override UX (AC-3) and any structure with a fixed allowance is unusable at off-design CTCs without manual rebalancing. Contained to override/varied-CTC flows, not the happy path.

### ISSUE-152 — Declared annual CTC accepts >2 decimal places (no numeric(18,2) input normalization/rejection)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · PARTIALLY RESOLVED (>2dp rejected, PR #363; JSON-string-numeric coercion = global NumberHandling → needs-decision) 2026-07-18
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-002 / TC-PAY-002-06 (step 6)
- **Title:** `annualCtc` with 3 decimal places (e.g. 600000.555) is accepted by both preview and assign without normalization or a validation error; TC-PAY-002-06 expects rejection or normalization to 2 dp per the numeric(18,2) contract.
- **Root cause:** No precision/scale validation on `annualCtc` before it enters `CtcBreakdownCalculator`/`AssignInternalAsync`. Derived component amounts ARE rounded to 2 dp (Math.Round AwayFromZero), but the declared CTC itself is used verbatim in the FR-6 tolerance check and echoed back at full precision. Confidence 90% (preview echoes `annualCtc:600000.555`; no validator rejects it; no log line). Persisted component amounts remain valid 2-dp, so DB integrity is not breached — only the declared CTC scale is unguarded.
- **Reproduction steps:** TA token + `acme`; `POST /api/v1/payroll/salary-assignments/preview` with `annualCtc:600000.555` → HTTP 200, body `annualCtc:600000.555`.
- **Evidence:** preview response `success:true, annualCtc:600000.555`. (Contrast: NaN and "600000 OR 1=1" → 400; zero/negative → "Annual CTC must be greater than zero".)
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — derived amounts still round to 2 dp and persist correctly; the unguarded scale only affects the declared-CTC echo + tolerance arithmetic by sub-cent amounts. Defense-in-depth/contract tidiness, no data corruption.

> ISSUE-152 addendum (TC-PAY-002-10): `annualCtc` also accepts JSON-string numerics like `"1e9"` and `"600000"` (System.Text.Json coerces them) rather than strictly rejecting non-numeric-typed input. Same lax-numeric-parsing class as above; LOW. SQLi/XSS in the `reason` field are safely stored as literal parameterized text (table intact, no schema leak) — security core PASSES.

### Isolation verdict (US-PAY-002 ISO-005..008) — salary-assignment surface is SELF-PROTECTED; does NOT extend BUG-003 (read + WRITE)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** (no new defect) — references existing BUG-003 (US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware JWT-vs-`X-Tenant-Subdomain` mismatch). NOT re-filed.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-002 / TC-PAY-ISO-005, -006, -007, -008
- **Finding:** The salary-assignment surface (preview, assign, bulk, compensation, revision-history) is fully tenant-isolated on BOTH reads and writes, INCLUDING under the BUG-003 mismatch (acme JWT + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal`):
  - **READ (ISO-005):** spoofed compensation GET → 404 `no_active_assignment`; revision-history GET → 200 with empty `[]`. No acme salary/revision data leaked under the techoneglobal context.
  - **WRITE (ISO-007) — the key arm:** spoofed assign to an acme employee (John Doe) under techoneglobal context → 404 `employee_not_found`, John Doe's esc rows unchanged (8→8). The assignment's employee-existence check (`Employees.AnyAsync(e.Id == employeeId)`) runs under the resolved tenant's EF global query filter, so a cross-tenant target is invisible → write rejected. `tenant_id` is server-stamped (TenantInterceptor); the request DTOs (`AssignSalaryStructureRequest`/`BulkAssignEntryDto`) carry NO `tenantId` field, so foreign-tenant injection is structurally impossible.
  - **Missing/unknown tenant (ISO-006):** no header → 400; unknown subdomain → 404; valid acme control → 200/201-equiv. No data read/written without a resolvable context.
  - **Cache (ISO-008):** no caching layer in `SalaryAssignmentService` — preview computed on-demand under the tenant filter; the TC's CONDITIONAL no-shared-cache-key assertion holds vacuously.
- **Root cause / proof:** Serilog RequestId `0HNMJDO06B26P` for the spoofed write shows `TenantId=019ef3c3...` (techoneglobal) and EF SQL `WHERE ... e.tenant_id = @ef_filter__TenantId AND e.id = @input_EmployeeId` returning no row → 404. Confidence 99% (log + DB before/after both confirm no cross-tenant write). Confirms the prior runner's READ-self-protected note and extends it: WRITE is self-protected too. The BUG-003 mismatch IS honored (tenant resolves to the header value), but because every salary operation is gated on the target employee/structure existing in the resolved tenant, BUG-003 yields no exploitable cross-tenant read OR write here — unlike the payroll-CONFIG surface (US-PAY-001) where config rows are directly addressable.

The entire US-PAY-003 story is written from the HR Officer's perspective ("As an HR Officer, I want to initiate and execute a monthly payroll run"; AC-1/precondition "HR Officer has Payroll.Run permission") yet that role cannot. Confidence: 95% (read the catalog + live 403 for hr@acme.test/manager@acme.test, 202 only for tenantadmin@acme.test). Same class as BUG-060 (HR lacks Payroll.Configure) — payroll permissions are TenantAdmin-centric vs the story personas.

- **Evidence:** HR initiate -> 403, MGR -> 403, EMP -> 403, TA -> 202/409. Catalog: HROfficer block has zero `Payroll.*` entries.

Not CRIT (a TenantAdmin/HRManager CAN run payroll, so the feature is reachable) but it breaks the primary persona's primary flow.

### ISSUE-153 — Idempotency-Key replay returns 409, not the original runId/202 (FR-9 contract not met)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #283, 2026-07-13) — `PayrollRunService.InitiateAsync` now returns the EXISTING run (success) when the same idempotency key is replayed for the SAME period (true idempotent replay, no duplicate run), instead of a 409. A key reused for a DIFFERENT period still 409s `duplicate_idempotency_key` (a key must identify one request — avoids silently returning the wrong period's run). The finding's own note that the code comment had been reworded to claim idempotent-return while the code still 409'd is now genuinely fixed. Test: same-period replay → same RunId + exactly one run row; different-period test intact. · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 / TC-PAY-003-10
- **Title:** Replaying `POST /api/v1/payroll/runs` with a previously-used `Idempotency-Key` returns 409 `duplicate_idempotency_key` instead of the SAME runId with 202/200. FR-9/TC-10 step 2 require an idempotent replay to return the existing run, not an error.
- **Root cause:** `PayrollRunService.InitiateAsync` — the idempotency branch (`existingByKey is not null`) returns `Result.Failure(... 409, "duplicate_idempotency_key")` rather than re-returning the existing run's `PayrollRunAcceptedDto`. The duplicate-run is correctly prevented (no second row, no second job), but a true idempotency key contract returns the prior result on replay so a client retry/double-click is transparent. Confidence: 95% (code + live: first POST 202 runId R, replay same key 409 with no runId). 
- **Reproduction:** `POST .../runs` with `Idempotency-Key: 2222...` for a locked period → 202 runId R1. Replay identical request → 409 `duplicate_idempotency_key`, body `data:null`. Client cannot recover R1 from the response.
- **Evidence:** first: success True runId 019f03ae-1350-...; replay: success False code duplicate_idempotency_key, data None.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the safety goal (no duplicate run) IS met; the gap is the contract/UX (a retrying client gets an error instead of the idempotent original). Not HIGH because no data corruption or duplicate run occurs.

### ISSUE-154 — No cancel / re-run endpoint for a payroll run; FR-7 re-run and BR-6 Cancelled transition unreachable via API
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #287, 2026-07-13) — added `POST runs/{id}/cancel` + `POST runs/{id}/rerun` (`Payroll.Run`-gated) → `IPayrollRunService.CancelAsync`/`RerunAsync`. **CANCEL** removes the run's slips + reverts its adjustments to Pending (via a new shared `IPayrollSlipCleaner` extracted from the processor's cleanup) + sets `Status=Cancelled`, freeing the period's partial-unique-index slot (`status <> 'Cancelled'`, verified string-stored). **RE-RUN** re-enqueues reprocessing of a `ReviewPending` run (ProcessAsync is idempotent — clears+replaces slips). Guards: cancel rejects Finalized/Cancelled/**Processing** (409, closes an in-flight race the enforcer caught); re-run rejects Finalized/in-flight/Cancelled/non-ReviewPending; `ProcessAsync` now bails on Cancelled (no resurrection). **FE:** Cancel/Re-run actions on the run-detail view (gated to the BE matrix) + 409 error-code messages. Tests: 9 BE (cancel-cleanup+free-period, rerun-replaces-slips, guard matrix, Processing-race, resurrection guard) + 12 FE. BE + FE green; integration-enforcer CONNECTED, test-authenticator AUTHENTIC. Follow-ups (P7): FE 409 double-toast, deferred Hangfire job-deletion, Postgres cancel-index test, TC-PAY-003-02 QA doc. · **Layer:** BE+FE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 / TC-PAY-003-02 (step 3), TC-PAY-003-08, TC-PAY-003-09 (step 5)
- **Title:** The payroll-run API surface (`PayrollRunsController`) exposes only initiate + reads. There is no endpoint to CANCEL a run (BR-6 "any pre-Finalized -> Cancelled") nor to RE-RUN a ReviewPending/Cancelled period (FR-7 "system SHALL support re-running ... previous slip data is replaced"). The processor's `ProcessAsync` *implements* re-run slip-replacement (`RemoveExistingSlipsAsync`) and FR-7 logic, but no controller route triggers it; and nothing transitions a run to Cancelled.
- **Root cause:** `PayrollRunsController` has POST `runs` (initiate) + 4 GETs only. The approval controller (US-PAY-004) adds submit/approve/reject/return/finalize but still NO cancel and NO re-run trigger. So FR-7 (re-run) and the BR-6 Cancelled state are dead at the API edge. Confidence: 90% (grepped all payroll controllers; processor has the logic, no caller). 
- **Reproduction:** No `POST .../runs/{id}/cancel` or `.../rerun` route exists; `grep -rn cancel src/backend/.../Payroll*Controller.cs` → none. TC-02 step 3 (cancel a run, then a new run for the period is accepted) and TC-08 steps 3-5 (cancel, re-run ReviewPending/Cancelled) cannot be exercised.
- **Evidence:** controller route inventory (initiate + list/get/summary/progress); approval controller (submit/approve/reject/return/finalize). No cancel/re-run anywhere.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-7 (re-run with slip replacement) and the Cancelled lifecycle are explicit story requirements that are unreachable; a stuck/incorrect non-finalized run cannot be cancelled or re-run by HR. Contained because a finalized run's correction path (adjustments, US-PAY-007) does exist.

### ISSUE-155 — LOP `calculation_basis` display rounds the daily rate, so "rate/day x days" doesn't equal the persisted LOP amount
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 / TC-PAY-003-05, TC-PAY-003-07
- **Title:** The LOP slip-detail `calculation_basis` shows e.g. "952.38/day x 20 days" while the persisted LOP `amount` is 19047.62. 952.38 x 20 = 19047.60, a 0.02 mismatch vs the stored figure.
- **Root cause:** the engine computes LOP at full precision ((20000/21) x 20 = 400000/21 = 19047.619... -> 19047.62 rounded once at the end — the correct, drift-free approach), but the displayed basis pre-rounds the daily rate to 952.38 for human display. The amount is right; only the human-readable basis text is internally inconsistent (rounded-rate x days != amount). Confidence: 92% (slip: amount 19047.62, basis "952.38/day x 20 days"; reconciliation gross-ded=net=signed-sum all EXACT at 30952.38).
- **Reproduction:** run payroll for an employee with LOP days where monthly_basic isn't divisible by working_days (basic 20000, working 21, lop 20); inspect the LOP detail line.
- **Evidence:** Loss of Pay|Deduction|19047.62|952.38/day x 20 days. Penny reconciliation otherwise exact.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — purely a display/explainability nit; the persisted amount and all slip totals reconcile to the penny. Could confuse an HR reviewer who re-multiplies the shown rate.

### ISSUE-156 — Mid-month joiner pro-ration uses CALENDAR-day fraction, not actual WORKING days (BR-4 deviation)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #282, 2026-07-13) — `ProRataPaidDays` now counts SHIFT working-days over `DOJ..monthEnd` (via `ShiftScheduleResolver`), and the pro-ration DENOMINATOR fallback was made shift-aware too (single-basis, fixing a mixed shift/calendar factor the first cut introduced). Tests assert PaidDays==9 (Mon-Fri) / ==11 (Mon-Sat, shift-set proof) + GrossEarnings==9000 (9/22 not 9/30). · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 / TC-PAY-003-06
- **Title:** `PayrollRunProcessor.ProRataPaidDays` pro-rates a mid-month joiner by the CALENDAR-day fraction of the month employed (`(monthEnd-doj+1)/(monthEnd-monthStart+1) x workingDaysInMonth`), but BR-4 specifies pro-ration on "actual working days from the date of joining." For a 22-working-day / 31-calendar-day May, a joiner on the 16th gets `22 x 16/31 = 11.35` working days rather than the true working-days-from-the-16th count.
- **Root cause:** the method's own comment acknowledges it: "Working-days granularity is the attendance module's domain; for the joiner case we pro-rate the working-days baseline by the fraction of the month actually employed (BR-4)." Calendar-day fraction != working-day fraction whenever weekends/holidays aren't evenly distributed. Confidence: 80% (code-analysis only — could not execute: no active acme employee has a DOJ inside a locked, runnable pay period, and seeding one requires mutating employee date_of_joining which is out of minimal-seed scope).
- **Reproduction:** assign a structure to an active employee whose `date_of_joining` falls mid-pay-period (e.g. 2026-05-16) for a locked May run; inspect the slip `working_days` / pro-rated gross vs the true working-days-from-DOJ.
- **Evidence:** `ProRataPaidDays` formula uses `DayNumber` (calendar) differences, not a working-day calendar.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — produces a materially wrong pro-rated salary whenever the employed window's weekend/holiday density differs from the month average; affects real money for every mid-month joiner. Not HIGH because it only triggers for joiners and the error is bounded by the weekend distribution.

### ISSUE-157 — Mid-month SEPARATOR not pro-rated when attendance has no row; separated employee can be paid a full month (BR-5 gap)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED-for-reachable (PR #282, 2026-07-13; see ISSUE-294) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** `ProRataPaidDays` gained a symmetric leaver branch — a `status_change→Terminated` `EmploymentHistory` effective date in-period bounds paid days to SHIFT working-days `monthStart..terminationDate` (engine-side guard for the no-attendance-row case). Test: leaver term Sep 10, no attendance → PaidDays==8, <22. **⚠ Reachability caveat:** the run selects only `Active`/`Probation`, so this fires only for an employee whose termination is recorded in EmploymentHistory but whose Status is still Active at run time (the realistic mid-month case). A fully `Terminated`-status employee is excluded from the regular run; their final pay depends on the F&F settlement path (`IPayrollFnFIntegration`, currently a **LogOnly stub**) → filed as **ISSUE-294** (pre-existing, not a regression).
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 / TC-PAY-003-06
- **Title:** Separation pro-ration (BR-5: "pro-rated ... up to the last working day") is NOT computed in the run engine; `ProRataPaidDays` only handles the JOINER case (DOJ after month start). For a mid-month separator the code relies entirely on the attendance pull's `TotalWorkingDays`. If attendance has no row for that employee (or the period pull degrades to empty), the employee falls back to the full-month working-days baseline — i.e. a full month's pay despite separating mid-period.
- **Root cause:** `ProRataPaidDays` returns `null` (full month) for any employee whose DOJ <= month start; there is no symmetric last-working-day check. The method comment states "Separation pro-ration (BR-5) is driven by the attendance working-days ... when present" — so BR-5 is only honored if attendance happens to carry the reduced working-days, with no engine-side guard from the termination date. Confidence: 82% (code-analysis only — same seeding constraint as ISSUE-156; not executed).
- **Reproduction:** set an active employee's last-working-day mid-period (e.g. 2026-05-15), no attendance rows, run a locked May payroll → expect ~half pay; impl would pay full month.
- **Evidence:** `ProRataPaidDays` has only the joiner branch; no termination/last-working-day handling.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — overpays a separating employee when attendance data is absent (the common case for someone who has left and stopped clocking in); real-money correctness gap. Not HIGH because it depends on the attendance pull being empty for that employee.

### US-PAY-003 isolation arms (TC-PAY-ISO-009..012) — verdict (references BUG-003, NOT re-filed)
- **ISO-010 (run/slip READ isolation): CLEAN / self-protected.** acme TA token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `GET /payroll/runs/{acme-runId}` 404 `run_not_found`; `GET /payroll/runs` (list) under tg context returns 0 runs (acme's runs NOT shown). Matched-context control (acme/acme) reads RUN5 200. No-bearer 401. The EF global query filter scopes run/slip reads to the resolved tenant, so a mismatched/foreign context yields 404, never a cross-tenant run/payslip. Reads do NOT extend BUG-003 (unlike US-PAY-001 config rows which leaked on read).
- **ISO-011 (run WRITE isolation): BUG-003 EXTENDS to the payroll-RUN write surface.** acme TA token (user 019efa61 = tenantadmin@acme.test) + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` + a tg attendance lock → `POST /payroll/runs` `{payMonth:2,payYear:2030}` returned 202 and created a `payroll_run` **stamped tenant_id=techoneglobal** with **initiated_by = the acme TA user**. The run even processed to ReviewPending under tg. An acme-authenticated principal wrote (and ran) a payroll run into another tenant purely by spoofing the subdomain header. Same root cause/locus as BUG-003 (US-AUTH-007 `TenantResolutionMiddleware`: the resolved tenant comes from the spoofable `X-Tenant-Subdomain`, never validated against the JWT tenant claim). The body cannot inject a foreign tenant_id (the InitiatePayrollRunRequest DTO carries no tenant_id — TenantInterceptor stamps from context), so ISO-011 step 1 (body injection) is correctly defended; the leak is the header-vs-token mismatch only. **Residue from this probe (1 tg run + its attendance lock) hard-deleted, tg verified back to 0 runs / 0 Feb-2030 locks; the pre-existing techoneglobal EMP-0001 "Cross Write" orphan was NOT touched.**
- **ISO-009 (cross-tenant COMPUTE isolation): CLEAN within a correctly-resolved context.** Once the tenant is resolved, the worker (`PayrollRunProcessor`) fetches employees/components/attendance through the EF global query filter, so a run computes only the resolved tenant's employees and stamps every payroll_run/slip/detail with that tenant_id (verified: the spoofed tg run stamped tg, the acme runs stamped acme; acme run-log lists only acme employees). The only cross-tenant exposure is the resolution-layer spoof (ISO-011), not a compute-pipeline bleed.
- **ISO-012 (SignalR / lock / cache isolation): CONDITIONAL / mostly vacuous — infra not implemented.** SignalR progress + email notification are a log-only seam (`IPayrollNotificationService.NotifyRunReadyForReviewAsync`; no real SignalR group/email) — no cross-tenant event channel exists to leak (FR-6 real-time deferred). No distributed lock (NFR-3): the service uses a partial unique index `ix_payroll_run_one_active_per_period` on (tenant, year, month) for non-cancelled runs + an in-service pre-check; the key is inherently tenant+period-scoped so tenant A's lock does NOT block tenant B's same period (assertion holds structurally — the unique index includes tenant_id). No Redis structure cache (NFR-7): reads always go through the tenant-filtered DB query, so no shared/global cache key exists to cross tenants. The progress endpoint is a tenant-scoped DB read (covered by ISO-010's 404).

### US-PAY-004 tenant-isolation result (NO new finding — payslip surface is SELF-PROTECTED, NOT a BUG-003 locus)
- The payslip read + write surfaces are tenant-isolated; **BUG-003 does NOT extend here**.
- **Read (ISO-013/014):** e2e-scoped session (platform admin + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: e2e`) targeting acme's run → 404 on list, single-download, and download-all; acme-scoped reads the same run → 200 (positive control). acme-bearer + e2e-header mismatch → 404; + no header → 400 (fail-closed); + invalid subdomain → 404. All payslip queries pass through the EF global query filter on `payroll_run`/`payroll_slip`, so a cross-tenant run is simply invisible.
- **Write (ISO-015):** generate/regenerate take NO request body (runId in route only) → body-injected tenant_id is structurally impossible. The Hangfire job arg is `_tenantContext.TenantId` (server-derived, `PayslipGenerationService.cs:82`); the blob path is `{tenantId}` (from `IFileStorage`) + GUID-derived `payroll/{runId}/{employeeId}.pdf` (`PayslipStoragePath.ForSlip`). All 3 generated slips carry acme's tenant_id.
- **Path traversal (TC-07/NFR-6):** `employeeId`/`runId` are `:guid`-route-constrained; `PayslipStoragePath.ForSlip` builds the path from GUIDs only and `AssertSafe` rejects `..`/rooted paths — traversal is structurally impossible.
- **NFR-5 (no JS in PDF):** scanned a generated PDF for `/JavaScript /JS /OpenAction /Launch /EmbeddedFile` → 0 hits (the 9 `/AA` matches are all `/AAAAAA+Lato-Bold` font-subset prefixes, not Additional-Action dicts). PDF is static.

### ISSUE-163 — Payslip PDF download filename omits zero-padding on month (`_5_` not `_05_`)
- **Type**: ISSUE · **Severity**: LOW · **Status**: OPEN · **Layer**: BE
- **Module/US/TC**: Payroll / US-PAY-005 / TC-PAY-005-03 (also affects US-PAY-004 admin download — same shared helper)
- **Title**: `Content-Disposition` filename is `EMP-0001_5_2026.pdf` but the spec (TC-PAY-005-03 step 2, US-PAY-004 BR-5 `{EmployeeNo}_{PayMonth}_{PayYear}.pdf`) implies a 2-digit zero-padded month → expected `EMP-0001_05_2026.pdf`.
- **Root cause** (95%): `PayslipStoragePath.DownloadFileName` (HRM.Application/Common/Payroll/PayslipStoragePath.cs:25-31) interpolates `{payMonth}` as a raw int with no `:D2` format. Shared by both the employee self-service download and the admin download, so both are non-padded.
- **Reproduction**: `GET /api/v1/payroll/my-payslips/{mayPayslipId}/pdf` as employee@acme.test (acme) → response header `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=EMP-0001_5_2026.pdf`.
- **Evidence**: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=EMP-0001_5_2026.pdf; filename*=UTF-8''EMP-0001_5_2026.pdf` (HTTP 200, application/pdf).
- **Severity rationale**: Cosmetic — file still downloads correctly and opens; only the filename text differs from the documented pattern. No functional/security impact. Spec could equally be read as not requiring padding; flagged as drift.

### ISSUE-164 — My-Payslips "search by pay period" (FR-6) is not implemented; only the year filter exists
- **Type**: ISSUE · **Severity**: LOW · **Status**: OPEN · **Layer**: BE
- **Module/US/TC**: Payroll / US-PAY-005 / TC-PAY-005-06 (steps 5 & 6)
- **Title**: FR-6 requires "filtering by year AND searching by pay period." The endpoint supports only `?year=`; there is no pay-period/month search param. `?search=`, `?month=`, `?q=` are silently ignored.
- **Root cause** (98%): `GetMyPayslipsQuery` (HRM.Application/Features/Payroll/Queries/MyPayslipQueries.cs) and `MyPayslipService.ListMineAsync` (MyPayslipService.cs:48-100) accept only `year/page/pageSize`; no month/search filter is wired. The controller `List` action exposes only `year,page,pageSize` query params.
- **Reproduction**: as employee@acme.test (acme) `GET /api/v1/payroll/my-payslips?search=May%202026&month=5&q=May` → returns ALL 3 slips (months [5,4,3]) — params ignored. There is no way to search a single pay period.
- **Evidence**: `?year=2026` → 3 items (works); `?search=May 2026&month=5&q=May` → 3 items (ignored, no filtering). Default pageSize=12, over-max clamps to 12, page beyond data → empty 200 (all correct).
- **Severity rationale**: LOW — the year filter (primary FR-6 half) works and pagination is correct; pay-period search is a secondary convenience filter, low blast radius. Could also be argued the FE does client-side search over the 12/page set; backend search is simply absent.

### ISSUE-165 — Payslip detail shows CURRENT department/designation, not point-in-time (BR-2 violation)
- **Type**: ISSUE · **Severity**: MED · **Status**: RESOLVED (PR #286, 2026-07-13) — added nullable `department_snapshot`/`designation_snapshot` columns to `payroll_slip` (CLI migration `Payroll_PayslipPointInTimeSnapshot`, applied on startup), captured (as resolved NAME strings) at generation in `PayrollRunProcessor`, and switched the read sites (`MyPayslipService.GetMineAsync`, `PayslipGenerationService.ListForRunAsync`, `PayslipBatchRenderer.BuildModel`) to prefer the snapshot with LIVE fallback when null (legacy slips). No back-fill (never bakes today's dept onto old slips). Tests: snapshot stamped at generation; **mutate-then-reread proves point-in-time (moves emp to Finance/Manager → slip still shows Engineering/Engineer)**; null-snapshot live fallback. BE suite green; integration-enforcer CONNECTED (migration clean, no missed read surface), test-authenticator AUTHENTIC. **Follow-up (LOW → P7):** PDF-regenerate + list-DTO snapshot-preference branches wired but not directly test-covered. · **Layer**: BE
- **Module/US/TC**: Payroll / US-PAY-005 / TC-PAY-005-07 (steps 2-3, BR-2)
- **Title**: A historical payslip's employee header (department, designation) is resolved from the LIVE Employee record at read time, so after a department transfer every past payslip retroactively shows the new department — violating BR-2 ("each historical payslip retains its point-in-time department/designation").
- **Root cause** (90%): `MyPayslipService.GetMineAsync` (MyPayslipService.cs:127-140) loads `Employees.DepartmentId`/`JobTitleId` for the CURRENT employee row, then resolves `Departments.Name` / `JobTitles.TitleName` live. The `payroll_slip` / `payroll_slip_detail` tables store no department/designation snapshot, so there is no point-in-time source to read from. Confirmed by schema: payroll_slip has no department_id/job_title_id column.
- **Reproduction**: Conceptual + code-confirmed (could not fully exercise live — would require transferring EMP-0001's department then re-reading an older slip; schema proves no snapshot exists). As employee@acme.test, `GET /api/v1/payroll/my-payslips/{anySlipId}` always returns the employee's current Department ("Engineering") regardless of the slip's pay period.
- **Evidence**: payroll_slip columns (DB): no department/designation column. Service reads `e.DepartmentId` from current Employees row. May-2026 detail returned department "Engineering" sourced from the live record.
- **Severity rationale**: MED — payslips are financial records of record; showing the wrong (current) department on a historical payslip is a data-accuracy/compliance concern, but salary figures themselves are correct and stored on the slip. Contained to the header display fields.

## US-PAY-006 — Statutory Deductions Configuration (test-runner, 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API run)
Scope: API-layer (curl + JWT, acme tenant) execution of TC-PAY-006-01..12 + TC-PAY-ISO-021..024. Routes: `/api/v1/payroll/statutory-rules` (List/GetById/Create/Update/Delete/clone-fiscal-year/test-calculation/fiscal-years), perm `Payroll.Configure` (Tenant Admin only). FE(:4200) DOWN + Docker unavailable → UI/a11y (TC-12) + cross-browser arms BLOCKED. Findings start BUG-072 / ISSUE-166 / ENH-017.

### TC-PAY-006-04 — PASS (FR-6 slab contiguity, create + update)
- All four invalid sets rejected 400: overlap [0-250K,200K-500K,500K-1M], gap [0-250K,300K-500K,500K-null], non-zero-start [100K-250K,...], zero-width [250K-250K] (latter also returns the explicit "upper bound must be greater than its lower bound" message). Valid contiguous set [0-250K,250-500K,500-1M,1M-null] accepted 201 with 4 ordered slabs. PUT introducing an overlap on the same rule also rejected 400 — contiguity is enforced on update too (Step 6). Note: the API returns a single generic contiguity message rather than identifying the specific offending range/gap (the inline-editor red-highlight + per-row identification is a FE concern, BLOCKED here). Residue (FY 2099-A rule + slabs) hard-deleted; baseline = 3 fixture rules confirmed.

### TC-PAY-006-06 — PASS (BR-2 taxable income, BR-6 below-threshold skip, floor) — 1 ISSUE (FR-7)
- BR-2 EXACT: gross 800K − exempt 50K − declared 100K = taxable 650K; progressive tax over FY26-27 slabs [0-300K@0, 300-600K@6, 600K-1.2M@18, 1.2M+@28] = 0 + 300K×6% (18000) + 50K×18% (9000) = **27,000** ✓. Tax base is the reduced 650K, never raw gross (Step 2 ✓). Below-threshold taxable 240K → tax 0, no line (Step 3 ✓). Boundary: taxable exactly 300K → tax 0; 300,001 → 0.06 tiny positive (Step 5 ✓). Exemptions exceeding gross floor taxable at 0 → tax 0, no negative base (Step 6 ✓).
- **Step 4 (explicit per-employee "tax-exempt status" flag)**: not exercisable via this config/test-calc API — BR-6 is realized only as the below-threshold (taxable within the 0% slab) skip, which covers the threshold case. A standalone tax-exempt-employee flag is an employee/payroll-run concern, not a statutory-config surface; functionally covered by the 0%-slab skip. Not filed as a defect.
- **ISSUE-166** (see below): FR-7 standard-deduction / Section-80C-equivalent exemption has NO stored config entity — exemptions are only ad-hoc per-call (`declaredMonthlyExemptions`/`exemptEarnings`). The TC precondition ("a standard-deduction exemption configured") cannot be satisfied.

### TC-PAY-006-07 — FAIL (BR-5 YTD not implemented) / BR-8 PASS — 1 ISSUE (ISSUE-167)
- BR-8 EXACT (Steps 1,2,6): EPF rule annual ceiling 180K → monthly ceiling 15K (180K/12); basic 20K capped to 15K × 12% = **1,800** employee + 1,800 employer (NOT 2,400 on the uncapped 20K). Basis label "Basic, ceiling 15000/mo". 12-month cumulative = 12×1,800 = 21,600 (per-period cap each month, no single month consumes the annual cap). Step 6 ("custom statutory rule ceiling, not annual/12"): only the annual/12 derivation exists — there is no per-period-override field, so the configured annual ÷ 12 is the only ceiling path (acceptable single-country Phase-1 behavior; not separately filed).
- **FAIL — BR-5 (Steps 3,4,5)**: year-to-date cumulative progressive tax is **not implemented**. `IStatutoryDeductionResolver.ResolveAsync(payYear, payMonth, wage, fiscalYearOverride)` carries no prior-YTD income parameter; tax is computed monthly in isolation. A period that crosses a slab boundary mid-year is NOT split across the lower/higher marginal bands based on YTD position. → **ISSUE-167**.

### TC-PAY-006-08 — PASS (authz model) — confirms BUG-060; 1 doc-drift ISSUE (ISSUE-168)
- TenantAdmin (`Payroll.Configure`): LIST 200, POST create 201, test-calc 200 (AC-1/AC-2/FR-5). HR / Manager / Employee: **403 on every endpoint** incl test-calc (the configure-permission gate covers the read-only preview too). Unauthenticated: **401** on LIST + POST. No record created on any denied attempt (verified — TC08 residue traced only to the TenantAdmin create, hard-deleted).
- **NFR-4 audit (Step 6) — PASS**: every create writes a queryable `audit_logs` row `action=StatutoryRule.Created`, `resource_type=StatutoryRule`, `resource_id`, before=null/after=snapshot JSON, tenant-scoped. (Update would write StatutoryRule.Updated with before+after; verified the logger path in StatutoryRuleService.) This is a positive — statutory config audit is genuinely persisted AND readable (contrast with several other modules' write-only audit gaps).
- **HR Officer = 403 confirms BUG-060** (HR Officer holds ZERO payroll permissions). The StatutoryRulesController XML doc comment claims "Payroll.Configure (the catalog permission HR Officer / Tenant Admin already hold, matching the story's persona)" — this is **inaccurate**: HR holds no payroll perms, so only Tenant Admin can configure. Per-brief: not re-filing BUG-060; logging the controller-comment-vs-reality drift as **ISSUE-168** (LOW doc-drift). US-PAY-006 persona is "Tenant Admin / HR Officer" but HR is effectively locked out — a product-vs-RBAC mismatch tracked under BUG-060.

### TC-PAY-006-09 — FAIL (over-magnitude → 500) — BUG-072 + 1 ISSUE (ISSUE-169)
- XSS rule_name `<script>alert(1)</script>` (Step 1): stored as the literal JSON string, EF-parameterised, never executed at the API layer (no HTML context server-side; FE escaping is its responsibility, BLOCKED here) — acceptable.
- SQLi fiscal_year `2026'; DROP TABLE tax_slab;--` (Step 2): rejected 400 by the >10-char max-length rule; EF parameterises regardless. **tax_slab / statutory_rule tables verified intact** post-test.
- Rate bounds (Step 3): 150 → 400 "Slab rate must be between 0 and 100"; -5 → 400. ✓
- **Step 4 — over-precision rate 12.345 → silently stored as 12.35** (round-half-up by the numeric(5,2) cast), 201, no validation message → **ISSUE-169** (LOW: within the TC's "rejected OR rounded" tolerance, but the rounding is implicit/undocumented and a tax-rate precision drift; a field-level reject or explicit documented round is preferable).
- **Step 5a — over-magnitude slab amount 1e18 → HTTP 500** "An unexpected error occurred" instead of a 400 field error → **BUG-072 (HIGH)**. Root cause (Serilog RequestId `0HNMJGENHI022:00000001`, ~99%): `Npgsql.PostgresException 22003: numeric field overflow` at `apply_typmod` (numeric.c:8091) — the value exceeds numeric(18,2); `TaxSlabInputValidator` validates lower bound + ordering but has **no upper-magnitude bound**, so the overflow escapes `StatutoryRuleService.CreateAsync` → `SaveChangesAsync` → DbUpdateException → ExceptionHandlingMiddleware → generic 500. No row persisted (rolled back) and the error body is clean (no SQL/PII leak — Step 6 partial pass).
- **Step 5b — non-numeric "abc" → 400** (JSON deserialization field error, leaks the .NET type name `System.Nullable[System.Decimal]` + LineNumber in the body — minor verbosity, rolled into the same class; the request still fails closed). Step 6: errors carry no cross-tenant/PII data; the 5b body does expose framework type info (low-value to an attacker). Net: input is fail-closed, but the over-magnitude 500 is a real validation-coverage gap.

### TC-PAY-006-11 — FAIL (Update endpoint 500 + BR-7 retro-guard absent) — BUG-073 + ISSUE-170; FR-5 PASS

### BUG-072 — Over-magnitude tax-slab amount (> numeric(18,2)) crashes statutory-rule create with HTTP 500 instead of a 400 field error
- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #123, verified 2026-07-02) · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-006 / TC-PAY-006-09
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/payroll/statutory-rules` with a slab amount exceeding numeric(18,2) (e.g. `slabTo: 1e18`) returns a generic 500 instead of validating the magnitude with a 400.
- **Root cause:** `TaxSlabInputValidator` (CreateStatutoryRuleValidator.cs) validates `SlabFrom >= 0`, `RatePercentage 0-100`, and `SlabTo > SlabFrom`, but has **no upper-magnitude bound** for slab amounts. The over-range value reaches `StatutoryRuleService.CreateAsync` → `SaveChangesAsync` and Postgres throws `22003: numeric field overflow` (`apply_typmod`, numeric.c:8091), surfaced as `DbUpdateException` → ExceptionHandlingMiddleware → generic 500. Serilog RequestId `0HNMJGENHI022:00000001`. Confidence: 99% (logged exception + SQLSTATE).
- **Reproduction:** TenantAdmin acme → `POST .../statutory-rules` IncomeTax with `taxSlabs:[{slabFrom:0,slabTo:1000000000000000000,...},{slabFrom:1e18,slabTo:null,...}]` → HTTP 500 `{"message":"An unexpected error occurred."}`. No row persisted (rolled back).
- **Evidence:** HTTP 500; Serilog `Npgsql.PostgresException 22003: numeric field overflow` under StatutoryRulesController.Create.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a malformed (or fat-fingered) numeric input on a financial-config endpoint yields an unhandled 500; should be a clean 400. No corruption (rolls back) so not CRIT, but it is an input-validation coverage gap on a Must-Have surface and a poor client contract.

### BUG-073 — PUT update of any statutory rule throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException → HTTP 500; the Update endpoint is non-functional for all rule types
- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #128, verified 2026-07-02) · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-006 / TC-PAY-006-11 (also blocks TC-04 step 6 update-revalidation being observable beyond the 400 path)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/payroll/statutory-rules/{id}` returns 500 for BOTH income-tax (slab) and EPF (social-security) rules — editing a statutory rule is impossible via the API.
- **Root cause:** `StatutoryRuleService.UpdateAsync` (line 141) replaces owned children wholesale — `_dbContext.TaxSlabs.RemoveRange(rule.TaxSlabs)` / `SocialSecurityRules.Remove(...)` then rebuilds with new ids — but under `TenantTransactionBehavior` (line 60) the EF change-tracker emits a stale UPDATE against an already-removed child row, so `SaveChangesAsync` throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException: expected to affect 1 row(s), but actually affected 0`. Serilog RequestId `0HNMJGENHI028:00000001`. Confidence: 95% (logged exception + stack at UpdateAsync:141; reproduced 3× incl identical-payload edit). Likely the same InMemory-masks-Postgres class as prior payroll bugs — the integration tests may not exercise the real-Postgres owned-children replace under the tenant transaction.
- **Reproduction:** TenantAdmin acme → `PUT .../statutory-rules/019f03f8-6525-...` (FY25-26 IncomeTax) with any taxSlabs (changed OR identical) → 500. Same for the EPF rule `019f03f8-9e32-...` with socialSecurity. Fixtures verified intact (rolled back).
- **Evidence:** HTTP 500 ×3; Serilog `DbUpdateConcurrencyException ... actually affected 0 row(s)` at StatutoryRuleService.UpdateAsync:141 under TenantTransactionBehavior:60.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a core CRUD verb (edit a tax slab / EPF rate) is completely broken for the whole config surface; the only way to change a rule is delete-and-recreate. Not CRIT because reads/creates/clone/test-calc work and no data is corrupted, but the primary "configure/adjust statutory rules" flow is non-functional.

### ISSUE-166 — FR-7 standard-deduction / Section-80C-equivalent exemption has no stored configuration entity
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (superseded by the multi-country tax framework, 2026-07-14) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** superseded by TAX-2 configurable exemptions (#291) — `StatutoryExemption` per-country config entity (FlatAmount/PercentOfGross/PercentOfComponent + cap + IsAnnual) feeds `ComputeTaxableIncome`.

- **Root cause:** No exemption/rebate entity, table, or config endpoint exists (grep across Domain/Application/Infrastructure: zero `rebate`/`standardDeduction`/`Section80`/`ExemptionRule`). Taxable income = gross − exempt − declared is computed correctly, but the *configured* exemption framework FR-7 describes is absent. Confidence: 90% (code grep + DTO review).

- **Severity rationale:** MED — a named FR is unbuilt; exemptions still work as caller-supplied values so the calc is correct, but tenants cannot persist a standard-deduction/rebate policy as config (it must be recomputed and passed each run).

### ISSUE-167 — BR-5 year-to-date cumulative progressive tax is not implemented (monthly-isolation only)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (superseded by the multi-country tax framework, 2026-07-14) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** superseded by TAX-3 YTD-cumulative (#292) — per-country `StatutoryRule.IsCumulative` flag; annual bands + tax(cumulative-FY)−withheld-YTD; TaxableIncome/IncomeTaxWithheld persisted per slip.
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-006 / TC-PAY-006-07
- **Title:** Progressive income tax is computed per period in isolation; there is no YTD-cumulative-income input, so a period crossing a slab boundary mid-year is not split across marginal bands by YTD position (BR-5).
- **Root cause:** `IStatutoryDeductionResolver.ResolveAsync(payYear, payMonth, wage, fiscalYearOverride)` carries no prior-YTD parameter; `StatutoryCalculator.ComputeProgressiveTax` slabs the single-period taxable income only. Confidence: 90% (interface signature + resolver code; no YTD/cumulative refs in the statutory path).
- **Reproduction:** test-calc with a period income straddling a slab edge is taxed as if the whole taxable income started at 0 for that month — no YTD carry.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — for high earners crossing bands mid-year, monthly-isolation can over-/under-withhold versus the YTD method within a year (final annual liability still reconciles if total taxable income is presented once). A correctness/withholding-accuracy gap, not a crash.

### BUG-074 · ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (#281) · BE — US-PAY-007 BR-3 negative-net warning at create time is effectively unreachable
> **RESOLVED (PR #281, 2026-07-13):** `WouldDriveNetNegativeAsync` no longer returns false when no persisted slip exists — it projects net from the employee's current salary structure (reusing `PayrollRunProcessor.BuildComponentInputs` + `PayrollSlipCalculator.Compute`), so the advisory fires for future-period adjustments. **Conservative** (baseline omits statutory → never false-warns, can under-warn; documented). Load-bearing test asserts no-slip path + warning; would fail on old code. Follow-ups filed: exact-statutory projection + `BulkCreateAsync` advisory gap (P7).
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-007 / TC-PAY-007-02, TC-PAY-007-03
- **Title:** `negativeNetWarning` only fires when a *computed slip already exists* for the effective period; for any normally-created adjustment it always returns false, so the BR-3 "warn HR before a deduction drives net negative" surface never actually warns.
- **Root cause (90%):** `PayrollAdjustmentService.WouldDriveNetNegativeAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/PayrollAdjustmentService.cs:449-471`) early-returns `false` when there is no persisted `PayrollSlip` for `(employeeId, year, month)`. Open future periods have no slip yet → warning never computed; targeting a Finalized period defers (BR-7) to the *next* period which also has no slip → still no warning. Net: the only way to get a warning is to re-target a period that already produced a slip, which the BR-7 deferral logic prevents. Verified: 999,999 deduction (Aug, no slip) → `negativeNetWarning=false`; 50,000 deduction targeting finalized June → deferred to July, `negativeNetWarning=false`. The against-slip projection (lines 466-469) is correct but unreachable in normal flow.
- **Reproduction:** acme, tenantadmin (Payroll.Configure). `POST /api/v1/payroll/adjustments {employeeId:EMP-0001, adjustmentType:Deduction, amount:999999, applicablePayMonth:8, applicablePayYear:2026}` → 201, `data.negativeNetWarning=false` despite employee net ≈ 33,421. Story TC-PAY-007-03 step 1 expects a create-time warning.
- **Evidence:** create response `negativeNetWarning:false` for amount 999999 and for 50000-deferred-to-July; code path early-return at :456-457 ("warning only fires once a run exists").
- **Severity rationale:** MED — contained: the run-time engine still prevents a finalized negative-net slip (separate guard); this is the *advisory* surface (BR-3 "warn HR") that is silent. No data corruption, but HR loses the documented pre-run safety signal.

### BUG-075 · ISSUE · LOW · OPEN · BE — US-PAY-007 supporting-document validation does not content-sniff (spoofed extension accepted) (NFR-5)
- **Module/US/TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-007 / TC-PAY-007-09
- **Title:** A file with a `.pdf` extension + `application/pdf` declared content-type but non-PDF bytes (GIF89a content) is accepted by `POST /adjustments/{id}/document`. NFR-5/TC-09 expects content-type sniffing to reject a renamed/spoofed file.
- **Root cause (95%):** `PayrollAdjustmentService` validates only `AllowedContentTypes` (declared) ∩ `AllowedExtensions` (lines 36-42, 339-340) — no magic-byte/file-signature check. The declared content-type is client-supplied (curl derives it from the `.pdf` extension), so extension+declared-type both pass while actual bytes are arbitrary.
- **Reproduction:** acme/tenantadmin. Upload `/tmp/doc.pdf` whose bytes start `GIF89a` (renamed): `POST /adjustments/{id}/document -F file=@doc.pdf` → **200 accepted**. Legit negatives all correct: `.exe`→400, `.xlsx`→400, 6 MB pdf→400, real pdf→200.
- **Evidence:** spoofed `doc.pdf` (GIF content) → HTTP 200; code has no signature check (only AllowedContentTypes/AllowedExtensions hash-set membership).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth: blob is private, served back with a fixed content-type, and extension/size/declared-type gates still block the obvious cases; but a determined uploader can stash non-PDF bytes under a `.pdf` name.

- **Conclusion:** Unlike the directly-addressable config rows in US-PAY-001 (which leak under BUG-003), the adjustments surface keys every read AND write off the tenant-scoped employee/EF-global-filter — matching the self-protected pattern of US-PAY-002/004/005/006. ## US-PAY-008 — Payroll Approval Workflow (test-runner, 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API run)

**Scope:** Execute TC-PAY-008-01..12 + ISO TC-PAY-ISO-029..032 against the running stack (API-layer, curl+JWT, acme tenant). Approval routes in `PayrollApprovalController` (`POST runs/{id}/submit-for-approval` [Payroll.Run], `/approve` `/reject` `/return` [Payroll.Approve], `/finalize` [Payroll.Run], GET `/approval-history` `/approval-summary` [Payroll.Run]). State machine: ReviewPending→AwaitingApproval→Approved→Finalized; reject→Rejected; return→ReviewPending. Maker-checker: submitter blocked from approving when ≥2 eligible Payroll.Approve users. UI/a11y/perf TCs BLOCKED (FE pinned-to-platform + Docker unavailable). Findings below.

### Persona / testability note (US-PAY-008)
- **Who holds payroll perms in acme:** ONLY two users hold `Payroll.Run` + `Payroll.Approve` — `tenantadmin@acme.test` (Tenant Admin) and `owner@techoneglobal.org` (Tenant Owner of acme, logs in with Admin@123!). `hr@acme.test` (HR Officer), `manager`, `employee` hold NO payroll-run/approve perms (the known BUG-060/BUG-071 HR/Manager payroll-perm gap — NOT re-filed).
- **KNOWN WRINKLE re-evaluated:** the prior claim "Tenant Admin lacks Payroll.Approve" does NOT hold for this reseeded persona set — `tenantadmin@acme.test` DOES hold `Payroll.Approve`. And because acme has **2** eligible approvers (tenantadmin + owner), the maker-checker rule is **ENFORCED** (not relaxed via small-team exception). The workflow IS testable: submitter=tenantadmin, second approver=owner.
- **No fresh ReviewPending run could be created via API:** June 2026 is already Finalized (`period_already_finalized` 409) and no other period has finalized attendance (`attendance_not_finalized` 409). To exercise the live state machine the single Finalized June run (id `019f0434-0d48-781f-b628-47b6904171d4`) was temporarily reset in-DB to ReviewPending, driven through the API, then **restored to its exact Finalized snapshot** (see cleanup note at end). DB creds from user-secrets; psql at PG18.

### Verdicts — no-mutation TCs (executed against the live Finalized run)
- **TC-PAY-008-09 (authz) — PASS.** emp(no payroll perms) Submit/Approve/Reject/Finalize → 403; hr(no Payroll.Approve) Approve → 403; hr(no Payroll.Run) Submit → 403; unauth Approve → 401; emp GET approval-history → 403; tenantadmin GET history → 200. Authz gate fires BEFORE the state machine (403 returned even on a Finalized run).
- **TC-PAY-008-05 (finalized terminal/immutable) — PASS.** On the Finalized run: Submit→409 invalid_transition, Approve→409, Reject→409, Return→409, Finalize→409 already_finalized. No PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoint exists on ANY payroll controller (slips/runs structurally immutable → FR-8 enforced by absence of a mutation surface, not a per-slip flag). BR-6 terminal honored.
- **TC-PAY-008-03 (direct finalize blocked / invalid transitions) — PARTIAL PASS.** Finalize-on-Finalized and the live ReviewPending→Finalize block (see below) are enforced (BR-1). Steps 2/4/5 (force-set Approved directly, revert Approved→AwaitingApproval, Rejected→Approved) have **NO API surface** — the only status mutations are the workflow verbs, each of which guards its source status, so arbitrary transitions are unreachable by construction. Verified the live ReviewPending→finalize block below.

### Verdicts — isolation TCs (BUG-003 arm)
- **TC-PAY-ISO-029 (cross-tenant read) — PASS.** acme token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` GET approval-history/approval-summary on the acme run id → **404 run_not_found** (the EF global query filter scopes the run load to the resolved tenant; the acme run is invisible from a techoneglobal context). No cross-tenant read leak.
- **TC-PAY-ISO-030 (IDOR / missing context) — PASS.** Random/foreign run id under acme session → 404 run_not_found; no header (missing tenant context) → 400 "Tenant context is not resolved." No IDOR.
- **TC-PAY-ISO-031 (cross-tenant write) — PASS.** acme token + techoneglobal header attempting Approve/Finalize on the acme run id → **404 run_not_found** — the write never reaches the acme run. tenant_id/actor_user_id/IP are all server-derived (TenantInterceptor + ICurrentUser + HttpContext IP), no client-supplied tenant/actor in the body is honored. **The approval read+write surface is self-protected and does NOT extend BUG-003** (BUG-003's run-CREATE leak does not apply here: every approval verb loads an EXISTING run scoped by the resolved tenant before acting). Verified acme run state unchanged after all isolation probes (status=Finalized, 2 history rows).
- **TC-PAY-ISO-032 (queue/badge cache + SignalR group tenant-scoping) — BLOCKED: not-implemented.** There is no "Pending Approvals" queue/badge-count endpoint or cache layer in the payroll approval surface (the controller exposes only per-run history/summary reads), and the notification seam (`IPayrollNotificationService.NotifyApprovalEventAsync`) is **log-only** (SignalR/email deferred to US-NTF). No cache key or SignalR group to assert. Conditional clause of the TC → no observable artifact. Recorded as ISSUE-172 (notification seam is log-only, NFR-1 unverifiable end-to-end).

### NEW FINDINGS (US-PAY-008)

**ISSUE-172 — Approval notifications are a log-only seam; SignalR/email delivery (AC-1/AC-2/AC-3, NFR-1) not implemented**
- Type: ISSUE · Severity: MED · Status: DEFERRED (blocked on US-NTF-006 delivery — see DF-14) · Layer: BE · Module: Payroll · US: US-PAY-008 · TC: TC-PAY-008-01/02/06/11, TC-PAY-ISO-032

The approval state machine + audit trail work; the missing piece is notification *delivery* (in-app/SignalR + email), the known cross-module dependency on the unbuilt **US-NTF-006 delivery** story. Building it is that story, not a bug fix. Parked as **DF-14** (BLOCKED on US-NTF-006). (A "Pending Approvals" queue/badge read-endpoint is a smaller sub-item and could be built independently of delivery if desired later.)
- Title: Approval-event notifications (approver-notified on submit, HR-notified on approve/reject) are not delivered — the notification call is a log-only stub.
- Root cause (confidence 95%): `PayrollApprovalService` calls `_notifications.NotifyApprovalEventAsync(...)` after each transition, but the implementation is the deferred log-only seam (the class XML-doc states "fires the log-only notification seam (real SignalR/email deferred — US-NTF)"; PayrollApprovalService.cs:106,169,213,253,304). No in-app/SignalR push, no email, no notification row. There is also no "Pending Approvals" queue/badge endpoint.
