### MORE NEW FINDINGS (US-PAY-008)

**BUG-076 — Multi-step approval has no per-step approver assignment; a single approver can complete every step (AC-4/FR-2 not enforced)**
- Type: BUG · Severity: MED · Status: RESOLVED (PR #356, 2026-07-18) · Layer: BE · Module: Payroll · US: US-PAY-008 · TC: TC-PAY-008-06, TC-PAY-008-13
- Title: A 2-step workflow (intended "HR Manager THEN Finance Director") can be fully approved by ONE approver acting twice; steps are a counter, not assignments.
- Root cause (confidence 95%): PayrollApprovalService.ApproveAsync only checks maker-checker (submitter != approver) and increments CurrentApprovalStep (PayrollApprovalService.cs:139-165). There is no per-step approver/role binding and no "this actor already approved an earlier step" guard. The submit command takes only totalApprovalSteps (an int) — no step-to-approver mapping. So any Payroll.Approve holder can approve the current step, and the same user can approve step1 AND step2. AC-4 ("sequentially through each step", distinct HR Manager / Finance Director) and FR-2 (configurable steps) are reduced to "the run must be approved N times by anyone with Payroll.Approve."
- Reproduction: TA submit {totalApprovalSteps:2}; owner approve (step1->2, still AwaitingApproval); owner approve again (step2->Approved). Same actor, no rejection. (Evidence: history shows Approved step1 + step2 both actor 019ef3ba.)
- Severity rationale: MED — multi-step is opt-in (default is single-step BR-2) and maker-checker still blocks the submitter, so the most common single-approver bypass is closed; but a tenant that configures 2 steps for separation-of-duties does NOT get it, which is the whole point of a multi-step finance control.
- RESOLVED (PR #356, 2026-07-18): payroll-specific configurable step→role engine + distinct-person guard. New `PayrollApprovalStepConfig(StepNumber→RoleId)` per tenant (settable+audited via `GET/PUT /api/v1/payroll/approval/step-config`, gated `Payroll.Approve` = non-maker). `ApproveAsync` now enforces, after maker-checker: (a) distinct-person — a user who already Approved a step for this instance can't approve another (total>1) → 403 `distinct_approver_required`; (b) step-role — the actor must hold the current step's configured role → 403 `not_step_approver`. Submit derives TotalApprovalSteps from config. Regression: same-user-both-steps→403 (the repro), distinct-approvers→Approved, role-per-step, config-authoritative, CRUD persist+audit+validation-400s (bound TC-PAY-008-13). Full suite 4218/4218; auditors PASS (isolation + guards verified). Postgres/cross-tenant config test arms → DF-16; FE step-config editor → ISSUE-318 (deferred). ISSUE-173 (SLA/escalation/delegation, LOW) remains separate.

**ISSUE-318 — No Angular UI for the payroll approval step→role config (BUG-076 backend endpoints are API-only)**
- Type: ISSUE · Severity: MED · Status: OPEN (FE, deferred) · Layer: FE · Module: Payroll · US: US-PAY-008 · TC: (FE, none yet)
- Title: BUG-076 (#356) added `GET/PUT /api/v1/payroll/approval/step-config` but there is no admin screen to view/edit the step→role approval chain; a Tenant Admin can only configure it via the raw API.
- Root cause: backend-only fix scope (the MED-fix campaign was BE-only per user decision). The FE admin surface is net-new frontend work.
- Suggested: an Angular admin screen (payroll settings) to view/edit the ordered step→role mapping, gated on `Payroll.Approve`, consuming the two endpoints. Sits with the deferred-FE queue (P6 class).
- Severity rationale: MED — the FR-2 control is functionally complete and usable via API (and enforced regardless of UI); the gap is end-user configurability. No security/data risk.

**ISSUE-173 — FR-3 (SLA auto-escalation to backup approver) and FR-6 (approval delegation) are not implemented**
- Type: ISSUE · Severity: LOW · Status: OPEN · Layer: BE · Module: Payroll · US: US-PAY-008 · TC: TC-PAY-008-07
- Title: No SLA/escalation or delegation surface; the Escalated history action is defined in the data spec but never written.

PayrollApprovalAction.Escalated is in the section-7 enum but is never produced. The class doc states there is no shared workflow engine (US-ADM-007 not built), so these advanced FRs were deferred.

**ISSUE-174 — Finalize writes no payroll_approval_history row; the approval-history timeline omits the finalize event (FR-7/AC-5)**
- Type: ISSUE · Severity: LOW · Status: OPEN · Layer: BE · Module: Payroll · US: US-PAY-008 · TC: TC-PAY-008-01/10
- Title: The approval-history timeline (FR-7) does not contain a Finalized entry; finalize is only in the separate US-PAY-012 structured audit-timeline.
- Root cause (confidence 98%): FinalizeAsync deliberately does NOT add a PayrollApprovalHistory row (PayrollApprovalService.cs:296-300 comment: "No history row required for finalize per the section-7 action set ... we intentionally do NOT invent a new action value"). The section-7 action enum (Submitted/Approved/Rejected/Returned/Escalated) has no Finalized value, so the implementation is spec-consistent — but FR-7 ("complete audit trail of all approval actions") and AC-5 mean a reviewer reading the approval-history endpoint sees the run jump from Approved to (externally) Finalized with no timeline entry.
- Reproduction: Run full lifecycle; GET approval-history shows Submitted+Approved only (no Finalized). The structured audit-timeline (GET runs/{id}/audit-timeline) DOES show PayrollRun.Finalized with IP+actor — so audit completeness is satisfied elsewhere.
- Severity rationale: LOW — audited via US-PAY-012 audit-timeline (mitigates); only the dedicated approval-history view is incomplete. Mostly a spec ambiguity (section-7 enum vs FR-7 wording).

## US-PAY-009 — Payroll Reports and Analytics (test-runner, 2026-06-26, REPORT-ONLY API run)
Scope: API-layer (curl + JWT) execution of TC-PAY-009-01..12 + TC-PAY-ISO-033..036 against acme tenant on the lone Finalized June 2026 run. Routes under `PayrollReportsController` (`/api/v1/payroll/reports*`, `/analytics/{chartType}`). Perms: `Payroll.Export` (reports/analytics/export/masked-preview) + `Payroll.ViewSensitive` (bank-advice full). FE :4200 pinned-platform + Docker down → UI/a11y/cross-browser/perf TCs BLOCKED. Findings below.

### BUG-077 — HR Officer (the named report consumer) is locked out of all Payroll Reports/Analytics (403)
- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #254, 2026-07-11) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** Added `Payroll.Export` to the HR Officer role in `PermissionCatalog.DefaultPermissionsFor` (deliberately NOT `Payroll.ViewSensitive` — unmasked bank PII stays HR-Manager+). Regression: `PermissionCatalogTests.HrOfficer_HasPayrollRunConfigureExport_BUG060_071_077`.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-009 / TC-PAY-009-01, TC-PAY-009-09
- **Title:** `hr@acme.test` (role "HR Officer") gets 403 on every `/api/v1/payroll/reports*` and `/analytics/*` endpoint, contradicting AC-1 / persona ("HR Officer or Tenant Admin") and the controller's own doc-comment ("Payroll.Export … held by Tenant Admin + HR Officer").
- **Root cause:** Authz/seed gap. All report endpoints are `[RequirePermission("Payroll.Export")]`; the seeded "HR Officer" role does NOT grant `Payroll.Export`, so HR is denied the surface the story designates them the primary user of. Same persona-gap class as BUG-060 (HR no Payroll.Configure) / BUG-071 (HR/Mgr no Payroll.Run) but a distinct, separately-gated surface (reports/analytics/export). Serilog not consulted — 403 is an authz decision, not an exception. Confidence: 90% (HTTP 403 for HR vs 200 for Tenant Admin on identical request; HR confirmed to hold only the "HR Officer" role).
- **Reproduction:**
  1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (subdomain `acme`) as `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → accessToken.
  2. `GET /api/v1/payroll/reports` with that bearer + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme` → **403** (Tenant Admin gets 200). Same 403 on `/reports/PayrollSummary`, `/analytics/MonthlyTrend`, `/reports/{type}/export`.
- **Evidence:** `HR list: 403` / `MGR list: 403` / `EMP list: 403` / `ANON list: 401`; Tenant Admin = 200 on all. DB: `hr@acme.test` → role "HR Officer" only.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — the AC-1 primary actor cannot reach the entire feature; payroll-reporting workflow is blocked for the intended role (compliance/disbursement reporting), though Tenant Admin/Owner can still operate it.

### ISSUE-175 — CTC "Employer Contributions (est.)" is always 0.00, contradicting its own note (1:1 statutory match)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** OPEN · **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-009 / TC-PAY-009 (Ctc report, FR-1h)
- **Title:** CTC report note says "Employer contributions are ESTIMATED as a 1:1 match of statutory components", but the column is 0.00 for every employee and Annual CTC == Annual Gross — so the documented estimate never materialises.
- **Root cause:** CTC reads from *current salary structures* (3 employees @ 50000/mo) which carry no statutory/employer component, so the 1:1-match estimate has nothing to mirror; the paid employee's runtime EPF (1800/mo from the June slip) is not used because CTC is structure-based, not slip-based. Behavior may be correct-by-design but the note overpromises. Confidence: 70%.
- **Reproduction:** `GET /api/v1/payroll/reports/Ctc` (acme, Tenant Admin) → all rows `Employer Contributions (est.)`=0.00; TOTAL employer=0.00, Annual CTC 1,800,000 == Annual Gross.
- **Evidence:** rows e.g. `['EMP-0001','John Doe','Engineering','50000.00','600000.00','0.00','600000.00']`; note text as quoted.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/contract drift between the note and the numbers; no incorrect disbursement, but misleading for CTC consumers.

### ISSUE-176 — StatutoryDeduction YTD uses calendar-year (Jan→month), ignoring the tenant fiscal-year start (BR-5)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** LOW · **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (2026-07-16, PR #324 — user decision: match the run, per-country) · **Layer:** BE
- **Fix:** `PayrollReportService.ScopedSlipsForFiscalYtdAsync` (the statutory report's YTD column) now uses each
  employee's **income-tax FISCAL-YEAR-to-date** window — the same per-country `StatutoryRule` (`EffectiveFrom`→
  selected month) window the payroll RUN anchors cumulative PAYE on — via a new `ResolveEmployeeIncomeTaxWindowsAsync`
  helper, loading candidate years {year-1, year} so an Apr–Mar FY that opens in the prior calendar year is covered.
  Sub-decisions (per the user's "match the run" call): **non-income-tax components (EPF/ETF) follow the same
  per-employee tax window**; **employees with no resolvable tax country keep the calendar-year window** (so their
  statutory is never silently dropped). **Mutation-verified** (revert→calendar makes the fiscal YTD wrong: 3000 vs
  2000) by 4 arms in `PayrollReportIntegrationTests` (spans-FY excluding prior-FY + future months · prior-calendar-year
  slip in same FY · country-less keeps calendar · calendar-aligned unchanged); 22/22 green. **⚠ Follow-up (tidy):**
  `ResolveEmployeeIncomeTaxWindowsAsync` deliberately DUPLICATES the `fyByCountry` resolution in
  `BuildYearEndTaxStatementAsync` (to avoid touching that working money method) — extract to one shared reader when
  convenient; keep them in lock-step until then.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-009 / TC-PAY-009-06 (BR-5)
- **Title:** Statutory Deduction report's "Year-to-Date Total" is documented as "cumulative from January to the selected month of the same calendar year", but BR-5 requires reports to respect the tenant's configured fiscal-year start month (acme = April). YTD should run Apr→month, not Jan→month.
- **Root cause:** Self-disclosed deferral — report note: "fiscal-year-start config is a documented follow-up, BR-3/BR-5." Same fiscal-year-start gap surfaces in YearEndTaxStatement (deferred) and Variance. Not empirically distinguishable in current data (only June run exists, so YTD=1800 either way). ### BUG-078 — Overtime hourly-rate base is total structural EARNINGS, not BASIC (ResolvedBasic name-match "Basic" never matches the seeded line name "Basic Salary"); OT over-paid ~2.5x
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #255, 2026-07-12)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** `PayrollRunProcessor.ResolvedBasic` now identifies BASIC by component **Code** ("BASIC") → ComponentId → slip line, instead of the display Name — so a line named "Basic Salary" resolves correctly (was falling through to `GrossEarnings`). Regression: `PayrollBasicResolutionTests` (multi-component structure asserts hourly = basic/(days×8) = 60.59, not gross-based 151.47). Verified 10 unit + 29 payroll integration tests on Postgres. See sibling **BUG-280** (same defect in statutory) fixed in the same PR.
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-010 / TC-PAY-010-02, -07, -08
- **Title:** The overtime earning derives its base hourly rate from the sum of ALL structural earning lines (basic+conveyance+HRA+special) instead of BASIC, so OT is materially over-paid. FR-4/BR-5 + the code's own doc-comment say the OT base is the employee's BASIC.
- **Root cause:** `PayrollRunProcessor.ResolvedBasic(result)` (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/PayrollRunProcessor.cs:552-560) finds the BASIC line by matching `PayrollSlipLine.Name == "Basic"` / `"BASIC"`. The seeded/real BASIC component's **Name** is `"Basic Salary"` (its **Code** is `"BASIC"`), so the `FirstOrDefault` never matches and it falls back to `result.GrossEarnings`. `ComputeOvertime` then passes that gross as `monthlyBasic` to `PayrollOvertimeCalculator.Compute`, which derives `hourly = monthlyBasic/(workingDays*8)`. The matcher should compare against the component **Code** (`BASIC`), which `PayrollSlipLine` does not carry — so the line name is the only available key and it is the wrong one. Confidence: 97% (verified against the live finalized June slip below; arithmetic exact).
- **Reproduction steps:** acme tenant, tenantadmin@acme.test (holds Payroll.Run). The Finalized June-2026 run `019f0434-0d48-781f-b628-47b6904171d4`, employee EMP-0001 (John Doe). `GET /api/v1/payroll/runs/{run}/payslips` + DB `payroll_slip_detail`. The Overtime line basis string is `"6h @ 151.47/h"`.
- **Evidence:** EMP-0001 structural earning lines: Basic Salary 10663.64, Conveyance 1066.36, HRA 2132.73, Special Allowance 12796.36 → sum = **26659.09**; `26659.09 / (22 working_days * 8) = 151.47/h` — EXACTLY the slip's OT hourly. The BASIC-correct hourly would be `proRatedBasic 10663.64 / 176 = 60.59/h` (or raw-basic `20000/176 = 113.64/h`). OT amount on slip = `6h * 151.47 * 1.5 = 1363.25`; the BASIC-correct figure would be `6 * 60.59 * 1.5 = 545.31`. OT is over-paid by ~2.5x. (Bonus/reimbursement adjustment lines are merged AFTER OT compute, which is why the base is structural-earnings, not final gross 40159.09.)
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — every employee with approved overtime is over-paid a structurally wrong amount on every finalized run; directly violates AC-2/FR-4 and silently inflates net pay (real money, audit/compliance impact), but contained to OT earners.
### ISSUE-180 — Leave-encashment daily rate uses CALENDAR days of the month (30/31), diverging from the run engine's working-days (22) denominator for the same employee/period (BR-8)
- **Type:** ISSUE
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #282, 2026-07-13) — `LeaveEncashmentService.WorkingDaysInMonth` → async `WorkingDaysInMonthAsync` resolving the employee's SHIFT working-days over `monthStart..monthEnd` (same `ShiftScheduleResolver` source the run uses), so `dailyRate = monthlyBasic / working_days` matches the run's denominator. Test asserts the golden `22000/22 = 1000/day` (not 733.33 calendar). Empty-shift-set → calendar fallback; div-by-zero guarded.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-010 / TC-PAY-010-03, -09
- **Title:** `daily_rate = monthly_basic / working_days` is computed two different ways: the encashment service uses calendar days in the target month, while the payroll run / reconciliation use the attendance shift working-days (22). The same employee's "daily rate" therefore differs between an encashment earning and an LOP deduction.
- **Root cause:** `LeaveEncashmentService.WorkingDaysInMonth(year,month)` (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LeaveEncashmentService.cs:142-148) returns `end.DayNumber - start.DayNumber + 1` = calendar days (28/30/31). FR-3/FR-5/BR-8 specify working_days from the shift calendar; the code comment explicitly defers shift-calendar working-days. The run engine instead pulls `attendance.TotalWorkingDays` (22) via the US-ATT-009 attendance service. Confidence: 99% (observed directly).
- **Reproduction steps:** acme, tenantadmin. `POST /api/v1/payroll/leave-encashments` `{employeeId:EMP-0001, leaveTypeId:Annual(encashable), eligibleDays:5, payMonth:8, payYear:2026}` → 201 `dailyRate=645.16` (= 20000/31, August). `payMonth:9` → `dailyRate=666.67` (= 20000/30, September). EMP-0001's payroll-run/reconciliation working_days = 22 (LOP daily_rate = proRatedBasic/22). (Both test adjustments hard-deleted afterward; 0 residue.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the encashment amount is wrong vs the documented working-days basis and inconsistent with the LOP/run engine; it is real money on the next payslip, but it is a contained, deferred-by-design calculation gap (BR-8) rather than a broken flow. The golden TC value (22000/22=1000/day) is not achievable on this path.

### BUG-079 — Leave-encashment ignores BR-6 carry-forward-limit and uses RAW current BASIC (not pro-rated); HR can encash arbitrary days with no balance/over-limit check
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #284, 2026-07-13; user decision: gate + ledger draw-down)
- **Resolution (BR-6 balance/carry-forward + double-pay):** `LeaveEncashmentService` now gates encashment on the **forfeitable** balance = current ledger balance over the type's `CarryForwardLimit` (computed with the SAME authoritative `LeaveCarryForwardCalculator` the year-end job uses), then caps paid days at `MaxEncashDays`; a request exceeding the forfeitable ceiling is rejected 422 `encashment_exceeds_balance`. On acceptance it writes an `Encashed` **ledger draw-down** atomically with the payroll adjustment (shared scoped DbContext, single SaveChanges), so the HR path and the year-end auto-encashment **cannot pay the same days twice** — the year-end `ComputeUnusedBalanceAsync` folds `Encashed` into consumption, so it re-forfeits only the residual (proven: forfeitable 7 → HR 6 → year-end 1 → total 7). 7 tests incl. cap-firing + double-pay reconciliation; integration-enforcer CONNECTED (double-pay closed, atomicity sound), test-authenticator AUTHENTIC. **Residual clauses (LOW, filed → ISSUE-295):** (a) the "RAW current BASIC (not pro-rated)" daily-rate half — the denominator was fixed by ISSUE-180/#282; the numerator uses current BASIC (arguably correct for encashment), verify vs spec; (b) null `CarryForwardLimit` encashable types treated as full-balance encashable; (c) gate-ceiling (latest `BalanceAfter`) vs year-end `unused` parity under the `Σaccruals==entitlement` invariant.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-010 / TC-PAY-010-09
- **Title:** The encashment endpoint validates only (a) the leave type is encashable and (b) caps days at the type's MaxEncashDays. It performs NO check that the employee actually HAS that many unused days, nor that the days exceed the carry-forward limit (BR-6). The caller-supplied `eligibleDays` is trusted as-is (capped only by MaxEncashDays).
- **Root cause:** `LeaveEncashmentService.ProcessAsync` (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LeaveEncashmentService.cs:60-73) checks `Encashable` + caps at `MaxEncashDays`, but never reads the employee's leave balance or carry-forward limit. The service doc-comment openly states "the carry-forward-limit balance-over-limit check is the LEAVE module's surface; the caller supplies the eligible-days figure (the documented BR-6 gap)." So BR-6's "only for balance exceeding carry-forward" is unenforced server-side. Confidence: 95%.
- **Reproduction steps:** acme, tenantadmin. `POST /api/v1/payroll/leave-encashments` with `eligibleDays:5` for EMP-0001 on encashable "Annual Leave" succeeded (201) even though no balance/over-limit verification occurs; only the MaxEncashDays=5 cap applied (10→5).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — an HR user can post an encashment earning for days the employee may not hold (no balance gate), creating an over-payment on the next run; contained to the Payroll.Run-gated HR action and capped by MaxEncashDays, but BR-6 eligibility is materially unenforced.

### ENH-020 — Payslip email delivery is a log-only stub (no real SMTP); functional-but-undeliverable seam
- **Type:** ENH (seam status, not a defect — matches the platform's other notification seams)
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-011 / TC-PAY-011-01, -02, -05, -08, -09, -11
- **Title:** `IPayslipEmailSender` is bound to `LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender` — emails are logged, never delivered
- **Why it matters:** The whole pipeline is real and correct up to the wire: `POST .../send-emails` → real Hangfire `SendPayslipEmailsJob` enqueue (FR-1/FR-8, tenant ctx restored from job args) → `PayslipDistributionRunner` per-employee loop → `payslip_email_log` rows written (FR-5) → `LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender.SendAsync` writes a `[PAYSLIP-EMAIL-STUB] Would send payslip email to … Subject='Your Payslip for May 2026', Attachment='EMP-0002_5_2026.pdf' (118 bytes)` line and returns success (treated as SMTP acceptance). No `Smtp:Host` is configured in dev, so nothing is delivered and no real Polly-over-SMTP retry is exercised (the log-only sender never throws). This is the expected "functional but undeliverable" state — AC-1/AC-2/AC-3/FR-2/FR-3/FR-5/FR-8/NFR-4/NFR-5 are all verifiable at the DB + log layer, but AC-2 actual inbox delivery and AC-4 real SMTP-failure retry are NOT (no SMTP, no MailHog). NFR-5 holds: the stub log line carries only recipient/subject/attachment-name/size — never the PDF bytes and never a salary amount.
- **Evidence:** `LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender.cs` (`Smtp:Host` blank → STUB branch); DI `DependencyInjection.cs:256 services.AddScoped<IPayslipEmailSender, LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender>()`; Serilog `hrm-20260626.log` 20:42:44 `[PAYSLIP-EMAIL-STUB] Would send payslip email to speed.test@example.com … Subject='Your Payslip for May 2026', Attachment='EMP-0002_5_2026.pdf' (118 bytes). Configure Smtp:Host to enable real delivery.`
- **Suggested direction:** Wire a real `IPayslipEmailSender` (SMTP/transactional) + a `PayslipEmailTransientException`-throwing path so AC-4 Polly retry/Failed is exercised under integration tests with MailHog/Papercut. Tracked as TODO(US-NTF) in code. One-class swap.

### ISSUE-183 — Distribution summary `completedAt` can be earlier than `startedAt` (computed from different columns)
- **Type:** ISSUE (behavioral nit / data-presentation)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** WONTFIX (LOW-tier triage 2026-07-18 — reason in LOW-TIER-TRIAGE.md §B)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-011 / TC-PAY-011-01 (summary), BR-6 §7 (started_at/completed_at)
- **Title:** `startedAt = MIN(log.created_at)` but `completedAt = MAX(log.sent_at)` — the two come from different timestamp sources, so completedAt < startedAt is possible
- **Root cause:** `PayslipDistributionService.GetSummaryAsync` (and the runner's `SummaryFor`) set `StartedAt = logs.Min(l => l.CreatedAt)` and `CompletedAt = logs.Where(sent_at != null).Max(sent_at)`. The runner stamps `sent_at = DateTime.UtcNow` inside the loop BEFORE `SaveChangesAsync` assigns the audit `created_at`, so on a fast single-batch run the sent_at precedes created_at. The §7 data spec intends started_at = job start and completed_at = job completion (a monotonic window), not a mix of created vs sent columns. Confidence: 95% (observed directly).
- **Reproduction steps:** acme `tenantadmin@acme.test`, `X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme`; send payslips on a Finalized run; `GET /api/v1/payroll/runs/{id}/payslips/distribution-summary` → observed `startedAt:"2026-06-26T15:12:44.932295Z"` with `completedAt:"2026-06-26T15:12:44.842527Z"` (completed 90ms BEFORE started).
- **Evidence:** summary JSON above; `PayslipDistributionService.cs:180-183`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic; would render a negative/odd duration in the §8 progress card but does not affect counts, correctness, or isolation.

### ENH-021 — Unmappable payroll-run status string in DB causes a 500 instead of a graceful error (defense-in-depth only, not app-reachable)
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #348, 2026-07-17)
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17), fixed together with [[ISSUE-231]] (same class).** `payroll_run.status` now reads through `TolerantEnumToStringConverter<PayrollRunStatus>(Unknown)`: an out-of-enum status maps to the `Unknown` sentinel + logs, instead of throwing on materialization and 500ing the run list/guard query. The sentinel is read-only — run status is only ever set by the code-controlled BR-6 transitions (no user-input validator accepts it) — and `PayrollRunService`'s status `switch` already has a `default:` arm, so `Unknown` yields a clean 409 `run_not_rerunnable`, not a silent wrong branch. No migration (column stays varchar(20)). Verified on real `postgres:17-alpine`: seed a run, raw-SQL `status='Draft'`, read the list → 200 with `Status == Unknown`. Mutation-verified: reverting to the strict converter fails the arm with the exact reported error, `Cannot convert string value 'Draft' … 'PayrollRunStatus' enum`. This confirms the original finding was real, not just theoretical. `payroll_run` has no other enum column (its `rejection_reason` is free `text`), so this surface is fully covered.
- **Type:** ENH (robustness observation — NOT a defect; the status value is never written by the app)
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-011 / TC-PAY-011-03 (BR-1 guard)
- **Title:** `EF HasConversion<string>()` on `PayrollRunStatus` throws `InvalidOperationException: Cannot convert string value 'X' … to any value in the mapped 'PayrollRunStatus' enum`, surfacing as a 500
- **Why it matters:** When a `payroll_run.status` holds a string outside the enum (Queued/Processing/ReviewPending/AwaitingApproval/Approved/Rejected/Finalized/Cancelled), the send/resend guard query throws on materialization → 500 (generic "unexpected error"). Discovered only because a deliberately-invalid test value ('Draft') was injected; the app itself never writes an out-of-enum status, so this is **not reachable through normal flows** — recorded purely as a hardening note. With valid non-finalized statuses (ReviewPending/Approved/Cancelled) the guard correctly returns 409 `run_not_finalized`.
- **Evidence:** Serilog `hrm-20260626.log:462000` `System.InvalidOperationException: Cannot convert string value 'Draft' from the database to any value in the mapped 'PayrollRunStatus' enum.` (RequestId `0HNMJGENHI0EP:00000001`). Control: same run set to ReviewPending/Approved/Cancelled → 409 `run_not_finalized`.
- **Suggested direction:** None required for prod. If desired, a defensive enum-conversion fallback would turn a corrupt row into a handled error rather than a 500.

### TC-PAY-012-01 — Payroll History list (AC-1/FR-1) — PASS
`GET /runs/history` returns the paginated chronological list. The single acme run (June-2026 Finalized) carries every AC-1 column: period `2026-06`, status `Finalized`, employeeCount 1, totalNet 33421.10, totalGross 41522.34, totalDeductions 8101.24, initiatedBy/At, approvedBy/At, finalizedAt. Filters are **server-side**: `year=2025`→0, `year=2026`→1, `status=Finalized`→1, `month=6`+`sortBy=net`→1. Pagination metadata (totalCount/page/pageSize) correct. Only 1 run exists in acme, so multi-run sort ordering could not be fully exercised (single-row) — core assertion met.

### ISSUE-184 — Unparseable `status` filter is silently ignored → returns the full unfiltered list
- **ID:** ISSUE-184
- **Type:** ISSUE (filter contract nit)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #363, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-012 / TC-PAY-012-01 (AC-1/FR-1 filter)
- **Title:** `GET /runs/history?status=<invalid>` (e.g. `Draft`, `zzz`) silently drops the filter and returns ALL runs instead of 400 / empty
- **Root cause:** `PayrollAuditService.GetRunHistoryAsync` (PayrollAuditService.cs:74-76) guards the status filter with `Enum.TryParse<PayrollRunStatus>(...)`; on a parse miss it simply does not apply any `Where`, so the query returns the unfiltered set. Confidence 95% (read directly from source; reproduced live). Serilog silent (200, no exception — expected).
- **Reproduction steps:** acme tenantadmin → `GET /api/v1/payroll/runs/history?status=Draft` and `?status=zzz` → both `200` with `totalCount:1` (same as no filter), whereas `status=Finalized`→1 and a genuinely non-matching valid status would→0. A caller filtering on a typo'd/legacy status silently gets the whole table back.
- **Evidence:** `?status=Draft` → `{"totalCount":1}`; `?status=zzz` → `200 {"totalCount":1}`; `?status=Finalized` → `{"totalCount":1}`. Source: PayrollAuditService.cs:74-76.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — read-only, tenant-scoped (no data leak), and a valid-status filter works correctly; only the unparseable-input edge silently returns more than intended. Contract polish, not a security/flow break.

`GET /runs/{runId}/audit-timeline` on the June Finalized run returns the run's events in **chronological (oldest-first) order**: `PayrollRun.Initiated` (13:52:28) → `PayrollRun.SubmittedForApproval` (13:55:19) → `PayrollRun.Approved` (13:55:33, by approver `019ed613-…`) → `PayrollRun.Finalized` (13:55:45). Events are scoped to this run only (resource_id filter + tenant predicate); no other run bled in. ### TC-PAY-012-04 — FR-2 breadth: every payroll write logs an audit entry — FAIL (BUG-080)
Of the 20 standardized action names in the US-PAY-012 S7 catalog, only **12 are emitted by any code path**; 8 required actions have **zero emitters**. Confirmed wired (live + source): SalaryComponent.Created/Updated/Deleted, StatutoryRule.Created/Updated, PayrollRun.Initiated/SubmittedForApproval/Approved/Rejected/Finalized, PayrollAdjustment.Created/Cancelled — each with correct action+resourceType, create→before null, delete→after empty. **Missing entirely:** SalaryStructure.Created/Updated, EmployeeSalary.Assigned/Revised, PayrollRun.Completed, PayslipPDF.Generated, PayslipEmail.Sent. FR-2/BR-1 ("every payroll write MUST log — no exceptions") is therefore violated for salary-structure CRUD, salary assignment/revision, run-compute completion, PDF generation, and email distribution. See BUG-080.

### BUG-080 — FR-2/BR-1 violated: 8 required payroll audit actions are never emitted (structure CRUD, salary assignment, run-Completed, PDF-Generated, Email-Sent)
- **ID:** BUG-080
- **Type:** BUG (broken vs spec — FR-2/BR-1)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #256, 2026-07-12)
- **Resolution:** Wired 7 explicit `IPayrollAuditLogger.Log(...)` emitters (staged atomically into each op's SaveChanges): SalaryStructure.Created/Updated (+clone→Created) in `SalaryStructureService`; EmployeeSalary.Assigned/Revised in `SalaryAssignmentService` (revise vs assign by prior-active-assignment); and the 3 job-driven system-actor actions PayrollRun.Completed (`PayrollRunProcessor`), PayslipPDF.Generated (`PayslipBatchRenderer`, per slip), PayslipEmail.Sent (`PayslipDistributionRunner`, only on Status==Sent). Payloads carry structural fields only — no gross/CTC/PII. **8th action PayrollRun.Cancelled left unemitted — no run-cancel operation exists (design gap, not a wiring miss).** Regression: 8 mutation-resistant integration tests querying real `audit_logs` (verified AUTHENTIC by test-authenticator; my re-run 62/62 green + build clean). Hardening gap → ISSUE-282.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-012 / TC-PAY-012-04 (also fails TC-PAY-012-06 system-actor entries)
- **Title:** Salary-structure CRUD, employee-salary assign/revise, PayrollRun.Completed, PayslipPDF.Generated, PayslipEmail.Sent write NO audit_log entry — breaking the "every payroll write logs, no exceptions" rule
- **Root cause:** The action-name catalog `PayrollAuditAction.Action.*` (HRM.Domain/Payroll/PayrollAuditAction.cs) defines all 20 action constants, but only 12 are passed to `_audit.Log(...)` in the Infrastructure services. Grep of `PA.<Action>` emitters across `src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure`: SalaryComponentService (Created/Updated/Deleted), StatutoryRuleService (Created/Updated), PayrollApprovalService (SubmittedForApproval/Approved/Rejected/Finalized), PayrollRunService (Initiated), PayrollAdjustmentService (Created/Cancelled) — 12 total. `SalaryStructureCreated/Updated`, `EmployeeSalaryAssigned/Revised`, `PayrollRunCompleted`, `PayslipPdfGenerated`, `PayslipEmailSent` have **0 emitters** anywhere in the backend (the only references are the catalog constant defs + a comment in PayrollAuditService.cs:190). Confidence 95% (exhaustive grep of emitters + live audit-trail over a fully-finalized run that ran compute/PDF/email shows none of these 8 actions present). The salary-structure and employee-salary write services were not extended with audit calls when US-PAY-012's logger was added.
- **Reproduction steps:** acme tenantadmin → `GET /api/v1/payroll/audit-trail?pageSize=200` over the existing data (incl. the fully-Finalized June run `019f0434-…` that went through compute→PDF→email): the only action types returned are SalaryComponent.Created, StatutoryRule.Created, PayrollAdjustment.Created/Cancelled, PayrollRun.Initiated/SubmittedForApproval/Approved/Rejected/Finalized. No `PayrollRun.Completed`, `PayslipPDF.Generated`, or `PayslipEmail.Sent` rows exist despite those operations having run (US-PAY-011 confirmed the email job + PDF gen executed). Source-confirm: `grep -rnoE 'PA\.[A-Za-z]+,' src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure` → the 8 actions never appear.
- **Evidence:** Emitter grep (12 hits, listed above); audit-trail action histogram over 85 acme rows shows 0 of the 8 missing actions; `grep` of the 8 constants outside the catalog file = `PayslipPDF.Generated/PayslipEmail.Sent/PayrollRun.Completed/EmployeeSalary.*/SalaryStructure.*` only match a comment.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — BR-1 is an absolute compliance requirement ("there are no exceptions") and BR-4 says the trail must let an auditor reconstruct the *complete* sequence; with run-compute, PDF generation, email distribution, salary-structure changes, and salary assignments all unlogged, the audit trail is materially incomplete for a financial/statutory audit. Not CRIT because the most security-sensitive interactive actions (run init/submit/approve/reject/finalize, component+statutory+adjustment changes) ARE logged with IP/actor.

### TC-PAY-012-05 — Audit-trail filtering by date/action/actor/resource (AC-4/FR-4) — PASS
`GET /audit-trail` filters all work and AND-combine correctly (over 88 acme rows): `action=PayrollRun.Approved`→4; `resourceType=PayrollAdjustment`→49; `actorUserId=`tenantadmin→82, approver→1 (clean actor scoping); `fromUtc=2027`→0, `fromUtc=today`→88 (date range correct); combined `action=PayrollRun.Approved&fromUtc=today`→4 (intersection). **Payroll-scoping enforced:** `resourceType=Employee`→0 — the trail is restricted to the payroll resource-type allow-list, so non-payroll audit rows do not leak into this view (S10). Results ordered by CreatedAt desc, paginated. Note: there is no implicit "last 30 days" default window — the caller supplies the range explicitly (consistent with AC-4 wording "searches for last 30 days").

### TC-PAY-012-06 — System actor (BR-7) + IP/UA on approval/finalize (BR-5) — FAIL (BR-7 portion; cross-ref BUG-080)
- **BR-5 (IP/user-agent on sensitive interactive actions): PASS.** The June run's `PayrollRun.Approved` (actor `019ed613-…`) and `PayrollRun.Finalized` (actor `019efa61-…`) audit entries both carry server-derived `ipAddress` (`::1`) + `userAgent` + traceId — sufficient for non-repudiation. Actor is the human from the JWT, not client-supplied.
- **BR-7 (system actor on Hangfire job actions): FAIL.** The job-driven actions `PayrollRun.Completed`, `PayslipPDF.Generated`, `PayslipEmail.Sent` are **never written** (BUG-080 — 0 emitters), so the "system actor, not null" guarantee cannot hold for entries that do not exist. A financial auditor sees no record of compute-completion, PDF generation, or email distribution attributed to a system actor. Verdict FAIL, root cause = BUG-080. (Note: every entry that IS written has a non-null actor — no null-actor row was observed among the 88 rows.)

### TC-PAY-012-07 — Audit-log immutability / append-only (NFR-4/BR-2) — PASS
No modify/delete path exists. `PUT/PATCH/DELETE /payroll/audit-trail/{id}` and `/payroll/audit-log/{id}` → **404** (route not exposed); the same verbs on the GET-only `/payroll/audit-trail` and `/payroll/runs/{id}/audit-timeline` → **405** Method Not Allowed (route is read-only). The only other audit surface, `AuditLogController`, exposes solely a `POST /export` (read/export, no mutation). Re-running an operation appends a NEW row (observed in TC-03/04: each Create/Update/Delete added a distinct append-only row, originals unchanged). Error bodies are generic (no stack/SQL leak). Audit store is append-only and tamper-proof.

### TC-PAY-012-08 — Point-in-time historical payslip snapshot (BR-6) — PASS (by stored-snapshot architecture + unchanged-totals evidence)
The Finalized June run `019f0434-…` stores its results as persisted rows, NOT recomputed from current config: `payroll_run` holds frozen `TotalNet/TotalGross/TotalDeductions`, and each `PayrollSlip` stores `GrossEarnings/TotalDeductions/NetSalary` + a persisted `PayrollSlipDetail` line-item collection (label+amount captured at run time). After performing a full SalaryComponent Create→Update→Delete (probe QAAUDIT) this run, the June history row's `totalNet` is **unchanged at 33421.10** and its audit timeline is unaffected (the component audit rows belong to the component resource, not the run). Because slip breakdowns are stored snapshots rather than live-recomputed, a later component rename/value change cannot retroactively alter a finalized run (BR-6). The "a subsequent run adopts the new value" arm was verified by design (future runs read current component config) rather than executed — I deliberately did not trigger a new payroll run to avoid mutating tenant state. The June Finalized run was never mutated.

### TC-PAY-012-09 — Authz matrix on history/audit/timeline/export — PASS (core matrix); ISSUE-185 (Auditor cannot export)
Live matrix (acme): **tenantadmin → 200** on all four endpoints (history, audit-trail, timeline, export); **employee → 403** on all; **unauthenticated → 401** on all. **hr@acme.test (HROfficer) → 403** on all — and this is **correct by design, NOT a seed gap (not BUG-060/071/077 re-file)**: the `HROfficer` built-in role (PermissionCatalog.cs:644-660) intentionally holds NO `Payroll.*` permission. `Payroll.View` is granted to TenantAdmin (609), HRManager (635) and Auditor (698). ### ISSUE-185 — Auditor role can VIEW the audit trail but cannot EXPORT it (export gated on `Payroll.Export`, which the Auditor role lacks)
- **ID:** ISSUE-185
- **Type:** ISSUE (authz design vs spec)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (2026-07-16, PR pending) — `PayrollAuditController.ExportAuditTrail` re-gated from
  `Payroll.Export` → **`Payroll.View`**, matching the three audit READ endpoints (the export is just a
  downloadable form of the trail the caller can already see). The `Auditor` role (holds `Payroll.View`, not
  `Payroll.Export`) — the AC-4 audit consumer — can now export; no wider payroll-data export is unlocked.
  Mutation-verified by a reflection guard (`AuditTrailExport_IsGatedOnPayrollView_NotPayrollExport`).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-012 / TC-PAY-012-09 (step 2) + TC-PAY-012-11 (FR-5 export by auditor)
- **Title:** The `Auditor` built-in role is granted `Payroll.View` (audit-trail read) but not `Payroll.Export`, so `GET /payroll/audit-trail/export` is unreachable for the very persona the story designates as the audit consumer
- **Root cause:** `PayrollAuditController.ExportAuditTrail` is gated `[RequirePermission("Payroll.Export")]` (PayrollAuditController.cs:109), but the `Auditor` role (PermissionCatalog.cs:692-700) holds `{ Audit.View, Employee.ViewAll, Leave.ViewAll, Leave.Reports, Attendance.ViewAll, Payroll.View, Reports.View, Reports.Export }` — it has `Reports.Export` but NOT `Payroll.Export`. AC-4 / TC-PAY-012-09 step 2 require the auditor to "view AND export the trail". Confidence 90% (read from catalog + controller; not executed live — no Auditor persona is seeded in acme, so the runtime 403 is inferred from the role→permission map, which the live tenantadmin/employee/hr results confirm is authoritative). Serilog N/A.
- **Reproduction steps:** Assign a user the `Auditor` role → it can `GET /payroll/audit-trail` (Payroll.View, 200) but `GET /payroll/audit-trail/export?format=csv` would 403 (lacks Payroll.Export). Could not be executed live: no `auditor@acme.test` persona exists in the seed (the four acme personas are tenantadmin/hr/manager/employee). Verified via the role-permission catalog, which the live TC-09 matrix proves is the enforced source of truth.
- **Evidence:** PermissionCatalog.cs:692-700 (Auditor permission set, no `Payroll.Export`); PayrollAuditController.cs:108-109 (export requires `Payroll.Export`). Live: the catalog mapping is authoritative (employee with `Payroll.ViewOwn` only → 403 on every US-PAY-012 endpoint, confirming RequirePermission enforces the exact string).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — defeats a primary AC-4 workflow (auditor exporting the trail for compliance) for the designated persona; contained because TenantAdmin/HRManager (who hold both Payroll.View and Payroll.Export) can still export, and it is read/export only (no data-integrity or cross-tenant impact). Either grant the Auditor role `Payroll.Export` or re-gate the audit-export on `Payroll.View`/`Audit.Export`.

### ISSUE-186 — Audit-trail export (CSV/Excel) omits the before/after JSON columns required by FR-5/BR-4
- **ID:** ISSUE-186
- **Type:** ISSUE (incomplete export vs FR-5)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (2026-07-16, PR pending) — `PayrollAuditService.ExportAuditTrailAsync` now appends
  **`Before` + `After`** columns (the jsonb fields already on the entity + in `PayrollAuditEntryDto`), so the
  exported CSV/XLSX conveys *what* changed (FR-5/BR-4 offline reconstruction), not merely *that* it changed.
  Mutation-verified (`ExportAuditTrail_IncludesBeforeAndAfterColumns` — header carries Before/After + the
  after-value is present; reverting the columns fails it).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-012 / TC-PAY-012-11 (step 1) / FR-5, BR-4
- **Title:** Exported audit trail (CSV + XLSX) contains no `before`/`after` columns, so the exported file cannot convey what actually changed
- **Root cause:** `PayrollAuditService.ExportAuditTrailAsync` (PayrollAuditService.cs:233-247) projects each audit row into only 8 columns (`Timestamp (UTC), Action, Resource Type, Resource Id, Actor User Id, Actor Emp No, IP Address, Trace Id`); the `Before`/`After` jsonb fields — present on the entity and returned by the JSON API (`PayrollAuditEntryDto`) — are not added to the export columns. Confidence 98% (source + live CSV header). Serilog N/A (200).
- **Reproduction steps:** acme tenantadmin → `GET /api/v1/payroll/audit-trail/export?format=csv&action=SalaryComponent.Updated` → CSV header `Timestamp (UTC),Action,Resource Type,Resource Id,Actor User Id,Actor Emp No,IP Address,Trace Id` — no `Before`/`After`. The on-screen/API view (`GET /audit-trail`) DOES return before/after, so the export is strictly less complete than the screen it backs.
- **Evidence:** Live CSV header (above); PayrollAuditService.cs:233 `Columns = new[] { "Timestamp (UTC)", "Action", "Resource Type", "Resource Id", "Actor User Id", "Actor Emp No", "IP Address", "Trace Id" }`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — FR-5 + BR-4 require the export to let an auditor reconstruct the change sequence; without before/after the exported file records *that* a component changed but not *from what to what*, defeating offline audit. Contained: the data is not lost (queryable via the API), only absent from the export artifact.

### TC-PAY-ISO-045 — Cross-tenant READ isolation (AC-5) — FAIL on audit-trail (BUG-003 EXTENDS, ISSUE-187); history + timeline self-protected
Acme token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` results:
- **`GET /runs/history` → self-protected.** Returns techoneglobal's run set (`totalCount:0`, empty — techoneglobal has no runs); acme's June run does NOT appear. PayrollRuns reads via the EF global query filter scoped to the subdomain-resolved tenant; no acme run leaks.
- **`GET /runs/{acmeRunId}/audit-timeline` → self-protected.** 404 `run_not_found` — the tenant-scoped existence check makes acme's run invisible under techoneglobal context; no acme event leaks.
- **`GET /audit-trail` → LEAKS (FAIL).** Returns **3 rows all stamped tenantId `019ef3c3-…` (techoneglobal)**, NOT acme's `019ef3ba-…`. The acme-token holder reads **techoneglobal's** payroll audit entries by flipping only the subdomain header. This is the **BUG-003** mechanism (subdomain-driven `_tenantContext.TenantId`, JWT tenant claim never validated against the subdomain; root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware) **extending** to the payroll audit-trail read surface — exactly as US-PAY-010 ISSUE-181 found on the reconciliation report. Recorded as ISSUE-187 (BUG-003 extension), NOT re-filed as a new BUG.

### TC-PAY-ISO-046 — Tenant-context rejection + IDOR (AC-5) — FAIL (export leak inherits BUG-003 via ISSUE-187); negative arms PASS
- **Missing tenant context (no subdomain header): PASS** — `/audit-trail` and `/runs/history` → **400** ("Tenant context is not resolved"); no fallback to a default tenant.
- **Invalid/non-existent subdomain: PASS** — `/audit-trail` with `X-Tenant-Subdomain: doesnotexist999` → **404 "Workspace not found"**; no data served.
- **Cross-tenant audit-trail export IDOR: FAIL** — acme token + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `GET /audit-trail/export?format=csv` returns **200 with 3 techoneglobal data rows** (same leak as the audit-trail list). Inherits BUG-003 via ISSUE-187.
- The per-run-timeline IDOR (acme reading a foreign run id) is blocked (404, see ISO-045). The leak is specifically the **unfiltered audit-trail list + its export**, which key off `_tenantContext.TenantId` (subdomain) with no JWT-tenant cross-check.

### ISSUE-187 — BUG-003 EXTENDS to the payroll audit-trail read + export (acme JWT + foreign subdomain header → foreign tenant's audit rows)
- **ID:** ISSUE-187
- **Type:** ISSUE (cross-tenant read leak — extension of the systemic BUG-003; root locus already filed as BUG-003 / US-AUTH-007, NOT re-filed)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (stale — verified 2026-07-06 fixed by the GLOBAL `TenantAccessGuardMiddleware` (#119); live cross-tenant probes — acme JWT + spoofed `X-Tenant-Subdomain` on non-`/tenant/*` routes payroll/onboarding/recruitment reads AND writes — all returned 403 `cross_tenant_denied`. The guard is not path-scoped; the original `/tenant/*`-only concern was incorrect.)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-012 / TC-PAY-ISO-045 + TC-PAY-ISO-046 (AC-5, FR-3/FR-4)
- **Title:** `GET /payroll/audit-trail` and `/payroll/audit-trail/export` return ANOTHER tenant's payroll audit rows when an authenticated user supplies that tenant's `X-Tenant-Subdomain` header — the JWT tenant claim is never validated against the resolved subdomain
- **Root cause:** `PayrollAuditService.BuildTrailQuery` scopes the audit query with `a.TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId` (PayrollAuditService.cs:146-149), and `_tenantContext.TenantId` is populated by `TenantResolutionMiddleware` purely from the request **subdomain** (dev: `X-Tenant-Subdomain`), with no check that it equals the JWT's `tenant_id` claim. This is the documented systemic **BUG-003** (root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware) — the same class that US-PAY-010 ISSUE-181 found on the reconciliation report. The audit-trail and its export both inherit it. Confidence 98% (reproduced live: distinct foreign tenantId in returned rows + source path). Note: the run-history list and the per-run timeline are self-protected by *behaviour* (they return the subdomain-tenant's own set / 404), so they don't *leak across* — but they too resolve tenant from the subdomain (same root mechanism).
- **Reproduction steps:** Login `tenantadmin@acme.test` (subdomain acme) to get the acme JWT. Then `GET /api/v1/payroll/audit-trail?pageSize=200` with `Authorization: Bearer <acme JWT>` + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: techoneglobal` → `200`, `totalCount:3`, every row `tenantId=019ef3c3-…` (techoneglobal). Same with `/audit-trail/export?format=csv` → 200, 3 techoneglobal data rows. Baseline (acme subdomain) returns acme's 88 rows (`019ef3ba-…`).
- **Evidence:** audit-trail (techoneglobal header) → `{"totalCount":3}`, distinct row tenantIds `{019ef3c3-16ce-7279-8e6d-bb5674ad4261}`; export CSV (techoneglobal header) → 200, sample row `2026-06-26 13:33:16Z,StatutoryRule.Created,StatutoryRule,019f0422-…` belonging to techoneglobal. Source: PayrollAuditService.cs:146-149; root locus TenantResolutionMiddleware (US-AUTH-007 / BUG-003).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — direct cross-tenant disclosure of another tenant's payroll audit trail (actors, actions, resource ids, IPs, trace ids) and a downloadable export of it, breaking AC-5 / FR-3 tenant isolation. Not a NEW root cause (it is BUG-003); filed as an extension so the audit-trail+export surface is tracked under the systemic fix. Mitigated only by the fix to BUG-003 (validate JWT tenant == resolved subdomain).

### TC-PAY-ISO-047 — Audit-write tenant-stamping; injected tenant_id/actor ignored (AC-5/FR-2/FR-3, BR-7) — PASS
Created a probe component under acme with `tenantId`/`TenantId`=`019ef3c3-…` (techoneglobal) and `actorUserId`=`00000000-…-000999` injected into the request body. The resulting `SalaryComponent.Created` audit row was stamped **tenantId=acme `019ef3ba-…`** (server-side via TenantInterceptor) and **actorUserId=`019efa61-…`** (the acme JWT user) — the injected values were entirely ignored (the command/DTO has no such fields). Querying that resourceId under techoneglobal context → `totalCount:0`: A's operation never wrote a B-attributed audit entry. Combined with TC-07 (no update/delete path), audit rows are server-tenant-stamped + append-only. (Note: this write path stamps from the *resolved* tenant context, so it is correct here; the cross-tenant exposure in ISSUE-187 is on the READ side via the subdomain header, a separate BUG-003 concern.)

### TC-PAY-ISO-048 — Tenant-scoped history/audit cache + export-file infrastructure (AC-5/FR-5/NFR-1) — PASS (CONDITIONAL: no cache/temp-file layer)
The conditional fallback (step 7) applies: `PayrollAuditService` has **no cache layer** (`IMemoryCache`/`IDistributedCache` absent) and the export has **no temp-file store** — `ExportAuditTrailAsync` builds an in-memory `byte[]` and streams it via `File(export.FileContent, contentType, fileName)` (PayrollAuditService.cs:251 + controller `File(...)`), so there is no persisted server-side file handle for another tenant to download. Every history/audit query is a direct EF query with the tenant scoping inline (PayrollRuns via the global filter; audit_log via the explicit `TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId` predicate) — no shared/global cache key exists to cross-pollute. The no-cross-tenant-cache-hit / no-export-file-leak guarantees hold at the infrastructure level. (Caveat: the *content* of an export can still be cross-tenant via the subdomain-context leak — ISSUE-187 — but that is the read tenant-context issue, not a cache/file-store leak; the file-store infra itself is clean.) Archival to cold storage (NFR-7) not implemented/observable — not asserted.

### TC-PAY-012-10 — Audit-query perf P95<=2s over 50k entries + async writes (NFR-1/2/3) — BLOCKED (no perf seed)
BLOCKED: no 50,000-entry / 1-year audit seed exists (acme has 88 payroll audit rows total) and no BRIN-index/perf observability harness is wired. Cannot meaningfully measure P95 over 1 year or the async-write decoupling without the seeded volume. Code note (not a verdict): audit-trail filters are EF range predicates on `CreatedAt`; whether a BRIN index on the timestamp column exists was not verified (NFR-3 is flagged as an extension point in the TC itself). Async-write decoupling (NFR-1) not exercised. Re-run when a perf dataset + index are provisioned.

### TC-PAY-012-12 — Accessibility + responsive (WCAG 2.1 AA, 360–1920px) — BLOCKED (FE down)
BLOCKED: this is a UI/a11y/cross-browser TC; FE :4200 is pinned-to-platform and Docker is unavailable, so the Payroll History table, run-detail audit timeline, diff view, filter bar, and export toolbar cannot be rendered/driven via Playwright + axe-core. No partial assertion possible at the API layer.

Held by TenantAdmin/HRManager/Auditor (View) — HROfficer holds NO payroll perm by design. Executor: `tenantadmin@acme.test`.

## US-NTF-001 -- In-App Notification System (Real-Time via SignalR) -- test-runner 2026-06-27 (API-layer; FE :4200 pinned-platform)

### ISSUE-188 -- In-app notification dispatcher has only ONE live producer (HR report export); the flagship AC-2 "leave approval -> real-time notification" is NOT wired
- **ID:** ISSUE-188
- **Type:** ISSUE (orphaned/under-wired feature -- the consumer API works, but no business event feeds it except one report-export path)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #121, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications / US-NTF-001 / TC-NTF-001-01, -02 (AC-2, FR-3/4, NFR-1)
- **Title:** INotificationService.CreateAndDispatchAsync (the persist+SignalR-push seam) is called by exactly ONE producer -- HrReportExportService (report-export-ready). Leave approval (the US-NTF-001 AC-2 headline scenario) and every other module emit nothing into the in-app notification table, so the bell/panel is empty in normal use.
- **Root cause:** Grep of the whole backend shows the only live caller of INotificationService.CreateAndDispatchAsync is HrReportExportService.cs:238 (type ReportExportReady). ApproveLeaveRequestCommandHandler contains NO notification dispatch. The pre-existing log-only INotificationDispatcher / LoggingNotificationDispatcher seam (Onboarding/Performance) is a SEPARATE, un-rewired seam that only writes Serilog -- it does not persist a Notification row or push via SignalR. Rewiring it was intentionally deferred when US-NTF-001 was built (vault notifications note). Net: the real-time in-app feature is plumbed on the READ side but starved on the producer side. Confidence 95% (whole-src grep + handler read).
- **Reproduction steps:** (1) GET /api/v1/notifications as any seeded acme user -> items:[] (DB notification table empty across ALL tenants -- 0 rows before seeding). (2) Approve a leave request -> no Notification row created. (3) grep -rn "CreateAndDispatchAsync" src/backend --include="*.cs" -> only HrReportExportService.cs:238 (excluding interface/impl/tests).
- **Evidence:** notification table row count = 0 (all tenants) before QA seeding. Single live caller HrReportExportService.cs:238. ApproveLeaveRequestCommandHandler notification grep -> NONE. INotificationDispatcher live callers = Onboarding job + checklist service (log-only).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH -- the feature's primary AC (AC-2: leave approval -> real-time in-app notification <2s) cannot occur in normal operation because no producer emits it; only an HR-report-export completion does. Delivery machinery is correct, so not CRIT -- but US-NTF-001's user-visible value is unrealized until the dispatcher is rewired. Known, intentionally-deferred wiring gap, tracked here against the story.

## US-NTF-002 -- Email Notification Templates per Tenant -- test-runner 2026-06-27 (API-layer; FE :4200 pinned-platform)

### BUG-081 -- Notification-template changes (save / reset) are NOT audited; FR-9 unmet (NotificationTemplate is not IAuditableEntity)
- **ID:** BUG-081
- **Type:** BUG (spec violation -- FR-9 / AC-3 / AC-4 require template changes logged in the tenant audit log with before/after)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (stale — auto-fixed by #272, confirmed by regression test in #280, 2026-07-13)
- **Resolution:** #272 (BUG-082) flipped the audit interceptor to opt-OUT, so `NotificationTemplate` (a non-`IAuditExempt` `BaseEntity`) is now auto-audited: PUT→`NotificationTemplate.Update`, reset (soft-delete)→`NotificationTemplate.Delete`. The finding's root cause (the opt-IN `IAuditableEntity` gate) no longer exists. Regression guard `BUG081_NotificationTemplate_write_is_audited` added in #280.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications / US-NTF-002 / TC-NTF-002-04, -10 (FR-9, NFR-6, AC-4)
- **Title:** Saving a tenant template override (PUT) and resetting to default (DELETE) persist the change but write NO audit_logs row -- the automatic before/after audit capture skips NotificationTemplate because the entity does not implement IAuditableEntity.
- **Root cause:** The automatic property-level before/after audit (AuditCaptureInterceptor) only captures entities implementing IAuditableEntity (AuditCaptureInterceptor.cs:78-81, ChangeTracker.Entries of IAuditableEntity). Only THREE entities implement it today: Department, JobTitle, LeaveRequest. NotificationTemplate is BaseEntity (NotificationTemplate.cs:13) but NOT IAuditableEntity, so its inserts/updates/soft-deletes generate no AuditLog row. NotificationTemplateService also writes no explicit audit row. Result: a tenant-admin customizing or resetting an email template leaves no audit trail. Confidence 97% (verified live: PUT then DELETE on leave_approved produced 0 audit_logs rows in the last 5 min for acme; interceptor source confirms the IAuditableEntity gate + the 3-entity allow-set).
- **Reproduction steps:** As tenantadmin@acme.test (subdomain acme): PUT /api/v1/notification-templates/leave_approved?language=en with a custom body (200, isCustom=true, version=1), then DELETE /api/v1/notification-templates/leave_approved?language=en (200, isCustom=false). Query audit_logs for tenant=acme created in the last 5 min -> 0 rows. Neither the save nor the reset is audited.
- **Evidence:** notification_template row created (version 1) then soft-deleted (is_deleted=t) -- the writes happened. audit_logs delta over the window = 0 rows. AuditCaptureInterceptor.cs:78-81 (IAuditableEntity gate); IAuditableEntity implementers = {Department, JobTitle, LeaveRequest} only; NotificationTemplate.cs:13 is BaseEntity-only.
- **Severity rationale:** MED -- the spec'd compliance/audit requirement (FR-9: log template changes; AC-4 reset must produce an audit record) is silently unmet, so there is no who-changed-what trail for tenant email templates. Not data loss or a security bypass on its own, so not HIGH; but it is a genuine missing control. Same root class as the broader US-NTF-004 limitation (auto-audit covers only 3 entity types) -- see the US-NTF-004 section.

### ISSUE-189 -- BUG-003 EXTENDS to notification-template WRITE: acme JWT + foreign subdomain header writes a template override into the FOREIGN tenant
- **ID:** ISSUE-189
- **Type:** ISSUE (cross-tenant WRITE leak -- extension of the systemic BUG-003; root locus BUG-003 / US-AUTH-007, NOT re-filed)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #119, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications / US-NTF-002 / TC-NTF-ISO-005, -006, -007 (AC-5, FR-10, NFR-2)
- **Title:** PUT /api/v1/notification-templates/{eventKey} stamps the override with the tenant resolved from the X-Tenant-Subdomain header, NOT the JWT tenant claim -- so an authenticated user of Tenant A can create/modify Tenant B's email template overrides by sending B's subdomain header with A's token.
- **Root cause:** Template writes resolve the tenant from _tenantContext.TenantId, which TenantResolutionMiddleware populates purely from the request subdomain (dev: X-Tenant-Subdomain), with no check that it equals the JWT tenant_id. This is the documented systemic BUG-003 (root locus US-AUTH-007 / TenantResolutionMiddleware) -- the same write-side class seen elsewhere. The override row is TenantInterceptor-stamped with the RESOLVED (subdomain) tenant, so it lands in the foreign tenant. Confidence 98% (reproduced live: distinct foreign tenant_id on the persisted row).
- **Reproduction steps:** Login tenantadmin@acme.test (subdomain acme) -> acme JWT (tenant_id 019ef3ba-...). PUT /api/v1/notification-templates/leave_approved?language=en with Authorization Bearer acme-JWT + X-Tenant-Subdomain techoneglobal + body subject "CROSS-TENANT WRITE PROBE" -> 200 "Template saved." version 1. DB: that override row is stamped tenant_id=techoneglobal (019ef3c3-...), is_deleted=f; a subsequent template list under techoneglobal shows leave_approved isCustom=true. (Probe row hard-deleted after verification.)
- **Evidence:** Persisted row notification_template.subject CROSS-TENANT WRITE PROBE joined to tenants -> subdomain=techoneglobal. List under techoneglobal after the write -> leave_approved isCustom=true. Root locus TenantResolutionMiddleware (US-AUTH-007 / BUG-003).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH -- a cross-tenant WRITE: Tenant A can silently replace Tenant B's customer-facing email templates (e.g. inject content into B's "Leave Approved" emails to B's employees). Write-side BUG-003 is materially worse than the read leak. Not a NEW root cause (it is BUG-003); filed as an extension so the template write surface is tracked under the systemic fix. Mitigated only by fixing BUG-003 (validate JWT tenant == resolved subdomain).

A second-language variant + dispatch-time language selection needs the send pipeline + a non-en seed; not fully exercised. Default (en) path PASS; multi-language selection not driven.
- **TC-NTF-002-07 (unresolved placeholder -> empty string, not raw token; send not aborted) -- PASS (BR-5).** Preview with does.not.exist renders empty, not the raw token; known placeholders still resolve; render not aborted.
- **TC-NTF-002-08 (non-admin cannot view/edit/save/reset/send-test) -- PASS.** HR and Employee both -> 403 on GET list (Tenant.ViewSettings required); write gate Tenant.ManageSettings. Only Tenant Admin/Owner reach the surface.
- **TC-NTF-002-09 (max 2 language variants per template) -- BLOCKED.** Needs creating 3 language variants to assert the 3rd is rejected; the plan-configurable cap path was not exercised (single-en seed). Not driven.
- **TC-NTF-002-10 (template change audited with before/after) -- FAIL (BUG-081).** The save WAS persisted but produced NO audit_logs row (NotificationTemplate is not IAuditableEntity). Before/after capture does not fire for this entity.
- **TC-NTF-002-11 (editor WCAG/keyboard/responsive) -- BLOCKED (FE down).** UI/a11y TC; SPA :4200 pinned-platform.
- **TC-NTF-002-12 (list Default/Custom + version/last-modified; load/render SLA) -- PASS (functional) / perf indicative.** List returns per-event override status; detail carries version (0 default, increments on save). Editor-load/render SLA not measured (no FE/perf harness) -- functional contract PASS.

### US-NTF-002 ISOLATION TCs -- verdicts
- **TC-NTF-ISO-005 (Tenant A custom template invisible/unusable to Tenant B; ID injection -> 404) -- PASS (read) but see ISSUE-189 (write).** READ: there is no tenant id in any route (eventKey-based); a tenant only ever sees its own override status via _tenantContext. Read-side does not disclose another tenant's override. (The WRITE-side cross-tenant leak is ISSUE-189.)
- **TC-NTF-ISO-006 (missing tenant ctx rejected; cross-tenant injection -> 404/ignored) -- FAIL (ISSUE-189).** Missing-subdomain + unknown-subdomain are rejected (400/404, consistent with the platform). BUT supplying a FOREIGN tenant subdomain with tenant A token is NOT rejected -- the write lands in tenant B (ISSUE-189). The cross-tenant-injection-ignored expectation fails on the write path.
- **TC-NTF-ISO-007 (EF filter blocks cross-tenant reads; writes tenant-stamped + audited; RLS deferred) -- FAIL (ISSUE-189 + BUG-081).** Writes ARE tenant-stamped -- but stamped to the SUBDOMAIN tenant, which is the leak (a write under techoneglobal context stamps techoneglobal, enabling cross-tenant authorship). And the write is not audited (BUG-081). RLS deferred as documented.
- **TC-NTF-ISO-008 (send/render pipeline selects templates strictly within recipient tenant) -- BLOCKED.** Requires driving the Hangfire send pipeline with a recipient in a known tenant; not exercised at the API layer. The template LOOKUP is _tenantContext-scoped in code, but given ISSUE-189 the context itself is subdomain-trusting -- flagged.

**US-NTF-002 tally (16 TCs): 7 PASS / 4 FAIL / 5 BLOCKED.** PASS: -01,-02,-03,-05,-07,-08,-12, + ISO-005(read). FAIL: -04,-10 (BUG-081 no template audit), ISO-006, ISO-007 (ISSUE-189 cross-tenant write + BUG-081). BLOCKED: -06,-09,-11, ISO-008 (multi-language/send-pipeline/FE). New findings: BUG-081 MED (template changes not audited -- NotificationTemplate not IAuditableEntity), ISSUE-189 HIGH (BUG-003 extends to template WRITE -- cross-tenant override authorship). New max: BUG-081 / ISSUE-189.

## US-NTF-003 -- Notification Preferences per User -- test-runner 2026-06-27 (API-layer; FE :4200 pinned-platform)

### ISSUE-190 -- BUG-003 EXTENDS to notification-preference WRITE: a user can write a preference row into a tenant they do NOT belong to (subdomain-trusted tenant context)
- **ID:** ISSUE-190
- **Type:** ISSUE (cross-tenant WRITE leak -- extension of the systemic BUG-003; root locus BUG-003 / US-AUTH-007, NOT re-filed)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #119, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications / US-NTF-003 / TC-NTF-003-09, -10, TC-NTF-ISO-009, -010, -011 (AC-5, FR-8, NFR-2, BR-4)
- **Title:** PUT /api/v1/notification-preferences/{category} stamps the row with the tenant resolved from the X-Tenant-Subdomain header, not the JWT tenant claim -- so an authenticated acme user can create a preference override stamped into the techoneglobal tenant (a tenant they have no membership in) by sending techoneglobal's subdomain header with their acme token.
- **Root cause:** Preference writes resolve tenant from _tenantContext.TenantId (subdomain-driven via TenantResolutionMiddleware; dev X-Tenant-Subdomain) and user from ICurrentUser (JWT sub), with no check that the JWT tenant_id == the resolved subdomain tenant, and no check that the user has an active membership in the resolved tenant. The row is TenantInterceptor-stamped with the resolved (foreign) tenant. Systemic BUG-003 (root locus US-AUTH-007). Confidence 95% (reproduced: acme EMP user_id wrote a notification_preference row stamped tenant_id=techoneglobal).
- **Reproduction steps:** Login employee@acme.test (subdomain acme) -> acme JWT (user 019efa61-e621-..., tenant 019ef3ba-...). PUT /api/v1/notification-preferences/LeaveUpdates with Authorization Bearer acme-JWT + X-Tenant-Subdomain techoneglobal + body {channelInApp:true,channelEmail:false} -> 200 success. DB: notification_preference row for that user_id is stamped tenant_id=techoneglobal (019ef3c3-...) -- a tenant the acme user has no membership in. (Probe row hard-deleted after verification.)
- **Evidence:** notification_preference row {user_id 019efa61-e621-..., tenant_id techoneglobal, category LeaveUpdates, channel_email f}. The acme user has no user_tenants membership in techoneglobal. Root locus TenantResolutionMiddleware (US-AUTH-007 / BUG-003).
- **Severity rationale:** MED -- a cross-tenant write, but the blast radius is narrower than the template leak: the row is keyed (tenant,user,category) and only affects the writing user's own future notification routing IF the platform ever evaluates that user under that foreign tenant (which itself requires the same broken context). It pollutes a foreign tenant's preference table with rows for a non-member and is a clear isolation breach (BR-4 "per tenant membership" without a membership check), but it does not expose or corrupt another USER's data. Not a NEW root cause (BUG-003); filed as an extension. Note: there is no client-supplied userId (route or body), so there is no classic cross-USER IDOR -- the leak is purely the tenant dimension.

### US-NTF-003 -- per-TC verdicts (test-runner 2026-06-27, API-layer)
- **TC-NTF-003-01 (disable email for Leave Updates -> in-app only, no email) -- PASS.** PUT LeaveUpdates {inApp:true,email:false} -> 200, persisted (re-GET confirms inApp=true,email=false). The dispatch-time suppression of email runs in the producer/worker (not driven; producer largely unwired per ISSUE-188) but the preference write + persistence is correct.
- **TC-NTF-003-02 (mandatory Security Alerts locked; cannot disable via API) -- PASS (BR-2).** SecurityAlerts is isMandatory=true (inApp+email both on); PUT both-off -> 422. Cannot be disabled server-side. (UI greyed-out/tooltip arm not driven -- FE down.)
- **TC-NTF-003-03 (new user inherits tenant default preferences) -- PASS (inheritance via effective matrix).** GET returns the effective matrix (8 categories) with tenant/system defaults where the user has no override (e.g. RecruitmentUpdates email=false by default). New-user-specific seeding not separately driven, but the cascade (defaults surfaced when no user override) is in force.
- **TC-NTF-003-04 (Reset to Defaults restores tenant defaults) -- PASS (FR-7).** After disabling LeaveUpdates email, POST /reset reverts it to inApp=true,email=true (tenant default). Cancel branch is a UI concern (not driven).
- **TC-NTF-003-05 (cannot disable BOTH channels for non-mandatory; >=1 stays on) -- PASS (BR-3).** PUT LeaveUpdates both-off -> 422 "At least one channel must remain enabled for Leave Updates." (code both_channels_off).
- **TC-NTF-003-06 (invalid IANA tz rejected; valid accepted; injection blocked) -- PASS.** PUT /quiet-hours valid {Asia/Colombo,23:00,07:00} -> 200; invalid tz "Not/AZone; DROP TABLE" -> 422 invalid_timezone (injection string rejected, not executed); invalid time "99:99" -> 422 invalid_time.
- **TC-NTF-003-07 (Quiet Hours queues email; in-app stays real-time) -- BLOCKED.** The queue-at-23:00 / release-after-07:00 worker path needs the Hangfire outbox + a producer; not exercisable at the API layer (and producer largely unwired). The quiet-hours SETTING persists correctly (TC-003-06).
- **TC-NTF-003-08 (preference change invalidates cache; next dispatch reflects change; Redis-conditional) -- PASS (conditional).** Redis absent on dev -> always-fresh DB lookup is in force (the write persists and a re-GET reflects it immediately). The cache-invalidation key shape is conditional/not-wired -- the always-correct DB path holds.
- **TC-NTF-003-09 (a user cannot modify another user's preferences; IDOR -> 404) -- PASS (no cross-user vector).** There is no userId in the route or body -- every operation targets ICurrentUser. A different token only ever edits its own prefs; there is no id to inject. (Tenant-dimension leak is ISSUE-190, a separate axis.)
- **TC-NTF-003-10 (unauthenticated / no-tenant-context rejected) -- PASS (auth/tenant) but tenant-injection FAIL (ISSUE-190).** No token -> 401; missing subdomain -> 400 (no default-tenant fallback). BUT a FOREIGN subdomain with a valid token is accepted and writes into that tenant (ISSUE-190) -- the cross-tenant-context arm fails.
- **TC-NTF-003-11 (toggles keyboard/ARIA; matrix collapses at 360px) -- BLOCKED (FE down).** UI/a11y TC; SPA :4200 pinned-platform.
- **TC-NTF-003-12 (page load <=500ms P95; dispatch lookup cheap; Redis cache conditional) -- BLOCKED/indicative.** No FE/perf harness; GET /preferences responds well under 500ms at the API layer (indicative), but the page-load SLA + Redis cache path are not measurable on dev.

### US-NTF-003 ISOLATION TCs -- verdicts
- **TC-NTF-ISO-009 (same user's prefs in Tenant X independent from Tenant Y) -- PARTIAL/FAIL (ISSUE-190).** Prefs ARE keyed (tenant,user) so they are nominally independent per membership -- but because the tenant is taken from the subdomain with no membership check, a user can write into a tenant they don't belong to (ISSUE-190), undermining the "per legitimate membership" guarantee.
- **TC-NTF-ISO-010 (cross-tenant pref ID injection -> 404; missing tenant ctx rejected) -- PARTIAL.** There is no preference ID in any route (category-based, current-user) so there is no id to inject cross-tenant -> the classic injection vector is absent (PASS). Missing tenant ctx -> 400 (PASS). But the foreign-subdomain write is accepted (ISSUE-190).
- **TC-NTF-ISO-011 (EF filter blocks cross-tenant reads; writes tenant-stamped; RLS deferred) -- FAIL (ISSUE-190).** Reads are tenant+user scoped (a user under a foreign subdomain sees that subdomain's defaults/their-own-rows-there, not another user's data). Writes are tenant-stamped to the SUBDOMAIN tenant -- which is the leak. RLS deferred as documented.
- **TC-NTF-ISO-012 (dispatch-time lookup + cache keys tenant+user scoped; Redis-conditional) -- PASS (conditional).** Lookup is tenant+user scoped; Redis cache absent on dev (always-fresh DB). Cache-key shape conditional/not-wired.

**US-NTF-003 tally (16 TCs): 9 PASS / 3 FAIL / 4 BLOCKED.** PASS: -01,-02,-03,-04,-05,-06,-08,-09, ISO-012. FAIL: -10 (tenant-injection arm, ISSUE-190), ISO-009, ISO-011 (ISSUE-190). PARTIAL counted toward FAIL where the isolation arm fails. BLOCKED: -07,-11,-12, ISO-010(partial; counted PASS for the injection-absent arm -> recorded BLOCKED-leaning PASS, listed under PASS-adjacent). New finding: ISSUE-190 MED (BUG-003 extends to preference WRITE; non-member can write into a foreign tenant). Preference functionality + validation SOLID (mandatory lock, both-off block, tz validation/injection-reject, reset, persistence). Probe pref row hard-deleted post-verify. New max: ISSUE-190.
