## Front-end UI / Accessibility Test Run — 2026-06-30 (REPORT-ONLY; Core HR module batch; real subdomain multi-tenancy)

Executed the Core HR **render + accessibility (Lighthouse/axe-core) + console** test arms against the running
Angular FE via `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` (acme tenant, native subdomain resolution), BE up on `:5000`.
Logged in as `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`. Tooling worked smoothly (Playwright MCP for
snapshot/console/interactions; Chrome DevTools MCP `lighthouse_audit` for the a11y score). Pages covered:
employee list, employee detail/profile, employee create/edit (wizard), departments (list/tree), job titles,
locations, bulk-import wizard, custom fields. **One new BUG (BUG-097), plus systemic BUG-096 / ISSUE-204
recurrences noted by reference.** No data writes; acme seed untouched.

### BUG-097 — Reloading or deep-linking ANY authenticated route logs the user out: the app bootstrap never attempts a silent session restore from the valid httpOnly refresh cookie, so the in-memory access token is lost on every full page load and the route guard bounces to `/auth/login`
- **ID:** BUG-097
- **Type:** BUG (broken vs spec — authenticated session does not survive a page reload / deep link, despite a live refresh cookie)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #260, 2026-07-12)
- **Resolution:** Added `AuthService.restoreSession()` — a silent `/auth/refresh` (httpOnly cookie) → `/auth/me` chain that re-mints the in-memory access token and hydrates the user/roles/permissions signals, swallowing 401/no-cookie (no navigate, no toast) so an anonymous first load boots cleanly. Wired it into a single sequential `APP_INITIALIZER` chained after tenant resolution (`initializeApp`: `tenantService.resolve().then(() => authService.restoreSession())` — one chained factory, not two concurrent initializers, so the tenant header is set before refresh and the guard reads the restored `currentUser` synchronously with no race). FE-only (the `/auth/refresh` + `/auth/me` capability already existed). Regression: `auth.service.spec.ts` — success hydrates the session; 401 resolves without navigating/toasting. Verified `npm run build` + 17/17 auth spec headless (`ChromeHeadlessNoSandbox`).
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Authentication / session persistence (US-AUTH-001 / US-AUTH-008) — surfaced while executing Core HR UI TCs (every deep-linked Core HR route is affected)
- **Title:** The access token is held **in-memory only** (deliberate XSS posture, `AuthService.accessToken`, no localStorage/sessionStorage). On a hard navigation (browser reload, pasted/deep-linked URL, new tab), the in-memory token is wiped and the SPA's `APP_INITIALIZER` only resolves the **tenant** from subdomain — it does **not** call the existing refresh/restore flow. So `authGuard` sees no token and redirects to `/auth/login`, even though the backend's httpOnly refresh cookie is still valid and a `refreshToken()`/`completeSsoLogin()`-style silent re-mint already exists in `AuthService`. Net effect: any reload/deep-link of `/dashboard`, `/employees`, `/departments`, etc. drops the user to the login screen.
- **Root cause:** `app.config.ts` registers exactly one `APP_INITIALIZER` → `initializeTenant` (deps: `TenantService`) which only does subdomain→tenant resolution. There is no app-bootstrap hook that calls `AuthService.refreshToken()` / a `restoreSession()` to silently re-mint the in-memory access token from the httpOnly refresh cookie before the router/guards run. The capability exists but is wired **only** to the SSO callback (`completeSsoLogin()`), not to general app load. Confidence: **HIGH** — verified live (token absent from both web-storages and JS-cookies; reload of an authenticated route deterministically lands on `/auth/login`) and corroborated by reading `auth.service.ts` (in-memory token, lines 39-40; refresh flow lines 141-173) + `app.config.ts` (single tenant-only initializer, lines 89-95). No backend log needed — this is a pure FE bootstrap-wiring gap.
- **Reproduction steps:** (1) `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/auth/login` → sign in as `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → lands on `/dashboard` (authenticated, works). (2) Hard-reload the page (or paste `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/dashboard` into the address bar, or open any authenticated route in a new tab). (3) Observe: the URL resolves to `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/auth/login` — you are logged out. Confirmed via `location.href` after `browser_navigate('/dashboard')` returning `…/auth/login`; `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` both empty, `document.cookie` empty (refresh token is httpOnly, present but never consumed on load).
- **Evidence:** Playwright `evaluate` → `{ local: [], session: [], localVals: "{}" }` (no persisted token); after `browser_navigate('http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/dashboard')` while authenticated, `location.href === "http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/auth/login"`. Login `POST /api/v1/auth/login => 200` (refresh cookie is set server-side). Code: `src/frontend/src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts` (in-memory `accessToken`, `refreshToken()`), `src/frontend/src/app/app.config.ts` lines 89-95 (only `initializeTenant`, no auth-restore initializer).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — breaks a primary expectation of a web app: a logged-in user who refreshes, opens a bookmark, or shares/deep-links a page is silently kicked to login and loses their place. It is not data-destructive and a re-login recovers, so not CRIT, but it degrades every authenticated flow and makes deep-linking/bookmarking unusable. The fix is a single app-bootstrap silent-refresh (the mechanism already exists). NOTE for this test batch: because of BUG-097, all Core HR pages below were reached via in-app SPA navigation (clicking sidebar links), not hard URL loads.

### BUG-098 — Leave-types list (and leave-application picker) throw a null-deref on any leave type with `color = null`: `getContrastTextColor` calls `.replace('#','')` on null
- **ID:** BUG-098
- **Type:** BUG (FE runtime null-deref — `TypeError` during render)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV-001 (leave types) + US-LV-003 (apply for leave) / `leave-management/TC-LV-001-*` UI arms
- **Title:** `getContrastTextColor(hex: string)` (`src/frontend/src/app/features/leave-management/models/leave-type.models.ts:127-128`) does `const c = hex.replace('#','')` with **no null/empty guard**. The DB allows `leave_types.color` to be NULL (acme currently has **8 of 13** leave types with `color = null`), and the type signature lies (`hex: string` while runtime passes `null`). The three call sites bind it directly in templates — `leave-type-list.component.ts:587`, `leave-type-form.component.ts:718`, `leave-application.component.ts:597` — so each null-color row throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replace')` during change detection.
- **Root cause:** missing null-coalescing (e.g. `(hex ?? '#000000').replace('#','')` or guard returning a default) at `leave-type.models.ts:128`; compounded by the DB/DTO permitting null `color` while the FE contract assumes a non-null hex. Confidence: **HIGH** — source line matches the thrown stack exactly; null-color rows confirmed in acme data (8/13).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → navigate (in-app, per BUG-097) to **Leave types**. The list renders the colored chips; rows whose `color` is null throw the TypeError (console) and the chip/contrast styling breaks. Same helper is hit on the employee **Apply for leave** type-picker.

### ISSUE-206 — FE employee form calls `GET /tenant/custom-fields/active?entityType=employee` → 404 (endpoint never implemented) — dynamic custom fields never render
- **Type:** ISSUE (contract drift / missing endpoint) · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (BE) (PR #339, 2026-07-17) · **Layer:** FE+BE
> **RESOLVED — BE (2026-07-17):** Implemented the missing endpoint `GET /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields/active?entityType=…` → new `GetActiveCustomFieldsQuery` → `CustomFieldService.GetActiveAsync` (returns the ACTIVE definitions for the entity type, ordered by DisplayOrder). Gated on `[Authorize]` only (NOT the admin `CustomField.View`): it returns non-sensitive field **definitions** and is needed by whoever uses the create/edit form (e.g. HR on the employee wizard) — gating it on the admin permission would 403 those users and leave the form still broken; tenant-scoped by the global filter. 2 arms (active+entity-filtered → single field; entityType-required → 400) + 42 existing green (44/44); mutation-verified (dropping `IsActive` fails the active-only arm). **FE render half** (the wizard consuming the response) is now unblocked but not verified here — needs a running-UI pass (env-gated) to close the FE side.
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-001 (employee create) + US-CHR-012 (custom fields) / TC-CHR-084, TC-CHR-296
- **Title:** When the **Add New Employee** wizard (`/employees/new`) loads, it issues `GET /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields/active?entityType=employee` to fetch the tenant's active custom-field definitions to render dynamically. The backend `CustomFieldsController` (`[Route("api/v1/tenant/custom-fields")]`) exposes only `[HttpGet]` (list) and `[HttpGet("{id:guid}")]` — there is **no `active` sub-route**, so the call returns **404 Not Found**. Consequently no dynamic/tenant-configured custom fields render on the create form (FR-9 / AC-6 flow).
- **Root cause:** FE↔BE contract mismatch — the Angular employee-form service expects an `/custom-fields/active?entityType=…` endpoint that was never implemented on `CustomFieldsController.cs` (only base-list + by-id exist). Confidence: **HIGH** — the 404 URL is captured live and the controller route table confirms the missing action. (This is the same class as the documented FE↔BE prefix/route-mismatch findings.)
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → Employees → **Add Employee** (→ `/employees/new`). Open DevTools/Network: `GET /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields/active?entityType=employee => 404`. No custom-field inputs appear in the wizard.
- **Evidence:** network `98. [GET] /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields/active?entityType=employee => [404] Not Found`; backend `CustomFieldsController.cs` route `api/v1/tenant/custom-fields` with only `[HttpGet]` (line 32) and `[HttpGet("{id:guid}")]` (line 51) — no `active` action.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the core wizard still renders and standard fields work; only the dynamic custom-field section is silently absent (a 404 swallowed in the console), so tenants that configured custom fields can't capture them at create time. Contained to the custom-fields feature.

### ISSUE-207 — Org Tree page shows "No departments found" empty-state despite departments existing (API 200)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #357, 2026-07-18) · **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-006 (Organization Tree) / TC-CHR-152, TC-CHR-154, TC-CHR-156, TC-CHR-158, TC-CHR-161, TC-CHR-169
- **Title:** `/org-tree` ("Organization Chart") renders its chrome (heading, Department-Hierarchy / Reporting-Structure view toggle, 100% zoom, "Export organization chart as PNG") but the chart body shows the empty-state **"No departments found. Create departments to see the organization chart."** even though the **Departments** page lists 51 departments for acme (3 Active: Engineering, Sales, engineering; rest Inactive QA residue). The page's own call `GET /api/v1/tenant/org-tree?view=department&depth=2` returns **200 OK**, so data is served but no nodes render.
- **Root cause:** Unconfirmed within budget. Two candidates: (a) the org-tree endpoint at `depth=2` returns only a hierarchy rooted on parent/child links and the Active departments are flat roots with no children, so the FE treats the result as empty; or (b) the FE maps the 200 payload's node array under the wrong key and falls through to the empty-state. The 200 response body could not be re-read from a raw fetch (interceptor-injected auth → manual fetch 401s). Confidence: **55%** it is a FE mapping/empty-detection gap rather than truly-empty data, given 3 Active departments exist. No JS exception is thrown (clean empty-state, not a crash).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → soft-nav to `/org-tree` (in-app; per BUG-097 a hard nav/reload logs out — used pushState+popstate to preserve session). The chart area shows the empty-state; Departments page concurrently shows 51 departments.
- **Evidence:** network `301. [GET] /api/v1/tenant/org-tree?view=department&depth=2 => 200 OK`; `main` empty-state text "No departments found."; Departments page `aria-label^="Edit department"` count = 51 (3 Active). a11y of org-tree chrome is otherwise good (`radiogroup "Organization tree view"`, labeled Export-PNG button).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the org-tree visualization is non-functional for acme (no nodes, so no node-click/search/expand/export-with-content), but it is a secondary visualization page, no crash, and may partly reflect thin active-hierarchy seed rather than a pure bug.
- **RESOLVED (PR #357, 2026-07-18):** confirmed candidate **(b) — a pure FE mapping bug** (not BE rooting). The GET endpoint returns an **object** `{ nodes, view, reportingViewAvailable }` (after the ApiResponse envelope is stripped), but `OrgTreeService` typed it as a bare `IOrgTreeNode[]` and passed it to `buildTreeFromFlat`, whose `for..of` **throws a TypeError on the object** → `treeRoots` stays `[]` → empty state. Fix: project `.nodes` (`map(r => r?.nodes ?? [])`) + `IOrgTreeResult` wire type. The masking unit test (flushed a bare array) now flushes the real object shape → genuine regression; 7/7 org-tree service specs pass. The 3 Active departments now render. Minor follow-up (nested `children` payload unused; FE lazy-loads) → DF-17.

### BUG-100 — Custom Fields management page: list template crashes on render + "Add Custom Field" button throws (modal never opens)
- **Type:** BUG · **Severity:** HIGH · **Status:** RESOLVED (stale — already fixed in commit 46d7ebb2, 2026-07-07; re-verified 2026-07-12) · **Layer:** FE
- **Resolution:** The crash was FE↔BE shape drift — the bare-array `GET /tenant/custom-fields` response was cast directly to `{definitions, planLimits}`, so `definitions` was `undefined` and both the template `definitions().length` and `openAddModal()` threw. Fixed in `46d7ebb2` ("fix(Theme-G): 4 FE↔BE shape-drift bugs"): `custom-field.service.ts` now maps the array→FE shape at the boundary (`toListResponse`, `group.fields ?? []`) so `definitions` is always an array; the `customFieldId`→`id` rename was also fixed. Covered by updated `custom-field-list.component.spec.ts` / `custom-field.service.spec.ts`. Stale-OPEN ledger entry — no further code change.
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-012 (Custom Fields) / TC-CHR-298, TC-CHR-306, TC-CHR-296, TC-CHR-314, TC-CHR-316
- **Title:** `/settings/custom-fields` ("Custom Fields") renders only its header + "Add Custom Field" button. - **Root cause:** The component reads `.length` on a value that is `undefined` rather than an array — both in the list template (`chunk-B6QPS6DS.js:921`) and in `openAddModal` (`chunk-B6QPS6DS.js:782`). Likely an uninitialized signal/array (e.g. existing-fields or dropdown-options collection) that the template and the add-handler both assume is always present. Same defect class as BUG-099 (employee list) — an array-typed field left undefined. Confidence: **75%** — thrown frames + component name are certain; exact undefined member not isolated within budget. Not a backend fault: the list endpoint is 200.

The list area shows the TypeError on render; clicking **Add Custom Field** logs `openAddModal` TypeError and no modal/dialog appears (DOM has no `[role="dialog"]`, page text unchanged).
- **Evidence:** console `ERROR TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') at CustomFieldListComponent_Template (chunk-B6QPS6DS.js:921:71)` and `… at _CustomFieldListComponent.openAddModal (chunk-B6QPS6DS.js:782:126)`; network `313. [GET] /api/v1/tenant/custom-fields?entityType=employee => 200 OK`; after click, `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')` is null and `main` innerText unchanged ("Custom Fields … Add Custom Field").

### BUG-101 — Carry-forward preview totals render `NaN` and every row shows 0: FE↔BE field-name contract mismatch (`carryForward`/`forfeited` vs `projectedCarryForward`/`projectedForfeiture`)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #159, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** FE (DATA contract)
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV-008 / TC-LV-168 (also visible on TC-LV-164/165 carry-forward-preview page)
- **Title:** On `/leave-types/carry-forward-preview` the summary strip shows **Carry-forward: NaN** and **Forfeited: NaN** (while "Employees × types: 55" is correct), and every one of the 55 employee×leave-type rows shows `0`/blank for both numeric columns — the HR carry-forward/forfeiture preview report is non-functional even though it renders.
- **Root cause:** FE↔BE JSON field-name mismatch. Backend `CarryForwardPreviewDto` (`HRM.Application/Features/LeaveCarryForward/DTOs/CarryForwardPreviewDto.cs:26,29`) serializes the numeric fields as `carryForward` and `forfeited`. The FE row model `ICarryForwardPreviewRow` (`src/frontend/.../models/carry-forward-preview.models.ts:34-36`) expects `projectedCarryForward` and `projectedForfeiture`, and the service does no rename mapping. Result: on every parsed row `r.projectedCarryForward === undefined` → the cell template `@if (r.projectedCarryForward > 0)` is false so it renders nothing (effectively "0"), and `sumTotals()` does `0 + undefined` → `NaN` for the summary cards (no `?? 0` guard). Confirmed live: `allRows()` had 55 rows, `typeof projectedCarryForward === 'undefined'` on all of them, `totals() === {carryForward: null/NaN, forfeiture: null/NaN, rows: 55}`. Confidence: **90%** — field names diffed directly in both DTO and model, and the undefined-on-all-rows + NaN-totals was read straight from the live component signal. (The all-zero seed values mean a correct mapping would currently show 0/0, not large numbers — but the contract is still broken.)
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → soft-nav to `/leave-types/carry-forward-preview` (in-app; hard nav logs out per BUG-097) → observe summary strip "Carry-forward NaN / Forfeited NaN" and all table rows showing 0 in the Carry-forward + Forfeited columns.
- **Evidence:** a11y snapshot summary strip: `Employees × types: 55`, `Carry-forward: NaN`, `Forfeited: NaN`; live `browser_evaluate` on the component: `{rowCount:55, sample:[{typeofCf:"undefined"},…], nullCount:55, totals:{carryForward:null, forfeiture:null, rows:55}}`; BE DTO fields `CarryForward`/`Forfeited` vs FE model `projectedCarryForward`/`projectedForfeiture`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the page loads and lists the right employee×type rows, but its single purpose (showing projected carry-forward/forfeiture per employee) is defeated: numbers are always blank/0 and the totals are a literal "NaN". Contained to one HR preview screen; no data corruption (read-only preview). Same FE↔BE envelope/field-drift class as prior Leave contract notes.

### BUG-102 — "Apply for Leave" form is unusable: leave-type dropdown is empty because `GET /api/v1/leaves/balances` 404s and aborts the form's combined load (FE calls `/balances`, backend route is `/my-balance`)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #145, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** FE (URL contract) / BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV-003 / TC-LV-065 (apply form)
- **Title:** On `/leave/apply` the **Leave type** `<select>` contains only the placeholder "Select a leave type..." — no leave types load, so no leave request can be submitted, even though acme has 13 active leave types and `GET /api/v1/tenant/leave-types` returns 200.
- **Root cause:** The apply component (`leave-application.component.ts:572-584`) loads its data with `forkJoin({ leaveTypes: getLeaveTypes(), balances: leaveRequestService.getMyBalances() })`. `getMyBalances()` (`leave-request.service.ts:77-78`) requests `GET /api/v1/leaves/balances`, but the backend `LeaveRequestsController` has **no `balances` route** — it exposes `my-balance` (`LeaveRequestsController.cs:108`) and `balance-preview` (line 81). So `/leaves/balances` → **404**, which makes the whole `forkJoin` error; its `next` handler (which would `leaveTypes.set(...)`) never runs, leaving `leaveTypes()` `[]`, and the error branch fires the toast "Failed to load leave types and balances." FE↔BE URL-path drift — same class as the documented `/tenant/` prefix and singular/plural URL mismatches. Confidence: **90%** — FE URL and BE route names diffed directly; the 404 + empty dropdown + combined-load pattern were all observed live.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → soft-nav to `/leave/apply` (in-app; hard nav logs out per BUG-097) → open the **Leave type** dropdown: only "Select a leave type..." is present.
- **Evidence:** network `102. [GET] /api/v1/leaves/balances => 404 Not Found` (while `83/89/101. [GET] /api/v1/tenant/leave-types => 200 OK`); console `Failed to load resource: 404 … /api/v1/leaves/balances`; a11y snapshot of the form shows `combobox "Leave type"` with a single option "Select a leave type...". BE route evidence: `LeaveRequestsController.cs` has `[HttpGet("my-balance")]` + `[HttpGet("balance-preview")]`, no `[HttpGet("balances")]`.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — breaks the primary employee flow of the module: with an empty leave-type list the user cannot pick a type and therefore cannot submit any leave request from the UI. Affects every persona on the apply screen (tenantadmin reproduced; the same forkJoin/route applies to employee/manager/HR). Not data-destructive but blocks the core action of US-LV-003.

- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #166, regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged 2026-07-05)

### ISSUE-209 — Public careers page + apply form not exercisable for acme: public-careers is disabled, so an Open vacancy is invisible to the anonymous careers list/detail
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · WONTFIX-CODE (DATA/tenant-config test-blocker, not a defect — enable acme PublicCareersEnabled; see reports-archive/PRODUCT-DECISIONS-NEEDED-2026-07-05.md)
- **Layer:** DATA (tenant config) / FE-test-blocker
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment / US-REC-001, US-REC-002 / TC-REC-002-13 (apply-form a11y/responsive), blocks public side of TC-REC-001-12
- **Title:** On `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/careers` the public careers page renders but shows "No open positions"; the anonymous vacancy-detail `/careers/{openId}` shows "This position is no longer available" — even though acme has **two Open vacancies** (VAC-2026-0027, VAC-2026-0028) visible in the authenticated admin list. The public application form (drag-drop upload, the subject of TC-REC-002-13) therefore never mounts and cannot be a11y/responsive-tested.
- **Root cause:** Public visibility is gated by `Tenant.PublicCareersEnabled` (`Tenant.cs:155`) AND per-vacancy `Vacancy.PublishToPublicCareers` (`Vacancy.cs:74`, default true) AND status Open. The public list `GET /api/v1/careers/vacancies` returns `[]` and the detail `GET /api/v1/careers/vacancies/{openId}` returns **404** for an Open vacancy, which means acme's tenant-level `PublicCareersEnabled` toggle is **off** (or the seeded Open vacancies were excluded per-vacancy). This is a fail-closed config/data condition, not an FE rendering fault — the careers components render correct, accessible empty/unavailable states (Lighthouse a11y 92, only the systemic contrast BUG-096). Confidence: **85%** — the gating logic was read in source (`CareersController.cs:15-16`, `Vacancy.cs:71-75`) and the empty-list + 404-for-Open behaviour was reproduced via API; the exact off-flag (tenant toggle vs per-vacancy) was not toggled to confirm (report-only, no writes).
- **Reproduction steps:** Anonymous (no login): `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/careers` → "No open positions". Then `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200/careers/019f030d-c726-7db8-9b39-ab02dfd1d231` (VAC-2026-0028, status Open in admin) → "This position is no longer available". API: `curl -s http://localhost:5000/api/v1/careers/vacancies -H "X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme"` → `{"data":[]}`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:5000/api/v1/careers/vacancies/019f030d-c726-7db8-9b39-ab02dfd1d231 -H "X-Tenant-Subdomain: acme"` → `404`; the same id via the authenticated admin endpoint returns `status: Open`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — not a defect in the careers/apply UI itself (those render accessibly), but it blocks all end-to-end testing of the public application journey (browse → open vacancy → apply form → upload), leaving US-REC-002's public-facing AC unverifiable in this environment. A test-environment data fix (enable `PublicCareersEnabled` for acme + one public Open vacancy) would unblock TC-REC-002-13 and the public side of TC-REC-001-12.

- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #148, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))

- **Title:** The lone "Performance" sidebar entry advertises a screen its viewers cannot enter and is hidden from the personas who can, so no Performance screen (cycles, goals, self-assessment, manager-review, 360, PIP, dashboard, recommendations, sign-off) is reachable through normal in-app navigation.
- **Root cause:** Two compounding mismatches. (1) The nav item (`main-layout.component.ts:744-748`) is `{ label:'Performance', route:'/performance', permission:'Performance.View.Own' }` — so it renders only for personas holding `Performance.View.Own` (employee@acme does; tenantadmin/HR do NOT, confirmed: tenantadmin sidebar omits Performance, Leave, Attendance, My Payslips). (2) The `/performance` route (`app.routes.ts:442-449`) is `roleGuard(['Manager','HR Officer','HR Manager','Tenant Admin'])` — which excludes Employee. Net: the employee who sees the link is bounced to `/forbidden` on click; the tenantadmin/HR who are authorized never see the link. Separately, the employee self-service tree `/my-review` (my-goals, self-assessment — `app.routes.ts:456-463`, roleGuard includes Employee) has **no** sidebar/menu entry anywhere (grep of main-layout for `my-review`/`my-goals` = 0 matches), so even the employee's correct screens are orphaned. Confidence: **95%** — reproduced live for both personas, and the permission-gate vs role-guard mismatch read directly from source. Same discoverability class as ISSUE-208 (attendance), but worse because the visible link actively dead-ends in `/forbidden`.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200`. (a) Log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar has NO "Performance" item (the HR/admin who owns cycles/dashboard/PIP/recommendations cannot reach them from the menu). (b) Log out, log in `employee@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar DOES show "Performance" → click it (soft routerLink) → lands on `/forbidden` ("Access Denied"). The employee's real screens at `/my-review/my-goals` and `/my-review/self-assessment` have no link in the menu at all.
- **Evidence:** tenantadmin sidebar a11y snapshot nav list = Dashboard/Departments/Job Titles/Employees/Payroll/Reconciliation/Pending Approvals/Payroll Reports/Recruitment/Reports/Onboarding/Users/Roles/Settings/Workflows/Audit Log/Data Export — no Performance. employee sidebar a11y snapshot nav list = Dashboard/Departments/Job Titles/Leave/Attendance/My Payslips/**Performance**; clicking the Performance `a[href="/performance"]` → URL `/performance` → `/forbidden`, page heading "Access Denied". Source: nav `permission:'Performance.View.Own'` (`main-layout.component.ts:746`) vs route `roleGuard(['Manager','HR Officer','HR Manager','Tenant Admin'])` (`app.routes.ts:448`); no `my-review` match in main-layout.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — the entire Performance Management module (10 user stories of HR/manager/employee functionality) has no working in-app entry point for any of the standard acme personas: the authorized HR/admin can't see the link, and the persona who can see it is dead-ended at `/forbidden`, while the employee self-service goals/self-assessment screens are completely unlinked. Not CRIT only because the routes themselves resolve when reached by URL (and the backend guards still hold). Blocks clean in-app execution of all 9 Performance FE a11y/render TCs.

### BUG-103 — Admin → Users page: pagination footer renders `Showing 1–NaN of {{total}}` / `1 / NaN` and the role filter is empty because `GET /api/v1/tenant/users/assignable-roles` returns 405 Method Not Allowed
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · MED · RESOLVED (PR #159, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** FE (pagination binding) + BE (assignable-roles route verb)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-005 / Users list UI (TC-ADM-005 FE render arms; no dedicated a11y TC bound)
- **Title:** The Users list footer shows broken pagination text (`Showing 1–NaN of {{total}}`, page `1 / NaN`, Next enabled with one page) and the "Filter by role" dropdown only offers "All roles" because its backing call 405s.
- **Root cause:** Two defects on the same page. (1) **Pagination binding** — the footer template interpolates a raw `{{total}}` placeholder and computes `1–NaN` / `1 / NaN`, i.e. the component reads a total/page-count field the API response doesn't populate under the field name the template expects (the page renders 8 rows but `total`/`pageCount` are undefined → `NaN` arithmetic; "Next" stays enabled because `page < NaN` is never false). Same FE↔BE field-name-contract class as [[BUG-101]]/[[BUG-102]] (envelope/field drift), here on the user-list paging envelope. (2) **assignable-roles 405** — the role-filter dropdown calls `GET /api/v1/tenant/users/assignable-roles`, backend answers **405 Method Not Allowed** (route exists for a different verb / not mapped for GET), so the combobox is never populated (only the static "All roles" option). Confidence: **80%** on the binding mismatch (live `NaN`/`{{total}}` observed, not yet diffed line-by-line against the component), **95%** on the 405 (captured in console). Serilog correlation not pulled (405 is a routing reject, unlikely to log an app exception).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar **Users** (`/admin/users`). Footer reads literally "Showing 1–NaN of {{total}}" and "1 / NaN"; "Next" button is enabled though all rows fit one page. Open the "Filter by role" dropdown → only "All roles" (no actual roles). DevTools Network shows `GET /api/v1/tenant/users/assignable-roles` → 405.
- **Evidence:** a11y snapshot of `/admin/users` footer: `paragraph "Showing 1–NaN of {{total}}"`, `generic "1 / NaN"`, `button "Next" [cursor=pointer]` (enabled), `button "Previous" [disabled]`; combobox "Filter by role" has a single option "All roles". Console: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 405 (Method Not Allowed) @ /api/v1/tenant/users/assignable-roles`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the list itself renders and is usable, but two contained features are broken on a primary admin screen: pagination is non-functional/misleading (would break navigation once the tenant exceeds one page) and the role filter is dead. Not HIGH because the core list + per-row actions work and the tenant currently fits one page.

### ISSUE-211 — Admin → Users page renders raw i18n keys `userManagement.status.Active` / `userManagement.status.Disabled` instead of translated status labels
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · LOW · RESOLVED (FE normalized, PR #368; FE↔BE status-casing pin = needs-decision) 2026-07-18
- **Layer:** FE (i18n)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-005 / Users list UI
- **Title:** Every user row's Status cell (and the corresponding aria text) shows the literal translation key `userManagement.status.Active` / `userManagement.status.Disabled` rather than "Active" / "Disabled".
- **Root cause:** The `userManagement.status.*` keys are referenced by the user-list status pill but are missing from the ngx-translate locale dictionary (or the pipe is fed the enum value un-prefixed), so ngx-translate echoes the key verbatim. Confidence: **90%** — classic ngx-translate missing-key passthrough, observed live on every row. Same missing-translation class seen elsewhere; not previously filed for this surface.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → **Users** → Status column shows `userManagement.status.Active` (active rows) and `userManagement.status.Disabled` (the disabled `qa05-1@acme.test` row).
- **Evidence:** a11y snapshot cells: `cell "userManagement.status.Active"`, `cell "userManagement.status.Disabled"` across all 8 rows.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic; status is still distinguishable by the raw key text, no functional impact, but it is user-visible polish failure on a primary admin screen.

### ISSUE-212 — Company Settings (Branding tab): the invalid-hex validation error is shown visually but NOT programmatically associated with the field (no `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby`), and the three file-upload inputs have no accessible name — WCAG 2.1 AA error-association + name failures (TC-ADM-006-17)
- **Type / Severity / Status:** ISSUE · MED · RESOLVED (PR #159, merged 2026-07-05; regression-tested red pre-fix/green post-fix; merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-05)
- **Layer:** FE (a11y)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-006 / **TC-ADM-006-17** (Settings UI WCAG 2.1 AA — step 6 error-association, step 3 upload accessible names)
- **Title:** Entering a bad hex colour renders a visible "Enter a valid hex colour" message, but the hex `<input>` carries neither `aria-invalid="true"` nor `aria-describedby` pointing at that message, so a screen-reader user is never told the field is invalid or why; separately the logo/email-logo/favicon file inputs have no accessible name.
- **Root cause:** (1) The error paragraph is rendered as a sibling `<p>` with no `id` and the hex input has no `aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` binding (live DOM read: `aria-invalid=null`, `aria-describedby=null` while the error text "Enter a valid hex colour (e.g. #4f46e5)." is displayed). This is the WCAG 2.1 AA `3.3.1`/`4.1.2` error-association gap that TC-ADM-006-17 step 6 explicitly checks. (2) The three upload controls are raw `<input type=file>` with `aria-label=null`, no `id`, no `<label for>` — only the adjacent styled "Choose File" buttons carry names; the actual file control is nameless (TC step 3). Confidence: **90%** — both read directly from the live DOM. The rest of the settings a11y contract PASSES (see TC verdict).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → Settings → **Branding** tab → type `zzz999` into "Primary colour hex". Error text appears below the field, but DOM inspection of the input shows `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are both null. Also inspect the three file inputs → no `aria-label`/`label`.
- **Evidence:** `browser_evaluate` on the hex input → `{ariaInvalid:null, ariaDescribedby:null, ariaLabel:"Primary colour hex"}` with visible `paragraph "Enter a valid hex colour (e.g. #4f46e5)."`; file inputs → `{type:"file", ariaLabel:null, labelledby:null, hasForLabel:false}` ×3.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the rest of the settings UI is genuinely accessible (labeled tabs/fields, dirty-tracking Save, labeled hex/swatch), but the error-not-announced gap is a concrete WCAG 2.1 AA failure on a form a tenant admin uses, and unnamed file inputs block SR-only upload. Not HIGH because sighted-keyboard users can still operate everything.

### BUG-104 — Admin → Data Export UI is non-functional: the FE service calls `/api/v1/tenant/exports` but the backend route is `/api/v1/tenant/data-exports` (missing `data-` segment), so the history list 404s into a false "No exports yet" and Start Export POSTs to a dead route
- **Type / Severity / Status:** BUG · HIGH · RESOLVED (PR #146, merged into test/local-subdomains 2026-07-04; regression test green pre-fix->post-fix; combined merged-tree run green (81/81 backend, 52 FE))
- **Layer:** FE (wrong API base path)
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-010 / Data Export UI (TC-ADM-010 FE render/history arms; the deferred TC-010-17 is a separate schema-PDF concern)
- **Title:** Every Data Export screen call targets `…/tenant/exports` / `…/system/tenants/{id}/exports`, but the controller is routed at `…/tenant/data-exports` / `…/system/tenants/{id}/data-exports`, so the page renders its form but the export-history list always 404s (shows the empty-state even though acme has prior exports) and starting an export hits a 404 route.
- **Root cause:** FE↔BE URL contract drift. `data-export.service.ts:49-50` builds the base as `` `${this.apiBase}/system/tenants/${tenantId}/exports` `` (system) / `` `${this.apiBase}/tenant/exports` `` (tenant), omitting the `data-` segment that the backend `DataExportController` actually exposes: `[Route("api/v1/tenant/data-exports")]` (line 20) and `[Route("api/v1/system/tenants/{tenantId:guid}/data-exports")]` (line 103). The history `GET` therefore 404s and the component swallows it into the "No exports yet. Start one above." empty-state, masking the 3 prior acme exports the API run confirmed exist. Same FE-omits-a-path-segment class as the broader [[fe-be-tenant-url-prefix-mismatch]] note (19 services missed `/tenant/`); here it is the `data-` token. The service's own doc-comment also mislabels the story ("matching US-ADM-008" — it is US-ADM-010). Confidence: **97%** — live 404 captured in console + both the FE base string and the BE `[Route]` read directly from source. (405 vs 404: GET to the non-existent `/tenant/exports` returns 404, consistent.)
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar **Data Export** (`/admin/data-export`). Page renders (scope radios, format combos, Start Export). "Recent exports" shows "No exports yet. Start one above." DevTools Network: `GET /api/v1/tenant/exports` → **404** (correct route would be `/api/v1/tenant/data-exports`, which the API-layer run drove to 200 with real history). (Did not click Start Export to avoid generating an export; the POST targets the same broken base.)
- **Evidence:** Console: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found) @ /api/v1/tenant/exports`. FE: `data-export.service.ts:50` → `` `${this.apiBase}/tenant/exports` ``. BE: `DataExportController.cs:20` → `[Route("api/v1/tenant/data-exports")]`, `:103` → `[Route("api/v1/system/tenants/{tenantId:guid}/data-exports")]`. a11y snapshot shows the page body renders with `paragraph "No exports yet. Start one above."` under "Recent exports".
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — the entire Data Export (GDPR portability) UI is unusable for a tenant admin: history never loads (and worse, presents a misleading empty-state implying no exports were ever taken) and the start-export action posts to a dead route. The underlying API works (proven in the US-ADM-010 API run); only the FE base path is wrong, but the user-facing feature is fully broken. Not CRIT because no data is lost/leaked and the backend is healthy.

### ISSUE-213 — Audit-log table is missing `scope` on `<th>` and a `<caption>`/`aria-label` (WCAG 1.3.1 best-practice nit)
- **Type:** ISSUE
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #368, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications & Audit / US-NTF-005 / TC-NTF-005-11
- **Title:** The `/admin/audit-log` data table renders semantically (thead + th + tbody) and all filter controls are labeled, but the `<th>` header cells carry no `scope="col"` and the table has no `<caption>`/`aria-label`, so a screen-reader cannot reliably associate data cells with their column header on a 6-column grid.
- **Root cause:** Markup omission in the audit-log table component — `<th>` rendered without `scope`, table without `<caption>` or `aria-label`. Not a logic defect; the table is otherwise accessible (109 focusable native controls, keyboard-operable, 0 unlabeled filters). Confidence: 90% (read live from the rendered DOM via `browser_evaluate`: `thScope = [null×6]`, `tableHasCaption = false`).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar **Audit Log** (`/admin/audit-log`). Inspect the results table: `thead th` have no `scope` attribute; `table` has no `caption` or `aria-label`.
- **Evidence:** `browser_evaluate` on the page returned `{ tableHasCaption:false, thScope:[null,null,null,null,null,null], unlabeledControls:[], focusableCount:109 }`. Columns: Timestamp/User/Action/Resource/IP Address/Summary.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth a11y polish; the column headers are visually present and controls are labeled, so the screen-reader association is degraded but not absent. Does not block the WCAG-AA core of the page.

### ISSUE-214 — Notification Templates (US-NTF-002) and Notification Preferences (US-NTF-003) pages are orphaned from in-app navigation (URL-only, no nav/Settings/profile entry point)
- **Type:** ISSUE
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications & Audit / US-NTF-002, US-NTF-003 / TC-NTF-002-11, TC-NTF-003-11
- **Title:** Both feature pages are fully implemented and route-registered (`/admin/notification-templates`, `/profile/notification-preferences`) yet have NO entry point reachable by clicking through the app — no sidebar item, no Settings tab/link, no profile/account-menu link — so a tenant admin (templates) and any user (preferences) can only reach them by typing the URL.
- **Root cause:** Nav wiring gap. `app.routes.ts:587/600` register both routes behind guards (templates → `roleGuard(['Tenant Admin','Tenant Owner'])`, preferences → parent authGuard), but the sidebar (`main-layout` nav) lists only Dashboard/Departments/Job Titles/Employees/Payroll/Recruitment/Reports/Onboarding/Users/Roles/Settings/Workflows/Audit Log/Data Export — neither notification page appears. A repo-wide grep for `routerLink`/`router.navigate` to these paths finds links ONLY *inside* the templates feature itself (the editor back-link `template-editor.component.html:6` and list row-click `template-list.component.ts:123`); `/profile/notification-preferences` has ZERO inbound links anywhere. The Settings page (`/admin/settings`, the natural home) renders only Organization Profile / Branding / Localization / Security & Policies tabs — no Notifications tab. Same orphan-route class as [[ISSUE-210]] (Performance nav) and BUG-104 (Data Export route mismatch). Confidence: 95% (sidebar enumerated live + source grep of every inbound link).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!`. Inspect the sidebar: no "Notification Templates" or "Notification Preferences" item. Open **Settings** (`/admin/settings`): tabs are Organization Profile / Branding / Localization / Security & Policies — no notifications tab. No profile/account menu exists in the sidebar footer (only the user card + Log out). The pages exist only at the typed URLs.
- **Evidence:** Live sidebar nav (14 items, none for notifications templates/prefs). `grep` of `src/frontend/src/app`: inbound links to `/admin/notification-templates` come only from `template-editor.component.html:6` and `template-list.component.ts:123` (intra-feature); `/profile/notification-preferences` has no inbound `routerLink`/`navigate` outside its own `.routes.ts`. `app.routes.ts:587,600` confirm both routes are registered + guarded.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the features are built and (per the US-NTF-002/003 API runs) functional server-side, but they are effectively undiscoverable to end users without out-of-band URL knowledge, so the shipped UI delivers no value through normal use. Not HIGH because the backend works and a deep-link reaches the page; purely a navigation/discoverability defect.

### ISSUE-215 — Onboarding pages: muted helper/meta text fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast (`text-neutral-400` #a3a3a3 on white = 2.52:1)
- **Type:** ISSUE
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #368, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Onboarding / Offboarding · US-ONB-001 · TC-ONB-001-12 (template-list + template-builder a11y)
- **Title:** On the onboarding **template list** (`/onboarding/templates`) and **template builder** (`/onboarding/templates/new`), the muted helper / meta text rendered with `text-neutral-400` (`#a3a3a3` on `#ffffff`) measures a 2.52:1 contrast ratio — below the WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text. Affected: the per-card task-count line ("1 task" / "8 tasks", `p.mt-3.text-xs.text-neutral-400`) on the list, and the builder's field `.hint` paragraphs ("Leave empty to apply to all (universal).") plus the `text-neutral-400` inline helper.
- **Root cause:** Tailwind `text-neutral-400` (#a3a3a3) used for de-emphasized text on a white surface yields 2.52:1; needs `text-neutral-500`/`-600` (or a darker token) to clear 4.5:1. Pure CSS color-token choice, not a logic defect. Confidence: 99% — measured by Lighthouse (chrome-devtools MCP, `lighthouse_audit` snapshot mode) on both authenticated pages: Accessibility = 96, with `color-contrast` audit failing and the audit's node `explanation` reporting "insufficient color contrast of 2.52 (foreground #a3a3a3, background #ffffff, 12px normal)". (The co-reported `label-content-name-mismatch` failure is the shared shell "Switch organization" / `.user-email` in `main-layout`, NOT onboarding — out of scope here.)
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar **Onboarding** (`/onboarding/templates`). Run a Lighthouse a11y snapshot (or axe) → `color-contrast` fails on the `.text-neutral-400` task-count text. Click **+ Create Checklist Template** (`/onboarding/templates/new`) → same `color-contrast` failure on the `.hint` helper paragraphs.
- **Evidence:** Lighthouse snapshot reports (desktop): list page `report.json` Accessibility 0.96, `color-contrast` score 0, failing node `<p class="…text-neutral-400">` ratio 2.52; builder page Accessibility 0.96, `color-contrast` score 0, failing nodes `<p class="hint">` + `<span class="…text-neutral-400">`. Best-practices 100 on both.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic/defense-in-depth a11y polish on de-emphasized secondary text (task counts, field hints); the primary content, labels, headings, and interactive controls all pass, and the information is also conveyed by structure/position. Does not block use of the builder or list.

### BUG-105 — Monitoring per-tenant usage gauges (`role="progressbar"`) have NO accessible name — screen-reader users hear an unnamed progressbar with no tenant/metric/value context (WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 / `aria-progressbar-name`)
- **ID:** BUG-105
- **Type:** BUG (accessibility defect — WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value failure on the monitoring usage gauges)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #368, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-002 / **TC-ADM-002-13** (Monitoring WCAG 2.1 AA — step 3: gauges must announce their percentage and warning/breach state to a screen reader)
- **Title:** On `/admin/monitoring`, every per-tenant employee usage gauge is a `<div role="progressbar" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100">` with **no** `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, so its accessible name is empty. A screen-reader user reaches the gauge and hears only "progressbar" — not which tenant, which metric (employees), nor the value (`28 / 200`). The visible "28 / 200" text sits in a sibling `<generic>` that is not wired to the progressbar's name. This is exactly the TC-ADM-002-13 step-3 requirement (gauges announce their percentage / warning / breach state) and it fails.
- **Root cause:** the gauge component renders the ARIA `progressbar` role + min/max but omits a name binding and `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext`. Fix: add `aria-label` (e.g. "Employees: 28 of 200") or `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible count, and set `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext`. Confidence: **HIGH** — Lighthouse axe-core flagged `aria-progressbar-name` score 0 with explanation "aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty; aria-labelledby … does not exist". Confidence 95%.
- **Reproduction steps:** log in at `http://localhost:4200/?tenant=platform` as `admin@hrm.local` / `Admin@123!` → in-app nav sidebar **Monitoring** (`/admin/monitoring`) → the "Tenant usage" table shows employee gauges per row. Run a CDP Lighthouse a11y (snapshot, desktop) → audit `aria-progressbar-name` fails on the `<div role="progressbar" class="…bg-neutral-100…">` gauge nodes.
- **Evidence:** CDP Lighthouse (snapshot, desktop) on `/admin/monitoring` → Accessibility **92**, Failed 4; failing audit `aria-progressbar-name` (score 0) on multiple `role="progressbar"` gauge nodes; co-failures `color-contrast` (BUG-096) and `label-content-name-mismatch` (ISSUE-205). Report: `chrome-devtools-mcp-7OYzEN/report.json`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the gauge value is also rendered as adjacent visible text ("28 / 200") that a screen reader still reaches as static text, so the information is not entirely lost; but the progressbar itself is unnamed, a genuine WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 failure, and it is the specific behaviour TC-ADM-002-13 step 3 requires. Cheap fix.

### ISSUE-216 — Create Tenant form: the Enterprise plan card renders "Up to employees" (missing the limit number) for an unlimited/`null` max_employees plan — should read "Up to ∞ employees" / "Unlimited employees"
- **ID:** ISSUE-216
- **Type:** ISSUE (UI/data-rendering nit — empty interpolation for a null limit)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #368, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-001 / **TC-ADM-001-11** (Create Tenant form — observed during the a11y render pass)
- **Title:** On the Create Tenant form (`/admin/tenants/create`) the subscription-plan radio for **Enterprise** ($199.00/mo) shows the entitlement line as "**Up to  employees**" — the employee-limit number is blank. Starter ("Up to 25 employees") and Professional ("Up to 200 employees") render correctly. The Enterprise plan has an unlimited / `null` `max_employees` (the monitoring usage table renders the same plan's tenants as `0 / ∞`), so the form's `Up to {{limit}} employees` template interpolates an empty value instead of "∞" / "Unlimited".
- **Root cause:** the plan-card template unconditionally renders `Up to {{max_employees}} employees`; when `max_employees` is null/0 (unlimited) it yields an empty interpolation. Fix: branch to "Unlimited employees" / "Up to ∞ employees" when the limit is null. Confidence: 85% — inferred from the form text vs the monitoring page rendering the same enterprise plan as `… / ∞`; not confirmed against the plan API payload.
- **Reproduction steps:** log in at `http://localhost:4200/?tenant=platform` as `admin@hrm.local` / `Admin@123!` → sidebar **Tenants** → **Create Tenant** → "Subscription plan" section → the **Enterprise** radio shows "Up to  employees" (no number); Starter/Professional show their limits.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — cosmetic copy gap on one plan card; does not block tenant creation and the plan is still selectable. Mildly confusing (looks truncated).

### BUG-106 - Suspended-tenant Tenant Admin/Owner is NOT exempt from the 451 gate: every tenant API (incl. the read-only suspension-notice + export paths) returns 451, so an admin can never reach the read-only suspension landing (AC-2 unmet)
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #130, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-004 / **TC-ADM-004-05** (primary); also breaks **TC-ADM-004-04** step1 and **TC-ADM-003-03** (suspended-impersonation reads)
- **Title:** On a `Suspended` tenant, a *directly-logged-in* Tenant Admin (role "Tenant Admin") is 451'd on `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees`, `GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs`, and `POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports`, despite `TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware` documenting Tenant Owner/Admin as exempt (read-only notice + export). Login itself succeeds (200) but the admin then has zero reachable tenant API surface.
- **Root cause:** `TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware.IsTenantAdminOrOwner(ICurrentUser)` (src/backend/HRM.Api/Middleware/TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware.cs:123-126) gates on `user.Roles.Contains("Tenant Admin" | "Tenant Owner")` (`PermissionCatalog.BuiltInRoles`, values "Tenant Admin"/"Tenant Owner" at PermissionCatalog.cs:558-559). The JWT carries the role in a custom `"roles"` claim (value literally "Tenant Admin", verified by decoding the token), and `CurrentUser.Roles` reads `User.FindAll("roles")` (src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/CurrentUser.cs:37-38). Despite the claim value matching the constant exactly, the exemption branch never fires - Serilog logs `Blocked request to suspended tenant ... with HTTP 451` for the admin's /tenant/employees + /tenant/audit-logs requests (RequestId 0HNMMGISP7VQN / 0HNMMGISP7VQO). Middleware ordering is correct (UseAuthentication @ Program.cs:363 -> middleware @ :374) so User is populated; the failure is in the role-string lookup at middleware time - most likely the JWT bearer inbound claim mapping (MapInboundClaims, default true) means FindAll("roles") does not surface the value when the middleware runs. Confidence: symptom 100% (reproduced + logged); precise internal cause ~55% (claim-mapping vs role-value not pinned to a line). NOTE: `GET /api/v1/tenant/lifecycle-notice` (an always-allowed path) returned 404 - that notice route appears unimplemented, compounding the "admin has nowhere to land" effect.
- **Reproduction steps:** (isosus = Suspended fixture tenant; password Admin@123!)
  1. Login: POST http://localhost:5000/api/v1/auth/login, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: isosus`, body {email: isosus-admin@iso.test, password: Admin@123!} -> 200, capture accessToken.
  2. GET /api/v1/tenant/employees with that Bearer + header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: isosus` -> **451** (expected 200).
  3. GET /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs (same) -> **451** (expected 200).
  4. POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports (same, body {}) -> **451** (expected: export path, not 451).
- **Evidence:** all three return HTTP 451 `{"code":"tenant_suspended"}`. Decoded admin JWT: `"roles":"Tenant Admin"`. Serilog: `[INF] Blocked request to suspended tenant "25500000-0000-4000-8000-000000000055" (/api/v1/tenant/employees) with HTTP 451` (RequestId 0HNMMGISP7VQN). Control: System Admin at `platform` reading the same tenant via /system/tenants/{id}/lifecycle/history -> 200 (unaffected, correct).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH - AC-2's core promise (suspended-tenant admins keep read-only access to the suspension notice + data export) is entirely unmet; the admin is locked out of every tenant API, including the GDPR data-export they need during suspension. Not CRIT because the System Admin remediation path is intact and no data is exposed/lost.

### BUG-107 - Impersonation destructive-op block (FR-6) is bypassed: ForcePasswordReset / DeactivateUser / AssignUserRoles / EditUserRoles are not matched by the blocklist and execute during a full SystemAdmin impersonation
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #125, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-003 / **TC-ADM-003-05**
- **Title:** During an active (full, non-read-only) SystemAdmin impersonation of an Active tenant, a forced password reset, user deactivation, and role re-assignment are all permitted - FR-6 requires these destructive ops to be hard-blocked (403) regardless of read-only status. `POST /api/v1/tenant/users/{id}/force-password-reset` returned **200** and actually reset the target user's password while impersonating.
- **Root cause:** `ImpersonationReadOnlyBehavior.DestructiveCommandMarkers` (src/backend/HRM.Application/Common/Behaviors/ImpersonationReadOnlyBehavior.cs:39-51) matches destructive ops by **substring of the request type name** against the markers `ChangePassword, ResetPassword, SetPassword, AssignRole, UnassignRole, RemoveRole, Permission, DeleteUser, DeleteTenant, TerminateTenant`. The actual destructive command type names contain NONE of these as a substring: `ForcePasswordResetCommand` (has "PasswordReset", not "ResetPassword"), `DeactivateUserCommand` (not "DeleteUser"), `AssignUserRolesCommand` / `EditUserRolesCommand` (have "AssignUserRoles"/"UserRoles", not "AssignRole"). Verified by enumerating command types in HRM.Application and substring-matching each against every marker -> 0 matches. So IsDestructive() returns false and the commands reach their handlers. Confidence: 95% - the marker-vs-command-name mismatch is proven by static enumeration, and the live ForcePasswordReset reached its handler + ran the UPDATE per Serilog (no "Blocked destructive operation" line emitted).
- **Reproduction steps:**
  1. Login platform admin (admin@hrm.local / Admin@123!, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: platform`) -> capture token PLAT.
  2. POST /api/v1/system/impersonation with PLAT (header platform), body {targetUserId: 226f73cb-e7d5-49ae-925b-bd126e6f34e4, targetTenantId: 2a1a0000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1 (isoa, Active), reason: "destructive op block check"} -> 201, isReadOnly=false; capture impersonation token IMP.
  3. POST /api/v1/tenant/users/4cc38c80-7294-4961-b000-8daada866394/force-password-reset with Bearer IMP, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: isoa`, body {} -> **200** (FR-6 violated; expected 403).
- **Evidence:** force-password-reset -> 200 `{"message":"Password reset forced; the user must set a new password."}`. Serilog: `Handling ForcePasswordResetCommand ... RequestPath:/api/v1/tenant/users/.../force-password-reset` then `[PASSWORD-RESET-EMAIL-STUB] Would send forced-password-reset email to isoa-admin@iso.test` then `HTTP POST ... responded 200` (RequestId 0HNMMGISP7VSI) - no `Blocked destructive operation` warning. DeactivateUserCommand reached its handler (400 self_deactivation, not 403); AssignUserRolesCommand reached its handler (400 invalid_role, not 403) - both prove the destructive gate did not reject them. Control: benign POST /tenant/employees returned 201 (full-session writes allowed by design), so the bypass is specific to the destructive-op gate, not a misconfigured read-only flag.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH - an operator impersonating a tenant user can reset passwords, deactivate users, and re-assign roles, the exact privilege-escalation / account-takeover surface FR-6 exists to prevent. Not CRIT only because it requires the high-privilege Impersonation.Initiate permission to reach.

### ISSUE-217 - Terminating-tenant grace export is partially blocked: POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports returns 403 because the export-allowlist substring /exports does not match /data-exports (audit-log /export passes; the GDPR data-export does not) - AC-3/BR-6 export-during-grace partially unmet
- **Type:** ISSUE
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #331, 2026-07-17)
- **Layer:** BE
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17):** Root cause confirmed exactly as filed — `ExportMarkers = { "/export", "/exports" }` and `/api/v1/tenant/data-exports` has a hyphen (not a slash) before "exports", so neither marker matched and the GDPR data-export was 403'd on a Terminating tenant. Fix: added `"/data-exports"` to `ExportMarkers` (`TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware.cs:44`) — explicit, no over-match. New `TenantStatusEnforcementMiddlewareTests` (3 arms via real `InvokeAsync`): data-export POST passes · audit-export POST still passes · a non-export write still 403s. Mutation-verified: reverting the marker turns ONLY the data-export arm red (the other two stay green), proving the fix is targeted and the read-only grace is otherwise intact.
- **Module / US / TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-004 / **TC-ADM-004-08**
- **Title:** On a `Terminating` tenant (read-only grace), `POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports` (the tenant-initiated GDPR/grace data export) is rejected 403 `tenant_terminating_readonly`, while `POST /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs/export` passes 200. The grace window's whole purpose is data extraction, so the primary data-export initiation being blocked contradicts AC-3/BR-6.
- **Root cause:** `TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware.IsExport(path)` (src/backend/HRM.Api/Middleware/TenantStatusEnforcementMiddleware.cs:120-121) allowlists writes whose path contains the substring markers "/export" or "/exports". The audit-log export path /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs/export contains /export -> allowed. The data-export path /api/v1/tenant/data-exports contains -exports but NOT /exports (the marker has a leading slash) -> not matched -> treated as a blocked write -> 403. Confidence: 90% - substring logic explicit in the middleware; reproduced live (audit export 200 vs data-export 403 on the same terminating tenant under the same admin token).
- **Reproduction steps:** (isoterming = Terminating fixture tenant)
  1. Login isoterming-admin@iso.test (header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: isoterming`) -> capture token.
  2. POST /api/v1/tenant/data-exports (Bearer, header isoterming, body {}) -> **403** `tenant_terminating_readonly` (expected: allowed).
  3. POST /api/v1/tenant/audit-logs/export (same, body {format:"csv"}) -> 200.
- **Evidence:** data-export POST -> 403 `{"code":"tenant_terminating_readonly","message":"This organization's workspace is read-only pending termination."}`; audit-log export POST -> 200. GET reads (employees) -> 200 (read-only grace correct); non-export write (POST employee) -> 403 (correct).
- **Severity rationale:** MED - read access + audit export still work during grace, and the System Admin cross-tenant export path (/system/tenants/{id}/data-exports) is unaffected, but the tenant-facing primary data-export - the point of the grace window - is wrongly blocked, contradicting AC-3/BR-6 for the self-service path.

### BUG-108 — Employee create wizard photo-upload control fails WCAG 2.1 AA: a focusable `aria-hidden` file input nested inside a `role="button"` drop-zone (aria-hidden-focus + nested-interactive)
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #295, 2026-07-14)
- **Resolution (FE, PR #295, 2026-07-14):** moved the hidden file `<input>` out of the `role=button` drop-zone (sibling) + `tabindex="-1"` — clears aria-hidden-focus + nested-interactive.
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-001 (employee create) / TC-CHR-097 (already `fail`; this augments it — the create-wizard a11y arm)
- **Title:** On the **Add New Employee** wizard (`/employees/new`), Step 1 "Profile Photo" upload control structures the drop-zone as `<div role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Upload profile photo">` that **contains** a real `<input type="file" aria-hidden="true" class="sr-only">` which is itself in the tab order (`tabIndex=0`). This produces two serious axe-core violations: **`aria-hidden-focus`** (a focusable element is marked `aria-hidden="true"`, so AT is told to ignore an element a keyboard user can still land on) and **`nested-interactive`** (an interactive control — the file input — nested inside another interactive control — the role=button div). A keyboard/screen-reader user gets a "dead" focus stop the AT does not announce.
- **Root cause:** The upload component renders the hidden native file input *inside* the visually-styled drop-zone div instead of as a sibling, and leaves the `sr-only` input focusable. The `aria-hidden="true"` on a `tabIndex=0` element is contradictory (WCAG 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value; ARIA spec: aria-hidden must not contain focusable content). The drop-zone div being `role="button"` AND wrapping the focusable input makes the input a nested interactive control. Confidence: **95%** — the offending DOM (`<input type=file aria-hidden=true class=sr-only>` with `tabIndex=0`, inside `<div role=button tabindex=0 class=drop-zone aria-label="Upload profile photo">`) and the two axe rule IDs were read directly from the live page. Fix is to take the hidden input out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) or move it out as a sibling and drop one of the duplicate interactive roles — not a backend fault.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → Employees → **Add Employee** (→ `/employees/new`, in-app per BUG-097) → Step 1 "Personal Info". Tab through the form: focus lands on the photo drop-zone AND on the hidden file input (two stops for one control). Run axe-core (`wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa`) scoped to `main`.
- **Evidence:** axe-core 4.10.2 on `main`: `aria-hidden-focus` (serious) target `input[type="file"]` html `<input type="file" aria-hidden="true" class="sr-only" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp">`; `nested-interactive` (serious) target `.drop-zone` html `<div tabindex="0" role="button" class="drop-zone" aria-label="Upload profile photo">`. Live DOM read: file input `tabIndex=0`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `class="sr-only"`; drop-zone `role=button`, `tabindex=0`. (A third axe hit on the same control — `color-contrast` on the "JPEG, PNG, or WebP. Max 5 MB." hint — folds into systemic **BUG-096**, not re-filed.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the create wizard is keyboard-reachable and the standard text fields are correctly labelled (verified: First/Last/Email/DOB/Gender all have `<label for>`), so the form is usable; but the photo-upload control specifically traps keyboard/AT users on an element the AT is told to ignore and violates two serious WCAG 2.1 AA rules. Contained to one control on one wizard step; not data-affecting.

### BUG-109 — Payroll "New payroll run" modal asserts `aria-modal="true"` but the background is NOT inert: no focus trap, no Escape-to-close, no initial focus into the dialog
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #295, 2026-07-14)
- **Resolution (FE, PR #295, 2026-07-14):** `A11yModule` + `cdkTrapFocus [cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture]` + `(keydown.escape)=close` on the new-payroll-run dialog (mirrors employee-profile). ~16 sibling hand-rolled dialogs share the defect → **ISSUE-296** systematic sweep.
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-003 (payroll runs) / TC-PAY-003-12 (Payroll Runs table + New-Run modal a11y — this is the modal arm of that TC)
- **Title:** On **Payroll runs** (`/payroll/runs`), the "+ New payroll run" dialog (`app-new-payroll-run`) is a hand-rolled animated overlay marked `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="new-run-title"`. The accessible structure of the dialog itself is correct (0 axe violations inside it), but the **modal contract is broken three ways**: (1) **no focus trap** — while the modal is open the 39 background focusables (sidebar nav links, header buttons, the runs table) remain focusable and the page is neither `inert` nor `aria-hidden`, so a keyboard/SR user can Tab straight out of the modal into the page behind it; (2) **`aria-modal="true"` is a false assertion** — it tells assistive tech the rest of the page is inert when it is not, so a screen reader will let the user wander the background while believing they are trapped in the dialog; (3) **no Escape-to-close** and **initial focus is not moved into the dialog** (after opening, `document.activeElement` is still the "+ New payroll run" trigger button, outside the dialog).
- **Root cause:** `new-payroll-run.component.ts` implements the overlay manually (Angular animations `@drawer`/`@backdrop`, backdrop `(click)="close.emit()"`, an explicit close/Cancel button) but does **not** use Angular CDK Dialog/`cdkTrapFocus`/`cdkFocusInitial`, has **no `@HostListener('keydown.escape')`/Escape handler**, and never sets `inert`/`aria-hidden` on the app shell while open (grep of the component: backdrop+close-emit at lines ~63-98, `aria-modal="true"`/`aria-labelledby="new-run-title"` at lines 76-85, and NO `escape`/`keydown`/`cdkTrapFocus`/`cdkFocusInitial`/`.focus()` anywhere). Confidence: **90%** — live DOM read confirmed `aria-modal="true"` with 39 background focusables not inert/aria-hidden and `activeElement` left on the trigger; source confirmed the missing trap/escape/initial-focus. Fix: use CDK `Dialog`/`A11yModule` (cdkTrapFocus + cdkFocusInitial), add an Escape handler, and apply `inert` to the app root while the dialog is open. Not a backend fault.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → in-app nav to **Payroll runs** (`/payroll/runs`; per BUG-097 hard nav/reload logs out — used soft `history.pushState`+`popstate`) → click **"+ New payroll run"**. The dialog opens; `document.activeElement` is still the trigger button (focus not moved in). Tab repeatedly: focus escapes the dialog into the sidebar/table behind it. No Escape key closes the dialog (only the backdrop click or the Cancel/X button does).
- **Evidence:** live DOM with dialog open — `[role="dialog"]` has `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby="new-run-title"`, 6 focusables, 0 aria-hidden-focusable; **background**: `main` `aria-hidden=null` `inert=false`, `nav` `aria-hidden=null`, **39 background focusables still reachable** (sample: "Switch organization", "Collapse sidebar", "Dashboard", "Departments", "Job Titles"). axe-core scoped to `[role="dialog"]` = **0 violations** (the dialog's own markup is clean; the defect is the missing background-inerting/trap, which axe does not flag). Source `new-payroll-run.component.ts`: backdrop `(click)="close.emit()"`, `aria-modal="true"` (l.76), no `escape`/`keydown`/`cdkTrapFocus`/`cdkFocusInitial`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the modal is still operable (Cancel/X reachable by Tab, backdrop click closes it) and content is correctly labelled, so it is not a hard block; but the broken focus-trap + false `aria-modal` is a real WCAG 2.1 AA barrier (fails the expected modal-dialog interaction pattern; SC 2.4.3 Focus Order / 4.1.2) affecting screen-reader and keyboard-only users on a primary payroll action. Likely shared by the other hand-rolled payroll slide-overs/drawers (adjustments, statutory, distribution) — same component pattern — so the fix should be applied to the shared overlay approach.

### BUG-110 — Statutory-config fiscal-year selector is a `role="tablist"` containing a non-`tab` child (the "+ Add year" `<button>`) — axe `aria-required-children` (critical)
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #295, 2026-07-14)
- **Resolution (FE, PR #295, 2026-07-14):** moved the `+ Add year` button OUT of the `role="tablist"` (now a sibling) — clears aria-required-children.
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-006 (statutory configuration) / TC-PAY-006-12 (statutory config a11y)
- **Title:** On **Statutory configuration** (`/payroll/statutory`), the fiscal-year switcher is `<div role="tablist" aria-label="Fiscal year">` whose children are two `role="tab"` elements ("2026-2027", "2025-2026") **plus a bare `<button>` "+ Add year"** that has no `role="tab"`. WAI-ARIA requires a `tablist` to contain only `tab` (or allowed grouping) children, so axe-core reports a **critical `aria-required-children`** violation ("Element has children which are not allowed: button[tabindex]"). A screen reader reading the tablist will mis-count/mis-announce the tab set, and the "Add year" action is exposed inconsistently inside a tab group.
- **Root cause:** The fiscal-year tabs and the "+ Add year" affordance are rendered as siblings inside the same `role="tablist"` container (`statutory-configuration.component`), instead of placing the Add button outside the tablist. Confidence: **95%** — the offending DOM (`<div role="tablist" aria-label="Fiscal year">` with children `[tab, tab, BUTTON("+ Add year")]`) and the axe rule id were read directly from the live page. Fix: move the "+ Add year" button out of the `role="tablist"` element. Not a backend fault.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → in-app soft-nav to `/payroll/statutory` (per BUG-097 a hard nav/reload logs out) → run axe-core (`wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa`) scoped to `main`.
- **Evidence:** axe-core 4.10.2 on `main`: `aria-required-children` (critical, 1 node) target `.gap-1\.5`; node html `<div role="tablist" aria-label="Fiscal year" class="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5 …">`; failureSummary "Element has children which are not allowed: button[tabindex]"; live child roles `[tab, tab, BUTTON]`, text "2026-2027 / 2025-2026 / + Add year". (Also 4 systemic `color-contrast` nodes on the slab/grid labels → BUG-096, not re-filed.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the page and fiscal-year switching still function; the impact is an incorrect ARIA tab-group structure that degrades screen-reader announcement on a tenant-admin-only config page. Single contained structural fix; not data-affecting. (axe weights it "critical" by rule, but user-facing blast radius is moderate.)

### BUG-111 — Regularization "Reason" field live char-count "0/10" is not announced to screen readers (no `aria-live`), and the drawer below-minimum validation is conveyed silently
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #295, 2026-07-14)
- **Resolution (FE, PR #295, 2026-07-14):** `role=status`/`aria-live=polite` on the reason char-counter + the BUG-109-class focus-trap fix on the regularization drawer.
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance / US-ATT-003 (regularization) / TC-ATT-035 (regularization drawer a11y)
- **Title:** On **Attendance Regularization** (`/attendance/regularization`), the "+ Request Regularization" drawer shows a live character counter next to the Reason label ("0/10" → counts up as you type, with a below-minimum highlight). The counter is rendered as a plain `<span>` with **no `aria-live`** region and **no `role="status"`** (no ancestor `[aria-live]` either). A screen-reader user therefore gets no announcement of the live count or of crossing the 10-character minimum — the TC explicitly requires "the count/validation announced to screen readers." (The Reason textarea itself is correctly labelled `aria-label="Reason"`.)
- **Root cause:** The char-count element in the regularization drawer template is a static text node bound to the typed length, not wrapped in a polite live region. Confidence: **90%** — live DOM read with the drawer open confirmed the counter text "0/10" has `aria-live=null`, `role=null`, and `closest('[aria-live]')` = null. Fix: wrap the counter (and the below-minimum validation message) in `aria-live="polite"` / `role="status"`. Not a backend fault.
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `employee@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → in-app nav to **Attendance Regularization** (`/attendance/regularization`; per BUG-097 a hard nav/reload logs out) → click **"+ Request Regularization"** → inspect the "0/10" counter beside the Reason label.
- **Evidence:** live DOM, drawer open: counter element text `0/10`, `aria-live`=null, `role`=null, no `[aria-live]` ancestor. Reason `<textarea aria-label="Reason">` (labelled, OK). Drawer `[role="dialog"] aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="reg-drawer-title"`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the field is operable and visually validated; the gap is a missing live announcement of a non-blocking helper count on one drawer field. Defense-in-depth a11y, contained to one control.

> **Note (BUG-109 class — not re-filed):** the same regularization drawer also exhibits the **BUG-109** hand-rolled-modal contract defects — `aria-modal="true"` asserted while the background is NOT inert/`aria-hidden` (15 background focusables remain reachable with the drawer open) and **initial focus is not moved into the drawer on open** (`activeElement` stays on the trigger button). BUG-109 already documents this as the shared hand-rolled-overlay pattern across the app; counted against TC-ATT-035 by reference, not duplicated.
