### ISSUE-226 — Offer free-text (custom clauses / benefits) stored & returned UNSANITIZED (stored-XSS defense-in-depth gap)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #275, 2026-07-13) · **Layer:** BE
- **Resolution:** sanitize-on-write in `OfferService.GenerateAsync` for `OfferedPosition`/`BenefitsSummary`/`CustomClauses`, reusing the already-DI-registered `IHtmlSanitizer` (`GanssHtmlSanitizer`, Ganss.Xss) — mirrors the `VacancyService`/`ReviewSignoffService` precedent; no new package. **Ticket premise corrected:** the PDF render path is a QuestPDF `.Text()` literal-glyph sink, NOT an HTML sink, so it was never exploitable; the real surface was the JSON read path the Angular FE renders. Sanitize-on-write covers the applicant-portal projection too (reads the stored value). Regression arms: unit (`<script>`/`onerror` stripped on DTO + persisted row, benign survives; + `javascript:`/inline-`style` allow-list pin) and integration (full DI + MediatR pipeline). BE 3671/3671; Offer filter 50/50; integration-enforcer CONNECTED, test-authenticator AUTHENTIC.
- **Module/US/TC:** Recruitment / US-REC-007 / TC-REC-007-13
- **Title:** `POST /api/v1/recruitment/offers` persists recruiter-supplied `customClauses`/`benefitsSummary` verbatim and `GET /offers/{id}` returns them verbatim — no server-side sanitization/encoding of HTML.
- **Root cause (70%):** Offer create/read path does no HTML sanitization; free-text is stored and echoed raw. Angular interpolation auto-escapes in the UI (so the in-app render is likely safe), but TC-REC-007-13 asserts sanitization specifically for the **generated PDF/HTML offer template** substitution path — if that path emits the stored string into HTML without encoding, it is stored XSS. The PDF-render encoding was NOT verified in this run (blocked separately), so this is filed as a defense-in-depth gap, not a confirmed live XSS.
- **Reproduction:** fntest, `Bearer <fntest-admin>` + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest`. Create offer for a Hired-track applicant with `"customClauses":"<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"`, `"benefitsSummary":"<script>alert(1)</script>"` → 200. `GET /api/v1/recruitment/offers/{offerId}` returns `customClauses:"<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"`, `benefitsSummary:"<script>alert(1)</script>"` (raw, unescaped).
- **Evidence:** offer OID `019f1d57-040b-705f-8a99-1941412d3a5b` (fntest) — readback shows both payloads verbatim. HTTP 200 on create + get.
- **Severity rationale:** Server stores/echoes attacker-controlled HTML; blast radius limited by Angular's default output escaping, but the PDF/HTML offer-template render path (unverified) could execute it and reaches candidates. Sanitize on store or on the PDF-render seam.

### BUG-121 — `GET /auth/me` and `GET /auth/my-tenants` return HTTP 500 whenever Redis is unreachable — no graceful fallback (breaks post-login hydration for every tenant/persona)
- **ID:** BUG-121
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #120, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE (+ INFRA config)
- **Module / US / TC:** Authentication / US-AUTH-006 (roles/permissions hydration) — surfaced while executing TC-AUTH-047 and the ADM plan-limit TCs (auth/me is the app's identity bootstrap).
- **Title:** With the running API pointed at a Redis that is down, `AuthService.GetMyTenantsAsync` calls `IDistributedCache.GetStringAsync("hrm:user:{id}:tenants")` and lets the `RedisConnectionException` propagate uncaught → `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` returns a generic 500. `/auth/me` (which calls `GetCurrentUserAsync` → `GetMyTenantsAsync`) and `/auth/my-tenants` both 500 for **every** persona (fntest-admin, platform admin all reproduced). By contrast `TenantResolutionMiddleware` catches the identical Redis failure and falls back to the DB (logs `WRN Tenant cache read failed for {sub}; falling back to database`), so resolution/login still work — the degradation handling is inconsistent between call sites.
- **Root cause:** (a) **config drift** — base `appsettings.json` sets `Cache:Redis = "localhost:6379,abortConnect=false,connectTimeout=1000"`; the intended dev value is blank (`appsettings.Development.json` blanks it → in-memory fallback), but the process is running with the non-blank base value and no Redis listening on 6379, so every cache op throws. (b) **missing resilience** — unlike the tenant-resolution read, `AuthService.GetMyTenantsAsync` has no try/catch-and-fallback around the distributed-cache read. Cited from the Serilog stack: `StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException: ... HMGET hrm:user:{id}:tenants; It was not possible to connect to the redis server(s). ConnectTimeout` → `AuthService.GetMyTenantsAsync` → `GetCurrentUserAsync` → `GetCurrentUserQueryHandler.Handle` → `AuthController.GetCurrentUser (AuthController.cs:187)`; request `RequestId 0HNMN7ROLJA6S:00000001`. Confidence: **HIGH** (logged exception + stack + confirmed config).
- **Reproduction steps:** with Redis not running on localhost:6379 (current state), `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest, fntest-admin@fn.test/Admin@123!) → 200 (login OK). Then `GET /api/v1/auth/me` and `GET /api/v1/auth/my-tenants` with that Bearer + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest` → **HTTP 500** `{"success":false,"message":"An unexpected error occurred..."}`. Same 500 for platform admin (`admin@hrm.local`, X-Tenant-Subdomain: platform).
- **Evidence:** live curl 2026-07-01 (500 on /me + /my-tenants across fntest & platform); Serilog `src/backend/HRM.Api/Logs/hrm-20260701.log` lines ~145240-145285 (RedisConnectionException stack ending at AuthController.cs:187); `appsettings.json:5` Redis non-blank vs `appsettings.Development.json:6` blank.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — `/auth/me` is the identity/permissions bootstrap called on every SPA load and after every tenant switch; a down (or briefly flapping) Redis takes the whole authenticated UI offline with a 500, even though login and tenant resolution survive. It is a hard availability dependency on a cache that the rest of the stack treats as optional/degradable. Not CRIT because it requires Redis to be down/unreachable (an infra condition), and login itself still succeeds.

### ISSUE-227 — Workflow plan-limit (`Tenant.MaxWorkflows`) enforcement ignores plan-limit OVERRIDES and the subscription plan's MaxWorkflows — only the `Tenant.MaxWorkflows` column snapshot is consulted (BUG-008 class)
- **Type:** ISSUE · **Severity:** MED · **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #126, verified 2026-07-02) · **Layer:** BE
- **Module/US/TC:** Admin Console / US-ADM-007 / TC-ADM-007-05 (also relates to US-ADM-009 override propagation)
- **Title:** `WorkflowService.EnsureWithinPlanLimitAsync` (`WorkflowService.cs:460-481`) resolves the workflow cap by reading only `Tenant.MaxWorkflows` (`SELECT MaxWorkflows FROM tenants WHERE id=@t`); `null` → treated as unlimited. It does NOT consult the `plan_limit_override` table nor the tenant's `SubscriptionPlan.MaxWorkflows`. Consequently a `max_workflows=2` **override** set via `POST /system/plans/overrides` has ZERO effect on create-time enforcement — same root pattern as the recorded BUG-008 (PlanLimitResolver/overrides have no live callers; enforcement reads the Tenant column snapshot).
- **Root cause (HIGH):** read directly from source — the limit query selects `t.MaxWorkflows` only; no `PlanLimitOverride`/plan join. Reproduced live: set `max_workflows=2` override on fntest, then created 3 ACTIVE workflows (`activate:true`) with 0 pre-existing active → all 3 returned 200, no `workflow_limit_reached`. fntest `Tenant.MaxWorkflows` is null so the snapshot path also allows unlimited.
- **Reproduction steps:** platform admin `POST /api/v1/system/plans/overrides {tenantId:fntest, limitKey:"max_workflows", value:2}` → 200. fntest-admin `POST /api/v1/tenant/workflows` with `"activate":true` three times (entityType Leave/Expense/Offer) → all 200 Active (limit 2 not enforced). The message-template and count logic ARE correct (`WorkflowService.cs:40-41`, counts `Status==Active`), so enforcement WOULD fire if `Tenant.MaxWorkflows` itself were set — but the override/plan resolution is the missing link.
- **Evidence:** live curl 2026-07-01 (override created id `019f1d6d-d778-...`, 3 active workflows created 200); `WorkflowService.cs:460-481` (Tenant.MaxWorkflows-only query). Override + all QA workflows cleaned up (override deleted, 16 QA workflows archived).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — the plan-limit override feature (a US-ADM-009 primitive) silently does not govern the workflow dimension; a platform operator setting a per-tenant workflow cap gets no enforcement. Contained to the workflow limit key and requires the operator to rely on overrides rather than the Tenant column. Duplicate-of-mechanism with BUG-008 (cross-reference).

### BUG-122 — Notification template per-language variant cap (BR-6 "max 2 language variants per template per tenant") is NOT enforced — an unlimited number of language variants can be saved
- **ID:** BUG-122
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #337, 2026-07-17)
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17):** `NotificationTemplateService.SaveAsync` now guards the NEW-language branch (`existing is null`) with a BR-6 cap of 2: it counts the tenant's distinct non-deleted language variants for the `(eventKey)` and rejects a 3rd with `422 variant_limit_reached`. An update to an existing language, or reactivating a reset one, is the `else` branch and never trips the cap; soft-deleted (reset) variants don't count; the count is tenant-scoped by the global filter. 3 arms (3rd-variant→422 · update-at-cap-allowed · cap-is-per-tenant) + 18 existing green (21/21); mutation-verified (disabling the cap fails only the reject arm). **Note:** BR-6 is described as plan-configurable (default 2) — implemented as a constant `MaxLanguageVariants = 2`; wiring it to `PlanLimitResolver` is a deferred follow-up (no plan-limit key exists for template variants yet).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications & Audit / US-NTF-002 / TC-NTF-002-09 (also touches TC-NTF-002-06)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/notification-templates/{eventKey}?language={lang}` upserts a per-(tenant, eventKey, language) override with no guard against BR-6's 2-variant-per-template cap. Saving a 3rd distinct language variant returns HTTP 200 "Template saved." instead of the expected 422/400 "max 2 variants" rejection.
- **Root cause (HIGH):** The `SaveTemplateCommand`/handler path for notification templates performs a language-keyed upsert with no count check of existing custom variants for the (tenant, eventKey) pair. A grep of `src/backend/HRM.Application/Features/Notifications` for any max-2 / variant-limit / BR-6 enforcement returns **zero matches** — the rule was specified but never implemented. There is no plan-limit resolution here either (BR-6 is described as "plan-configurable", default 2), so the cap is simply absent. Confidence HIGH (reproduced live + confirmed no enforcement code exists).
- **Reproduction steps:** fntest, `Bearer <fntest-admin@fn.test>` + `X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest`. On the seeded `leave_approved` template: `PUT …/leave_approved?language=en` → 200 (1 of 2); `PUT …/leave_approved?language=es` → 200 (2 of 2, at the boundary); `PUT …/leave_approved?language=fr` → **200 "Template saved."** (should be rejected as the 3rd variant). Readback `GET …/leave_approved?language={en|es|fr}` shows all three persisted with `isCustom:true`.
- **Evidence:** live curl 2026-07-01 — all three PUTs returned `{"success":true,...,"message":"Template saved."}` with distinct `language` values; readback confirms en/es/fr all `isCustom:true`. No BR-6 enforcement code found in the Notifications feature.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — contained to the template-authoring surface (Tenant.ManageSettings, admin-only); no data-corruption or cross-tenant impact, but a documented business rule (and its plan-configurable limit) is entirely unenforced, so a tenant admin can create arbitrarily many language variants, defeating BR-6 and any plan-tier differentiation built on it. The per-language selection mechanism itself works (variants persist and retrieve distinctly).

### BUG-123 — Dashboard widgets degrade badly at scale: p95 829ms + 60s TIMEOUTS at 50k employees / 50 VU (report aggregations stay fast — it's the widget path)
- **ID:** BUG-123
- **Type:** BUG (performance — SLA breach + request timeouts at scale)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** PARTIALLY RESOLVED (PR #259, 2026-07-12) — remainder split to ISSUE-285 (decision-gated)
- **Done (PR #259):** the attendance-today KPI + live-board "all"/"team" scope loaders no longer materialize whole `Employee` entities — they project to a 6-column `DashboardEmployee(Id, FirstName, LastName, EmployeeNo, DepartmentId, LocationId)` (LocationId is load-bearing for location-specific-holiday precedence). Removes a full-table entity scan on the hot path; also resolves ISSUE-284 item #2. Output identical (new multi-location oracle test; 56/56 dashboard tests green, build clean).
- **Remainder → [[ISSUE-285]] (decision-gated, P4-perf):** (1) UpcomingBirthdays in-memory month/day scan needs an indexed day-of-year computed column (**EF migration** — a schema decision) or cache-warming; (2) 8 widgets run sequentially — parallelism needs `IDbContextFactory`; (3) the p95<800ms/no-60s-timeout **SLA at 50k/50-VU is a k6 perf-rig assertion**, not confirmable in-loop. Do NOT close BUG-123 until ISSUE-285 lands on the rig.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Reports/Dashboard / US-RPT-005 (dashboard) / perf scale TCs (TC-ADM-002-12 class, dashboard-at-scale)
- **Title:** k6 at **50,000 employees / 50 VU** (5 min): `GET /api/v1/dashboard/widgets` p95 **829.66ms** (SLA <800ms), **avg 951ms, max 60s**, with **13 request TIMEOUTS** (http_req_failed). Employee list p95 also regresses to **477ms** (>400 SLA; was 145ms at 5k). By contrast the HR **report aggregations** (headcount/dept-distribution/employment-type) stay fast at 50k (p95 166–169ms) — so the problem is specific to the **dashboard widget** composition path, not aggregation in general.
- **Root cause:** the dashboard-widgets endpoint composes multiple per-widget queries (headcount, turnover, recent-joiners, open-positions, pending-leave, onboarding-in-progress) that do not scale to 50k — likely N+1 / un-indexed scans / no pre-aggregation, and under 50-VU concurrency some exceed the 60s command timeout. Confidence: **HIGH** — measured (`perf/results/50k-hot.json`; widget p95 829ms, max 60s, 13 fails) vs the same run at 5k (106ms, 0 fails) and vs report-generate at 50k (166ms). (Redis cache was UP during the run, so this is the cold/miss + concurrent-recompute cost.)
- **Reproduction steps:** seed `perf` tenant to 50k employees (`perf/seed/seed-perf-tenant.sql -v emp_count=50000`); `k6 run perf/scripts/01-hot-reads.js` → `http_req_duration{name:widgets}` p95 >800ms + timeouts. At 5k the same run passes.
- **Evidence:** `perf/results/50k-hot.json` / `50K-console.log`: widgets p95 829.66ms, max 1m0s, 13/8550 failed; employees p95 477.72ms. Scale-reads run: report aggregations 166–169ms (fine).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — at a realistic large-tenant size the primary landing page (dashboard) breaches SLA and some requests hard-timeout (60s) under modest concurrency, which is a user-facing availability problem. Fix = index/pre-aggregate the widget queries (or cache-warm + shorter timeout + graceful per-widget degradation).

### ISSUE-228 — SignalR/Redis notification delivery is fully wired and LIVE, but every on-demand in-app producer is a log-only seam or unreachable — no in-app notification is ever delivered over the socket in practice
- **ID:** ISSUE-228
- **Type:** ISSUE (behavioral gap / dead delivery channel — infrastructure present, producers absent)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Notifications & Audit + Reports + Attendance / US-NTF-001, US-NTF-003, US-RPT-004, US-ATT-010 / TC-NTF-003-07, TC-RPT-004-02, TC-ATT-139 (S5 live-WS check)
- **Title:** The real-time notification path is proven live end-to-end (negotiate → WebSocket handshake → `NotificationHub` connect → per-user Redis-backplane group subscription), yet NO on-demand producer reaches it for a connected user: the domain producers are DI-registered as **log-only seams** (`LogOnlyLeaveNotificationService` for `ILeaveNotificationService`; `LoggingNotificationDispatcher` for `INotificationDispatcher`), and the one genuinely socket-pushing producer (`HrReportExportService`→`SignalRNotificationService.CreateAndDispatchAsync`) only fires on the **>=1000-row async branch** which is **unreachable** because all HR reports aggregate to <1000 rows. Net effect: the in-app SignalR channel is effectively dead-lettered.
- **Root cause (~90%, code + live probe):** Program.cs registers `INotificationDispatcher`→`HRM.Api.Notifications.LoggingNotificationDispatcher` (log-only, no `IHubContext` send) and `ILeaveNotificationService`→`LogOnlyLeaveNotificationService`; only `INotificationService`→`SignalRNotificationService` actually pushes over the hub (group `t:{tenantId}:user:{userId}`, method `ReceiveNotification`, `NotificationHub.cs:44`), and its live callers (`HrReportExportService`, `LopService`, two Hangfire jobs) are either gated behind the unreachable >=1000-row async export branch or not on-demand triggerable for a self-connected user. So the wiring gap is the known platform-wide "US-NTF seam built, not wired" state — but its consequence (a live socket with no live producer) had not been captured as a single finding.
- **Reproduction steps:** (1) `docker exec hrm-redis redis-cli ping` → PONG; `redis-cli pubsub channels 'hrm:signalr:*'` shows `hrm:signalr:HRM.Api.Hubs.NotificationHub:all`/`:groups` (backplane up). (2) Login `fntest-admin@fn.test`/`Admin@123!` (X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest); `POST /hubs/notifications/negotiate?negotiateVersion=1` → HTTP 200 with `availableTransports` incl. WebSockets. (3) Connect a `@microsoft/signalr` client (WebSockets) → state `Connected`; while connected, `redis-cli pubsub channels` now additionally shows the per-user group channel `hrm:signalr:HRM.Api.Hubs.NotificationHub:group:t:3f000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000f:user:ade50404-804c-4548-a5ce-b0511013a747` + `:user:ade50404...` + `:connection:...`. (4) Trigger the only on-demand self-targeted producer — `POST /api/v1/reports/headcount/export {"format":"csv"}` — returns `status:"Completed", rowCount:7` (inline sync, <1000 rows) and **no `ReceiveNotification` frame arrives** over the socket. (5) The leave-approval in-app producer is `LogOnlyLeaveNotificationService` (never pushes).
- **Evidence:** live 2026-07-01 — negotiate HTTP 200; SignalR client `CONNECTED state=Connected connectionId=…`; Redis `pubsub channels` group/user/connection channels present while connected; headcount export `{status:Completed,rowCount:7}` inline, `DELIVERED=false` after a 15s open socket with the export fired mid-window.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — this is the intended deferred state (US-NTF), not a regression, and no data is lost (notifications are persisted to `notifications` where the persisting producers run); but it means the entire real-time in-app channel currently delivers nothing to end users, so any AC that promises "in-app real-time delivery" (US-NTF-003 BR-5, US-RPT-004 FR-8, US-ATT-010 NFR-2) is unmet in practice. Consolidates the S5-block reason for TC-NTF-003-07 / TC-RPT-004-02 / TC-ATT-139. Fix = wire the domain producers (leave/regularization/report-async) to `INotificationService`/the SignalR dispatcher instead of the log-only seams.

### ISSUE-229 — Payslip email BR-4 "tenant configured sender domain" is not implementable: `ResolveFromAddress()` always returns null (no per-tenant sender-domain config surface exists), so every tenant's payslip email uses the system-default From
- **ID:** ISSUE-229
- **Type:** ISSUE (behavioral/spec gap — documented deferral, defense-in-depth)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Payroll / US-PAY-011 / TC-PAY-011-08 (step 4), TC-PAY-ISO-044 (step 2). FR-8, BR-4.
- **Title:** BR-4 requires each tenant's payslip email "From" to use the tenant's configured sender domain (e.g. `payroll@acme.yourhrm.com`), else the system default. `PayslipDistributionRunner.ResolveFromAddress()` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/PayslipDistributionRunner.cs:314`) is hard-coded `=> null` with the comment "No tenant sender-domain config surface exists yet, so this returns null (the sender uses the system default)." There is no tenant payroll-settings entity/column for a sender address, so the "tenant configured sender domain" half of BR-4 is unimplementable through any surface — every tenant falls back to the system default From. (Cross-tenant sender BLEED is NOT possible — since the value is always the constant default, no tenant's configured domain can leak into another's mail; the isolation guarantee of TC-PAY-ISO-044 step 2 still holds trivially.)
- **Root cause (~99%, code-confirmed):** `ResolveFromAddress() => null` at PayslipDistributionRunner.cs:314; `PayslipEmailMessage` is constructed with `fromAddress` = that null (PayslipDistributionRunner.cs:158), and `LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender` only references `message.FromAddress` in a TODO comment (LogOnlyPayslipEmailSender.cs:44) — the From is never actually applied because delivery is the log-only stub. A per-tenant sender-domain config surface + a real SMTP sender are both deferred (US-NTF).
- **Reproduction steps:** fntest (`X-Tenant-Subdomain: fntest`, `fntest-admin@fn.test`/`Admin@123!`), Finalized run `019f2180-1991-730d-9607-b72d7b5ccfab`. `POST /api/v1/payroll/runs/{runId}/payslips/send-emails {}` → 202 queued. Serilog `src/backend/HRM.Api/Logs/hrm-20260702.log` shows 9 `[PAYSLIP-EMAIL-STUB] Would send payslip email to fnempN@fn.test … Subject='Your Payslip for June 2026'` lines — none carry a tenant-specific From (the stub logs recipient/subject/attachment only; the code path never sets a tenant sender). Grep confirms `ResolveFromAddress() => null`.
- **Evidence:** PayslipDistributionRunner.cs:312-314 (`=> null` with deferral comment); 9 stub log lines 2026-07-02 12:10:11 with no tenant From; no `sender`/`from_address`/sender-domain column on any tenant/payroll-settings table (schema grep negative).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the TC itself permits the system-default fallback ("still a valid, tenant-appropriate address, never another tenant's domain"), no cross-tenant sender bleed is possible (the value is a constant), and delivery is a log-only stub with no real recipients today. It is a genuine but contained BR-4 spec gap that only materializes once a real SMTP sender + a per-tenant sender-domain config are added. Not a security or data issue.

### BUG-124 — Leave BalanceSummary/Utilization reports N+1 at scale: time out (500 after 90s) at 5,000 employees, breaking the report + both export SLAs
- **ID:** BUG-124
- **Type:** BUG (performance / scalability)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #258, 2026-07-12)
- **Resolution:** Replaced the per-(employee×leave-type) entitlement resolution (~325k sequential round-trips at 5k×13) with a new `ILeaveEntitlementService.ComputeProratedEntitlementsBatchAsync` — TWO queries (overrides + active rules) then in-memory resolution via the pure `LeaveEntitlementEngine`, mirroring `ComputeEffectiveEntitlementAsync` exactly (probation gate → override → most-specific rule → default → pro-rata; identical UTC reference date). Rewrote both call sites (`BuildBalanceSummaryAsync`, `ComputeUtilizationAggregatesAsync` — the latter also fixes the UtilizationByDepartment chart); removed the orphaned per-pair wrapper. No index/migration. Regression: correctness test asserts batch == per-pair for every branch incl. a mid-year joiner (Jane=10.08=20×184/365), + a "one batch, not N" assertion. Build clean + 89/89 leave tests. (Perf-rig SLA confirmation deferred — N+1 removed, query count now constant.) Partially unblocks ISSUE-230 (oversized-export routing still builds full report first — separate ticket).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV (reports/export) / TC-LV-248, TC-LV-249, TC-LV-240
- **Title:** `LeaveReportService.BuildBalanceSummaryAsync` resolves entitlement **per employee × leave-type** (`ResolveEntitlementAsync` in a nested loop → ~5,000 × 13 sequential EF round-trips); `BuildUtilizationAsync`/`ComputeUtilizationAggregatesAsync` has the same non-scaling shape. At the platform's own NFR-1 target scale (5,000 employees) neither report completes — the request returns **500 after ~90s**. The lighter reports that do NOT resolve per-employee entitlement (Absenteeism, LopSummary) return in ~100ms, isolating the N+1 as the cause.
- **Root cause (~90%, code + live Serilog):** per-employee/per-leave-type `ResolveEntitlementAsync` calls inside `BuildBalanceSummaryAsync`/`BuildUtilizationAsync` (`src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Services/LeaveReportService.cs`), no set-based/batched entitlement resolution. Query time, not error — 200 never returned; the request is killed at the 90s ceiling.
- **Reproduction steps:** login `perfadmin@perf.test`/`Admin@123!`, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: perf` (5,000 employees, 6,200 leave_request, 13 leave_types seeded). `curl "http://localhost:5000/api/v1/leaves/reports/BalanceSummary?Year=2026"` → HTTP 000 (client timeout 90s); `/Utilization` → HTTP 000 @25s; `/Absenteeism` → 200 in ~100ms.
- **Evidence:** Serilog RequestId `0HNMN7ROLJCHR`: `[ERR] Error handling GetLeaveReportQuery after 90078ms`, `[ERR] HTTP GET …/BalanceSummary responded 500 in 90089ms`, stack `LeaveReportService.ResolveEntitlementAsync ← BuildBalanceSummaryAsync ← GenerateReportCoreAsync`. Absenteeism P95 = 102ms (n=32).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — the primary leave-reporting flow (balance/utilization) is unusable at the documented NFR-1 scale, and it cascades to block both the sync-export (TC-LV-249) and large-export (TC-LV-240) SLAs, since export first generates the same report inline. Fix = batch/set-based entitlement resolution (single query per report, not per employee).

### BUG-125 — Attendance `payroll-data` endpoint: P95 ~28s at 5,000 employees (5.7x over the <=5s SLA), not served from the materialized monthly summary
- **ID:** BUG-125
- **Type:** BUG (performance / scalability)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #257, 2026-07-12)
- **⚠ Root-cause correction:** the finding's ~70% hypothesis (recompute per-employee over raw `attendance_log`) was WRONG. The rollup already comes from the materialized monthly summary (fast — the sibling `reconciliation` on the same call measures 0.21s). The real cause was `AttendancePayrollService.WorkingDaysAsync` — a **shift-resolution N+1** (2-3 queries per employee inside the loop → ~15k round-trips at 5k).
- **Resolution:** Extracted a shared batched `ShiftScheduleResolver` (default shift + all effective assignments + referenced shifts = 3 fixed queries regardless of employee count; latest-effective + default fallback resolved in memory, byte-for-byte identical selection). `GetPayrollDataAsync` now resolves working-days once for all employees. Same fix applied to the sibling N+1 → **BUG-283**. No migration (existing indexes cover it). Regression: `AttendancePayrollIntegrationTests...BUG125` (calendar-oracle, assigned-vs-default). Verified build clean + 40/40 attendance tests. **Note:** the p95-under-SLA-at-5k claim itself is a perf-rig assertion — the fix removes the N+1 (query count now constant); on-rig confirmation deferred (see ISSUE-282-class perf-rig note).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Attendance / US-ATT (payroll-data handoff) / TC-ATT-126
- **Title:** `GET /api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2026-06` returns all 5,000 rows correctly but at **P95 28.4s / min 11.2s / p50 12.7s** — grossly over the <=5s NFR-1. The sibling materialized reads (`summary/monthly` 0.34s, `reconciliation` 0.21s) are fast, so payroll-data is NOT reading the pre-materialized `attendance_monthly_summary` path the TC assumes.
- **Root cause (~70%, timing + contrast):** payroll-data appears to recompute/aggregate per-employee over raw `attendance_log` at request time rather than reading the materialized monthly summary; 200 responses (no exception in Serilog) — the cost is query time, not error. (Confidence 70% pending a source read of the payroll-data query path.)
- **Reproduction steps:** login `perfadmin@perf.test`/`Admin@123!`, header `X-Tenant-Subdomain: perf`, with 150,000 attendance_log rows (June 2026, 5,000 emp × 30 days) + a generated monthly summary. `curl -w "%{time_total}" "http://localhost:5000/api/v1/attendance/payroll-data?month=2026-06"` → ~11-28s per call.
- **Evidence:** P95 28.4s over 6 reqs (2 warmup discarded); `summary/monthly` P95 0.34s and `reconciliation` P95 0.21s on the same tenant/volume.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — payroll-data is the attendance→payroll integration handoff; ~28s per pull directly blocks a 5,000-employee payroll run from meeting its SLA. Fix = serve payroll-data from the materialized summary (or a set-based aggregate) instead of per-request recomputation over raw logs.

### ISSUE-230 — Leave large-export background threshold is unreachable: the full report is generated inline before the row-count queue check
- **ID:** ISSUE-230
- **Type:** ISSUE (design flaw)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #336, 2026-07-17)
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17):** `ExportReportAsync` now routes on a CHEAP row-count **upper bound** (`EstimateExportRowCountAsync` — a couple of `COUNT` queries: every report is employee-driven, so BalanceSummary/CarryForward ≈ employees×leaveTypes, the rest ≤ employees) computed BEFORE any generation. Only the sync branch (estimate ≤ threshold) generates inline; the oversized report is queued without being materialised, so it can no longer hang before reaching the 202 path. Over-estimating only queues a borderline report to the (correct) background job. New arm `Export_LargeDataset_RoutesToBackground_WithoutGeneratingInline_Issue230` asserts the entitlement batch (the expensive generation work) is **never invoked** for a queued export — mutation-verified: making the estimate generate first (the pre-fix ordering) fails exactly that arm. 38/38 LeaveReportService arms green.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV (export) / TC-LV-240
- **Title:** `LeaveReportService.ExportReport` calls `GenerateReportCoreAsync` with `PageSize = int.MaxValue` to obtain the full row count **before** the `rowCount > SyncExportRowThreshold(5000)` routing that decides sync-vs-Hangfire (svc ~line 180 vs ~line 189). So any report large enough to warrant the background path must first be fully generated inline — which for the only >5,000-row report (BalanceSummary) is exactly the request that hangs (see BUG-124). The 202/queue logic and `LeaveReportExportJob` wiring exist but can never be exercised live for an oversized report.
- **Root cause (~95%, code-read):** ordering in `ExportReport` — count-via-full-generation precedes the threshold routing; the AC-5 background-export protection is defeated by its own pre-check.
- **Reproduction steps:** `curl "http://localhost:5000/api/v1/leaves/reports/BalanceSummary/export?format=xlsx"` (perf tenant) → HTTP 000 @30s (never reaches the 202 queue path).
- **Evidence:** `LeaveReportService.ExportReport` lines ~180 (full-count generation) vs ~189 (`rowCount > 5000` routing), read this run.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — real design flaw that defeats AC-5's oversized-export protection, but contingent on the same underlying N+1 (BUG-124); fixing the N+1 still leaves the whole report built in-memory before routing, so both want addressing.

### ISSUE-231 — Recruitment pipeline board hard-500s on an unmapped `ApplicationSource` enum value; a single bad row poisons the whole board query
- **ID:** ISSUE-231
- **Type:** ISSUE (robustness / defense-in-depth)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (PR #348, 2026-07-17)
> **RESOLVED (2026-07-17).** Root cause confirmed: EF's strict enum→string converter (strict since EF Core 6, dotnet/efcore#24084) throws during **materialization**, so one bad row aborts the whole result set. **Researched first — no library exists** (no maintained NuGet tolerant-enum converter; EF 10 / Npgsql add nothing), so the sanctioned small custom `ValueConverter` was the right call. Added `TolerantEnumToStringConverter<TEnum>` (`HRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Converters/`): WRITE side unchanged (`v.ToString()`, injective → `Where(x => x.Stage == s)` still translates server-side), READ side maps an unknown string to an explicit **`Unknown` sentinel + logs**. Generalises the bespoke `LeaveLedgerConfiguration.ParseEntryType` (BUG-037/086) prior art. Applied to `applicant.stage` + `applicant.source`, and — **found by `@integration-enforcer`, same class on a higher-traffic surface** — `applicant_stage_history.from_stage`/`.to_stage`, where one corrupt row 500s the **entire recruitment dashboard**. The sentinel is read-only (stage-move + submit validators `.NotEqual(Unknown)`; excluded from the board's stage columns + the dashboard's source buckets). **No migration** (column stays varchar(20); no schema diff). Verified on real `postgres:17-alpine` (the only way to plant an out-of-enum string — raw SQL; InMemory reads through the same converter and cannot reproduce it): 4 arms — materialization tolerance, the real **board service** returns 200 with the bad-source card showing `Unknown`, the real **dashboard** returns 200, and the payroll-run list; 43/43 green incl. existing recruitment suites. **Mutation-verified:** reverting each converter to strict fails its arm with the exact production error (`Cannot convert string value 'CareerSite'/'LegacyPhoneScreen'`) — the dashboard mutation empirically proved the enforcer's HIGH finding real, not theoretical.
> **Documented residual (see [[DEFERRED-FOLLOWUPS]] DF-11/DF-12):** `applicant.rejection_reason` + `applicant_stage_history.rejection_reason` (a **different, nullable** `RejectionReason` enum) remain **strict**, so a corrupt rejection_reason can **still 500** the board/detail — the board is therefore only *partially* hardened. Rarer (only ever set on rejected rows, always to a validated value) and needs its own `Unknown` member + nullable converter → decision. FE has no `Unknown` badge (blank, no crash).
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Recruitment / US-REC-003 / TC-REC-003-12
- **Title:** `GET /recruitment/vacancies/{id}/pipeline` throws `System.InvalidOperationException: Cannot convert string value '<x>' from the database to any value in the mapped 'ApplicationSource' enum` (thrown in `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Query` during materialization) if ANY applicant row on the vacancy has a `source` string outside the mapped enum (`Public/Internal/Referral`, `HRM.Domain/Enums/ApplicationSource.cs`). One unmapped row 500s the entire board for every user. (Surfaced by a test-seed that used `source='CareerSite'`; the write API validates the enum so it should not occur through normal use — hence LOW — but the read path has no graceful fallback for a bad-data row.)
- **Root cause (~95%, Serilog):** EF enum value-conversion has no fallback/default for unknown strings; the projection iterates all applicants, so one bad row aborts the whole query.
- **Reproduction steps:** insert an applicant with `source` not in the enum, then `GET /recruitment/vacancies/{id}/pipeline` → 500. (After correcting the seed to `Public`, the board returns 200 at P95 0.027s — see TC-REC-003-12 pass.)
- **Evidence:** Serilog RequestId `0HNMN7ROLJC9E` — `InvalidOperationException … 'CareerSite' … 'ApplicationSource'`.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — data-contingent (write path validates the enum, so normal use won't produce it), but a defense-in-depth gap: the board should not be fully unavailable because of one malformed row.

### ENH-024 — Disabled "Send payslips" button gives screen-reader users no reason (no `aria-describedby` to the disabling hint)
- **ID:** ENH-024
- **Type:** ENH (accessibility improvement)

Suggested direction: wire the hint via `aria-describedby` on the button.

### BUG-126 — Onboarding overdue-notification Hangfire job 500s on a `jsonb ~~ jsonb` LIKE (idempotency check), retries forever
- **ID:** BUG-126
- **Type:** BUG (broken vs spec)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #131, verified 2026-07-02)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Onboarding / US-ONB (overdue-task notifications) / (caught during BUG-003/007 verification, no bound TC)
- **Title:** The onboarding overdue-task notification job's "once-per-day" idempotency check does `o.Payload.Contains(task.Id.ToString())` where `OnboardingNotificationOutbox.Payload` is a **jsonb** column (`OnboardingChecklistService.cs:702`). Npgsql cannot translate `string.Contains` on jsonb → `42883: operator does not exist: jsonb ~~ jsonb`. The query aborts (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Query.QueryIterationFailed`), the Hangfire job fails and **retries indefinitely** (observed live: job '513', retry 5/10, 30 failures in the startup window). This is the **same class as BUG-007** (jsonb `Contains` untranslatable) but in a background job, so it never surfaces as an HTTP 500 — it just silently fails on every run, so overdue-task notifications are never sent AND the idempotency guard is dead.
- **Root cause (~98%, live Serilog + code-read):** `OnboardingChecklistService.cs:702` — `.Contains()` on the jsonb `Payload` column inside `AnyAsync(...)`. Should match on a structured column (e.g. a dedicated `TaskId`/`ResourceId` column or `NotificationType` + a scalar key), or cast/compare without a jsonb LIKE.
- **Reproduction steps:** start the API (Development) against Postgres with any overdue onboarding checklist task → the recurring overdue-notification job runs → Serilog logs `operator does not exist: jsonb ~~ jsonb` + `Failed to process the job '<id>'` (Hangfire AutomaticRetry).
- **Evidence:** `src/backend/HRM.Api/Logs/hrm-<date>.log` this run — `Npgsql.PostgresException 42883: operator does not exist: jsonb ~~ jsonb` with `EventId 10100 QueryIterationFailed`, followed by `Hangfire.AutomaticRetryAttribute Failed to process the job '513'`. Source: `OnboardingChecklistService.cs:702` (`o.Payload.Contains(task.Id.ToString())`).
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a background feature (overdue notifications) is entirely broken on Postgres and burns retry capacity every cycle; not user-facing 500 and data-contingent on overdue tasks existing, so not HIGH. Trivial fix (same remedy as BUG-007). Found by verification, not previously in the ledger.

### ISSUE-233 — Core-HR list/table pages have ARIA-structure a11y nits: Departments card grid skips heading level (h1→h3) and the Job Titles desktop `role="table"` contains disallowed `role="button"` children
- **ID:** ISSUE-233
- **Type:** ISSUE (accessibility contract nit)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #135, merged — departments card h3->h2 heading-order; job-titles tr role=button removed; live a11y 96)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-004 (Departments) + US-CHR-005 (Job Titles) / TC-CHR-030, TC-CHR-061
- **Title:** Two distinct, genuine (non-contrast) Lighthouse a11y failures on the Core-HR non-employee list pages, surfaced during the responsive/a11y rig pass on `acme.myhrm.org:4200` (hr@acme.test): (a) **Departments** (`/departments`, list view) — the department **cards use `<h3.text-base>`** for each department name with the page title as `<h1>` and no intervening `<h2>`, so Lighthouse `heading-order` fails ("Heading elements are not in a sequentially-descending order"); (b) **Job Titles** (`/job-titles`, desktop) — the list is `<table role="table">` whose descendants include `role="button"` elements, so Lighthouse `aria-required-children` fails ("Element has children which are not allowed: [role=button]"). Distinct component from BUG-110 (that is a payroll `role="tablist"` with a non-`tab` child) — same axe rule, different element/root-cause.
- **Root cause:** (a) `app-department-list` card template emits `h3` for the card title without an enclosing `h2` section heading (heading hierarchy skips a level). (b) `app-job-title-list` desktop table declares `role="table"` (or relies on native `<table>` semantics) but places interactive `role="button"` controls as row/cell descendants in a way that violates the ARIA table required-children contract; the accessible structure should use `rowgroup`/`row`/`cell` (or `gridcell` under `role="grid"`) with the buttons inside cells. Confidence: **90%** — Lighthouse node selectors point at `div.card-notion > … > h3.text-base` and `div.page-container > div.card-notion > div.hidden > table.w-full` respectively; exact template lines not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → in-app nav to **Departments**, run Chrome DevTools MCP `lighthouse_audit` (accessibility, snapshot) → `heading-order` fails. Nav to **Job Titles**, re-run → `aria-required-children` fails. (Both pages also fail `color-contrast` = systemic BUG-096, and `label-content-name-mismatch` on the tenant-switcher = known ISSUE-205 — those are NOT this finding.)
- **Evidence:** Lighthouse snapshot (desktop, 1440×900) — Departments **Accessibility 94** (Passed 31 / Failed 4): failing audits `color-contrast` (BUG-096), `heading-order` (this), `label-content-name-mismatch` (ISSUE-205 tenant-switcher + clickable card role=button), `agent-accessibility-tree` (agentic, informative). Job Titles **Accessibility 92** (Passed 36 / Failed 4): `aria-required-children` (this, node `…table.w-full`, explanation "Element has children which are not allowed: [role=button]"), `color-contrast` (BUG-096), `label-content-name-mismatch` (ISSUE-205), `agent-accessibility-tree`. Reports: `chrome-devtools-mcp-qBx16g/report.json` (Departments), `chrome-devtools-mcp-X2MxcV/report.json` (Job Titles).
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — defense-in-depth WCAG 1.3.1 (heading structure) / 4.1.2 (ARIA table semantics) nits on secondary management pages; screen-reader navigation is degraded (mis-announced heading outline / table row-count) but no functional block, no crash, and the visible layout is correct. Both are localized template fixes.

### ISSUE-234 — Leave Types list page has 4 genuine (non-contrast) a11y failures, most seriously a `role="switch"` toggle with no `aria-checked` and no accessible name — SR users cannot perceive or operate the per-leave-type active toggle
- **ID:** ISSUE-234
- **Type:** ISSUE (accessibility defect — WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value + 1.3.1 Info & Relationships)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #135, merged — leave-types th scope=col, drag div->button, switch/drag null-data aria fallbacks; live a11y 96)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV-001 (Leave Types) / TC-LV-035, TC-LV-036
- **Title:** The Leave Types list (`/leave-types`, component `ng-c1673730939`) fails four distinct Lighthouse/axe a11y audits beyond the known systemic noise: (1) **`aria-required-attr` + `button-name`** — each row's active/inactive toggle is a `<button type="button" role="switch" class="toggle-switch">` that has **neither `aria-checked` nor any accessible name** (no inner text, no `aria-label`), so a screen-reader user cannot tell the toggle's on/off state nor what it toggles; (2) **`aria-prohibited-attr`** — the CDK drag-reorder handles are `<div cdkdraghandle class="cdk-drag-handle" aria-label="Drag to reorder …">` with **no role**, so `aria-label` is prohibited and dropped (the reorder affordance is invisible to AT); (3) **`td-has-header`** — the leave-types `<table role="table">` has data `<td>` cells with no associated header cells. The toggle defect (1) is the material one: it is an unlabeled, state-less switch controlling whether a leave type is active.
- **Root cause:** `app-leave-type-list` template — the toggle `<button role="switch">` binds visual on/off state via CSS class only, without `[attr.aria-checked]` or an `aria-label`; the drag handle puts `aria-label` on a role-less `div`; the table markup omits `<th scope>`/header associations for its data cells. Confidence: **92%** — Lighthouse node snippets pinpoint `button.toggle-switch`, `div.cdk-drag-handle[aria-label]`, and `table.w-full` on the leave-types component; template lines not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `hr@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → SPA-nav to **Leave Types** (`/leave-types`) → run Chrome DevTools MCP `lighthouse_audit` (accessibility, snapshot). Failing audits: `aria-required-attr`, `button-name`, `aria-prohibited-attr`, `td-has-header` (plus systemic `color-contrast`=BUG-096 and `label-content-name-mismatch`=ISSUE-205, which are NOT this finding).
- **Evidence:** Lighthouse snapshot (desktop, 1440×900) — Leave Types **Accessibility 82** (Passed 31 / Failed 7). New failures with node explanations: `aria-required-attr` → "Required ARIA attribute not present: aria-checked" on `button.toggle-switch`; `button-name` → "Element does not have inner text … aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty" on the same buttons; `aria-prohibited-attr` → "aria-label attribute cannot be used on a div with no valid role attribute" on `div.cdk-drag-handle`; `td-has-header` → "Some non-empty data cells do not have table headers" on `table.w-full`. Report: `chrome-devtools-mcp-a2A1vm/report.json`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a primary interactive control (the active/inactive switch, one per leave type) is completely opaque to screen-reader and voice-control users (no name, no state), which is a functional block for AT users managing leave-type configuration, not merely cosmetic. Sighted/keyboard use is unaffected and no crash, so not HIGH. All four are localized template fixes on one component.

### BUG-127 — Employee Directory card click navigates to `/employees/undefined` (NG04008) — profile is NOT reachable via the intended in-app click path even though BUG-099 is fixed and the list now renders
- **ID:** BUG-127
- **Type:** BUG
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #133, verified live 2026-07-03 — card click → /employees/{guid} loads profile; Documents tab renders, no .filter crash)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-002 (Employee Directory/Profile) / surfaced while re-testing the BUG-099-unblocked TCs (TC-CHR-233/121/235/210/292/288/110)
- **Title:** With BUG-099 fixed the Employee Directory list renders (20 cards, "Showing 1-20 of 35"), but **clicking any employee card does nothing and throws `RuntimeError: NG04008: The requested path contains undefined segment at index 1`** in the console. The card's click/navigation builds a router path whose employee-id segment is `undefined` (i.e. `navigate(['/employees', undefined])`), so the directory→profile flow — the whole reason the BUG-099 fix mattered — is still broken for real users. The profile page itself is fully functional (confirmed by navigating directly via the Angular Router to `/employees/{id}`), so the defect is isolated to the card's id binding, not the profile route.
- **Root cause (~80%, FE code):** the employee-card click handler / `[routerLink]` references an employee-id property that resolves to `undefined` on the card's data object, even though the list DTO clearly exposes `id` (verified: the `@for` `$implicit` context on `.employee-card` has `id: "019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74"` populated). Almost certainly a field-drift: the template navigates with a mis-named field (e.g. `employee.employeeId`) instead of `employee.id`. The **same field-drift also produces a co-occurring `NG0955` warning** — the list `@for` track expression yields an **empty key `""` for all 20 rows** ("Duplicated keys … key '' at index 0 and 1 …"), i.e. it tracks by the same undefined/empty field rather than `id`, causing duplicate-key churn and defeating row identity on updates. Both symptoms point at one wrong property reference in the employee-list/card template. (No server log involved — pure client-side Angular routing error.)
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → SPA-nav to **Employees** → the directory renders 20 cards. Click any card (e.g. "John Doe") → nothing navigates; DevTools console logs `ERROR RuntimeError: NG04008: The requested path contains undefined segment at index 1`. Compare: navigating the Router directly to `/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74` renders the full Employee Profile correctly.
- **Evidence:** Console (this session, `/employees`): `msgid=203/205/207 [error] ERROR RuntimeError: NG04008: The requested path contains undefined segment at index 1` (one per card-click attempt); `msgid=200/204/206/208 [warn] NG0955 … Duplicated keys were: key "" at index "0" and "1" … through index 18/19` (20 employee rows). `ng.getContext('.employee-card').$implicit` = `{id:"019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74", employeeNo:"EMP-0001", …}` (id present). Direct Router nav to `/employees/{id}` → profile renders (banner "John Doe / Active", tabs Personal…Compensation).
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — breaks the primary Core-HR navigation flow (open an employee's profile by clicking their directory card); every profile-detail feature (status change, documents, edit, timeline, compensation) is unreachable through the intended UI even though the pages themselves work. Not CRIT because the list still renders and the profile is reachable by URL/router, so it is a broken-link-class defect, not data loss or a crash. One localized template fix (correct the id field used in the card's routerLink/navigate and `@for` track).

### ISSUE-235 — "Change Employee Status" modal does not move focus into the dialog on open and does not close on Escape — WCAG 2.1 AA focus-management failure (TC-CHR-235)
- **ID:** ISSUE-235
- **Type:** ISSUE (accessibility defect — WCAG 2.1 AA 2.4.3 Focus Order / 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap escape)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #134, merged — cdkTrapFocus auto-capture: focus moves into dialog + Escape closes; live-verified focusInside=true)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-009 (Employee Status Change) / TC-CHR-235
- **Title:** The employee-profile **Change Employee Status** modal is otherwise well-structured for a11y (`role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby="status-modal-title"`, all form fields labeled with required-indicators — New Status, Effective Date, Reason), **but on open it does NOT move keyboard focus into the dialog** — focus remains on the "Change employee status" trigger button behind the modal (`document.activeElement` = the trigger, `dialog.contains(activeElement) === false`). A screen-reader/keyboard user is not placed in the dialog and the dialog content is not announced. Additionally, **Escape did not close the modal** (dispatched keydown Escape → dialog still present), i.e. no keyboard dismiss. This fails TC-CHR-235 steps 2 (first focusable element receives focus / focus trapped) and 5 (Escape closes, focus returns).
- **Root cause (~85%, FE code):** the status-change modal component does not implement initial focus management / focus-trap on open (no `cdkTrapFocus` + `cdkFocusInitial`, no programmatic `.focus()` of the first field, no `autoFocus`) and has no `(keydown.escape)`/overlay Escape handler. It appears to be a custom (non-CDK-overlay) dialog that renders `aria-modal` markup without the accompanying focus behavior. Confidence 85% — behavior directly observed; template/component lines not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → open an employee profile (Router-nav to `/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74`, since BUG-127 blocks the card click) → click **"Change employee status"**. Modal opens. Via DevTools evaluate: `document.activeElement` is still the trigger button ("Change employee status"), `dialog.contains(activeElement)` is `false`. Dispatch `keydown` Escape on the dialog/document → dialog remains open.
- **Evidence:** evaluate result `{activeTag:"BUTTON", activeLabel:"Change employee status", focusInsideDialog:false, dialogHasAriaModal:"true", dialogLabelledby:"status-modal-title", selectOptionCount:1}`; after Escape dispatch `{dialogStillOpen:true}`. Modal a11y-tree: `dialog "Change Employee Status" modal` with `heading level 3`, `button "Close status change dialog"`, `combobox "New Status *"`, `Date "Effective Date *"`, `textbox "Reason *" multiline required`, `button "Cancel"`, `button "Continue"`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a concrete WCAG 2.1 AA focus-management failure (focus not moved into a modal dialog + no Escape dismiss) on a control HR uses to change employment status; screen-reader/keyboard-only users are left outside the dialog. Not HIGH because the dialog markup is otherwise correct (labeled, aria-modal) and sighted-mouse users can operate and close it via Cancel/Close; the Escape-dispatch was synthetic so real-keyboard behavior may differ, but initial-focus-not-moved is unambiguous. Localized component fix (focus-trap + initial focus + Escape handler).

### BUG-236 — Employee-profile Documents tab crashes on render: the `EmployeeDocuments` component calls `.filter()` on the paginated `{items, totalCount}` envelope instead of `.items`, so the document list + upload form never render even when documents exist (same class as BUG-099)
- **ID:** BUG-236
- **Type:** BUG (FE render crash — existing data not displayed)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #133, verified live 2026-07-03 — card click → /employees/{guid} loads profile; Documents tab renders, no .filter crash)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-008 (Employee Documents) / TC-CHR-210
- **Title:** Opening an employee profile's **Documents** tab throws `TypeError: this.documents(...).filter is not a function` on every change-detection cycle (observed 7×). The documents API `GET /api/v1/tenant/employees/{id}/documents` returns a **paginated envelope** `{"success":true,"data":{"items":[...],"totalCount":2}}`; after the global unwrap interceptor the component receives `{items:[...], totalCount:2}` (an object) and calls `.filter(...)` on it as if it were an array. Result: the document **list body never renders** and all category-tab counts show **0** — even though John Doe (EMP-0001) has **2** real documents (`tiny.pdf`, `ten.pdf`) returned in the 200 response. The **"Upload Document"** button also opens **no** form/modal/file-input/dropzone (no overlay, no `input[type=file]` appears on click) — the broken component template can't render the upload UI either. Only the filter-tab shell (All/Contracts/IDs/Certificates/Other) and the Upload button chrome render.
- **Root cause (~90%, FE code):** the `app-employee-documents` component stores the service response directly into its `documents` signal/state and calls `documents().filter(...)` in the template/computed to build the per-category views; the endpoint is paginated (`{items, totalCount}`) so `documents()` is a non-array object and `.filter` is undefined. This is the **same root-cause class as BUG-099** (EmployeeList `.length` on the paginated envelope) in a sibling component — the FE consumes `data` as a bare array but the API ships `{items,totalCount}`. Fix is to read `response.items` (or `.data.items`). Confidence 90% — console stack (`this.documents(...).filter is not a function`, chunk change-detection) + the exact 200 envelope shape are captured; component source lines not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → Router-nav to `/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74` (BUG-127 blocks the card click) → click the **Documents** tab. Console shows `ERROR TypeError: this.documents(...).filter is not a function` (7×). The list body is empty and every category tab reads count `0`. Click **Upload Document** → nothing opens (verified: no `.cdk-overlay-container` content, no `[role=dialog]`, no `input[type=file]`, no dropzone).
- **Evidence:** console `msgid=241 [error] ERROR TypeError: this.documents(...).filter is not a function (2 args) [7 times]`. Network `reqid=791 GET .../employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74/documents [200]` body: `{"success":true,"data":{"items":[{"id":"019efd82-…","fileName":"tiny.pdf",…,"description":"<script>alert(1)</script>"},{"id":"019efd80-…","fileName":"ten.pdf",…}],"totalCount":2}}`. Upload-click probe returned `{fileInputs:[], hasOverlay:false, hasDialog:false, dropzone:null, browseBtn:null}`.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a primary Core-HR flow (view/manage an employee's documents) is entirely non-functional: existing documents are invisible and the upload path can't be opened, on every employee profile. Not CRIT because it is contained to the Documents tab (the rest of the profile renders) and the data is intact server-side (BE returns 200 with the documents). Blocks TC-CHR-210 (the a11y arm can't exercise list rows/download/delete/upload-form). Note: one stored document's `description` is a raw `<script>alert(1)</script>` payload (from prior testing) — not rendered now due to the crash; re-verify Angular escaping once the list renders.

### ISSUE-237 — Reporting-manager selector modal has WCAG 2.1 AA focus-management + autocomplete-announcement failures: focus is not moved into the dialog on open, Escape does not dismiss, and the search has no aria-live / combobox semantics so results are not announced (TC-CHR-292)
- **ID:** ISSUE-237
- **Type:** ISSUE (accessibility defect — WCAG 2.1 AA 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.1.2 keyboard-escape, 4.1.3 Status Messages / 4.1.2 Name-Role-Value)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED-PARTIAL (PR #134, merged — focus-trap + Escape + aria-live done; full ARIA combobox arrow-key pattern deferred as noted)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-011 (Manager Assignment) / TC-CHR-292
- **Title:** The **reporting-manager selector modal** (Employee profile → Employment tab → "Change reporting manager") is partially a11y-correct — `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby="manager-modal-title"`, the search field has an accessible name (`aria-label="Search for a manager"`), and the Close button has a name ("Close manager selector") — **but it has four WCAG failures**: (1) on open, focus is **NOT moved into the dialog** — `document.activeElement` remains the "Employment" tab trigger button behind the modal (`dialog.contains(activeElement) === false`); (2) **Escape does not close** the modal (dispatched keydown Escape on dialog + document → dialog still present); (3) the type-ahead search has **no `aria-live` region** anywhere in the dialog, so result changes ("No active employees found" / result rows) are **not announced** to screen readers (TC-CHR-292 step 3); (4) the search input is a plain `<input type="search">` — **not an ARIA combobox** (no `role="combobox"`, no `aria-expanded`, no `aria-controls`) and the results container exposes **no `role="listbox"`/`role="option"`**, so arrow-key result navigation is not announced (steps 4, 9). This is the **same focus/Escape class as ISSUE-235** (status-change modal) in a different component, plus autocomplete-specific gaps.
- **Root cause (~85%, FE code):** the manager-selector modal component renders `aria-modal` dialog markup without the accompanying focus behavior (no `cdkTrapFocus`/`cdkFocusInitial`, no programmatic first-field `.focus()`) and no overlay/`(keydown.escape)` dismiss handler; the autocomplete is built as a bare search input + results div rather than the ARIA combobox pattern (input `role=combobox`+`aria-expanded`+`aria-controls` → `role=listbox`/`option`) and lacks an `aria-live` status region for result counts. Confidence 85% — all four behaviors directly observed via DevTools evaluate; component/template source not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → Router-nav to `/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74` (BUG-127 blocks the card click) → **Employment** tab → click **"Change"** (aria-label "Change reporting manager"). Modal opens. Evaluate: `dialog.contains(document.activeElement)` = `false` (active = "Employment" tab button); dispatch keydown Escape → dialog still open; `dialog.querySelector('[aria-live]')` = none; input is `type=search` with no `role`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`; `dialog.querySelector('[role=listbox],[role=option]')` = none.
- **Evidence:** open-probe `{dialogRole:"dialog", ariaModal:"true", ariaLabel:"manager-modal-title", focusInDialog:false, activeTag:"BUTTON", activeLabel:"Employment", searchInput:{type:"search", ariaLabel:"Search for a manager", role:null, ariaExpanded:null, ariaControls:null}, liveRegions:[], buttons:["Close manager selector"]}`; escape-probe `{dialogStillOpenAfterEscape:true, resultsHaveListboxRole:false}`.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — concrete WCAG 2.1 AA failures (focus not moved into a modal, no Escape dismiss, autocomplete results not announced) on the HR manager-assignment control; screen-reader/keyboard users are left outside the dialog and get no result feedback. Not HIGH because the dialog is otherwise labeled/aria-modal, the search field has an accessible name, and sighted-mouse users can operate/close it; the Escape check was synthetic (real-keyboard may differ) but focus-not-moved and missing aria-live/combobox roles are unambiguous. Localized fix (focus-trap + initial focus + Escape + ARIA combobox/live pattern).

### BUG-238 — Documents-tab category filter uses `role="tab"` buttons with NO `role="tablist"` parent (and no `aria-controls`/roving tabindex) — axe/Lighthouse `aria-required-parent` (serious), fails WCAG 2.1 AA
- **ID:** BUG-238
- **Type:** BUG (accessibility defect — WAI-ARIA tab pattern / WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 Name-Role-Value)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #135, merged — documents category nav role=tablist added; aria-required-parent gone)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-008 (Employee Documents) / TC-CHR-210
- **Title:** On the employee-profile **Documents** tab, the document **category filter** ("All / Contracts / IDs / Certificates / Other") is rendered as five `<button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected="…">` elements inside a plain `<nav aria-label="Document category filter">` that has **no `role="tablist"`**. WAI-ARIA requires every `role="tab"` to be contained by a `role="tablist"` parent, so axe-core/Lighthouse report a **serious `aria-required-parent`** violation (`"[role]s are not contained by their required parent element"`, 5 nodes). The tabs additionally have **no `aria-controls`** pointing at a tabpanel and **no roving `tabindex`** (all five buttons have `tabindex=null` → all five are in the tab order instead of the single-active-tab roving pattern). A screen reader will not announce these as a coherent tab set, and keyboard users get no arrow-key tab semantics. This is the **inverse rule** of BUG-110 / ISSUE-233 (those are `aria-required-children`: a `tablist` holding a non-`tab` child) — here the `tab`s are present but their required `tablist` parent is missing, on a different component.
- **Root cause (~90%, FE code):** the `app-employee-documents` category-filter template emits the filter buttons with `role="tab"`+`aria-selected` but wraps them in a semantically-plain `<nav>` (labelled, but no `role="tablist"`), and does not wire `aria-controls`→ the document-list panel nor manage a roving `tabindex`. Fix: add `role="tablist"` to the container (or drop `role="tab"` and use a filter/`aria-pressed` toggle pattern instead), link `aria-controls`, and apply roving-tabindex. Confidence 90% — the offending DOM was read live via DevTools evaluate (`navRole:null`, `tabCount:5`, `firstTab` `role="tab"`, `parentRole:null`, `parentTag:"NAV"`, `tabTabindex:[null,null,null,null,null]`, `tabHasAriaControls:false`) and corroborated by the Lighthouse `aria-required-parent` audit; component source not opened (report-only).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → log in `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → **Employees** → click **John Doe** card (`/employees/019efced-88a9-7825-a8e0-7571318deb74`) → **Documents** tab. Run Lighthouse a11y (snapshot) → `aria-required-parent` fails (5 `.tab-btn[role=tab]` nodes). Or DevTools: `document.querySelector('nav[aria-label="Document category filter"]').getAttribute('role')` → `null`, while its children carry `role="tab"`.
- **Evidence:** Lighthouse snapshot (desktop) Accessibility = **90**, failed audit `aria-required-parent` — `"[role]s are not contained by their required parent element"`, node `<button type="button" role="tab" class="tab-btn …" aria-selected="false">` (×5). DevTools evaluate: `{navRole:null, navTag:"NAV", tabCount:5, tabHasAriaControls:false, tabTabindex:[null,null,null,null,null], parentRole:null, parentTag:"NAV"}`. (Same audit run also flagged systemic `color-contrast` → **BUG-096**, not re-filed, and `label-content-name-mismatch` on the sidebar "Switch organization" + profile "Change employee status" chrome buttons — outside this TC's document-management scope, noted not filed.)
- **Severity rationale:** MED — a genuine, tool-confirmed *serious* WCAG 2.1 AA violation on the document-management UI: screen-reader/keyboard users lose coherent tab semantics for the category filter. Not HIGH because the filter is still operable by sighted-mouse users, the buttons are individually focusable with accessible names + `aria-selected`, and the fix is a localized markup change; it is a defense-in-depth/AT-parity defect, not a functional break. Fails TC-CHR-210 step 12 ("no critical or serious WCAG 2.1 AA violations").

### BUG-239 — Leave Types list crashes each row's render when a leave type has a null `color` (`getContrastTextColor` → `null.replace`), silently dropping that row's DOM + a11y attributes
- **ID:** BUG-239
- **Type:** BUG (FE render crash — TypeError thrown during change detection)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** RESOLVED (fix in PR #135; discovered + fixed 2026-07-03 while verifying the leave-types a11y work)
- **Layer:** FE
- **Module / US / TC:** Leave Management / US-LV-001 (Leave Types) / surfaced via TC-CHR-210 a11y verification (leave-types list)
- **Title:** On `/leave-types`, any leave type with a **null `color`** (legacy/QA rows) crashes that row's render: the template `[style.color]="getContrastColor(lt.color)"` calls `getContrastTextColor(null)` which does `null.replace('#','')` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replace')`. Thrown during change detection, it **aborts the whole row's render**, so the row's drag handle + active/inactive `role="switch"` toggle render **without** their `aria-label`/`aria-checked` — which is what surfaced as the page's Lighthouse `button-name` + `aria-required-attr` failures (a11y score stuck at 86).
- **Root cause (FE):** `getContrastTextColor(hex: string)` in `src/frontend/src/app/features/leave-management/models/leave-type.models.ts` had no null/blank guard before `hex.replace(...)`. The FE model types `color` as non-null but the backend/seed data allows null. **Same null-guard bug class as BUG-099/127/236** (FE assumes a field is always present; a null value breaks render).
- **Reproduction steps:** `http://acme.myhrm.org:4200` → `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` → `/leave-types`. Console shows `TypeError … reading 'replace' at getContrastTextColor → LeaveTypeListComponent.getContrastColor` once per null-color row (8 such QA rows in acme). Those rows' `.drag-handle`/`[role=switch]` have no `aria-label`/`aria-checked`; Lighthouse a11y flags `button-name` + `aria-required-attr`.
- **Evidence:** live probe — 8 `.drag-handle` and 22 `[role=switch]` missing aria attrs (of 13/26) before fix; after the null guard: 0 missing, crash gone, Lighthouse a11y **86 → 96**, `button-name` + `aria-required-attr` PASS.
- **Fix:** null guard in `getContrastTextColor` (returns `'#000000'` for null/blank) + defensive aria fallbacks on the drag button + switch (`lt.isActive ?? false`, `lt.name || 'leave type'`). PR #135.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — Angular's per-row error handler isolates the throw so the page still loads and other rows render, but every null-color row silently loses its interactive controls' a11y (and the noisy per-row console errors). Root cause of the leave-types a11y failures; a real render-correctness defect, not only an a11y nit.

### BUG-240 — `[Authorize(Roles=…)]` endpoints always 403 for the correct role: JWT carries roles in a custom `roles` claim but `TokenValidationParameters.RoleClaimType` is never set to `"roles"` (with `MapInboundClaims=false`), so role-based authorization can never match
- **ID:** BUG-240
- **Type:** BUG (broken authorization — over-restrictive deny, blocks a primary admin flow)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #136, merged 2026-07-03 — RoleClaimType='roles'; regression test PASS + live-verified PUT /tenant/auth-settings 200, was 403)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Authentication / US-AUTH-005 / TC-AUTH-032 (also blocks TC-AUTH-029/034 which need `mfaPolicy=required` set via this endpoint)
- **Title:** `PUT /api/v1/tenant/auth-settings` is gated with `[Authorize(Roles = "Tenant Admin,Tenant Owner,System Admin")]`. A genuine Tenant Admin (`tenantadmin@acme.test`, JWT `roles` claim = `"Tenant Admin"`) receives HTTP 403 (empty body) on every PUT, while GET (plain `[Authorize]`) returns 200. Root cause is a JWT claim-type mismatch: `JwtService` emits the role in a claim named `"roles"`, `Program.cs` sets `MapInboundClaims = false` (no remap to `ClaimTypes.Role`), and `GetTokenValidationParameters()` never sets `RoleClaimType = "roles"` — so ASP.NET's role check reads the default `ClaimTypes.Role`, which is absent → role match always fails → 403. Every `[Authorize(Roles=…)]` endpoint is affected; the Admin controllers deliberately avoided this (their XML comments note "JWT carries roles in a custom 'roles' claim (not ClaimTypes.Role), so the established permission-policy gate is used rather than `[Authorize(Roles=…)]`"), but `TenantAuthSettingsController` and `TenantUsersController` still use role-based authz and are broken.
- **Root cause (~95%, BE config):** `src/backend/HRM.Infrastructure/Identity/JwtService.cs` `GetTokenValidationParameters()` (lines 181-191) omits `RoleClaimType = "roles"`; combined with `MapInboundClaims = false` (`src/backend/HRM.Api/Program.cs:79`) and the `roles`-named claim (`JwtService.cs:59,121`). Fix: set `RoleClaimType = "roles"` on the `TokenValidationParameters` handed to the JWT bearer handler (+ an integration test over a role-gated endpoint). Confidence 95% — reproduced live (403 for correct role, 200 on GET), config confirmed in source, and the codebase's own comments document that role claims are not `ClaimTypes.Role`.
- **Reproduction steps:** login `tenantadmin@acme.test` / `Admin@123!` on subdomain `acme` (role claim decodes to `"Tenant Admin"`, 83 permissions). `PUT /api/v1/tenant/auth-settings` with `{"mfaPolicy":"required","mfaRequiredRoles":["Employee"]}` and that bearer → HTTP 403 empty body; the change does not persist (subsequent GET still `mfaPolicy:"optional"`). `GET /api/v1/tenant/auth-settings` with the same token → 200. Same 403 expected on `TenantUsersController.cs:278/305/333` (`[Authorize(Roles = "Tenant Admin,Tenant Owner")]`).
- **Evidence:** admin JWT `roles`=`"Tenant Admin"`; PUT auth-settings → HTTP=403 (empty); GET auth-settings → 200 `{mfaPolicy:"optional",mfaRequiredRoles:[],idleTimeoutMinutes:60,…}`; PUT `mfaPolicy:"invalid_value"` also 403 (never reaches validation). Employee PUT → 403 (correct). Source lines: `JwtService.cs:59`, `Program.cs:79`, `JwtService.cs:181-191`.
- **Severity rationale:** HIGH — a primary tenant-admin flow (managing the tenant MFA/auth policy, plus 3 user-management endpoints) is entirely unreachable by the role that owns it, with no workaround short of a code change. Functional deny (fail-closed, not a leak) so not CRIT, but it breaks a core capability and blocks the `mfaPolicy=required` precondition for TC-AUTH-029/034/037.

### ISSUE-241 — Recovery-code login succeeds but the response carries no "regenerate your recovery codes" prompt/flag (US-AUTH-005 AC-7, TC-AUTH-030 step 8)
- **ID:** ISSUE-241
- **Type:** ISSUE (missing secondary behavior / contract nit)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Status:** RESOLVED (PR #367, 2026-07-18)
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Authentication / US-AUTH-005 / TC-AUTH-030 (step 8)
- **Title:** Logging in via a recovery code (`POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/challenge` with `{email, code:<recoveryCode>}`) correctly issues tokens and marks the code used, but the returned `LoginResponse` has no field prompting the user to regenerate recovery codes (e.g. `promptRegenerateRecoveryCodes: true`) and no warning message. TC-AUTH-030 step 8 expects the response (or a follow-up notification) to nudge the user to regenerate/re-enroll after burning a code. `LoginResponse` exposes only `{accessToken,user,tenant,permissions,mfaChallenge,mfaMethod,mfaEnrollmentRequired,refreshToken}` — none signal remaining-code depletion.
- **Root cause (~85%, BE):** `VerifyMfaLoginAsync` (`AuthService.cs:1052-1062`) marks the matched recovery code `UsedAt` and issues tokens via the shared path, but never sets a regenerate hint, and `LoginResponse` has no such property. Confidence 85% (a separate notification channel was not exhaustively checked).
- **Reproduction steps:** enroll+verify MFA on `employee@acme.test`; `POST /auth/login` → challenge; `POST /auth/mfa/challenge` `{email, code:"<recovery code>"}` → 200 with `accessToken`, response JSON has no `promptRegenerate*`/warning key.
- **Evidence:** recovery-code challenge → HTTP 200, `data` keys = accessToken/user/tenant/permissions/mfaChallenge/mfaMethod/mfaEnrollmentRequired/refreshToken; no regenerate flag. Recovery single-use + `mfa_recovery_code_used` audit DO work.
- **Severity rationale:** LOW — the security-critical behavior (recovery login works, single-use, audited) is correct; only the UX safeguard reminding a user their codes are depleting is absent.

### ISSUE-242 — Required custom-fields are only validated when a (partial) `customFields` object is sent; omitting `customFields` entirely bypasses the required-field check on employee creation (US-CHR-001 AC-6/FR-9)
- **ID:** ISSUE-242
- **Type:** ISSUE (validation asymmetry / required-field bypass)
- **Severity:** MED
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (2026-07-16, PR pending). **⚠ The earlier "DEFERRED — no validation exists, must ADD
  it" conclusion was WRONG** (it inferred from behaviour without opening the source). The validation DOES exist and
  is correct: `CustomFieldService.ValidateCustomFieldValuesAsync` treats an empty/omitted payload as "no values
  supplied" and flags every active REQUIRED definition (`CustomFieldService.cs:401-437`). The bug was a pure
  **null-skip**: `EmployeeService.CreateAsync` only CALLED the validator `if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.CustomFields))`,
  so omitting the object entirely skipped it → 201 bypass. Fix: **call the validator unconditionally** (it already
  handles the empty case). Mutation-verified (`Create_EnforcesRequiredCustomFields_EvenWhenCustomFieldsOmitted` —
  restoring the guard makes the create wrongly succeed). 84/84 green across the employee/custom-field suites.
- **Layer:** BE
- **Module / US / TC:** Core HR / US-CHR-001 / surfaced during TC-CHR-075 execution
- **Title:** Tenant `acme` has required custom fields ("Nickname", "Shirt Size"). `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees` with a partial `customFields` (e.g. `{"nickname":"Johnny"}`) is correctly rejected 400 ("Custom field 'Shirt Size' is required."). But the same create with `customFields` omitted altogether returns 201 Created — the required-custom-field validation appears to run only when the `customFields` payload is present/non-null, so a caller can skip all required custom fields by not sending the object, creating employees that violate the tenant's required-custom-field configuration.
- **Root cause (~70%, BE):** likely the custom-field validator short-circuits when the incoming `CustomFields` string is null/empty rather than treating "no custom fields provided" as "all required custom fields missing." Confidence 70% — inferred from the 201-vs-400 asymmetry via API; validator source not opened (report-only). Needs a clean confirming repro (two identical creates differing only by presence of `customFields`).
- **Reproduction steps:** as `hr@acme.test` on `acme`, `POST /api/v1/tenant/employees` with valid active `departmentId`/`jobTitleId`, `employmentType:"FullTime"`, and no `customFields` → 201. Repeat with `customFields:"{\"nickname\":\"Johnny\"}"` → 400 "Custom field 'Shirt Size' is required."
- **Evidence:** create without `customFields` (firstName `<script>alert('x')</script>`, `xss<ts>@acme.test`) → HTTP 201, employee persisted; create with partial `customFields` (`cfprobe<ts>@acme.test`) → HTTP 400 required-field error. Both used the same active department/job-title.
- **Severity rationale:** MED — data-integrity gap: the tenant admin's "required" custom-field policy is silently bypassable by API callers (and any create path that doesn't populate `customFields`), producing employee records missing mandated data. Contained (not a security/tenant-isolation breach) so not HIGH; moderate confidence pending a controlled repro.
